entries.text: lucknowi dum biryani awadhi/lucknowi pakki biryani: meat and rice cooked separately, then sealed and finished on dum gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb basmati rice yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic saffron green cardamom black cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf mace (javitri) kewra water mint ghee atta (wholewheat flour) salt cook the mutton with yogurt, ginger, garlic, half the birista, the whole spices and salt until tender and almost dry, about 45 minutes. this is the korma base. boil the soaked rice in heavily salted water with a bay leaf until it is 70% done — the grain should still have a firm core when pressed. layer: meat at the bottom, rice over it, then the saffron milk, remaining birista, mint, kewra and ghee across the top. seal the lid with a rope of atta dough, or cover tightly with foil and a lid. cook on the lowest possible heat for 25 minutes — over a tawa if your burner runs hot — or in a 160c oven. rest 10 minutes before breaking the seal, then lift from the bottom with a flat spoon so the grains stay whole.

entries.title: Murgh Korma
entries.snippet: pale, fragrant chicken in a yogurt and cashew gravy with no chilli heat to speak of
entries.text: murgh korma awadhi/lucknowi pale, fragrant chicken in a yogurt and cashew gravy with no chilli heat to speak of gluten-free healthier chicken yogurt / dahi onion cashews almonds ghee ginger garlic coriander powder fennel powder green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mace (javitri) white pepper saffron kewra water water salt fry two sliced onions in 3 tbsp ghee over medium heat until evenly brown, 10–12 minutes. drain and reserve the birista. grind the soaked cashews, almonds and half the birista to a smooth paste with 4 tbsp water. in the same ghee add the remaining ghee, bay leaf, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them swell for 30 seconds. add the third sliced onion and cook gently until soft and pale gold, 6 minutes, without letting it colour further. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell lifts. add the chicken and turn it in the masala over medium heat for 5 minutes, until it turns opaque but takes no colour. take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt in three additions, then return to the lowest flame and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the fat separates. stir in the nut paste, coriander powder, fennel powder, mace, white pepper and salt and cook 4 minutes. pour in 300ml warm water, cover and simmer very gently 20–25 minutes until the chicken is tender. finish with the saffron milk, kewra water and the remaining birista crushed over the top. rest covered 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Murgh Musallam
entries.snippet: a whole chicken stuffed with boiled eggs and simmered in a rich birista and nut gravy
entries.text: murgh musallam awadhi/lucknowi a whole chicken stuffed with boiled eggs and simmered in a rich birista and nut gravy gluten-free chicken eggs yogurt / dahi onion cashews almonds ginger garlic ghee kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder garam masala green cardamom black cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mace (javitri) nutmeg saffron cream kewra water salt water fry 3 of the sliced onions in 4 tbsp ghee over medium heat until deep brown, 14-16 minutes. drain on paper and let them go crisp, then grind half to a paste with the cashews, almonds and 4 tbsp water. rub the chicken all over and into the slashes with half the ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp salt and the kashmiri chilli. whisk the yogurt with the coriander powder and coat the bird. refrigerate 4 hours. push the boiled eggs into the cavity and tie the legs together with kitchen string so the stuffing stays put. heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a wide heavy pan and brown the marinated chicken on all sides, 8-10 minutes, turning with two spoons. lift it out and reserve any marinade left in the bowl. in the same pan crackle the bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves and both cardamoms for 30 seconds, then add the remaining sliced onion and cook to soft gold, 7 minutes. add the rest of the ginger-garlic paste, fry 2 minutes, then stir in the nut-and-birista paste and the reserved marinade. bhuno on medium heat 8 minutes, until the gravy thickens and ghee rims the pan. pour in the hot water with the mace, nutmeg and salt and bring to a simmer. lower the chicken in breast-side down, spooning gravy over it. cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat 45 minutes, turning the bird once at the halfway mark and basting twice. uncover, spoon over the cream and saffron milk and cook 5 minutes more to glaze. if you want a browned top, slide the open pan under a hot oven grill for 4 minutes. finish with the kewra water, rest 10 minutes, then carve at the table with the remaining crushed birista scattered over.

entries.title: Mutton Kaliya
entries.snippet: the everyday turmeric-yellow mutton curry of Lucknow kitchens, lighter and sharper than korma
entries.text: mutton kaliya awadhi/lucknowi the everyday turmeric-yellow mutton curry of lucknow kitchens, lighter and sharper than korma gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi onion ghee ginger garlic turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mace (javitri) saffron kewra water salt water fry the sliced onion in the ghee over medium heat until evenly deep brown, 12-14 minutes. lift it out onto paper and reserve. in the same ghee add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and both cardamoms. when they swell and smell sweet, about 40 seconds, add the chopped onion and cook to pale gold, 6 minutes. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes and the fat looks glossy. add the mutton and brown it hard over high heat for 8 minutes, until the pieces are seared on all sides and the pan is dry. take the pan off the heat for a minute, then whisk in the yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly. return to low heat. add the turmeric, coriander, chilli, fennel and dry ginger powders with the salt. bhuno over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, until the ghee separates and pools at the edges. pour in the hot water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 50-60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until the meat gives to a spoon. crush the reserved birista between your palms and stir it in with the ground mace. simmer uncovered 5 minutes to thicken. take off the heat, stir in the saffron milk and kewra water, cover and rest 10 minutes before serving with sheermal or plain rice.

entries.title: Mutton Korma
entries.snippet: slow-braised mutton in a dark, nut-thickened yogurt gravy scented with black cardamom
entries.text: mutton korma awadhi/lucknowi slow-braised mutton in a dark, nut-thickened yogurt gravy scented with black cardamom gluten-free healthier mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi onion ghee cashews melon seeds (magaz) poppy seeds (khus khus) ginger garlic coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mace (javitri) nutmeg saffron kewra water water salt fry the sliced onions in 4 tbsp ghee over medium heat until deep brown, 12–14 minutes. drain the birista and reserve the ghee. grind the soaked seeds and nuts with two-thirds of the birista and 5 tbsp water to a smooth paste. heat the reserved ghee with the remaining 2 tbsp, add the bay leaves, black and green cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them crackle 40 seconds. lift the mutton out of the marinade and brown it in batches over high heat, 4 minutes a batch. return all of it to the pan. lower the flame, pour in the leftover yogurt marinade a ladle at a time and stir without stopping for 8 minutes until the fat rims the pan. add the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, mace and salt and bhuno for 5 minutes, splashing in a little hot water each time it catches. stir in the nut paste and cook 4 minutes until it darkens a shade and smells toasted. add 500ml hot water, bring to a bare simmer, cover tightly and cook 60–70 minutes until the meat pulls off the bone. uncover and reduce 5 minutes if the gravy is looser than a pouring cream. finish with saffron milk, kewra water, grated nutmeg and the reserved birista. rest covered 10 minutes.

entries.title: Muzaffar
entries.snippet: saffron-yellow fine vermicelli fried in ghee and glazed with syrup, khoya and slivered nuts
entries.text: muzaffar awadhi/lucknowi saffron-yellow fine vermicelli fried in ghee and glazed with syrup, khoya and slivered nuts vegetarian vermicelli (semiya) ghee sugar water khoya / mawa saffron milk green cardamom almonds pistachios raisins (kishmish) kewra water warm 3 tbsp ghee in a kadhai on low heat and add the broken vermicelli. roast 6-8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it is a deep even brown and smells toasty. tip the roasted vermicelli onto a plate so it stops cooking. in the same pan bring the sugar and water to a boil and cook 4 minutes, until the syrup is slightly sticky between finger and thumb but nowhere near thread stage. stir the saffron milk and ground cardamom into the syrup. add the roasted vermicelli to the simmering syrup, stir once, cover and cook on the lowest heat 6-8 minutes, until the strands are soft and the syrup is almost gone. fry the almonds, pistachios and raisins in the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan for 90 seconds, until the nuts are gold and the raisins swell. uncover the vermicelli, scatter over the crumbled khoya and half the fried nuts, and fold through gently with a fork. sprinkle the kewra water, cover off the heat and rest 5 minutes. serve warm, topped with the remaining nuts and raisins.

entries.title: Nargisi Kofta
entries.snippet: boiled eggs sheathed in spiced mutton mince, fried and halved into a korma gravy
entries.text: nargisi kofta awadhi/lucknowi boiled eggs sheathed in spiced mutton mince, fried and halved into a korma gravy gluten-free eggs mutton / lamb chana dal besan (gram flour) onion ginger garlic green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) yogurt / dahi cashews ghee neutral oil coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala green cardamom cinnamon cloves mace (javitri) saffron water salt simmer the mince with the drained chana dal, one sliced onion, ginger and garlic pastes, salt and 150ml water until dry, about 20 minutes. cool, then grind to a stiff paste and knead in the roasted besan, green chilli, chopped coriander and half the garam masala. refrigerate 45 minutes. divide into 6, flatten each into a disc on your wet palm and wrap it around an egg, sealing every seam. deep fry two at a time in medium-hot oil, turning, until an even deep brown, 3–4 minutes. drain and set aside. for the gravy, fry the two remaining sliced onions in 2 tbsp ghee until deep brown, 12 minutes. drain, cool and grind with the soaked cashews and 4 tbsp water. heat the remaining ghee with the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 30 seconds, then add the onion-cashew paste and cook 5 minutes. off the heat, whisk in the yogurt in three additions, return to a low flame and stir 6 minutes until the fat separates. add the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, mace, remaining garam masala and salt and cook 3 minutes, then pour in 350ml warm water and simmer 12 minutes. halve each kofta lengthways with a sharp knife so the egg shows, and lay them cut side up in the gravy. spoon the gravy over, add the saffron milk, cover and rest off the heat 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Nihari
entries.snippet: Overnight shank stew, thickened with wheat flour and finished with ginger and lime
entries.text: nihari awadhi/lucknowi overnight shank stew, thickened with wheat flour and finished with ginger and lime nut-free healthier mutton / lamb atta (wholewheat flour) onion ginger garlic fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala black cardamom cinnamon bay leaf lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) green chilli ghee salt brown the sliced onion in ghee, then add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook until the raw smell goes. add the powdered spices with a splash of water so they do not scorch, then the mutton. turn it in the masala over high heat until sealed. add 2 litres of water and the whole spices. bring to a boil, then drop to the barest simmer, cover, and cook 4-5 hours until the meat slides off the bone. whisk the atta into a cup of cold water until perfectly smooth and stir it into the pot. simmer 30 minutes more, stirring often, until the gravy coats a spoon. rest off the heat 20 minutes; the fat will rise. do not skim it — that layer is the point. serve with julienned ginger, green chilli, coriander and a hard squeeze of lemon at the table.

entries.title: Shahi Tukda
entries.snippet: ghee-fried bread soaked in saffron syrup under a blanket of thick rabri
entries.text: shahi tukda awadhi/lucknowi ghee-fried bread soaked in saffron syrup under a blanket of thick rabri vegetarian no-onion-garlic sliced bread ghee milk khoya / mawa sugar water saffron green cardamom pistachios almonds rose water simmer the milk in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat, scraping the cream back in from the sides every few minutes, until reduced to about a third, 40–45 minutes. stir in the grated khoya, 3 tbsp sugar, half the saffron milk and half the cardamom powder and cook 5 minutes more. set the rabri aside to cool a little. meanwhile boil the 150g sugar with 150ml water for 5 minutes to a thin one-string syrup, then stir in the remaining saffron milk and the rose water. cut each bread slice into two triangles. fry them in ghee over medium heat until deep golden and crisp on both sides, 2 minutes a side, adding ghee as needed. drain on paper. dip each fried triangle into the warm syrup for 5 seconds a side and lift it straight out onto a serving plate. arrange the soaked bread in a single overlapping layer and spoon the warm rabri over the top. scatter with pistachios, almonds and the remaining cardamom powder. chill 1 hour before serving so the rabri sets and the bread softens through.

entries.title: Shami Kebab
entries.snippet: dense little mutton and chana dal patties, smooth inside and crisp at the edge
entries.text: shami kebab awadhi/lucknowi dense little mutton and chana dal patties, smooth inside and crisp at the edge gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb chana dal onion garlic ginger dried red chillies black cardamom green cardamom cinnamon cloves black pepper water eggs green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) mint garam masala lemon / lime ghee salt pressure cook the mutton, drained dal, quartered onion, garlic, ginger, whole chillies, black cardamom, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, salt and 250ml water for 5 whistles, about 20 minutes. open the lid and boil hard, stirring, until every trace of liquid has gone and the mix looks dry and sandy, 8–10 minutes. cool completely, then pick out the cinnamon stick and black cardamom shell and grind the rest to a smooth, tight paste with no added water. knead in the finely chopped onion, green chilli, coriander, mint, garam masala and the beaten egg. taste for salt now. divide into 12 and shape into flat discs 5cm across and 1.5cm thick. refrigerate 30 minutes. heat 2 tbsp ghee on a tawa over medium heat and lay in the kebabs without crowding. fry 3–4 minutes a side until a deep brown crust forms, adding the remaining ghee as you turn. drain on paper, rest 2 minutes and serve hot with lemon wedges and sliced onion.

entries.title: Sheermal
entries.snippet: slightly sweet saffron-milk flatbread, soft as brioche, brushed with ghee
entries.text: sheermal awadhi/lucknowi slightly sweet saffron-milk flatbread, soft as brioche, brushed with ghee vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic plain flour (maida) milk ghee sugar yogurt / dahi baking soda saffron green cardamom salt dissolve the sugar and salt in the warm milk and stir in the yogurt. mix the maida with the baking soda, rub in 60g of the melted ghee until it looks like breadcrumbs, then add half the saffron milk. add the milk mixture gradually and knead 10 minutes to a soft, smooth, slightly sticky dough. cover with a damp cloth and rest 1 hour at room temperature. knock back, divide into 8 and roll each into a disc 15cm across and 5mm thick. prick all over with a fork. bake at 220c on a preheated tray for 6–7 minutes, until the surface is set and just speckled. pull the tray out, brush each bread generously with the remaining saffron milk and melted ghee, and return for 3 minutes. dust with cardamom powder, stack under a cloth and serve warm with korma or kebabs.

entries.title: Ulte Tawe Ka Paratha
entries.snippet: wafer-thin layered paratha cooked on the back of an upturned tawa
entries.text: ulte tawe ka paratha awadhi/lucknowi wafer-thin layered paratha cooked on the back of an upturned tawa vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic plain flour (maida) atta (wholewheat flour) milk water ghee sugar salt mix the maida, atta, salt and sugar, rub in 2 tbsp of the melted ghee, then bring together with the warm milk and enough warm water to make a soft dough. knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover with a damp cloth and rest 45 minutes. divide into 8 and roll one ball into a 20cm disc. brush it all over with melted ghee, dust lightly with dry maida, then cut a slit from centre to edge and roll it tightly into a cone. press the cone down onto its point into a flat pastry and rest 10 minutes. repeat with the rest. roll each pastry out to a very thin disc, 22–24cm across, working from the centre outwards. set the tawa upside down over medium heat and let it get properly hot, 4 minutes. drape a paratha over the convex surface and cook 60–90 seconds until the underside is spotted brown and it lifts freely. flip with tongs, brush with ghee and cook 60 seconds more, pressing the edges down onto the metal. crush the hot paratha lightly between your palms to open the layers and serve at once with galouti or korma.

entries.title: Warqi Paratha
entries.snippet: a many-layered flaky paratha that shatters into thin leaves, the Lucknow bread for korma
entries.text: warqi paratha awadhi/lucknowi a many-layered flaky paratha that shatters into thin leaves, the lucknow bread for korma vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) ghee rice flour milk water sugar salt rub 2 tbsp ghee into the maida with the salt and sugar until the flour looks like damp breadcrumbs and holds when squeezed. add the warm milk, then water a little at a time, and knead 6-8 minutes to a soft, smooth dough that is slightly stickier than chapati dough. cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. divide into 4 balls. roll one out into a thin round about 22cm across, as even as you can get it. spread 1 heaped tsp of the ghee-and-rice-flour paste right to the edges, then pleat the round into a narrow fan, folding it back and forth in 1.5cm concertina folds. stretch the pleated strip gently, then coil it into a spiral like a snail shell and tuck the end underneath. rest 10 minutes. press the coil flat with your palm and roll it out to about 15cm, using the lightest pressure you can. repeat with the rest. cook on a medium-hot tawa 1.5 minutes a side until pale brown spots appear, then brush with ghee and press the edges down with a cloth as it puffs. lift off and immediately clap the paratha between your palms once — the leaves separate and fan out.

entries.title: Zarda
entries.snippet: saffron sweet rice studded with nuts and raisins, served at the end of a dastarkhwan
entries.text: zarda awadhi/lucknowi saffron sweet rice studded with nuts and raisins, served at the end of a dastarkhwan vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice sugar ghee saffron green cardamom cloves cinnamon khoya / mawa almonds pistachios cashews raisins (kishmish) dried coconut (copra) kewra water water salt fry the almonds, pistachios, cashews and coconut in 2 tbsp ghee until just gold, 2 minutes, then the raisins for 20 seconds until they puff. drain and set aside. boil 1.2 litres of water with the salt, half the saffron milk, the cardamom and cloves. add the drained rice and cook uncovered for 6–7 minutes, until the grains are 80 percent done and still firm at the core. drain thoroughly in a colander and leave 5 minutes to steam dry. in a heavy pan melt the remaining 3 tbsp ghee, add the sugar and 100ml water and stir until it dissolves into a thin syrup, 3 minutes. fold the drained rice gently into the syrup with the remaining saffron milk, using a flat spoon and lifting rather than stirring. cover tightly, put a heavy lid or a weight on top and cook on the lowest possible heat for 15 minutes. uncover: the syrup should be absorbed and the grains separate and glossy. if wet, cook uncovered 3 minutes more. scatter over the fried nuts, raisins, crumbled khoya and kewra water, cover again and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving warm.

entries.title: Aloo Posto
entries.snippet: potatoes cooked down in a nutty poppy seed paste, mild and quietly rich
entries.text: aloo posto bengali potatoes cooked down in a nutty poppy seed paste, mild and quietly rich vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato poppy seeds (khus khus) green chilli mustard oil nigella seeds (kalonji) turmeric powder sugar salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds to lose its raw bite. return to medium heat, add the nigella seeds and let them sputter for 10 seconds. drain the potatoes, pat dry, and add them with the turmeric and salt. fry 6-7 minutes, turning, until the edges are pale gold. pour in 180ml water, cover, and simmer 10-12 minutes until a knife slides through the potato with slight resistance. stir in the poppy seed paste and the slit green chillies. cook uncovered on low for 6-8 minutes. the gravy is ready when it clings to the potatoes and you can see oil at the edge of the pan. add the sugar, check the salt, and finish with the remaining 1 tbsp raw mustard oil off the heat. rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Basanti Pulao
entries.snippet: sweet saffron-yellow ghee rice studded with cashews and raisins
entries.text: basanti pulao bengali sweet saffron-yellow ghee rice studded with cashews and raisins vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice ghee turmeric powder saffron cashews raisins (kishmish) bay leaf green cardamom cinnamon cloves ginger sugar salt water heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the cashews until golden, about 90 seconds. lift out. fry the raisins in the same ghee for 20 seconds until they swell, then lift them out too. add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them puff for 20 seconds. add the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds. tip in the marinated rice and fry very gently for 3 minutes, folding rather than stirring. pour in 500ml hot water with the sugar, the saffron and its soaking water, and the rest of the salt. bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest possible heat for 12 minutes. turn off the heat and leave it covered and undisturbed for 10 minutes. uncover, fork through the fried cashews and raisins, and serve with kosha mangsho or a dry vegetable.

entries.title: Begun Bhaja
entries.snippet: thick eggplant slices fried until the edges go dark and lacy
entries.text: begun bhaja bengali thick eggplant slices fried until the edges go dark and lacy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic eggplant / brinjal turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar rice flour mustard oil salt heat the mustard oil in a wide tawa until it smokes, then lower the heat to medium. lay in the eggplant rounds in a single layer, leaving space between them. fry 3-4 minutes without touching them, until the underside is deep brown and the edge looks frilled. turn once with a flat spatula and fry the second side 3 minutes. press the centre lightly — it should give completely, with no firm core left. lift onto kitchen paper and fry the next batch, adding a little more oil if the pan looks dry. serve immediately alongside hot rice and dal, while the edges are still crisp.

entries.title: Bengali Alur Dom
entries.snippet: baby potatoes sealed in a tangy yogurt and ginger gravy, the standard partner to luchi
entries.text: bengali alur dom bengali baby potatoes sealed in a tangy yogurt and ginger gravy, the standard partner to luchi vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier potato yogurt / dahi tomato ginger cumin seeds dried red chillies bay leaf asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala green chilli sugar salt mustard oil ghee water heat the mustard oil to smoking point in a kadhai and let it settle off the heat for 30 seconds. fry the boiled potatoes with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a pinch of salt over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes, until the skins are blistered and gold all over, then lift them out. add the bay leaf, 1 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli to the oil and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida. fry the ginger paste for 1 minute, until it loses its raw smell. add the pureed tomato with the remaining turmeric, kashmiri chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 minutes, until the oil separates cleanly at the sides. pull the pan off the heat, beat in the whisked yogurt, then set it back on the lowest flame and cook 3 minutes without boiling. return the potatoes with the sugar, salt and slit chillies and turn them in the masala for 3 minutes so every one is coated. add the water, bring to a simmer, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. uncover, raise the heat and reduce for 3 minutes until the gravy clings to the potatoes rather than pooling. stir through the garam masala, the ghee and the roasted bhaja moshla, cover and rest 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Bengali Ghugni
entries.snippet: white peas stewed soft with fried coconut slivers and a dust of roasted spice
entries.text: bengali ghugni bengali white peas stewed soft with fried coconut slivers and a dust of roasted spice vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free dried white peas (safed matar) potato onion ginger tomato coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds dried red chillies bay leaf turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala tamarind baking soda green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime sugar salt mustard oil water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds. fry the coconut slivers over medium heat for about 90 seconds, until they turn light brown at the edges, and lift them out. fry the diced potato in the same oil for 5 minutes until golden, then set aside. add the bay leaf, 1 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli and let them crackle for 20 seconds. add the chopped onion and fry for 8 minutes, stirring, until deep gold at the edges. stir in the ginger paste and cook 1 minute, then add the tomato with the chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 minutes until the oil separates. tip in the cooked peas with their liquid, the fried potato, the sugar and salt, and the remaining 100ml water. simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, crushing a ladleful of peas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy. stir in the tamarind pulp and slit chillies and cook 2 minutes more, then check the salt. serve in bowls topped with the fried coconut, raw chopped onion, coriander, a dusting of bhaja moshla and garam masala, with lemon wedges alongside.

entries.title: Chingri Bhapa
entries.snippet: prawns steamed in mustard, coconut and green chilli until just set and sweet
entries.text: chingri bhapa bengali prawns steamed in mustard, coconut and green chilli until just set and sweet pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier prawns mustard seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli turmeric powder sugar salt mustard oil coconut milk water grind the soaked mustard and poppy seeds with three green chillies, the coconut and 3 tbsp water to a smooth paste. beat 3 tbsp of the mustard oil into the paste along with the remaining turmeric, the sugar, salt and the coconut milk if using. fold the prawns through the paste until evenly coated and let them sit 10 minutes. spread the prawns in a single layer in the tiffin box, scrape in every bit of paste, and tuck in the two whole chillies. spoon the last tablespoon of raw mustard oil over the surface and close the lid tightly. stand the box in a pan with water a third of the way up its sides, cover, and steam on medium for 15 minutes. turn off the heat and leave the box shut for 5 minutes to finish in its own steam. open away from your face and serve immediately with hot plain rice.

entries.title: Chingri Malai Curry
entries.snippet: prawns in a sweet cardamom-scented coconut milk gravy
entries.text: chingri malai curry bengali prawns in a sweet cardamom-scented coconut milk gravy pescatarian gluten-free nut-free healthier prawns coconut milk onion ginger turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf green chilli mustard oil ghee sugar garam masala salt heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool for 30 seconds, then sear the prawns 45 seconds a side until they just turn pink at the edges. lift them out immediately. add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves to the same oil and let them puff for 20 seconds. add the onion paste and fry 7-8 minutes on medium until it turns pale gold and the oil begins to separate. stir in the ginger paste, the remaining turmeric and the kashmiri chilli and cook 1 minute. pour in the coconut milk with the sugar and salt, stirring as you go. simmer on low, uncovered, for 6-7 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. return the prawns with the slit green chillies and cook exactly 2 minutes. turn off the heat, stir in the ghee and garam masala, and cover for 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Cholar Dal
entries.snippet: bengal gram simmered sweet-spiced with coconut slivers and raisins
entries.text: cholar dal bengali bengal gram simmered sweet-spiced with coconut slivers and raisins vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal coconut (fresh or desiccated) raisins (kishmish) ghee cumin seeds bay leaf dried red chillies cinnamon green cardamom cloves ginger turmeric powder sugar garam masala salt water drain the soaked dal and pressure cook with 700ml water, the turmeric and half the salt for 2 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. open the cooker and mash lightly against the side with a spoon — about a quarter of the dal, no more. keep it on low heat while you make the tempering. heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan. add the bay leaves, dried red chillies, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds. add the cumin seeds and grated ginger and fry 20 seconds until fragrant. pour the whole tempering into the dal, stir, and simmer 8 minutes uncovered. add the sugar and raisins and cook another 3 minutes until the raisins plump. stir in the garam masala and most of the fried coconut. check the salt. scatter the last of the coconut over the top and serve hot with luchi.

entries.title: Dhokar Dalna
entries.snippet: diamonds of fried chana dal cake simmered in a gingery potato gravy
entries.text: dhokar dalna bengali diamonds of fried chana dal cake simmered in a gingery potato gravy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal potato tomato ginger green chilli asafoetida (hing) cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala mustard oil ghee sugar salt water heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai, add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, the nigella and half the asafoetida, and let them crackle for 15 seconds. add the dal paste with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt. stir constantly over medium heat for 10-12 minutes. tip the hot mixture onto the oiled tray and press it flat to about 1.5cm with the back of a wet spoon. cool 30 minutes, then cut into diamonds. heat 3 tbsp oil and fry the diamonds in batches, 2-3 minutes a side, until crusted and deep gold, handling them with a flat spatula. drain and set aside. in the same pan fry the potato quarters with a pinch of turmeric for 5 minutes until golden. set aside. add the last 1 tbsp oil, the bay leaves, remaining cumin seeds and asafoetida, and crackle 15 seconds. add the remaining ginger paste and cook 1 minute, then the tomato puree and all the ground spices. fry this masala 6-8 minutes, sprinkling in a tablespoon of water whenever it sticks, until the oil separates at the edges. add the potatoes, 600ml water, the slit chilli, sugar and salt. simmer covered 15 minutes until the potato is tender. slide in the fried dhoka pieces and simmer uncovered 3-4 minutes only. finish with the garam masala and ghee, rest 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

entries.title: Dimer Dalna
entries.snippet: boiled eggs fried golden then simmered in a spiced potato gravy
entries.text: dimer dalna bengali boiled eggs fried golden then simmered in a spiced potato gravy vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free eggs potato onion tomato ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder cumin seeds bay leaf garam masala mustard oil sugar coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil to smoking in a kadhai, then reduce to medium. roll the pricked eggs in 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and fry them 3-4 minutes, turning, until blistered and golden. lift out. fry the halved potatoes in the same oil for 6 minutes until browned on the cut sides. set aside. add the bay leaves and cumin seeds to the oil and let them crackle 15 seconds. add the chopped onion and fry 8-10 minutes until deep golden brown. stir in the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute, then add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down. add the spice paste and fry 5-6 minutes, splashing in water whenever it catches, until oil pools at the edge. return the potatoes with 500ml water, the sugar and salt. simmer covered 15 minutes until tender. add the fried eggs and simmer uncovered 5 minutes so they take on colour. stir in the garam masala, scatter the coriander leaves, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or luchi.

entries.title: Doi Maach
entries.snippet: fish poached in whisked yogurt with cardamom and ginger, tangy and pale gold
entries.text: doi maach bengali fish poached in whisked yogurt with cardamom and ginger, tangy and pale gold pescatarian gluten-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) yogurt / dahi onion ginger turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf green chilli mustard oil ghee sugar salt water heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool it slightly, then fry the fish steaks 2-3 minutes a side until just set. lift out. pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil. add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds. add the onion paste and fry 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it is pale gold and no longer smells sharp. add the ginger paste and cook 1 minute more. take the pan off the heat entirely and let it cool for a full minute. add the spiced yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring continuously, until it is all in and smooth. return to the lowest heat and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring in one direction, until the gravy thickens and gloss appears on the surface. add 150ml water, the sugar, salt and slit chillies and bring to the barest simmer. slide the fish back in, spoon the gravy over, and cook 5 minutes covered. finish with the ghee off the heat and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Echorer Dalna
entries.snippet: green jackfruit simmered in a gingery gravy until it eats like meat
entries.text: echorer dalna bengali green jackfruit simmered in a gingery gravy until it eats like meat vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier raw jackfruit (kathal) potato ginger tomato cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon green cardamom cloves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala sugar salt mustard oil ghee water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then let it cool for 30 seconds. fry the quartered potatoes with a pinch of turmeric and salt over medium heat for 6 minutes, until golden on all sides, and set aside. fry the drained jackfruit pieces in the same oil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until they are patched with brown. lift them out. into the remaining oil add the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida. add the ginger paste and fry for 1 minute, until it stops smelling raw. add the chopped tomato with the turmeric, chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, mashing as you go, until the oil separates and pools at the edges. return the jackfruit and potato, add the salt and sugar, and turn everything in the masala for 3 minutes. pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the gravy has thickened to coat a spoon. uncover, stir in the ghee and garam masala, and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with rice or luchi.

entries.title: Ilish Bhapa
entries.snippet: hilsa steamed in raw mustard paste and mustard oil, sharp and unapologetic
entries.text: ilish bhapa bengali hilsa steamed in raw mustard paste and mustard oil, sharp and unapologetic pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard seeds green chilli turmeric powder salt sugar mustard oil coconut (fresh or desiccated) water grind the soaked mustard seeds with four green chillies, the sugar and 3 tbsp of the soaking water to a smooth, pourable paste. mix the paste with the coconut, 4 tbsp of the mustard oil, the remaining turmeric and salt to taste. turn the fish pieces gently in this mixture until each is fully coated, and let them sit 10 minutes. lay the fish in a single layer in the tiffin box, pour over any leftover paste and tuck in the two whole green chillies. spoon the last tablespoon of raw mustard oil over the top and close the lid tightly. set the box in a pan with water coming a third of the way up its sides, cover the pan, and steam on medium for 20 to 22 minutes. turn off the heat and leave the box closed for a further 5 minutes. open carefully, away from your face, and serve with hot plain rice, spooning the mustard oil from the box over each portion.

entries.title: Kosha Mangsho
entries.snippet: Mutton slow-fried in its own masala until almost dry and very dark
entries.text: kosha mangsho bengali mutton slow-fried in its own masala until almost dry and very dark gluten-free nut-free mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala bay leaf cinnamon green cardamom sugar mustard oil potato salt marinate the mutton with yogurt, turmeric and salt for an hour. heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, then caramelise the sugar until it darkens — this is where the colour comes from. add the whole spices and sliced onion and fry until genuinely brown, 12-15 minutes. add ginger, garlic and the powdered spices, then the marinated mutton. now begin koshano: fry over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 30-40 minutes. when the oil separates and the meat is deep brown, add just enough hot water to cover, cover the pan and simmer 30-40 minutes until tender. add the fried potatoes for the last 10 minutes, finish with garam masala, and reduce until the gravy clings.

entries.title: Kumror Chokka
entries.snippet: sweet pumpkin and chickpeas tempered with panch phoron, cooked until the edges collapse
entries.text: kumror chokka bengali sweet pumpkin and chickpeas tempered with panch phoron, cooked until the edges collapse vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier pumpkin chickpeas (kabuli chana) potato panch phoron dried red chillies bay leaf ginger asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder sugar salt mustard oil coconut (fresh or desiccated) garam masala water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then take it off the heat for half a minute to settle. fry the potato chunks with a pinch of the turmeric over medium heat for 5 minutes, until the edges are golden, then lift them out. into the same oil add the panch phoron, broken chillies and bay leaf and let them pop for about 20 seconds. stir in the asafoetida and grated ginger and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant. add the turmeric, chilli, cumin and coriander powders with 2 tbsp water and fry this paste for 2 minutes, until the oil beads at the edges. return the potato and add the pumpkin, cooked chickpeas, salt and sugar. toss everything in the masala for 2 minutes. pour in 100ml water, cover, and cook on low for 15 minutes until the pumpkin gives way under a spoon. mash four or five pieces of pumpkin against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy, add the coconut and cook uncovered for 3 minutes. sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with luchi or rice.

entries.title: Labra
entries.snippet: a soft mixed vegetable torkari fragrant with panch phoron and ginger
entries.text: labra bengali a soft mixed vegetable torkari fragrant with panch phoron and ginger vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier pumpkin potato sweet potato eggplant / brinjal raw banana / plantain french beans cabbage panch phoron dried red chillies bay leaf ginger turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) asafoetida (hing) mustard oil sugar garam masala salt water heat the mustard oil to smoking in a wide kadhai, then reduce the heat. add the bay leaves, dried red chillies and the remaining 1/2 tsp whole panch phoron. let them crackle 15 seconds. add the asafoetida and the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds. tip in the potato and sweet potato and fry 4 minutes until the edges are translucent. add the pumpkin, raw banana, beans and cabbage with the turmeric, cumin powder and salt. fold gently for 3 minutes. add the eggplant last, along with 200ml water. cover and cook on low for 18-20 minutes. uncover: the pumpkin should have collapsed and be binding everything into a rough mash. cook uncovered 4-5 minutes to drive off the last of the water. stir in the sugar, garam masala and the crushed toasted panch phoron. rest 5 minutes and serve with khichuri or rice.

entries.title: Lau Ghonto
entries.snippet: bottle gourd cooked down to a soft mash with roasted moong dal and ghee
entries.text: lau ghonto bengali bottle gourd cooked down to a soft mash with roasted moong dal and ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier bottle gourd (lauki) moong dal ginger green chilli cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder sugar salt mustard oil ghee garam masala coconut (fresh or desiccated) water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it just begins to smoke, then pull it off the flame for 30 seconds. return the pan to medium heat and drop in the bay leaf and cumin seeds. they should crackle within 20 seconds. add the grated ginger and slit chillies and stir for 30 seconds, until the ginger smells sweet rather than raw. tip in the diced gourd with the turmeric and salt, stir to coat, then cover and cook on medium-low for 12 minutes. uncover, add the roasted moong dal and the water, and simmer uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes until the dal is soft and the mixture mounds on a spoon. stir in the sugar and grated coconut and cook another 2 minutes, mashing a few pieces of gourd against the side of the pan to thicken it. take the pan off the heat, stir through the ghee and garam masala, and cover for 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Luchi
entries.snippet: small white maida puris that puff into balloons, the sunday-morning bread
entries.text: luchi bengali small white maida puris that puff into balloons, the sunday-morning bread vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic plain flour (maida) ghee salt sugar water neutral oil mix the maida, salt and sugar, then rub in the ghee with your fingertips for 2 minutes until it looks like damp sand. add the lukewarm water a little at a time and knead 6-8 minutes into a smooth, firm, non-sticky dough. cover and rest 20 minutes. divide into 20 balls the size of a large marble and roll each into a 9cm circle, greasing the board with a drop of oil rather than dusting with flour. heat the oil in a deep kadhai to 180c — a scrap of dough should rise to the surface within 2 seconds. slide in one luchi. it will sink, then float within 3 seconds. press the centre down gently with the back of a slotted spoon for 3-4 seconds and it will balloon. flip and fry the second side 15 seconds only. luchi should stay white and blond, never brown. drain upright in a colander rather than flat on paper so they stay puffed. serve straight away with cholar dal or aloo dum.

entries.title: Macher Jhol
entries.snippet: a thin turmeric and ginger fish broth built around fried rohu steaks
entries.text: macher jhol bengali a thin turmeric and ginger fish broth built around fried rohu steaks pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) potato tomato eggplant / brinjal turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) ginger nigella seeds (kalonji) green chilli mustard oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower to medium-high. slide in the fish steaks and fry 3 minutes a side until the surface is firm and browned. lift the fish out onto a plate and leave the oil in the pan. fry the potato wedges in the same oil for 5 minutes until golden at the edges, then add the eggplant for 2 minutes. push the vegetables aside, add the nigella seeds to the clear space and let them pop for 10 seconds. stir in the spice paste and fry 2-3 minutes until it darkens and stops smelling raw. add the tomato, slit chillies, 700ml water and salt. bring to a boil and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender. return the fish steaks, spooning gravy over them, and simmer 4 minutes only. turn off the heat, scatter the coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Mishti Doi
entries.snippet: milk boiled down with caramelised jaggery and set into a thick fudgy curd
entries.text: mishti doi bengali milk boiled down with caramelised jaggery and set into a thick fudgy curd vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic milk jaggery sugar yogurt / dahi green cardamom bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pan, then lower the heat and simmer 30-35 minutes, scraping the skin at the sides back in each time, until it reduces to about 900ml. meanwhile melt the 2 tbsp sugar in a small dry pan over medium heat until it turns the colour of dark honey, about 4 minutes. stir the caramel into the reduced milk — it will hiss — and cook 2 minutes more. add the chopped jaggery and cardamom and stir off the heat until fully dissolved. cool the milk to 45c — warm to a fingertip but not hot enough to sting. whisk the starter yogurt smooth in a cup, then whisk in a ladle of the warm milk. pour that back into the pan, stir twice only, and pour into the earthenware bowl or ramekins. cover and leave in a warm, draught-free place — a switched-off oven with the light on works well — for 6-8 hours without moving it. when it is set firm enough that the surface does not wobble as a whole, chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

entries.title: Panch Mishali Chorchori
entries.snippet: five vegetables cooked dry in their own steam with panch phoron and ground mustard
entries.text: panch mishali chorchori bengali five vegetables cooked dry in their own steam with panch phoron and ground mustard vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier potato eggplant / brinjal pumpkin radish (mooli) french beans mustard seeds panch phoron dried red chillies green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar salt mustard oil water heat the mustard oil in a wide kadhai until it smokes, then rest it off the heat for 30 seconds. add the panch phoron and dried chillies and let them crackle for 20 seconds. add the potato and radish batons with the turmeric and salt and stir-fry uncovered for 5 minutes. add the pumpkin, beans and eggplant with the slit green chillies, toss well, then cover and cook on low for 10 minutes. uncover and check: the vegetables should be nearly tender and the pan almost dry. add a spoon of water only if it is sticking. stir in the mustard paste, chilli powder and sugar, and cook uncovered for 5 minutes so the raw mustard cooks off. raise the heat for a final 2 to 3 minutes to let the edges of the vegetables catch and brown a little. take off the heat, spoon over the last teaspoon of raw mustard oil if you like it sharp, and serve with rice and dal.

entries.title: Patishapta
entries.snippet: thin rice-flour crepes rolled around coconut and jaggery, the sweet of poush month
entries.text: patishapta bengali thin rice-flour crepes rolled around coconut and jaggery, the sweet of poush month vegetarian nut-free rice flour plain flour (maida) rava / sooji (semolina) milk sugar salt coconut (fresh or desiccated) jaggery khoya / mawa green cardamom ghee water cook the grated coconut with the jaggery in a kadhai over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides in a single mass. stir in the khoya, 2 tbsp milk and half the cardamom and cook 3 minutes more, then spread the filling on a plate to cool. whisk the rice flour, maida, rava, sugar, salt and remaining cardamom with the milk until completely lump-free, then rest the batter 30 minutes. divide the cooled filling into 8 portions and shape each into a short log about 8cm long. heat a tawa over medium-low and wipe it with ghee. it is ready when a drop of batter sets in about 3 seconds without hissing violently. pour a small ladle of batter into the centre and spread it with the back of the ladle into a 15cm oval, thin at the edges. cook undisturbed for about 90 seconds, until the surface looks dry and matte and the edges lift away on their own. lay a log of filling along one edge and roll the crepe over it into a tight cylinder using a spatula. slide the roll onto a plate seam-side down and repeat, wiping the tawa with ghee between each. serve warm, or at room temperature with a spoonful of warmed nolen gur poured over.

entries.title: Payesh
entries.snippet: rice cooked slowly down in milk with cardamom and date palm jaggery
entries.text: payesh bengali rice cooked slowly down in milk with cardamom and date palm jaggery vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic milk rice (short/medium grain) jaggery sugar green cardamom bay leaf ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) salt bring the milk to a boil with the bay leaf and bruised cardamom, then lower to a bare simmer. simmer 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the skin from the sides back in, until it has reduced by about a quarter. add the drained, ghee-coated rice and the pinch of salt. cook on low for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes so nothing sticks, until the grains are completely soft and the milk has thickened to the consistency of pouring cream. fry the cashews and raisins in a dry pan for 90 seconds until the cashews are gold and the raisins swell. stir them into the payesh and cook 2 minutes more. take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 8-10 minutes — the surface should no longer be steaming hard. stir in the chopped jaggery and the sugar if using until fully dissolved. do not put the pan back on the heat. cool to room temperature, then chill at least 2 hours before serving.

entries.title: Peyaji
entries.snippet: crisp onion fritters shot through with nigella and green chilli
entries.text: peyaji bengali crisp onion fritters shot through with nigella and green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free onion besan (gram flour) rice flour nigella seeds (kalonji) green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder baking soda coriander leaves (cilantro) mustard oil salt squeeze the salted onions lightly with your hands to bring out their water, keeping the liquid in the bowl. add the besan, rice flour, nigella, green chilli, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander leaves and mix with your fingers. the mixture should just cling together in a ragged clump — add 1 tsp water at a time only if it is genuinely dry. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then bring it down to a steady 170c. drop in irregular clumps the size of a walnut, six or seven at a time. fry 4-5 minutes, turning once at the halfway point, until deep amber and no longer bubbling hard. lift onto a wire rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp. fry the next batch, letting the oil come back up to temperature between batches, and serve hot with rice and dal or on their own with mustard.

entries.title: Potoler Dorma
entries.snippet: hollowed pointed gourd stuffed with paneer and coconut in a delicate poppy seed gravy
entries.text: potoler dorma bengali hollowed pointed gourd stuffed with paneer and coconut in a delicate poppy seed gravy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier pointed gourd (parwal) paneer coconut (fresh or desiccated) poppy seeds (khus khus) raisins (kishmish) ginger green chilli yogurt / dahi tomato cumin seeds bay leaf green cardamom cinnamon cloves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala sugar salt mustard oil ghee water rub the hollowed gourds with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a little salt and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry. heat 2 tbsp mustard oil and fry the crumbled paneer with the ginger, minced chillies, coconut, raisins, chopped gourd flesh, a pinch of salt and 1/4 tsp garam masala for 5 minutes, until dry and crumbly. cool slightly. pack the stuffing tightly into the gourds, pressing it in with the back of a teaspoon. heat the remaining mustard oil to smoking, cool it 30 seconds, then shallow-fry the stuffed gourds for 5 to 6 minutes, turning carefully, until blistered and golden. lift out. into the same oil add the bay leaf, cumin seeds, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, then the asafoetida, and let them crackle 20 seconds. add the pureed tomato with the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook for 5 minutes until the oil separates. take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt, then return it to the lowest flame and cook for 3 minutes without letting it boil. stir in the poppy seed paste, the sugar and salt, and cook 2 minutes more. pour in the water, bring to a bare simmer, then slide the stuffed gourds in and cook covered on low for 12 minutes, spooning gravy over them twice. finish with the ghee and remaining garam masala and rest 5 minutes before serving with basanti pulao or luchi.

entries.title: Radhaballavi
entries.snippet: puffed white bread stuffed with fennel-scented ground urad dal
entries.text: radhaballavi bengali puffed white bread stuffed with fennel-scented ground urad dal vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic plain flour (maida) urad dal (black gram) ghee fennel powder fennel seeds (saunf) ginger asafoetida (hing) dry ginger powder (saunth) cumin powder (jeera) red chilli powder green chilli sugar salt neutral oil water heat 2 tbsp of the frying oil in a pan, add the asafoetida, crushed fennel seeds and grated ginger, and let them fizz for 20 seconds. add the ground dal with the fennel powder, dry ginger, cumin, chilli powder, sugar and salt, and cook on low for 10 to 12 minutes, breaking up lumps, until it is dry and sandy. spread the filling on a plate to cool completely, then divide it into 12 balls. knead the rested dough for a minute and divide it into 12 equal balls. flatten each dough ball into a 7cm disc with a thicker centre, place a ball of filling in the middle and gather the edges over the top, pinching them shut. rest the stuffed balls seam-side down for 10 minutes, then roll each gently into a 10cm disc using oil, not flour, on the board. heat the remaining oil in a kadhai to 180c. a scrap of dough should rise to the surface in about 3 seconds. slide in one radhaballavi, press it lightly under the oil with a slotted spoon for 5 seconds, and it will balloon. fry 40 seconds a side, until pale gold rather than brown, and lift onto a rack. repeat with the rest, keeping the oil steady between batches, and serve hot with alur dom.

entries.title: Rasgulla
entries.snippet: Chhena dumplings boiled in light syrup until they double and turn spongy
entries.text: rasgulla bengali chhena dumplings boiled in light syrup until they double and turn spongy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free milk lemon / lime sugar green cardamom rose water plain flour (maida) water bring the milk to a boil, take it off the heat, and add lemon juice a little at a time until the curds separate cleanly from greenish whey. strain through muslin and rinse under cold water to wash out the acid. hang 30 minutes — no longer. knead the chhena on a plate with the heel of your hand for 8-10 minutes, until it goes from grainy to smooth and slightly greasy. work in the maida if using. roll into 12 crack-free balls, smaller than you want them finished — they double. bring the sugar and water to a rolling boil with the cardamom. slide the balls in, cover, and boil hard for 15 minutes. cool in the syrup, add rose water, and chill at least 4 hours before serving.

entries.title: Rui Macher Kalia
entries.snippet: fried rohu steaks in a deep onion and ginger gravy, the wedding-lunch fish curry
entries.text: rui macher kalia bengali fried rohu steaks in a deep onion and ginger gravy, the wedding-lunch fish curry pescatarian gluten-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) potato onion ginger garlic tomato yogurt / dahi bay leaf green cardamom cinnamon cloves turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala green chilli sugar salt mustard oil ghee water heat 5 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes. slide in the fish steaks, two or three at a time, and fry 3 minutes on the first side without touching them, then 2 minutes on the second. lift out onto a plate. fry the potato quarters in the same oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside with the fish. add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, then the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, and let them crackle for 20 seconds. add the onion paste and cook on medium for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until it is deep gold and no longer smells raw. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes more. add the pureed tomato with the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until the oil pulls away to the sides of the pan. take the pan off the heat, beat in the yogurt, then cook on the lowest flame for 3 minutes without boiling. add the water, sugar, salt, slit chillies and the fried potatoes, and simmer covered for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender. slide the fish back in, spoon gravy over each piece, and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes. do not stir. finish with the ghee and garam masala, cover and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Sandesh
entries.snippet: fresh chhena kneaded with sugar into a soft barely-cooked milk sweet
entries.text: sandesh bengali fresh chhena kneaded with sugar into a soft barely-cooked milk sweet vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic milk lemon / lime sugar green cardamom saffron water bring the milk to a full boil in a heavy pan, then turn the heat off completely. wait 60 seconds, then add the diluted lemon juice a spoonful at a time, stirring slowly, until the curds separate and the whey runs pale green. pour into the muslin-lined colander and rinse the curds under cold water for 30 seconds to wash off the lemon and stop the cooking. gather the muslin, squeeze gently, and hang for 30 minutes. tip the chhena onto a clean surface and knead with the heel of your hand for 8-10 minutes until it goes from grainy to completely smooth and slightly greasy. work in the powdered sugar and cardamom and knead 2 minutes more. transfer to a non-stick pan and cook on the lowest heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides in a mass. spread on a plate and cool 15 minutes until it is comfortable to handle but still warm. divide into 12 while still warm, roll each into a ball and flatten slightly, pressing a strand of saffron or a thumbprint into the top. cool completely before serving.

entries.title: Shorshe Ilish
entries.snippet: Hilsa poached in a raw mustard paste, the dish Bengal argues about most
entries.text: shorshe ilish bengali hilsa poached in a raw mustard paste, the dish bengal argues about most gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard seeds green chilli turmeric powder nigella seeds (kalonji) mustard oil salt soak the mustard seeds 20 minutes in warm water, then grind with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste. strain if you want it silky. rub the fish with turmeric and salt and rest 10 minutes. heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, then take it off the heat for a moment — this removes the raw pungency. return to low heat, add the nigella, then the mustard paste thinned with half a cup of water, the remaining chillies and salt. simmer 3 minutes. slide in the fish in a single layer, spoon the sauce over, cover and cook 8 minutes. do not stir — shake the pan. finish with a tablespoon of raw mustard oil poured over, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Shukto
entries.snippet: a gently bitter mixed vegetable stew in milk, eaten first with rice
entries.text: shukto bengali a gently bitter mixed vegetable stew in milk, eaten first with rice vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier bitter gourd (karela) drumstick (moringa pod) raw banana / plantain sweet potato eggplant / brinjal radish (mooli) milk mustard seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) panch phoron fennel seeds (saunf) ginger bay leaf mustard oil ghee sugar salt water heat 2 tbsp mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, then fry the bitter gourd rounds 3-4 minutes until browned at the edges. lift out and set aside. in the same oil, fry the eggplant and raw banana for 3 minutes until just coloured. set aside. add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the bay leaf and the panch phoron, and let it crackle for 15 seconds. add the ginger paste and cook 30 seconds until it smells sweet rather than raw. add the drumstick, radish and sweet potato with the salt and 300ml water. cover and simmer 12 minutes. return the fried vegetables to the pan and simmer uncovered 5 minutes more. stir the mustard and poppy paste into the milk, then pour it in and bring to the barest simmer. cook 4-5 minutes until the gravy is the thickness of single cream. add the sugar and crushed fennel, taste for salt, and finish with the ghee off the heat. rest 10 minutes. shukto is served slightly warm, not piping hot, at the start of the meal.

entries.title: Aloo Parwal ki Tarkari
entries.snippet: dry pointed gourd and potato sabzi tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil
entries.text: aloo parwal ki tarkari bihari dry pointed gourd and potato sabzi tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pointed gourd (parwal) potato mustard oil panch phoron garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes lightly, then drop the flame to medium. add the panch phoron and wait 20 seconds for the fenugreek to darken and the fennel to smell sweet. throw in the crushed garlic and green chillies and fry 40 seconds until the garlic is pale gold. add the potato fingers and fry 5 minutes, turning, until the edges are translucent and starting to colour. add the parwal and fry a further 5 minutes until the cut faces are blistered and browned in patches. sprinkle over the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and toss for 1 minute. add the 4 tbsp water, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, shaking the pan twice. uncover, check that a knife slides through the potato, and cook off any remaining moisture for 2 minutes. stir through the amchur and coriander leaves, rest 2 minutes and serve with roti or dal-bhaat.

entries.title: Aloo ki Bhujia
entries.snippet: dry potato fingers tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil, crisp at the edges and no onion in sight
entries.text: aloo ki bhujia bihari dry potato fingers tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil, crisp at the edges and no onion in sight vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato mustard oil panch phoron dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder green chilli amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then drop the heat to medium. crackle the panch phoron and broken red chillies for 15-20 seconds, until the fenugreek seeds darken and the mustard seeds start popping. add the asafoetida, swirl once, then tip in the potato fingers and 3/4 tsp salt. toss to coat and spread the potatoes in one layer. fry undisturbed 4 minutes, then turn and fry 4 minutes more. sprinkle over the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder and toss gently to coat every piece. cover and cook on low for 8 minutes, shaking the pan twice, until a potato finger crushes easily against the side. uncover, raise the heat and fry a final 3-4 minutes until the edges are golden and crisped. add the slit green chillies and amchur, toss, and finish off the heat with coriander leaves. serve with dal and rice or with hot puris.

entries.title: Anarsa
entries.snippet: ghee-fried discs of soaked ground rice and jaggery, crusted with sesame
entries.text: anarsa bihari ghee-fried discs of soaked ground rice and jaggery, crusted with sesame vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) jaggery ghee sesame seeds milk poppy seeds (khus khus) green cardamom rub the grated jaggery into the ground rice flour with your fingertips until it looks like damp sand, 5 minutes. work in 2 tbsp ghee and the crushed cardamom and knead to a stiff dough that just holds when squeezed; add the milk a teaspoon at a time only if it crumbles. cover and rest the dough at room temperature for 24 hours, by which time it will have softened and smell faintly fermented. pinch off lime-sized balls, press each one into the plate of sesame, and flatten to a 7cm disc about 6mm thick, sesame side up. heat the ghee in a kadhai to a gentle 160c — a crumb of dough should rise slowly with fine bubbles, not fizz. slide in one disc, sesame side down, and fry undisturbed for 90 seconds until it lifts and floats. spoon hot ghee over the top rather than turning it, and fry a further 3 to 4 minutes until deep reddish-brown and the bubbling slows. lift each anarsa out with a slotted spoon and stand it on edge against the side of a colander to drain for 5 minutes. cool completely before eating — they crisp as they cool and are fragile while hot.

entries.title: Baingan Chokha
entries.snippet: fire-roasted aubergine mashed with raw mustard oil, garlic and green chilli
entries.text: baingan chokha bihari fire-roasted aubergine mashed with raw mustard oil, garlic and green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier eggplant / brinjal garlic green chilli onion mustard oil salt coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime tomato rub the aubergines with a few drops of oil and set them straight on a medium gas flame. roast 18 to 22 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the skin is blistered black all over and the flesh has collapsed inward. roast the tomato on the flame alongside for the last 6 minutes until its skin splits and blackens. rest the aubergines 5 minutes, then peel off every scrap of charred skin — do not rinse them under the tap or you wash the smoke away. mash the flesh coarsely with a fork along with the roasted tomato; leave some texture rather than making a puree. crush the 4 raw garlic cloves to a rough paste with a pinch of salt and stir them through. fold in the onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, salt and the raw mustard oil. squeeze over the lemon, taste for salt and serve at room temperature with litti, roti or rice and dal.

entries.title: Bihari Khichdi
entries.snippet: loose moong dal and rice khichdi eaten with ghee, chokha and pickle
entries.text: bihari khichdi bihari loose moong dal and rice khichdi eaten with ghee, chokha and pickle vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) moong dal ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies bay leaf turmeric powder ginger green chilli salt water cauliflower peas drain the soaked rice and dal well. heat 2 tbsp ghee in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds until they darken a shade. add the asafoetida, broken red chillies and bay leaf and fry 10 seconds — the hing should foam and smell sharp. stir in the ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant. add the cauliflower and peas if using and fry 3 minutes until the florets pick up a little colour. tip in the drained rice and dal with the turmeric and fry 2 minutes, stirring, until every grain is coated in ghee. pour in the water, add salt, close the cooker and cook on high for 3 whistles, then off the heat for 10 minutes. open the cooker and stir hard for 30 seconds; it should be loose enough to pour off a spoon. add hot water a splash at a time if it has set. serve into bowls and spoon the remaining ghee over each portion at the table, with chokha, papad and pickle alongside.

entries.title: Bihari Murgh Jhor
entries.snippet: thin, fiery home-style chicken curry cooked down in mustard oil with potatoes
entries.text: bihari murgh jhor bihari thin, fiery home-style chicken curry cooked down in mustard oil with potatoes gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken mustard oil onion garlic ginger tomato turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala cumin seeds bay leaf black cardamom green chilli salt water potato coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil until it smokes lightly, then take it off the flame for 30 seconds to settle. fry the potato halves for 5 minutes until golden on the cut faces, then lift them out and set aside. crackle the cumin seeds, bay leaves and black cardamom in the same oil for 30 seconds. add the onion and fry on medium for 12 minutes until it is properly brown and pulling away from the pan. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell goes. add the tomato, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and cook 6 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil beads at the edge. tip in the chicken and fry on high for 8 minutes, turning the pieces, until they are sealed and coated in dark masala. return the potatoes, pour in the hot water, add the green chillies and salt, and bring to a boil. simmer uncovered for 18 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the gravy has reduced by about a third — it should stay thin and pourable. stir in the garam masala, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or roti.

entries.title: Champaran Ahuna Mutton
entries.snippet: handi mutton sealed with dough and slow-cooked in mustard oil with whole garlic
entries.text: champaran ahuna mutton bihari handi mutton sealed with dough and slow-cooked in mustard oil with whole garlic nut-free mutton / lamb mustard oil garlic onion ginger yogurt / dahi dried red chillies red chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder garam masala black cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf salt water atta (wholewheat flour) coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil in a heavy pot until it thins and stops smelling sharp, about 3 minutes, then cool it slightly. fry the bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, black cardamom and whole dried chillies for 40 seconds until they swell and smell toasty. add the sliced onion and cook on medium until deep brown at the edges, 15 to 18 minutes. tip in the whole peeled garlic cloves and fry 3 minutes until they turn pale gold and lose their raw bite. add the marinated mutton and fry hard on high heat for 12 minutes, stirring, until the yogurt dries off and the oil separates at the sides. stir in the coriander powder and cook 2 minutes more, splashing in a tablespoon of water if it catches. pour in the 100 ml water, taste for salt, and bring to a hard boil for 2 minutes. press the rope of dough around the rim, clamp the lid on and cook on the lowest heat for 75 minutes without opening it. crack the seal, discard the dough, and check the meat — it should slide off the bone under a spoon. if not, reseal and give it 15 minutes more. scatter over the garam masala and coriander leaves, stir once, and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving.

entries.title: Dahi Chura Gud
entries.snippet: beaten rice softened in cold yogurt with jaggery, the Makar Sankranti breakfast
entries.text: dahi chura gud bihari beaten rice softened in cold yogurt with jaggery, the makar sankranti breakfast vegetarian gluten-free nut-free poha (flattened rice) yogurt / dahi jaggery milk sugar rinse the thick poha in a colander under cold water and shake it dry. let it drain and swell for 10 minutes; the flakes should be soft enough to crush between two fingers but still separate. whisk the chilled yogurt smooth in a large bowl with a pinch of salt. loosen it with the cold milk if it is stiff — you want the consistency of thin cream. fold the drained poha into the yogurt and leave it 5 minutes to absorb. taste and stir in the sugar only if the mixture is flat. serve into bowls with a generous pile of jaggery shards on the side of each portion, to be broken off and eaten with each spoonful.

entries.title: Dal Pitha
entries.snippet: steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coarse spiced chana dal, tempered in mustard oil
entries.text: dal pitha bihari steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coarse spiced chana dal, tempered in mustard oil vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice flour chana dal garlic ginger green chilli cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder mustard oil panch phoron dried red chillies coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water grind the drained chana dal with the garlic, ginger, green chilli, 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1 tsp salt to a coarse, sandy mixture with no added water. heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, add the asafoetida and turmeric, then the ground dal, and fry over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until it dries out and smells cooked. bring 450ml water to a rolling boil with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp mustard oil. take the pan off the heat, tip in the rice flour all at once and stir hard with a wooden spoon until it comes together into a shaggy mass. cover and leave 5 minutes. knead the warm dough with oiled palms for 4-5 minutes until it is completely smooth and takes a fingerprint without cracking. pinch off walnut-sized pieces, roll each into a ball and press into a 8cm disc between oiled palms. place a heaped teaspoon of the dal filling in the centre, fold into a half-moon and press the edge shut, crimping it with your fingers. steam the pithas in a single layer over boiling water for 12-15 minutes, until the surface turns glossy and no longer looks chalky. heat the remaining mustard oil until it smokes faintly, then crackle the panch phoron, remaining cumin seeds and broken red chillies for 20 seconds. toss the steamed pithas in the temper for 2 minutes so they take on a light crust, scatter over the coriander leaves and serve hot with chutney.

entries.title: Dhuska
entries.snippet: jharkhandi deep-fried rice and chana dal discs, crisp outside and soft within
entries.text: dhuska bihari jharkhandi deep-fried rice and chana dal discs, crisp outside and soft within vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) chana dal ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin seeds salt water neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) drain the soaked rice and dal thoroughly, shaking the colander dry. grind them with the ginger, green chillies and 150 ml water into a thick, slightly grainy batter — the texture of idli batter, not smooth. beat in the turmeric, chilli powder, cumin seeds and salt, then rest the batter 2 hours covered. stir in the coriander leaves and whisk the batter hard for 30 seconds to aerate it. heat the oil in a kadhai to 180c — a drop of batter should rise and sizzle within 3 seconds. slide in ladlefuls of batter, 3 at a time, easing each one into a rough 10cm disc as it hits the oil. fry 2 minutes until they puff and float, then turn and fry another 2 to 3 minutes until deep gold and crisp at the edges. lift onto a rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp, and repeat with the rest of the batter. serve hot with ghugni or aloo chokha.

entries.title: Ghugni
entries.snippet: dried white peas stewed soft with mustard oil, ginger and cumin, finished with lemon and black salt
entries.text: ghugni bihari dried white peas stewed soft with mustard oil, ginger and cumin, finished with lemon and black salt vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier dried white peas (safed matar) potato onion garlic ginger tomato mustard oil cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala black salt (kala namak) green chilli lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water drain the soaked peas and pressure cook them with 600ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 3 whistles, then 10 minutes on low. they should crush easily between finger and thumb but still hold their shape. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then lower the heat and let it settle for 30 seconds. crackle the cumin seeds and bay leaf for 20 seconds until the cumin darkens and smells toasted. add the chopped onion and fry over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until deep golden brown at the edges. stir in the garlic and grated ginger and cook 90 seconds, until the raw smell goes. add the tomato and cook 6-8 minutes, pressing it down, until it breaks up and the oil separates at the edges of the pan. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder with a splash of water and fry 1 minute so the spices do not burn. tip in the diced potato with 200ml water and cook covered 10 minutes, until the potato is just tender. add the cooked peas with their liquid and the slit green chillies. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes, mashing a ladleful of peas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy. stir in the garam masala, taste for salt, and finish off the heat with lemon juice, black salt, julienned ginger and coriander leaves.

entries.title: Kadhi Bari
entries.snippet: fried gram-flour dumplings soaked soft in a tart yogurt gravy with a mustard-oil temper
