entries.text: kadhi bari bihari fried gram-flour dumplings soaked soft in a tart yogurt gravy with a mustard-oil temper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) yogurt / dahi neutral oil mustard oil onion garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) baking soda coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water whisk 150g besan with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp turmeric, the baking soda and about 120ml water into a thick batter, then beat hard for 5 minutes until it is pale and fluffy. heat the neutral oil to 170c and drop in walnut-sized spoonfuls of batter. fry 4-5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and hollow-sounding. drain the bari on paper, then soak them in warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze gently. whisk the sour yogurt with the remaining 50g besan, the rest of the turmeric, the chilli powder and 1.2 litres water until absolutely smooth. heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and the fenugreek seeds for 15 seconds. add the chopped onion, garlic, ginger and green chillies and fry 6-8 minutes until the onion turns golden. pour in the yogurt mixture and bring it to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction. once boiling, lower the heat and simmer uncovered 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the kadhi coats a spoon and the raw besan smell is gone. add salt and slip in the squeezed bari. simmer another 8 minutes so they drink up the gravy. in a small pan heat the remaining 1 tbsp mustard oil, crackle the mustard seeds, remaining cumin, nigella, broken red chillies and asafoetida for 20 seconds, and pour it over the kadhi. scatter with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Litti Chokha
entries.snippet: baked wheat balls stuffed with spiced roasted gram, dipped in ghee and crushed over smoky brinjal mash
entries.text: litti chokha bihari baked wheat balls stuffed with spiced roasted gram, dipped in ghee and crushed over smoky brinjal mash vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) sattu (roasted gram flour) mustard oil ghee carom seeds (ajwain) nigella seeds (kalonji) garlic ginger green chilli lemon / lime eggplant / brinjal potato tomato onion coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water rub 2 tbsp mustard oil and 1 tsp salt into the atta until a squeezed handful holds its shape, then add water a little at a time to make a stiff, smooth dough. cover the dough and rest it 30 minutes. mix the sattu with the garlic, ginger, 4 chopped green chillies, the ajwain, nigella, juice of half the lemon, 3 tbsp mustard oil and 1 tsp salt, rubbing it through your fingers. divide the dough into 10 balls. cup each in your palm, press a hollow, pack in a heaped tablespoon of the sattu mix, then pinch the seam closed and roll smooth. bake at 200c for 25 minutes, turning once at the halfway mark, until the litti are dry, cracked across the top and pale brown. meanwhile rub the brinjal with a little oil and hold it directly over a gas flame, turning, for 10-12 minutes until the skin blisters black and the flesh slumps. char the tomatoes the same way for 5 minutes. boil the potatoes 15 minutes until a knife slides in without resistance, then drain and peel. peel the charred brinjal and tomatoes and mash them with the potato, chopped onion, remaining 2 green chillies, 1 tbsp mustard oil, the juice of the remaining lemon half and salt. fold in the coriander leaves and taste — chokha should be sharp with lemon and raw mustard oil, not bland. dip each hot litti in the melted ghee, holding it under for a few seconds so it soaks, then crush it open and serve over the chokha.

entries.title: Machhli ka Jhor
entries.snippet: river fish simmered in a thin, fiery mustard-oil gravy sharpened with ground mustard seed
entries.text: machhli ka jhor bihari river fish simmered in a thin, fiery mustard-oil gravy sharpened with ground mustard seed pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard oil mustard seeds onion garlic ginger tomato turmeric powder red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat 5 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes and the sharp smell dies down, then lower the heat. fry the fish steaks in batches, 2 minutes a side, until the surface is set and pale gold. lift out and set aside. in the same oil add the remaining 2 tbsp, then crackle the cumin seeds and nigella for 20 seconds. add the onion paste and fry 8-10 minutes over medium heat until it loses its raw smell and turns light brown at the edges. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes, until the oil starts to bead at the sides. add the chopped tomato and cook 6 minutes, mashing it down, until it collapses completely. mix the remaining 1 tsp turmeric, the chilli powder, kashmiri chilli and coriander powder with 3 tbsp water and fry this paste for 3-4 minutes until the oil separates and floats clear. stir in the ground mustard paste and cook exactly 1 minute, no longer. pour in 500ml water with the slit green chillies and 1 tsp salt and bring to a boil. the gravy should be thin, like a light broth. slide the fried fish back in, lower the heat and simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes, spooning gravy over the pieces rather than stirring. rest 5 minutes off the heat, scatter with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Malpua
entries.snippet: fennel-scented flour pancakes fried in ghee with lace-crisp edges, steeped in light sugar syrup
entries.text: malpua bihari fennel-scented flour pancakes fried in ghee with lace-crisp edges, steeped in light sugar syrup vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) milk khoya / mawa sugar water fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom ghee saffron boil the 300g sugar with 150ml water for 5-6 minutes to a thin one-string syrup, stir in the saffron milk, and keep it warm over the lowest heat. whisk the maida with the grated khoya, 2 tbsp sugar, crushed fennel and ground cardamom. add the milk in three additions, whisking to a smooth, lump-free batter the consistency of thick pouring cream. cover and rest the batter 30 minutes, then check it — it should ribbon off the spoon and settle back in about 3 seconds. heat 2cm of ghee in a small kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter rises at once with a fizz. pour in a ladleful of batter from a height of about 10cm so it spreads into a 10cm round with frilled edges. fry two at a time at most. fry for 2 minutes without touching it, until the edges turn golden and lift on their own. turn once with a slotted spoon and fry the second side 90 seconds, spooning hot ghee over the centre. lift out, drain for a few seconds, then slide straight into the warm syrup and soak 4-5 minutes a side. lift out of the syrup and serve warm, with rabri or on their own.

entries.title: Mithila Machh Posto
entries.snippet: river fish simmered in a ground poppy seed and mustard gravy, no onion or garlic
entries.text: mithila machh posto bihari river fish simmered in a ground poppy seed and mustard gravy, no onion or garlic pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) poppy seeds (khus khus) mustard seeds mustard oil nigella seeds (kalonji) green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked poppy and mustard seeds with 2 of the green chillies and 3 tbsp of their soaking water to a smooth pale paste. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the flame. slide in the fish and fry 2 minutes a side until the surface is set and pale gold, then lift out onto a plate. crackle the nigella seeds in the remaining oil for 20 seconds until they smell smoky. add the ground paste with the remaining turmeric and the chilli powder and cook on low for 4 minutes, stirring constantly. pour in the water, add the remaining slit chillies and salt, and simmer 5 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. return the fish, spoon gravy over each piece, cover and simmer 6 minutes on low. drizzle over 1 tsp raw mustard oil, scatter the coriander and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Namkeen Sattu Sharbat
entries.snippet: savoury roasted gram drink with black salt, lemon and roasted cumin, drunk cold through the summer
entries.text: namkeen sattu sharbat bihari savoury roasted gram drink with black salt, lemon and roasted cumin, drunk cold through the summer vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free sattu (roasted gram flour) water black salt (kala namak) cumin seeds lemon / lime green chilli onion mint coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the cumin seeds in the same pan for about 1 minute, until they darken and pop, then crush them coarsely. whisk the sattu with just 100ml of the chilled water to a completely smooth, thick paste. whisk in the remaining 400ml chilled water in a steady stream until the drink is thin and even. stir in the black salt, plain salt, roasted crushed cumin and the juice of the whole lemon. add the green chilli, onion, mint and coriander leaves and stir once. taste and adjust — it should be sour and salty first, with the roasted flour underneath. serve immediately in tall glasses.

entries.title: Sarson Wala Aloo
entries.snippet: boiled potatoes turned through a sharp ground mustard paste, no onion or garlic
entries.text: sarson wala aloo bihari boiled potatoes turned through a sharp ground mustard paste, no onion or garlic vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato mustard seeds green chilli mustard oil nigella seeds (kalonji) turmeric powder salt water poppy seeds (khus khus) coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked mustard and poppy seeds with 2 green chillies, a pinch of salt and 3 tbsp of the soaking water to a smooth paste. heat the mustard oil until it smokes, then lower the flame and let it settle 30 seconds. crackle the nigella seeds for 20 seconds until they pop and smell smoky. add the potato chunks and fry 6 minutes, turning gently, until the edges are crisp and golden. push the potatoes to one side, add the turmeric to the clear oil and let it bloom for 10 seconds. stir in the ground mustard paste and cook on low for 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until it loses its raw smell. pour in the water, add the slit chillies and salt, and simmer 6 minutes until the gravy clings to the potatoes. take off the heat, scatter the coriander and drizzle over 1 tsp raw mustard oil before serving with rice or puri.

entries.title: Sattu ka Paratha
entries.snippet: wheat flatbread packed with garlicky roasted gram flour, sharp with mustard oil and ajwain
entries.text: sattu ka paratha bihari wheat flatbread packed with garlicky roasted gram flour, sharp with mustard oil and ajwain vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) sattu (roasted gram flour) mustard oil carom seeds (ajwain) nigella seeds (kalonji) garlic ginger green chilli onion lemon / lime amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water knead the atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp mustard oil and enough water to make a soft, pliable dough, about 6 minutes. cover with a damp cloth and rest 20 minutes. mix the sattu with the garlic, ginger, green chilli, onion, ajwain, nigella, amchur, coriander leaves, lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard oil and 3/4 tsp salt. divide the dough into 8 balls. roll one into a 10cm disc, mound 2 tbsp of filling in the centre, gather the edges over the top and pinch shut. flatten the sealed ball gently with your palm, dust with flour and roll out to about 18cm, pressing lightly and evenly from the centre. cook on a hot tawa for 1 minute until pale spots appear, flip, and cook the second side 1 minute. brush both sides with mustard oil and cook another minute a side, pressing the edges with a cloth, until brown blisters form. serve straight off the tawa with plain yogurt, chokha or a spoon of pickle.

entries.title: Tamatar Chokha
entries.snippet: charred tomatoes crushed with garlic, chilli and mustard oil into a smoky relish
entries.text: tamatar chokha bihari charred tomatoes crushed with garlic, chilli and mustard oil into a smoky relish vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier tomato garlic green chilli onion mustard oil salt black salt (kala namak) coriander leaves (cilantro) ginger set the tomatoes directly on a medium gas flame, resting them on the trivet. roast 10 to 12 minutes, turning with tongs, until the skins are blackened and split and the tomatoes slump. char the skewered garlic for the last 3 minutes until the cloves are spotted brown and soft. rest 5 minutes, then slip off and discard the blackened skins, saving any juice on the plate. mash the tomato flesh and roasted garlic together with a fork into a coarse pulp. crush the 3 raw garlic cloves with a pinch of salt and stir them in with the ginger. fold in the onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, salt, black salt and the raw mustard oil. taste and serve at room temperature with litti, sattu paratha or a plate of khichdi.

entries.title: Thekua
entries.snippet: hard, jaggery-sweetened wheat biscuits fried in ghee, made in every home for Chhath
entries.text: thekua bihari hard, jaggery-sweetened wheat biscuits fried in ghee, made in every home for chhath vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) jaggery water ghee fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom coconut (fresh or desiccated) neutral oil salt heat the water with the jaggery over low heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until it dissolves completely, then strain and cool to lukewarm. rub the melted ghee into the atta with the salt for 3-4 minutes, until the flour looks damp and clumps when pressed. mix in the crushed fennel, ground cardamom and grated coconut. add the jaggery water a little at a time and bring it together into a very stiff dough. do not knead it smooth. pinch off lime-sized pieces, roll into balls, then flatten each to about 1cm thick. press each disc onto a thekua mould, or score a criss-cross pattern with the back of a fork. heat the frying oil to 150c — low, not hot. a piece of dough should rise slowly after a few seconds. fry in batches for 8-10 minutes, turning often, until the thekua are a deep even brown and float high in the oil. lift out and drain on a rack, not on paper, and let them cool completely — they harden as they cool.

entries.title: Tilkut
entries.snippet: gaya's winter sweet of pounded roasted sesame and jaggery, dry and shattering
entries.text: tilkut bihari gaya's winter sweet of pounded roasted sesame and jaggery, dry and shattering vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free sesame seeds jaggery water neutral oil green cardamom dry-roast the sesame in a heavy kadhai on medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the seeds turn pale gold and start popping. tip the roasted sesame onto a cold plate to stop the cooking and cool it completely. pound about two-thirds of the sesame coarsely in a mortar, or pulse briefly in a grinder, leaving the rest whole. melt the jaggery with the water in the same kadhai on low heat, stirring until it dissolves, about 5 minutes. boil the syrup for 6 to 8 minutes to the hard-ball stage: a drop into cold water should set into a firm ball you can snap. take the pan off the heat, stir in the crushed cardamom, then work in all the sesame quickly until evenly coated. turn the mass out onto a greased surface and, while it is just cool enough to handle, pinch off walnut-sized pieces. flatten each piece into a 6cm disc with your greased palm and press the pounded sesame in firmly. leave the discs to cool and harden on a rack for 30 minutes before stacking.

entries.title: Chettinad Chicken Curry
entries.snippet: bone-in chicken in a freshly roasted masala of pepper, fennel and stone flower
entries.text: chettinad chicken curry tamil nadu bone-in chicken in a freshly roasted masala of pepper, fennel and stone flower gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) poppy seeds (khus khus) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cinnamon cloves star anise stone flower (dagad phool) bay leaf turmeric powder salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, coriander powder, black pepper, cumin, fennel, poppy seeds, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and stone flower in a dry pan over low heat for 4-5 minutes. add the grated coconut to the same pan and roast a further 3 minutes until it turns the colour of weak tea. cool the mixture completely, then grind to a fine powder, add 100ml water and grind again to a smooth thick paste. heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai and add the bay leaf and curry leaves; they will spit for a few seconds. add the shallots and fry over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and browning at the edges. grind the ginger and garlic to a coarse paste, add it to the pan and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell goes. add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until they collapse and the oil starts to separate at the sides. stir in the ground masala paste and fry on low for 6-8 minutes, scraping the base, until the oil rises dark red around the edges. add the chicken and turn it in the masala for 5 minutes so every piece is coated and sealed. pour in 200ml water, season with salt, cover and simmer 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy clings. rest off the heat 5 minutes, then scatter the coriander leaves and serve with rice or dosai.

entries.title: Chettinad Eral Masala
entries.snippet: prawns in a dark, freshly ground masala of pepper, fennel and stone flower
entries.text: chettinad eral masala tamil nadu prawns in a dark, freshly ground masala of pepper, fennel and stone flower pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier prawns sesame oil (gingelly / til) shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger curry leaves turmeric powder dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves green cardamom poppy seeds (khus khus) dried coconut (copra) lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the red chillies, coriander, pepper, fennel, cumin, stone flower, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and poppy seeds in a dry pan over low heat, 4-5 minutes. add the grated coconut to the same pan and roast a further 2 minutes, until it turns the colour of milky tea. cool completely. grind the roasted spices with 4 tbsp water to a thick, dark paste. heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai and fry the curry leaves for 10 seconds until they blister. add the shallots and cook over medium heat until soft and gold at the edges, about 8 minutes. stir in the crushed garlic and ginger and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes. add the tomatoes, turmeric and salt. cook until the tomatoes collapse and oil beads at the edge, about 6 minutes. add the ground masala and fry it hard for 5 minutes, adding a splash of water whenever it catches, until the paste darkens and oil separates. pour in 150ml water, bring to a simmer and cook 4 minutes to a thick, clinging gravy. slide in the prawns, cover and cook 3-4 minutes, until they curl and turn opaque. turn off the heat immediately. finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or dosai.

entries.title: Chettinad Kara Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: fiery tamarind gravy with drumstick, brinjal and whole shallots
entries.text: chettinad kara kuzhambu tamil nadu fiery tamarind gravy with drumstick, brinjal and whole shallots vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier drumstick (moringa pod) eggplant / brinjal shallots (small red onions) garlic tomato tamarind sambar powder red chilli powder turmeric powder black pepper fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) toor dal (pigeon pea) asafoetida (hing) curry leaves dried red chillies sesame oil (gingelly / til) jaggery salt water heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai and add the mustard seeds; when they pop, add the toor dal, fenugreek, cumin and fennel. fry 30 seconds until the dal is golden, then add the asafoetida, red chillies and curry leaves. add the whole shallots and garlic and fry 8 minutes over medium heat until browned and softening. add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down into the oil. lower the heat, add the sambar powder, chilli powder, turmeric and cracked pepper and fry 1 minute. add the drumstick pieces and turn them in the masala for 2 minutes. pour in the tamarind extract and 150ml water, season with salt and bring to a rolling boil. simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the raw tamarind smell is gone and the gravy has darkened. add the brinjals and simmer a further 8 minutes until they are tender but still holding their shape. stir in the jaggery and simmer 2 minutes more, until the oil floats clear on top. rest 15 minutes off the heat and serve with rice and a spoonful of the oil from the top.

entries.title: Chettinad Kozhi Biryani
entries.snippet: short-grain seeraga samba rice cooked with chicken, mint and whole spice
entries.text: chettinad kozhi biryani tamil nadu short-grain seeraga samba rice cooked with chicken, mint and whole spice gluten-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) chicken yogurt / dahi ghee sesame oil (gingelly / til) onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli mint coriander leaves (cilantro) curry leaves black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves green cardamom bay leaf mace (javitri) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder lemon / lime water salt heat the ghee and gingelly oil together in a heavy pot. fry the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf, mace, stone flower and fennel for 40 seconds, until they lift and smell sweet. add the sliced onion and fry 12 minutes, until evenly deep gold. keep a spoonful back for the top. stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste, green chillies and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes. add the tomatoes, coriander powder and crushed pepper and cook 8 minutes, until the tomatoes have gone to pulp and oil shows at the sides. add the marinated chicken with all its yogurt and fry on high 6 minutes, until the yogurt tightens around the pieces and stops looking watery. throw in the mint and coriander leaves and cook 2 minutes, until they wilt into the masala. pour in 750ml water, add the lemon juice and salt, and bring to a hard boil. taste it now — the liquid should be slightly saltier than you want the finished rice. drain the rice and stir it in. boil uncovered on high until the water level drops to the surface of the rice, about 6 minutes. cover tightly, drop the heat to the lowest setting and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid. turn off the heat and leave it covered another 10 minutes. fork through gently from the edges inward, top with the reserved fried onion and serve with onion raita and brinjal curry.

entries.title: Chettinad Meen Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: sharp tamarind fish curry with fenugreek and gingelly oil
entries.text: chettinad meen kuzhambu tamil nadu sharp tamarind fish curry with fenugreek and gingelly oil pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) tamarind shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic red chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder black pepper fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds fennel seeds (saunf) curry leaves coconut (fresh or desiccated) sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water heat the gingelly oil in a clay pot or kadhai and add the mustard seeds; wait for them to pop. add the fenugreek and fennel seeds and fry 20 seconds until the fenugreek turns one shade darker. add the curry leaves, shallots and crushed garlic and fry 7 minutes until the shallots are soft and golden. add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until pulpy. lower the heat, add the chilli powder, coriander powder, remaining turmeric and cracked pepper, and fry 1 minute in the oil. pour in the strained tamarind water and 100ml plain water, season with salt and bring to a boil. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes until the raw sourness has cooked off and the gravy has reduced by a third. grind the coconut with 50ml water and stir it in, then simmer 3 minutes. slide in the fish pieces in a single layer, spoon gravy over them and simmer 6-8 minutes without stirring. take it off the heat and leave it at least 2 hours before eating; the curry sets and sweetens as it stands.

entries.title: Chettinad Meen Varuval
entries.snippet: fish fried crisp under a red pepper-and-fennel paste, ready in half an hour
entries.text: chettinad meen varuval tamil nadu fish fried crisp under a red pepper-and-fennel paste, ready in half an hour pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) sesame oil (gingelly / til) kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder black pepper fennel powder coriander powder turmeric powder ginger garlic rice flour tamarind curry leaves lemon / lime salt mix the kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, pepper, fennel, coriander, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, tamarind pulp and salt into a thick paste with 1 tbsp water. rub the paste into the scored fish, working it into the cuts. rest 30 minutes. just before frying, dust the rice flour over both sides and press it on lightly. heat the gingelly oil on a tawa over medium-high until a crumb of masala sizzles immediately. lay the fish down and do not touch it for 4 minutes. the edges should go opaque and the underside deep rust-red. turn once and fry the second side 3-4 minutes. throw the curry leaves into the hot oil at the side of the pan for the last 20 seconds, until they crackle. drain briefly, top with the fried leaves and serve hot with lemon wedges.

entries.title: Chettinad Muttai Masala
entries.snippet: boiled eggs simmered in a roasted coconut and pepper masala
entries.text: chettinad muttai masala tamil nadu boiled eggs simmered in a roasted coconut and pepper masala vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier eggs shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds stone flower (dagad phool) cinnamon cloves star anise poppy seeds (khus khus) turmeric powder curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, coriander powder, pepper, fennel, cumin, poppy seeds, stone flower, cinnamon, cloves and star anise over low heat for 4 minutes. add the coconut and roast 3 minutes more until it smells toasty and turns pale brown. cool completely and grind with 100ml water to a smooth paste. heat 2 tbsp of the gingelly oil in a kadhai, add the scored eggs with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a pinch of salt, and fry 3 minutes turning until the skins are blistered and golden. lift the eggs out and set aside; add the remaining oil and the curry leaves to the same pan. fry the shallots for 6 minutes until golden, then add the ginger and garlic pounded to a paste and fry 2 minutes. add the tomatoes and remaining turmeric and cook 5 minutes until pulpy and the oil shows at the edges. stir in the ground masala and fry on low for 6 minutes until it darkens and the oil separates. add 250ml water and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. slip the fried eggs in, spoon gravy over them and simmer 5 minutes on the lowest heat. rest 5 minutes, scatter the coriander and serve with rice or chapati.

entries.title: Chettinad Mutton Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: slow-cooked goat in a dark coconut and roasted-spice gravy
entries.text: chettinad mutton kuzhambu tamil nadu slow-cooked goat in a dark coconut and roasted-spice gravy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) poppy seeds (khus khus) fennel seeds (saunf) black pepper dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves green cardamom curry leaves turmeric powder sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, coriander powder, pepper, cumin, fennel, poppy seeds, stone flower, star anise, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom over low heat for 5 minutes until aromatic. add the grated coconut and roast 4 minutes more until it is an even light brown. cool fully, then grind with 150ml water to a smooth paste. heat the gingelly oil in the pressure cooker base, add the curry leaves and let them splutter. add the shallots and fry 8 minutes until deep gold, then add the ginger and garlic ground to a paste and fry 2 minutes. add the mutton and brown it hard over high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until the pieces are seared all over. add the tomatoes and cook 4 minutes until they break down. stir in the ground masala and fry on low for 8 minutes until the oil separates and the paste darkens to brick. pour in 450ml water, season with salt, close the cooker and cook for 5 whistles, then on low for 12 minutes. let the pressure drop naturally, open, and simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and glosses. finish with the chopped coriander and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice or idiyappam.

entries.title: Chettinad Nandu Masala
entries.snippet: crab in a thick roasted masala of pepper, fennel and coconut
entries.text: chettinad nandu masala tamil nadu crab in a thick roasted masala of pepper, fennel and coconut pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier crab shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds coriander powder poppy seeds (khus khus) stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves turmeric powder curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) lemon / lime salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the red chillies, pepper, fennel, cumin, coriander powder, poppy seeds, stone flower, star anise, cinnamon and cloves over low heat for 4-5 minutes until fragrant. add the coconut and roast 3 minutes until light brown, then cool completely and grind with 100ml water to a coarse paste. heat the gingelly oil in a wide kadhai and crackle two sprigs of curry leaves. add the shallots and fry 7 minutes over medium heat until deep golden. pound the ginger and garlic to a paste, add it and fry 2 minutes until the raw edge is gone. add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until they collapse and the oil shows. stir in the ground masala and fry on low for 8 minutes, scraping constantly, until it is thick, dark and oily at the edges. add 150ml water and salt, bring to a boil and simmer 3 minutes. add the crab pieces and claws, turn them through the masala, cover and cook 8-10 minutes on medium. uncover and cook 4 minutes on high, tossing, until the masala clings to every piece and there is almost no free liquid. fry the last curry leaf sprig in a spoon of oil, scatter it over with the coriander, squeeze on the lemon and serve hot with plenty of napkins.

entries.title: Chettinad Pepper Chicken
entries.snippet: semi-dry milagu kozhi varuval, hot with coarsely cracked black pepper
entries.text: chettinad pepper chicken tamil nadu semi-dry milagu kozhi varuval, hot with coarsely cracked black pepper gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds shallots (small red onions) garlic ginger curry leaves dried red chillies turmeric powder coriander powder sesame oil (gingelly / til) lemon / lime salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai until it shimmers, then add the fennel, cumin and broken red chillies. add two sprigs of curry leaves and stand back — they will crackle hard for 10 seconds. tip in the shallots and fry 6 minutes over medium-high heat until browned at the edges. add the garlic and ginger and fry 90 seconds until fragrant. stir in the coriander powder and cook 30 seconds, just until it darkens. add the marinated chicken and fry on high for 5 minutes, turning, until the pieces are opaque and catching colour. pour in 100ml water, cover and cook 10 minutes on medium until the chicken is done through. uncover, add the remaining 1 tbsp cracked pepper and stir-fry 5-6 minutes on high until the liquid has gone and the masala is a dark clinging coat. fry the last sprig of curry leaves in the residual oil at the side of the pan for 20 seconds until crisp. squeeze over the lemon, scatter the crisp curry leaves and coriander, and serve hot with rice or parotta.

entries.title: Chettinad Urulai Roast
entries.snippet: potatoes fried crisp in gingelly oil with pepper, fennel and torn curry leaves
entries.text: chettinad urulai roast tamil nadu potatoes fried crisp in gingelly oil with pepper, fennel and torn curry leaves vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato sesame oil (gingelly / til) shallots (small red onions) garlic curry leaves mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) black pepper fennel powder red chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder rice flour coriander leaves (cilantro) salt toss the cold potato cubes with turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, fennel and salt, then dust with the rice flour. heat the gingelly oil in a wide kadhai, crackle the mustard seeds and let the urad dal turn gold, about 40 seconds. add the torn curry leaves and let them blister for 10 seconds. add the shallots and garlic and fry until translucent and just catching colour, 4 minutes. tip in the potatoes in a single layer and leave them alone for 5 minutes. turn once, spread out again and fry another 5 minutes. repeat once more, about 15 minutes of frying in total. crush in the black pepper off the heat and toss twice. scatter coriander leaves and serve hot alongside rasam and rice.

entries.title: Idiyappam
entries.snippet: steamed rice-flour string hoppers, soft as lace, eaten with coconut and curry
entries.text: idiyappam tamil nadu steamed rice-flour string hoppers, soft as lace, eaten with coconut and curry vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour water coconut oil coconut (fresh or desiccated) sugar salt bring the water to a rolling boil with the salt and 1 tbsp of the coconut oil. pour the boiling water over the flour all at once and mix with the handle of a wooden spoon until there is no dry flour left. cover and let it sit 5 minutes so the flour drinks the water. knead while still hot, with wet hands, into a smooth non-sticky dough. it should feel like soft clay and not crack when rolled into a ball. grease the steamer plates with coconut oil and scatter a teaspoon of grated coconut on each. fill the press, and squeeze the dough onto the plates in overlapping spirals, one layer thick. steam 6-8 minutes, until the strands turn from chalky white to glossy and translucent at the edges. rest 2 minutes before lifting them off — they firm up and release cleanly. repeat with the rest of the dough, keeping it covered between batches. serve warm with the remaining grated coconut, and a mutton or chicken kuzhambu, or with sweetened coconut milk.

entries.title: Kandarappam
entries.snippet: deep-fried jaggery and mixed-dal fritter from the festival kitchen
entries.text: kandarappam tamil nadu deep-fried jaggery and mixed-dal fritter from the festival kitchen vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal urad dal (black gram) moong dal jaggery coconut (fresh or desiccated) dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom sesame seeds rice flour salt water neutral oil drain the soaked rice and dals and grind to a slightly coarse batter with about 80ml water, thicker than dosa batter. melt the jaggery with 40ml water over low heat until it dissolves, then strain through a fine sieve into the batter. stir in the chopped coconut, crushed cardamom, dry ginger powder, sesame and salt. cover and rest the batter 1 hour at room temperature; it should be thick enough to drop slowly off a spoon. if it has loosened, beat in the rice flour a spoon at a time until it holds a soft mound. heat the oil in a kadhai to medium — a drop of batter should rise in about 4 seconds. slide in tablespoons of batter, 4 or 5 at a time, and fry 3 minutes until the undersides are deep brown. turn each one and fry a further 2-3 minutes until the edges are crisp and the centre puffed. lift onto a rack rather than paper so the crust stays crisp, and repeat with the rest of the batter. cool 10 minutes before eating — the inside is molten jaggery straight out of the pan.

entries.title: Kathirikai Chettinad
entries.snippet: small aubergines simmered in a roasted coconut, pepper and poppy-seed masala
entries.text: kathirikai chettinad tamil nadu small aubergines simmered in a roasted coconut, pepper and poppy-seed masala vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier eggplant / brinjal sesame oil (gingelly / til) shallots (small red onions) tomato garlic ginger tamarind curry leaves turmeric powder dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves poppy seeds (khus khus) coconut (fresh or desiccated) mustard seeds jaggery coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the chillies, coriander powder, pepper, fennel, cumin, stone flower, star anise, cinnamon, cloves and poppy seeds over low heat for 5 minutes. add the grated coconut and roast 2 minutes more, until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. cool. grind the roasted mixture with the garlic, ginger and 5 tbsp water to a smooth paste. heat 3 tbsp gingelly oil in a kadhai and fry the drained aubergines over medium-high heat, turning, for 5 minutes until blistered and part-collapsed. lift out. add the last tablespoon of oil, crackle the mustard seeds, then the curry leaves. fry the shallots until soft and brown at the edges, 8 minutes, then add the tomatoes and turmeric and cook until they break down, 5 minutes. add the ground masala and fry 5 minutes, splashing in water when it sticks, until the paste darkens and oil rims the pan. pour in the strained tamarind water and 150ml plain water, add salt and the jaggery, and simmer 8 minutes. return the aubergines, cover and cook on low 8 minutes, until they are silky and the gravy coats a spoon. rest 10 minutes off the heat, scatter coriander leaves and serve with rice or idli.

entries.title: Kuzhi Paniyaram
entries.snippet: savoury batter dumplings with shallot and curry leaf, crisp outside and soft within
entries.text: kuzhi paniyaram tamil nadu savoury batter dumplings with shallot and curry leaf, crisp outside and soft within vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) shallots (small red onions) green chilli ginger curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) mustard seeds chana dal asafoetida (hing) black pepper sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt water grind the urad dal and fenugreek with 120ml water to a light fluffy paste, then grind the rice with 130ml water to a slightly grainy batter. mix the two together by hand with the salt, cover and leave 8-10 hours in a warm place until risen and faintly sour. heat 2 tbsp gingelly oil in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds and fry the chana dal 40 seconds until golden. add the shallots, green chilli and ginger and fry 4 minutes until the shallots are translucent and just colouring. stir in the curry leaves, asafoetida and cracked pepper, cook 20 seconds and take off the heat. fold the tempering and the coriander into the fermented batter; it should be thick, like a dropping cake batter. heat the paniyaram pan on medium and put 1/4 tsp gingelly oil into each well. fill each well three-quarters full with batter, cover and cook 4 minutes until the tops are set and matte and the edges pull away. turn each ball with a skewer or the handle of a spoon and cook uncovered 3 minutes more until browned all round. serve straight from the pan with coconut chutney or a spoon of the day's kuzhambu.

entries.title: Mutton Chukka Varuval
entries.snippet: slow-cooked mutton fried down dry until every piece is coated in black masala
entries.text: mutton chukka varuval tamil nadu slow-cooked mutton fried down dry until every piece is coated in black masala gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb sesame oil (gingelly / til) shallots (small red onions) garlic ginger curry leaves turmeric powder black pepper dried red chillies coriander powder fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds stone flower (dagad phool) star anise cinnamon cloves dried coconut (copra) coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt dry-roast the chillies, coriander, fennel, cumin, stone flower, star anise, cinnamon, cloves and 1 tsp of the pepper over low heat for 5 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker. cool and grind fine with the coconut. pressure cook the mutton with turmeric, half the crushed garlic and ginger, one sprig of curry leaves, salt and 250ml water for 5 whistles, then 15 minutes on low. release the pressure naturally and check: the meat should give when pressed with a spoon. if not, cook 2 more whistles. drain the mutton, keeping the stock. heat the gingelly oil in a kadhai and fry the remaining curry leaves 10 seconds. add the shallots and fry over medium heat until deep brown at the edges, about 10 minutes. add the rest of the garlic and ginger, fry 2 minutes, then add the ground masala and fry 4 minutes with a splash of the stock. tip in the drained mutton and toss so every piece is coated. add 100ml of the reserved stock. now fry it down over medium-low heat, stirring every couple of minutes, for 20-25 minutes, until the liquid is gone and the masala clings darkly to the meat. crush in the remaining 1 tsp pepper off the heat, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes.

entries.title: Mutton Kola Urundai
entries.snippet: deep-fried mince and lentil balls, dense and heavy with pepper and fennel
entries.text: mutton kola urundai tamil nadu deep-fried mince and lentil balls, dense and heavy with pepper and fennel gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb chana dal shallots (small red onions) garlic ginger curry leaves black pepper fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds dried red chillies cloves cinnamon star anise stone flower (dagad phool) turmeric powder coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) rice flour neutral oil salt boil the minced mutton with the turmeric, salt and 100ml water for 10 minutes, until it is cooked and dry. drain and cool. dry-roast the pepper, fennel, cumin, chillies, cloves, cinnamon, star anise and stone flower for 3 minutes over low heat, then cool. grind the drained chana dal coarsely with the roasted spices — you want texture, not a paste. add the cooked mince, shallots, garlic, ginger, curry leaves, coconut and coriander leaves and pulse to a thick, sticky mass. check the bind by rolling one ball. if it cracks or sags, work in the rice flour a spoon at a time. chill 20 minutes. roll into smooth balls the size of a small lime, about 18 of them, pressing firmly. heat the oil to 170c — a pinch of the mix should rise in 3 seconds without browning instantly. fry in batches of 5-6 for 5-6 minutes, turning, until deep mahogany brown and firm. drain on paper and rest 3 minutes before eating.

entries.title: Nandu Rasam
entries.snippet: thin, fiercely peppery crab broth drunk from a tumbler before the meal
entries.text: nandu rasam tamil nadu thin, fiercely peppery crab broth drunk from a tumbler before the meal pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier crab tamarind tomato garlic black pepper cumin seeds dried red chillies curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) sesame oil (gingelly / til) coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt pound the pepper, cumin, dried chillies and 4 of the garlic cloves coarsely in a blender — pulse it, do not powder it. boil the crab pieces in 600ml water with turmeric and salt for 10 minutes. skim the grey foam off the top. lift the crab out and set aside; keep the cooking liquor. add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, remaining garlic, one sprig of curry leaves and half the pounded masala to the crab liquor. simmer uncovered 12 minutes, until the raw sourness of the tamarind has gone and the liquid smells sweet at the edges. return the crab, add the rest of the pounded masala and bring just to the point of frothing — bubbles at the rim, no rolling boil. turn it off. in a small pan heat the gingelly oil, crackle the mustard seeds, add the fenugreek, asafoetida and remaining curry leaves, and pour it over. cover and rest 5 minutes, then stir through the coriander leaves and serve hot with rice, or on its own in small steel tumblers.

entries.title: Paal Paniyaram
entries.snippet: fried rice-and-urad dumplings soaked in warm sweet coconut milk
entries.text: paal paniyaram tamil nadu fried rice-and-urad dumplings soaked in warm sweet coconut milk vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) coconut milk jaggery sugar green cardamom coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil water salt grind the soaked urad dal with 50ml water to a light, fluffy paste, 4-5 minutes in the blender. grind the soaked rice separately with 50ml water to a slightly grainy paste, like fine semolina. fold the two together with the salt to a thick dropping batter. rest 30 minutes. melt the jaggery in 100ml water over low heat, then strain out the grit. warm the coconut milk with the strained jaggery syrup, the crushed cardamom and the sugar over the lowest heat, until it just steams. take it off and keep it warm. heat the coconut oil in a kadhai to 170c. fry the coconut pieces for 30 seconds until gold and lift them out. drop in teaspoons of batter, 8-10 at a time, and fry 4-5 minutes, turning, until they puff and turn even gold. drain briefly, then drop the hot dumplings straight into the warm sweetened coconut milk. let them soak at least 20 minutes, until they have swollen and gone soft all the way through. serve warm or at room temperature, topped with the fried coconut.

entries.title: Vellai Paniyaram
entries.snippet: pale lacy rice-and-urad fritters, crisp at the rim and soft in the middle
entries.text: vellai paniyaram tamil nadu pale lacy rice-and-urad fritters, crisp at the rim and soft in the middle vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) rice flour sugar salt water neutral oil coconut oil drain the soaked rice and dal and grind with 150ml water to a very smooth batter, stopping to scrape down twice. beat in the salt, sugar and coconut oil, then rest the batter 30 minutes covered. check the consistency: it should ribbon off the spoon and settle back in about 3 seconds. tighten with rice flour if it is thinner than that. heat the oil in a kadhai to a steady medium — a drop of batter should sink briefly, then rise within 3 seconds without browning. wet a small ladle, pour a ladleful of batter from about 10cm above the oil so it spreads into a disc. fry 2 minutes, spooning hot oil over the top, until the edges frill up and turn lacy. turn once and fry 90 seconds more until the fritter is puffed and set but still pale. lift onto a rack, salt lightly if you like, and fry the rest three or four at a time. serve hot with a thin coconut chutney or, in the chettinad way, alongside a peppery mutton kuzhambu.

entries.title: Alsande Tonak
entries.snippet: black-eyed peas in a roasted coconut masala, the everyday Goan Hindu curry
entries.text: alsande tonak goan black-eyed peas in a roasted coconut masala, the everyday goan hindu curry vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier lobia (black-eyed peas) coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon turmeric powder onion garlic tamarind jaggery coconut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt drain the soaked peas and pressure-cook them with 3 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt for 3 whistles, about 12 minutes. they should give completely under a thumb but hold their shape. dry-roast the grated coconut in a heavy pan over low heat 10 minutes, stirring, until it is evenly brown and smells toasted. add the chillies, coriander powder, cumin, pepper, cloves and cinnamon to the pan and roast 90 seconds more. grind the roasted coconut and spices with the turmeric and 200ml warm water to a smooth thick paste. heat the coconut oil in a pot and fry the onion 8 minutes until soft and light gold, then add the garlic for 1 minute. stir in the ground masala and cook 6-8 minutes until it darkens by a shade and oil separates at the edges. tip in the cooked peas with their liquid, add 200ml hot water and salt, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the gravy thickens. stir in the tamarind pulp and jaggery, simmer 3 minutes, then taste. it should read sour first, then sweet, then hot. finish with coriander leaves and serve with rice or with pav.

entries.title: Ambot Tik
entries.snippet: a sharp coconut-free fish curry that is exactly what its name says, sour and hot
entries.text: ambot tik goan a sharp coconut-free fish curry that is exactly what its name says, sour and hot pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies tamarind vinegar kokum garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper turmeric powder coriander powder onion neutral oil salt water grind the chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, turmeric and coriander powder with the vinegar and 3 tbsp water to a fine paste. heat the oil and fry the chopped onion over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft and pale gold. add the masala paste and fry 6-7 minutes until it darkens and the oil beads at the edge of the pan. pour in the tamarind water and the rest of the water, add the kokum and salt, and bring to a simmer. simmer uncovered 10 minutes so the gravy reduces slightly and turns glossy. taste and balance: it should be assertively sour and hot. add a pinch of salt or a splash of vinegar rather than sugar. slide in the fish, shake the pan to settle the pieces, and simmer 7-8 minutes until opaque through. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Baath Cake
entries.snippet: dense semolina and coconut cake, rested overnight and eaten in thin slices with tea
entries.text: baath cake goan dense semolina and coconut cake, rested overnight and eaten in thin slices with tea vegetarian nut-free healthier rava / sooji (semolina) coconut (fresh or desiccated) sugar eggs butter milk coconut milk green cardamom nutmeg baking soda ghee salt whisk the sugar into the melted butter until the mixture looks like wet sand, about 2 minutes. beat in the eggs one at a time, then the milk and coconut milk, until smooth and pourable. fold in the semolina, grated coconut, nutmeg, cardamom and salt. the batter will be thick and slightly grainy at this stage. cover and rest at room temperature 6 hours or overnight in the refrigerator. it will thicken considerably as the semolina drinks. heat the oven to 170c. grease a 20cm round tin with ghee and line the base with paper. stir the baking soda through the rested batter and pour it into the tin, levelling the top with a spatula. bake 55-65 minutes until the top is deep golden brown and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs. cool in the tin a full hour before turning out — the cake is fragile while warm. cool completely, then cut into thin wedges or squares. it slices cleanly only when cold.

entries.title: Batata Song
entries.snippet: quick potato curry sharp with vinegar and slow-browned onion, a weeknight standby
entries.text: batata song goan quick potato curry sharp with vinegar and slow-browned onion, a weeknight standby vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier potato onion dried red chillies vinegar turmeric powder garlic coconut oil sugar coriander leaves (cilantro) salt grind the soaked chillies with the garlic and 2 tbsp of the vinegar to a smooth thick paste. use no water. heat the coconut oil in a kadhai and fry the onion over medium heat 12-14 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and jammy. add the chilli paste and turmeric and fry 4 minutes until the raw vinegar smell burns off and oil shows at the edges. add the potato cubes and turn them gently until every piece is coated red. pour in 100ml hot water with the salt and sugar and simmer 5 minutes so the potato takes up the masala. taste and add a splash more vinegar if it needs lifting. song should be noticeably sour. cook uncovered 2 minutes more to leave it thick and clinging rather than saucy, then scatter over the coriander.

entries.title: Bebinca
entries.snippet: Goa's layered coconut and egg cake, one grilled layer at a time
entries.text: bebinca goan goa's layered coconut and egg cake, one grilled layer at a time vegetarian nut-free coconut milk eggs plain flour (maida) sugar ghee nutmeg green cardamom salt whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale, then beat in the coconut milk, flour, nutmeg, cardamom and salt to a smooth, pourable batter. rest 30 minutes. heat the oven to 180c with the grill element on. brush a deep tin generously with ghee and warm it. pour in a thin ladle of batter — about 5mm — and grill 8-10 minutes until the top is browned and set. brush the baked layer with ghee, pour the next ladle over, and grill again. repeat for at least seven layers. cool completely in the tin, then turn out. slicing warm will tear the layers apart. serve at room temperature in thin wedges.

entries.title: Chicken Cafreal
entries.snippet: chicken marinated green with coriander, chilli and vinegar, then fried dry
entries.text: chicken cafreal goan chicken marinated green with coriander, chilli and vinegar, then fried dry gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken coriander leaves (cilantro) green chilli garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon turmeric powder vinegar lemon / lime sugar potato neutral oil salt grind the coriander with stalks, green chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, turmeric, vinegar, lemon juice, sugar and 1 tsp salt to a thick green paste. use no water. rub the paste hard into the slashed chicken, working it into the cuts. cover and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight. heat the oil in a heavy kadhai and lay in the chicken in a single layer, scraping the marinade back into the bowl. fry 4 minutes a side over medium-high heat until the surface is seared and patchy brown. add the reserved marinade and 4 tbsp water, cover, and cook on low for 20 minutes, turning the pieces twice. meanwhile fry the quartered potatoes in a separate pan until gold and cooked through, about 12 minutes. uncover, raise the heat and cook 5-6 minutes more until the sauce has reduced to a thick coating that clings to the chicken. check with a knife at the thickest part of the thigh — the juices should run clear. squeeze over lemon and serve with the potatoes and pav.

entries.title: Chicken Xacuti
entries.snippet: dark roasted-coconut curry heavy with whole spice, the Goan Catholic Sunday chicken
entries.text: chicken xacuti goan dark roasted-coconut curry heavy with whole spice, the goan catholic sunday chicken gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) black pepper cloves cinnamon star anise nutmeg mace (javitri) stone flower (dagad phool) turmeric powder onion ginger garlic tamarind coconut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the coconut in a kadhai over low heat, stirring constantly, 10-12 minutes until it is the colour of milk chocolate. tip it out onto a plate. in the same pan roast the chillies, coriander powder, cumin, poppy seeds, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, star anise, mace and stone flower for 2 minutes until fragrant. grind the roasted coconut and spices with the nutmeg and about 200ml warm water to a very smooth, thick paste. give it a full 3-4 minutes in the blender. heat the coconut oil and fry the sliced onion 12 minutes until deep gold and collapsing. add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell lifts. add the marinated chicken and turn it over high heat 6-8 minutes until the pieces are sealed and no longer pink outside. stir in the ground masala and cook it down 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and oil beads at the edges. pour in 400ml hot water, season with salt, cover and simmer 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy coats a spoon. stir in the tamarind pulp, simmer 3 minutes more, and taste for salt and sourness. finish with coriander leaves.

entries.title: Fish Caldine
entries.snippet: gentle yellow coconut curry, turmeric-led and barely chilli-hot
entries.text: fish caldine goan gentle yellow coconut curry, turmeric-led and barely chilli-hot gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pescatarian healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut (fresh or desiccated) turmeric powder cumin seeds coriander powder black pepper green chilli onion garlic ginger vinegar coconut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt grind 1 cup of the coconut with the cumin, coriander powder, pepper and 150ml warm water to a very smooth paste. strain if your blender is not powerful. grind the remaining coconut with 250ml warm water and set this thinner second extraction aside separately. heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and fry the onion 6 minutes until soft and just turning gold at the edges. add the garlic, ginger and slit green chillies and cook 2 minutes until fragrant. stir in the turmeric off the heat for 20 seconds so it blooms without burning, then return the pan to a low flame. pour in the thin coconut extraction, season with salt and simmer 8 minutes until slightly reduced. lower the fish in one layer, cover and cook 6-7 minutes, spooning gravy over it, until the flesh flakes at the thickest point. pour in the thick coconut paste and warm it through 3 minutes without letting it boil. take off the heat, stir in the vinegar, and rest 10 minutes. finish with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Goan Dodol
entries.snippet: a dark, dense coconut and palm jaggery fudge stirred until it leaves the pan
entries.text: goan dodol goan a dark, dense coconut and palm jaggery fudge stirred until it leaves the pan vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free coconut milk jaggery rice flour cashews green cardamom salt coconut oil melt the jaggery with 200ml water over low heat, then strain through a fine sieve to remove the grit. whisk the rice flour into 2 cups of the cold coconut milk until smooth, then combine with the rest of the coconut milk, the strained jaggery syrup and the salt in a heavy kadhai. bring to a simmer over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a flat wooden spoon that reaches the corners. after about 25 minutes it will thicken to the consistency of a thick custard and turn light brown. keep stirring over low heat. at around 50 minutes it darkens to milk chocolate and starts to come away from the sides in sheets. at around 75-85 minutes the oil separates and glistens on the surface and the mass rolls as one lump behind the spoon. stir in the cashews and crushed cardamom and cook 2 minutes more. tip it immediately into the greased tray and press flat with a greased scraper to about 2cm thick. cool completely at room temperature, 4-6 hours, until firm enough to cut into diamonds.

entries.title: Goan Fish Curry
entries.snippet: the everyday coconut and kokum curry that gets eaten with rice twice a day
entries.text: goan fish curry goan the everyday coconut and kokum curry that gets eaten with rice twice a day pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut (fresh or desiccated) kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds turmeric powder black pepper garlic ginger tamarind kokum onion green chilli okra / bhindi coconut oil salt water grind the coconut, kashmiri chillies, coriander powder, cumin, turmeric, pepper, garlic and ginger to a very smooth paste with about 150ml water. heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and soften the sliced onion over medium heat for 5 minutes, until translucent, not browned. pour in the ground masala and cook 4 minutes, stirring, until it darkens a shade and smells toasted rather than raw. add the remaining water, the tamarind extract, kokum, green chillies and salt. bring to a gentle simmer. simmer uncovered 8 minutes, until the surface carries a thin rim of orange oil. slide in the okra, if using, and cook 3 minutes until just tender. lower the fish in a single layer. do not stir — shake the pan instead. cook 6-7 minutes, until the flesh turns opaque and pulls from the bone when nudged. take it off the heat and leave it 10 minutes before serving with par-boiled rice.

entries.title: Goan Sausage Pulao
entries.snippet: smoky vinegary chouriço cooked through rice until every grain is stained red
entries.text: goan sausage pulao goan smoky vinegary chouriço cooked through rice until every grain is stained red gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork basmati rice onion tomato potato green chilli bay leaf cloves cinnamon black pepper turmeric powder coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime water salt fry the chopped sausage in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, until the fat runs out red and the edges crisp. lift out the sausage with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat behind. in the same fat, fry the bay leaves, cloves and cinnamon for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the sliced onion and cook 8 minutes, until deep gold. stir in the tomato, green chillies, pepper and turmeric and cook 4 minutes, until the tomato collapses. add the potato cubes and the drained rice and turn them through the fat for 2 minutes, until every grain is coated and glossy. return the sausage, pour in the water, taste for salt and bring to a hard boil. cover tightly, drop to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid. rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes, then fork through the coriander and serve with lemon.

entries.title: Goan Xacuti
entries.snippet: Chicken in a dark roasted-coconut masala with poppy seeds and star anise
entries.text: goan xacuti goan chicken in a dark roasted-coconut masala with poppy seeds and star anise gluten-free dairy-free healthier chicken coconut (fresh or desiccated) onion dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) star anise cinnamon cloves black pepper nutmeg turmeric powder ginger garlic tamarind neutral oil salt dry roast the grated coconut over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until deep brown and nutty, 10-15 minutes. be patient and do not walk away; it turns from brown to burnt in seconds. tip onto a plate to stop the cooking. in the same pan, roast the dried chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, poppy seeds, star anise, cinnamon, cloves and pepper separately until fragrant, about 2 minutes. cool. blend the roasted coconut and spices with the ginger, garlic, turmeric and enough water to make a very smooth, thick paste. take your time here; grittiness will not cook out. heat the oil and fry the sliced onion until well browned, 10 minutes. add the masala paste and cook, stirring, until it darkens and the oil separates, 8-10 minutes. add the chicken and salt and turn it in the masala over high heat until sealed all over. add about 2 cups of hot water, bring to a simmer, cover and cook 25-30 minutes until the chicken is tender. stir in the tamarind pulp and the nutmeg. simmer uncovered 5 minutes to balance the sourness. rest before serving; xacuti is better after an hour.

entries.title: Khatkhate
entries.snippet: the Saraswat temple stew of eight vegetables in coconut, no onion or garlic anywhere
entries.text: khatkhate goan the saraswat temple stew of eight vegetables in coconut, no onion or garlic anywhere vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) pumpkin yam (suran) raw banana / plantain sweet potato drumstick (moringa pod) french beans colocasia (arbi) coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper tamarind jaggery coconut oil salt water boil the toor dal in 400ml water for 20 minutes, until soft enough to crush against the side of the pot. meanwhile grind the coconut, dried chillies and coriander powder with 150ml water to a coarse-ish paste — a little texture is right here. add the yam, colocasia and raw banana to the dal with the rest of the water and 1 tsp salt. simmer 10 minutes. add the sweet potato and drumstick and simmer 6 minutes. add the pumpkin and french beans and cook 5 minutes, until everything yields to a knife but still holds its shape. stir in the ground coconut paste, the tamarind extract and the jaggery. simmer gently 8 minutes, stirring only occasionally so the pieces stay whole. crush in the pepper, check the salt, and take it off the heat. it should be sweet, sour and mildly hot in that order. trickle over the raw coconut oil just before serving with rice.

entries.title: Kismur
entries.snippet: dry prawn and coconut salad, crunchy and sour, eaten alongside rice and curry
entries.text: kismur goan dry prawn and coconut salad, crunchy and sour, eaten alongside rice and curry gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pescatarian dried fish coconut (fresh or desiccated) onion dried red chillies red chilli powder turmeric powder tamarind green chilli coconut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the drained prawns in a kadhai over medium heat 4-5 minutes until they are crisp and rattle in the pan. tip them onto a plate to cool, then crush lightly with your fingers into coarse pieces. in the same pan warm the coconut oil and fry the broken dried chillies 30 seconds until they darken. add the grated coconut and toast 3-4 minutes, stirring, until it is dry and pale gold at the edges. stir in the chilli powder and turmeric and take the pan off the heat immediately. let the coconut cool to room temperature, then fold in the crushed prawns, chopped onion and green chilli. add the tamarind pulp and toss thoroughly with your hands. taste, then salt — the prawns may have brought enough. finish with coriander leaves and serve within a couple of hours, while the onion is still crunchy.

entries.title: Mackerel Uddamethi
entries.snippet: saraswat mackerel curry built on toasted urad dal and fenugreek, sour and slightly bitter
entries.text: mackerel uddamethi goan saraswat mackerel curry built on toasted urad dal and fenugreek, sour and slightly bitter gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pescatarian healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies coriander powder turmeric powder tamarind onion green chilli coconut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt warm 1 tbsp of the coconut oil and roast the urad dal over low heat 3 minutes until it turns reddish and smells nutty. add the fenugreek seeds and roast 30 seconds only, then the chillies and coriander powder for another minute. grind the roasted mixture with the grated coconut, turmeric and 200ml water to a smooth, pourable paste. heat the remaining oil in a wide pan and soften the onion 5 minutes until translucent but not coloured. pour in the ground masala with another 150ml water, add the green chilli and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer. simmer 6-7 minutes, stirring, until the raw coconut smell is gone and the surface glistens. slide in the mackerel in a single layer, spoon gravy over it, and cook 6 minutes without stirring. add the tamarind pulp, simmer 2 minutes more, and take it off the heat. rest 10 minutes before serving with rice. scatter over the coriander leaves at the table.

entries.title: Patoleo
entries.snippet: steamed rice parcels of coconut and jaggery, made for the feast of the Assumption
entries.text: patoleo goan steamed rice parcels of coconut and jaggery, made for the feast of the assumption vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour coconut (fresh or desiccated) jaggery green cardamom sesame seeds salt water melt the jaggery with 4 tbsp water over low heat until it dissolves, about 3 minutes, then strain out the grit. return it to the pan with the grated coconut and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until the mixture pulls together and leaves the sides of the pan. stir in the crushed cardamom and roasted sesame and set the filling aside to cool completely. bring the water to a boil with the salt, pour it over the rice flour and mix with a spoon, then knead into a soft, smooth dough once cool enough to touch. rest the dough 10 minutes under a damp cloth. spread a thin, even layer of dough over half of each turmeric leaf with wet fingers, about 3mm thick, leaving a clear border. spoon 2 tbsp of the coconut filling along the centre and fold the leaf over to close the parcel. stack the parcels in a steamer, not too tightly, and steam over rolling water for 20-25 minutes. they are done when the leaf has darkened and the rice looks translucent and pulls away cleanly. rest 5 minutes before opening.

entries.title: Pork Indad
entries.snippet: sweet-sour vinegar pork lifted with dates and jaggery, the milder cousin of vindaloo
entries.text: pork indad goan sweet-sour vinegar pork lifted with dates and jaggery, the milder cousin of vindaloo gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork dried red chillies vinegar garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper cinnamon cloves turmeric powder dates jaggery onion neutral oil salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, cinnamon, cloves and turmeric with the vinegar to a smooth thick paste. use no water at all. rub half the paste into the pork with 1 tsp salt and leave it to marinate as above. heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onion 12 minutes until soft and evenly gold. add the remaining masala paste and cook 6-8 minutes over medium heat until it darkens and oil pools at the sides. add the marinated pork and turn it over high heat 8 minutes until sealed on all sides and coated in masala. pour in 300ml hot water, bring to a boil, then drop to a bare simmer, cover and cook 50 minutes until a knife slides into the meat without resistance. add the dates and jaggery and simmer uncovered 12 minutes more, until the dates have softened and the gravy is glossy and thick. taste and balance: indad should land sweet, then sour, then warm with pepper. add vinegar or jaggery a teaspoon at a time. rest off the heat 20 minutes before serving, with sannas or crusty pav.

entries.title: Pork Vindaloo
entries.snippet: Vinegar-and-garlic pork, descended from Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos
entries.text: pork vindaloo goan vinegar-and-garlic pork, descended from portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork dried red chillies vinegar garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper cinnamon cloves green cardamom turmeric powder jaggery onion neutral oil salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger and whole spices with the vinegar to a smooth, thick paste. use no water. rub half the paste into the pork with salt and marinate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight refrigerated. fry the onion in oil until soft and golden, then add the remaining masala paste and cook until the oil separates. add the pork with its marinade and turn it over high heat until sealed and coated. add a cup of hot water, cover, and simmer 60 minutes until the pork is tender and the fat has rendered into the gravy. balance with jaggery and salt. rest overnight if you can — vindaloo is markedly better on day two.

entries.title: Prawn Balchao
entries.snippet: a fierce vinegar-and-chilli prawn pickle eaten a spoonful at a time
entries.text: prawn balchao goan a fierce vinegar-and-chilli prawn pickle eaten a spoonful at a time pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier prawns kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies vinegar garlic ginger cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon turmeric powder onion sugar neutral oil salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon and turmeric to a thick paste using only the soaking vinegar, no water. toss the prawns with 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of turmeric and fry them in 2 tbsp of the oil over high heat for 2 minutes, until they just turn pink. lift them out. pour the rest of the oil into the same kadhai and fry the chopped onion over medium heat for 12-15 minutes, until dark gold and jammy. add the ground masala and fry 10 minutes, stirring often, until the oil separates and pools clearly at the edges. stir in the sugar and salt and cook 2 more minutes. return the prawns, stir to coat, and cook 3 minutes on low. take it off the heat and cool completely, uncovered, in the pan. pack into a dry jar, pressing down so the oil covers the surface. leave 2 days before eating.

entries.title: Prawn Rissois
entries.snippet: crisp half-moon pastries with a creamy prawn filling, the standard Goan party snack
entries.text: prawn rissois goan crisp half-moon pastries with a creamy prawn filling, the standard goan party snack pescatarian plain flour (maida) milk water butter prawns onion green chilli garlic black pepper coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime eggs sliced bread neutral oil salt for the filling, cook the onion, garlic and green chilli in 1 tbsp butter over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. add the chopped prawns, pepper and salt and cook 3 minutes, until just pink, then stir in 2 tbsp of the flour and 1/2 cup of the milk. cook 3-4 minutes more, stirring, until it thickens into a stiff paste that holds a ridge. finish with lemon and coriander and chill 1 hour. for the dough, bring the water, remaining milk, remaining butter and 1 tsp salt to a rolling boil. tip in the rest of the flour all at once and beat hard with a wooden spoon until it forms a single ball that leaves the pan clean, about 2 minutes. turn it out, and as soon as you can bear the heat, knead 5 minutes until smooth and elastic. cover and rest 15 minutes. roll the warm dough thin, about 2mm, and cut 9cm rounds. place a heaped teaspoon of filling on each round, fold into a half-moon and seal the edge firmly, pressing out any air. dip each in beaten egg, then press into the breadcrumbs to coat evenly. chill 20 minutes. heat the oil to 175c — a crumb dropped in should sizzle and rise at once — and fry in batches of five for 3 minutes, until deep gold. drain on a rack, not paper, and serve hot.

entries.title: Recheado Mackerel
entries.snippet: whole mackerel stuffed with red vinegar masala and shallow-fried crisp
entries.text: recheado mackerel goan whole mackerel stuffed with red vinegar masala and shallow-fried crisp pescatarian dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies vinegar garlic ginger cumin seeds cloves cinnamon black pepper turmeric powder tamarind sugar rava / sooji (semolina) neutral oil salt lemon / lime grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, pepper, turmeric, tamarind, sugar and 1 tsp salt with the vinegar to a thick, smooth paste. slit each mackerel along the belly and, with a small knife, open a second pocket along the backbone from the outside. pack 1.5 tbsp of paste into each fish, inside the belly and into the pocket, and smear a thin film over the skin. rest the stuffed fish 20 minutes on a plate in the fridge. spread the rava on a plate and press each fish into it on both sides, shaking off the loose grains. heat the oil on a flat tawa over medium heat until a grain of rava sizzles on contact. lay in the fish and fry 5-6 minutes without moving it, until the underside is crusted and deep red-brown. turn once with a wide spatula and fry another 4-5 minutes. drain briefly on paper and serve hot with lemon wedges, rice and a plain dal.

entries.title: Sanna
entries.snippet: soft spongy steamed rice cakes, faintly sweet, eaten with sorpotel
entries.text: sanna goan soft spongy steamed rice cakes, faintly sweet, eaten with sorpotel vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) sugar eno / fruit salt salt water drain the soaked rice and grind it with the grated coconut, cooked rice and just enough water to a thick, smooth batter — thicker than pancake batter, like idli batter. stir in the sugar, cover loosely, and leave in a warm place for 8-10 hours, or overnight. by morning it should have risen by half, smell yeasty and sweet, and be full of small bubbles. stir in the salt gently, from the edges inwards, keeping as much air in as you can. if the batter never rose, fold in the eno now and steam immediately. grease small steel bowls or idli moulds and fill each two-thirds full. steam over rolling water for 12-15 minutes, with the lid wrapped in a cloth to stop condensation dripping back. test with a skewer at the centre — it should come out clean and the surface should spring back. rest 5 minutes, then run a knife around each and turn them out. serve warm with sorpotel or a pork curry.

entries.title: Solkadhi
entries.snippet: cool pink kokum and coconut milk, drunk at the end of a fish meal to settle it
entries.text: solkadhi goan cool pink kokum and coconut milk, drunk at the end of a fish meal to settle it vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free kokum coconut (fresh or desiccated) water garlic green chilli cumin seeds coconut oil mustard seeds curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) sugar salt grind the coconut with 400ml of the warm water for 3 minutes, then strain through muslin, squeezing hard. this is the thick first extraction. return the pressed coconut to the blender with the remaining 200ml water, grind again and strain into the same bowl. crush the garlic, green chilli and cumin to a rough paste in a mortar. stir the crushed paste and the squeezed kokum water into the coconut milk. it should turn a soft rose pink. season with salt, and a pinch of sugar only if it tastes harsh. rest 20 minutes for the colour to deepen and the garlic to bloom. for the optional tempering, heat the coconut oil, pop the mustard seeds, throw in the curry leaves and pour it over the top. chill 30 minutes and stir well before serving, in glasses on their own or ladled over hot rice.

entries.title: Sorpotel
entries.snippet: the vinegary pork and liver stew that gets cooked days before a Goan wedding
