entries.text: sorpotel goan the vinegary pork and liver stew that gets cooked days before a goan wedding gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies vinegar cumin seeds cloves cinnamon black pepper turmeric powder garlic ginger onion green chilli sugar salt water boil the pork and liver together in the water with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric for 25 minutes, until firm but not falling apart. keep the stock. cool the meat, then cut it into small 1cm dice. it should be knife-cut, never minced. fry the diced pork and liver in 3 tbsp of its own rendered fat over high heat, in batches, until the edges brown, about 5 minutes a batch. grind the soaked chillies, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, pepper, turmeric, garlic and ginger with the remaining vinegar to a fine paste. in the same pot, cook the chopped onion in the fat over medium heat for 10 minutes, until soft and gold. add the ground masala and fry 8-10 minutes until the oil separates and the raw vinegar smell has gone. return the meat, add the reserved stock, green chillies, sugar and salt. simmer uncovered 30 minutes, stirring now and then. stop when the gravy is thick enough to coat the meat and a distinct layer of red fat sits on top. cool completely and refrigerate. reheat and simmer 5 minutes each day for three days before serving with sanna or crusty pav.

entries.title: Sungtachi Kodi
entries.snippet: everyday prawn and drumstick curry in a thin red coconut masala
entries.text: sungtachi kodi goan everyday prawn and drumstick curry in a thin red coconut masala gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pescatarian healthier prawns drumstick (moringa pod) coconut (fresh or desiccated) kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds turmeric powder garlic onion kokum green chilli coconut oil salt grind the coconut, kashmiri chillies, coriander powder, cumin, turmeric and garlic with 250ml warm water to a completely smooth paste. boil the drumstick pieces in 250ml salted water for 8 minutes, until a fingernail marks the flesh easily. keep the water. heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and soften the onion 5 minutes until translucent. pour in the ground masala along with the drumstick and its cooking water, add the green chillies and salt, and bring to a simmer. simmer 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the raw smell of the coconut has gone and the curry looks glossy rather than chalky. add the kokum with its soaking water and simmer 2 minutes. slide in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes only, until they curl and turn opaque. take off the heat, check the salt and sourness, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Tondak
entries.snippet: dried white peas in a roasted coconut and cashew masala, thick and faintly sweet
entries.text: tondak goan dried white peas in a roasted coconut and cashew masala, thick and faintly sweet vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier dried white peas (safed matar) cashews coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried red chillies kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon turmeric powder onion garlic tamarind jaggery coconut oil salt water pressure cook the drained peas with 400ml water and 1/2 tsp salt for 3 whistles, about 12 minutes, until soft but not split. keep the cooking water. dry-roast the grated coconut in a pan over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns the colour of weak tea. add the dried chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, pepper, cloves and cinnamon to the pan and roast 1 minute more, until fragrant. grind the roasted coconut and spices with the soaked cashews, turmeric, garlic and 150ml water to a thick, smooth paste. heat the coconut oil and fry the chopped onion 8 minutes, until well browned at the edges. add the ground masala and fry 6 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and the oil shows at the sides. tip in the cooked peas with their water and the remaining water. simmer 12 minutes. stir in the tamarind and jaggery, check the salt, and simmer 5 minutes more until the gravy is thick enough to hold a spoon mark. rest 10 minutes and serve with rice or pao.

entries.title: Bajra no Rotlo
entries.snippet: thick hand-patted pearl-millet flatbread, nutty and dense, eaten hot under melting butter
entries.text: bajra no rotlo gujarati thick hand-patted pearl-millet flatbread, nutty and dense, eaten hot under melting butter vegetarian gluten-free nut-free bajra (pearl millet) flour water salt butter jaggery warm the flour in a bowl with the salt, then add the hot water in stages, mixing with a spoon at first, then your hand. knead 3-4 minutes into a smooth, warm, slightly tacky dough. it should hold a ball without cracking at the edges. heat a heavy tawa over medium heat until a drop of water skitters across it. take a lemon-sized ball, wet your palms, and pat it flat on a clean board or a sheet of plastic, rotating a quarter turn between pats, into a disc about 12cm across and 8mm thick. lift it on your palm and lay it flat on the hot tawa in one movement. cook 90 seconds until the underside is speckled, then flip and cook the second side 2 minutes, pressing the edges with a cloth so it puffs. lift the rotlo with tongs and hold it 20-30 seconds directly over the flame, first side down, until it balloons. repeat with the rest, stacking them under a cloth. serve hot with a knob of butter pressed into the centre and a lump of jaggery, or alongside ringan no olo.

entries.title: Basundi
entries.snippet: milk reduced slowly to a thick grainy cream, scented with cardamom and saffron
entries.text: basundi gujarati milk reduced slowly to a thick grainy cream, scented with cardamom and saffron vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic milk sugar saffron green cardamom almonds pistachios nutmeg bring the milk to a boil in a wide heavy pan over medium heat, stirring so it does not stick. lower the heat and simmer, stirring every few minutes and scraping the base each time. as a skin forms at the edges, keep pushing it back into the milk. these layers are what make basundi grainy rather than smooth. crush the saffron into 2 tbsp of the hot milk and set it aside to bloom. continue reducing for 45-55 minutes, until the milk has come down to about half its volume and coats a spoon thickly. add the sugar and cook 8 minutes more; the milk will loosen briefly, then thicken again. stir in the saffron milk, ground cardamom and nutmeg, and take the pan off the heat. cool to room temperature, then chill 3 hours; it thickens noticeably as it cools. serve cold in small bowls with the almonds and pistachios scattered over, or warm alongside puris.

entries.title: Bataka Poha
entries.snippet: flattened rice tossed with potato, peanuts and lemon, ready in twenty minutes
entries.text: bataka poha gujarati flattened rice tossed with potato, peanuts and lemon, ready in twenty minutes vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier poha (flattened rice) potato onion peanuts green chilli curry leaves mustard seeds cumin seeds turmeric powder sugar lemon / lime neutral oil asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) coconut (fresh or desiccated) salt fry the peanuts in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until they darken and smell toasted, then lift them out and set aside. in the same oil pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves, green chilli and asafoetida. add the diced potato, cover, and cook on medium-low 8 minutes, shaking the pan, until tender and lightly golden. add the onion and fry 3 minutes until soft and translucent. tip in the seasoned poha and fold it through gently with a flat spatula, lifting rather than stirring. cover and steam on the lowest heat 3 minutes, until the poha is hot, plump and pale yellow throughout. turn off the heat, add the lemon juice and the fried peanuts, and fold once. scatter the coriander and coconut over and serve hot with a wedge of lemon.

entries.title: Batata nu Shaak
entries.snippet: everyday tomato-tempered potatoes, faintly sweet and sour, the standard partner to thepla
entries.text: batata nu shaak gujarati everyday tomato-tempered potatoes, faintly sweet and sour, the standard partner to thepla vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier potato tomato neutral oil mustard seeds cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) curry leaves green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder jaggery lemon / lime salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds until they stop popping, then add the cumin. add the asafoetida, curry leaves and slit green chillies and let them sputter for 10 seconds. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder off the direct flame for 5 seconds so they bloom without burning. add the chopped tomato and cook 5-6 minutes over medium heat until it collapses and the oil shows at the edges. tip in the broken potatoes and salt and turn them gently until yellow all over. pour in the water, bring to a simmer, cover and cook 8 minutes on low. uncover, add the jaggery and mash a few pieces of potato against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy. simmer uncovered 3-4 minutes more until it is loose but clinging, then take off the heat. stir in the lemon juice and coriander and check the balance — it should read salty first, then sweet, then sour.

entries.title: Bhinda Sambhariya
entries.snippet: whole okra stuffed with a peanut, coconut and sesame masala, cooked gently in a covered pan
entries.text: bhinda sambhariya gujarati whole okra stuffed with a peanut, coconut and sesame masala, cooked gently in a covered pan vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free no-onion-garlic okra / bhindi peanuts besan (gram flour) sesame seeds coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar lemon / lime ginger green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) salt top and tail the okra and slit each pod lengthways down one side, stopping short of both ends so it stays whole. mix the ground peanut, roasted besan, sesame, coconut, all the ground spices, sugar, salt, ginger, chilli, coriander leaves and lemon juice into a crumbly stuffing. press the stuffing into each pod with a small spoon or your fingertip, filling but not splitting them. heat the oil in a wide kadhai, pop the mustard seeds and add the asafoetida. lay the stuffed okra in a single layer and let them sit undisturbed 4 minutes to blister on the underside. turn each pod gently with tongs, cover, and cook on low heat 12 minutes. uncover, shake the pan and cook 5 minutes more until the okra is tender, the surfaces are lightly browned and no sliminess remains. scatter over any leftover stuffing, let it toast for a minute, and serve with rotli.

entries.title: Dal Dhokli
entries.snippet: spiced wheat diamonds simmered soft in sweet-sour toor dal, a one-pot supper
entries.text: dal dhokli gujarati spiced wheat diamonds simmered soft in sweet-sour toor dal, a one-pot supper vegetarian toor dal (pigeon pea) atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder red chilli powder neutral oil jaggery tamarind peanuts ghee mustard seeds cumin seeds cinnamon cloves dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dal with the peanuts, 1/2 tsp turmeric and 800ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. meanwhile knead the atta, besan, ajwain, remaining turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, salt and 2 tbsp oil with about 70ml water into a stiff dough. cover and rest 20 minutes. whisk the cooked dal smooth, add the remaining water, tamarind, jaggery, ginger, green chilli, remaining chilli powder and salt, and bring to a simmer. roll the dough very thin, 2mm, and cut into 4cm diamonds. bring the dal to a rolling boil and drop the diamonds in a few at a time, stirring gently between additions. simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the dhokli are cooked through and the dal has thickened around them. heat the ghee, pop the mustard and cumin seeds with the cinnamon, cloves and dried chilli. add the curry leaves and asafoetida, then pour the tempering over the pot. simmer 3 minutes more, thinning with hot water to a thick soup. scatter the coriander over and serve in bowls with a spoon of ghee and raw chopped onion on the side.

entries.title: Doodhpak
entries.snippet: rice simmered down slowly in milk until thick, scented with saffron and cardamom
entries.text: doodhpak gujarati rice simmered down slowly in milk until thick, scented with saffron and cardamom vegetarian gluten-free milk basmati rice sugar green cardamom saffron almonds pistachios ghee nutmeg grease a heavy-bottomed pan with the ghee and bring the milk to a boil over medium heat, stirring so it does not catch. add the drained rice and lower the heat to a bare simmer. cook uncovered for 40-45 minutes, stirring every 4-5 minutes and scraping the base and sides each time. when the milk has reduced by about a third and coats the back of a spoon, the rice should be completely soft and starting to break. add the sugar and stir 5 minutes. the mixture will loosen noticeably before it thickens again. stir in the saffron milk and the ground cardamom and simmer 5 minutes more. add the slivered almonds and cook a final 3 minutes. it should be pourable but leave a clear trail behind the spoon. take off the heat, grate over a scraping of nutmeg and scatter the pistachios. cool to room temperature, then chill at least 3 hours. serve cold with hot puri.

entries.title: Dudhi na Muthiya
entries.snippet: steamed bottle-gourd and flour rolls, sliced and crisped in a sesame tempering
entries.text: dudhi na muthiya gujarati steamed bottle-gourd and flour rolls, sliced and crisped in a sesame tempering vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free bottle gourd (lauki) atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) rava / sooji (semolina) ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder sugar lemon / lime salt baking soda neutral oil mustard seeds sesame seeds asafoetida (hing) curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) coconut (fresh or desiccated) mix the grated dudhi with the atta, besan, rava, ginger, green chilli, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, sugar, salt, lemon juice, baking soda and 3 tbsp oil. bring it together into a soft dough using only the reserved dudhi juice. it should be softer than chapati dough but hold a shape. oil your palms and roll the dough into 3 logs about 5cm thick. set them on a greased steamer plate. steam over boiling water for 22-25 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the surface is matte, not tacky. cool completely, at least 30 minutes, then cut into 1.5cm slices. heat the remaining 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the sesame, asafoetida and curry leaves. lay the slices in and fry over medium heat, turning once, 4-5 minutes a side until the edges are golden and crisp. scatter with coriander and coconut and serve hot with chai or plain yogurt.

entries.title: Fafda
entries.snippet: crisp-chewy strips of fried gram flour dough, the classic sunday breakfast
entries.text: fafda gujarati crisp-chewy strips of fried gram flour dough, the classic sunday breakfast vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic besan (gram flour) baking soda carom seeds (ajwain) black pepper turmeric powder neutral oil water green chilli salt mix the besan, ajwain, black pepper and turmeric in a wide bowl. rub in the 3 tbsp oil until the mixture holds its shape when squeezed. add the soda-and-salt water gradually and knead 8 minutes into a smooth, firm, elastic dough. cover and rest 20 minutes. pinch off a walnut-sized piece, place it on an oiled surface, and press it away from you with the heel of your palm into a long strip about 12cm by 3cm. lift the strip with a flat scraper and lay it on an oiled tray while you press the rest. heat the frying oil to 175c — a scrap of dough should rise steadily, not violently. slide in 3-4 strips at a time and fry 2-3 minutes, turning once, until pale gold and no longer bubbling hard. drain on a rack, not paper, so both faces stay crisp. fry the slit green chillies for 30 seconds, salt them, and serve alongside with kadhi or papaya sambharo.

entries.title: Gujarati Dal
entries.snippet: thin toor dal balanced sweet with jaggery and sharp with tamarind
entries.text: gujarati dal gujarati thin toor dal balanced sweet with jaggery and sharp with tamarind vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic toor dal (pigeon pea) water turmeric powder jaggery tamarind peanuts tomato ginger green chilli curry leaves ghee mustard seeds cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) cinnamon cloves dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) red chilli powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dal with the peanuts, turmeric and 700ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. whisk the cooked dal smooth and thin it with the remaining water until it pours easily from a ladle. add the tamarind pulp, jaggery, tomato, ginger, green chilli and salt and simmer 12 minutes. taste and adjust — it should read sweet, then sour, then salty, with heat arriving last. heat the ghee in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds. add the cumin, fenugreek, cinnamon, cloves and dried red chilli and let them darken 15 seconds. add the curry leaves, chilli powder and asafoetida off the heat, then pour the whole tempering into the dal. simmer 3 minutes more, scatter the coriander over and serve with rice and a spoon of ghee.

entries.title: Gujarati Kadhi
entries.snippet: thin sweet-sour yogurt and gram flour soup, drunk as much as eaten
entries.text: gujarati kadhi gujarati thin sweet-sour yogurt and gram flour soup, drunk as much as eaten vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) water jaggery ginger green chilli ghee cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) cloves cinnamon dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan into the yogurt until completely smooth, then thin it with the water a little at a time. stir in the turmeric, jaggery, ginger, green chilli and salt, and set the pan over medium heat. bring it to a boil stirring constantly in one direction, about 8 minutes. it will foam up as it reaches the boil. drop the heat and simmer 10 minutes, until the raw besan smell is gone and the kadhi coats a spoon thinly. heat the ghee in a small pan and add the mustard seeds; wait for them to pop. add the cumin, fenugreek, cloves, cinnamon and dried red chilli, and let them darken for 15 seconds. add the curry leaves and asafoetida, stand back from the spatter, and pour the tempering straight into the kadhi. simmer 2 minutes more, scatter the coriander over and serve hot with plain rice or khichdi.

entries.title: Gujarati Khichdi
entries.snippet: soft rice and moong dal cooked to a porridge, eaten with kadhi and ghee
entries.text: gujarati khichdi gujarati soft rice and moong dal cooked to a porridge, eaten with kadhi and ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier rice (short/medium grain) moong dal water ghee cumin seeds turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli black pepper salt heat half the ghee in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds until they turn a shade darker. add the asafoetida, ginger and green chilli and let them sizzle 10 seconds. tip in the drained rice and dal and stir 2 minutes until every grain is glossed with ghee. add the water, turmeric and salt and stir well, scraping the base. close the cooker and cook for 4 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure fall on its own. open, whisk briefly and thin with hot water if it has set firm — it should slump off a spoon. crack the black pepper over, pour the remaining ghee on top and serve with kadhi.

entries.title: Guvar nu Shaak
entries.snippet: cluster beans cooked down with crushed peanut and sesame until the bitterness turns nutty
entries.text: guvar nu shaak gujarati cluster beans cooked down with crushed peanut and sesame until the bitterness turns nutty vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free cluster beans (guar) peanuts sesame seeds garlic green chilli groundnut oil mustard seeds carom seeds (ajwain) asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder jaggery salt water lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the ajwain and asafoetida. add the crushed garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute until the garlic smells sweet. tip in the cut guvar and turn it through the oil for 3-4 minutes until the pods turn a brighter green. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and stir 30 seconds. pour in the water, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, stirring twice. check a pod — it should be tender enough to crush between finger and thumb with no snap. give it 5 minutes more if not. uncover, add the crushed peanut, sesame and jaggery and cook 4-5 minutes until the water has gone and the beans are coated in a dry, nutty masala. take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and coriander, and serve with rotli and dal-bhaat.

entries.title: Handvo
entries.snippet: savoury fermented rice and lentil cake with a crisp sesame crust
entries.text: handvo gujarati savoury fermented rice and lentil cake with a crisp sesame crust vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) chana dal toor dal (pigeon pea) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) yogurt / dahi bottle gourd (lauki) ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar eno / fruit salt neutral oil mustard seeds cumin seeds sesame seeds curry leaves dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) salt coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked, drained rice and dals with the yogurt to a coarse batter, thick enough to drop off the spoon in a lump. cover and leave in a warm place 8-10 hours to ferment. fold in the grated bottle gourd, ginger, chilli, turmeric, chilli powder, sugar, salt and coriander. heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy 22cm pan, crackle the mustard and cumin seeds, then add the curry leaves, dried chilli and asafoetida. stir most of this tempering into the batter, leaving a spoonful and its oil in the pan. beat in the eno, pour the batter into the pan, level it and scatter the remaining sesame over the top. cover and cook on the lowest heat 25 minutes, until the top is set and a skewer comes out clean. drizzle the remaining oil around the edge, flip the cake or slide it under a hot grill, and cook 10 minutes more until the crust is deep brown and crisp. rest 10 minutes in the pan before cutting into squares.

entries.title: Khaman
entries.snippet: soft steamed gram-flour squares soaked in a sweet mustard-seed tempering
entries.text: khaman gujarati soft steamed gram-flour squares soaked in a sweet mustard-seed tempering vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free besan (gram flour) water sugar lemon / lime green chilli ginger turmeric powder salt eno / fruit salt neutral oil mustard seeds sesame seeds asafoetida (hing) curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) coconut (fresh or desiccated) whisk the besan with 160ml water, 1 tbsp sugar, the ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, salt, 2 tbsp oil and the lemon juice into a smooth batter the thickness of pancake batter. rest 15 minutes. bring the steamer to a hard boil and oil the tin. stir the eno into the batter with a teaspoon of water, whisk hard for 10 seconds until it froths and doubles, and pour straight into the tin. steam covered on high for 15-18 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean and the top springs back. lift out, rest 5 minutes, then cut into 4cm diamonds and loosen them in the tin. heat the remaining 3 tbsp oil, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the sesame, asafoetida, curry leaves and slit chillies. stand back — the leaves spit. pour in 120ml water and 4 tbsp sugar, bring to a boil and cook 1 minute until the sugar dissolves. spoon the hot tempering evenly over the cut khaman, tipping the tin so it reaches the corners. leave 10 minutes to drink it in. scatter with coriander and grated coconut and serve warm with green chutney.

entries.title: Khaman Dhokla
entries.snippet: Steamed, aerated gram flour squares with a sweet-sour mustard tempering
entries.text: khaman dhokla gujarati steamed, aerated gram flour squares with a sweet-sour mustard tempering vegetarian vegan gluten-free nut-free dairy-free besan (gram flour) rava / sooji (semolina) yogurt / dahi eno / fruit salt ginger green chilli turmeric powder lemon / lime sugar mustard seeds sesame seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt set a steamer to boil and grease a shallow tin. whisk the besan, rava, yogurt, turmeric, ginger, chilli, salt, 1 tbsp oil and about 3/4 cup water into a smooth, thick-but-pourable batter. rest 10 minutes. stir in the juice of half a lemon. add the eno, whisk briskly for 20 seconds as it foams and visibly lightens, and pour immediately into the tin. steam covered on high for 15-18 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the surface springs back. cool 10 minutes, then cut into squares. for the tempering, heat the remaining oil, splutter the mustard seeds, add the sesame, curry leaves, asafoetida and any remaining slit chillies. take the pan off the heat and carefully add 1/3 cup water, the sugar and the remaining lemon juice. return to the heat and simmer just until the sugar dissolves. spoon the warm tempering evenly over the dhokla and leave it 15 minutes to soak in fully. scatter with coriander before serving.

entries.title: Khandvi
entries.snippet: silky gram flour sheets rolled tight and dressed with mustard seeds and coconut
entries.text: khandvi gujarati silky gram flour sheets rolled tight and dressed with mustard seeds and coconut vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic besan (gram flour) buttermilk (chaas) turmeric powder ginger green chilli asafoetida (hing) neutral oil mustard seeds sesame seeds curry leaves coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan, buttermilk, turmeric, ginger, chilli paste, asafoetida and salt to a completely smooth, lump-free batter. pour into a heavy pan and cook over medium heat, stirring without pause with a flat spatula. after 10-12 minutes it will thicken to a glossy paste that pulls away from the sides of the pan. test it: spread a teaspoon on an oiled tray, wait 30 seconds and try to peel it up. if it lifts clean, it is ready; if it smears, cook 2 minutes more and test again. working fast, pour the batter onto the oiled trays and spread it paper-thin with a flat scraper. let it cool 5 minutes until set and no longer tacky, then cut into strips about 6cm wide. roll each strip up tightly from one end and stand the rolls on a serving plate. heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the sesame, slit chillies, curry leaves and a pinch of asafoetida, and pour it over the rolls. scatter the coconut and coriander over and serve at room temperature.

entries.title: Khichu
entries.snippet: scalded rice-flour dough spiked with green chilli and cumin, eaten hot with a pool of oil
entries.text: khichu gujarati scalded rice-flour dough spiked with green chilli and cumin, eaten hot with a pool of oil vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour water green chilli cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) baking soda salt neutral oil sesame seeds red chilli powder bring the water, salt, cumin seeds, chopped green chilli, asafoetida and baking soda to a rolling boil in a heavy pan. turn the heat to low and tip in all the rice flour at once. do not stir yet. cover and leave 2 minutes so the flour steams through. now beat hard with a wooden spoon until it comes together into a single lump with no dry pockets, about 2 minutes. cover again and steam on the lowest heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring once, until the dough looks glossy and pulls away from the sides. wet your palm with cold water and knead the hot dough in the pan for a minute until smooth and elastic. pinch off portions, shape into rough rounds and press a dimple into each with your thumb. pour a spoonful of oil into every dimple, dust with chilli powder and sesame, and eat immediately with the oil running.

entries.title: Lasaniya Batata
entries.snippet: baby potatoes crushed and simmered in a fierce red garlic masala
entries.text: lasaniya batata gujarati baby potatoes crushed and simmered in a fierce red garlic masala vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato garlic kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder groundnut oil cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) sesame seeds green chilli salt water lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) boil the baby potatoes until just tender, drain and cool 10 minutes. press each potato with the flat of your palm until the skin splits and it flattens slightly. leave the skins on. heat the oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin seeds, add the asafoetida and the crushed garlic. fry the garlic over medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes until it turns pale gold and the raw edge goes. stir in the spice paste and the ground sesame and cook 2 minutes until the oil rises red around the edges. add the crushed potatoes and slit green chillies and turn them through the masala until every piece is coated. pour in the water, season with salt, cover and simmer on low for 10-12 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally. uncover and cook 4-5 minutes more until the gravy clings thickly to the potatoes and pools of red oil sit on top. finish with lemon juice and coriander and serve with bajra rotlo or plain khichdi.

entries.title: Mag ni Dal
entries.snippet: loose split yellow moong finished with a ghee and cumin tempering, the plainest weekday dal
entries.text: mag ni dal gujarati loose split yellow moong finished with a ghee and cumin tempering, the plainest weekday dal vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier moong dal water turmeric powder salt ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies curry leaves ginger green chilli lemon / lime black pepper coriander leaves (cilantro) put the rinsed dal, water and turmeric in a pressure cooker and cook 3 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. in an open pan, simmer 30-35 minutes topping up water. open up and whisk the dal briefly — it should be loose enough to pour, like thin cream. add hot water if it has tightened. stir in salt, the grated ginger and the slit green chillies and simmer 5 minutes. heat the ghee in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the cumin seeds and let them turn a shade darker and smell toasted. add the broken dried chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida and pull the pan off the heat after 5 seconds. pour the tempering into the dal — it should hiss — and clap the lid on for a minute to trap the aroma. stir in the lemon juice and cracked pepper off the heat. scatter with coriander and serve over plain rice with a spoon of extra ghee.

entries.title: Methi Muthiya
entries.snippet: steamed fenugreek dumplings squeezed by hand, then tossed in a sesame tempering
entries.text: methi muthiya gujarati steamed fenugreek dumplings squeezed by hand, then tossed in a sesame tempering vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free fenugreek leaves (methi) atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) jowar (sorghum) flour sesame seeds carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder sugar ginger green chilli lemon / lime baking soda neutral oil mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt mix the flours, sesame, ajwain, ground spices, sugar, salt, ginger, chilli and lemon juice in a bowl. add the squeezed methi and 2 tbsp of the oil and work it into a stiff dough, using the methi water only if needed. work in the baking soda, then divide the dough into four and roll each into a log about 4cm thick, squeezing it in your fist so it keeps the finger marks that give muthiya its name. steam the logs 20 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the surface is dry. cool completely, at least 20 minutes, then cut into 2cm slices. heat the remaining oil in a kadhai, pop the mustard seeds, and add the curry leaves and asafoetida. add the slices and pan-fry 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until the cut faces are golden and crisp. scatter the coconut and coriander over and serve hot with tea or masala chai.

entries.title: Methi Thepla
entries.snippet: soft fenugreek-flecked flatbreads that travel for days without going stale
entries.text: methi thepla gujarati soft fenugreek-flecked flatbreads that travel for days without going stale vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) fenugreek leaves (methi) yogurt / dahi ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder carom seeds (ajwain) sesame seeds neutral oil ghee salt water mix the atta, besan, chopped methi, all the spices, sesame and salt in a wide bowl. rub in the 2 tbsp oil until the flour looks like damp sand, then add the yogurt, ginger and chilli. bring it together with water added a spoonful at a time into a soft, pliable dough — softer than roti dough. cover and rest the dough 20 minutes. divide into 12 balls and roll each to a thin round about 15cm across, dusting lightly with atta. cook on a hot tawa 40 seconds, until small bubbles rise, then flip. smear ghee on the cooked side, flip again, and press the edges down with a cloth so it puffs and browns in spots. stack the cooked theplas in a cloth-lined box so they steam each other soft.

entries.title: Patra
entries.snippet: colocasia leaves layered with spiced tamarind gram paste, steamed then crisped
entries.text: patra gujarati colocasia leaves layered with spiced tamarind gram paste, steamed then crisped vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic colocasia (arbi) besan (gram flour) tamarind jaggery ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) carom seeds (ajwain) sesame seeds asafoetida (hing) neutral oil mustard seeds coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water whisk the besan with the tamarind pulp, jaggery, ginger, chilli, all the ground spices, ajwain, asafoetida and salt, adding water slowly to a thick spreadable paste. taste the paste. it should be aggressively sweet-sour and salty; the leaves dilute it a great deal. lay a leaf vein-side up, spread a thin even layer of paste over it, and place a second leaf on top pointing the other way. build stacks of three or four leaves, pasting between each. fold the two long sides inward, spread paste on the fold, then roll up tightly from the base into a firm log. steam the logs 30 minutes, until a skewer slides in without resistance and the outside is dull and dry to the touch. cool completely, then cut into 1.5cm slices. heat the oil in a kadhai, pop the mustard seeds with the sesame, and lay the slices in a single layer. shallow-fry 3 minutes a side until the edges are crisp and browned. scatter the coconut and coriander over and serve warm with tea.

entries.title: Ringan no Olo
entries.snippet: fire-roasted aubergine mashed with raw garlic and green chilli, smoky and fierce
entries.text: ringan no olo gujarati fire-roasted aubergine mashed with raw garlic and green chilli, smoky and fierce vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier eggplant / brinjal garlic green chilli onion tomato groundnut oil cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder salt lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) set the aubergines straight on a medium gas flame, turning every couple of minutes, 12-15 minutes in all, until the skin is blistered black all over and the flesh has collapsed. rest them in a covered bowl 5 minutes, then peel off the charred skin and mash the flesh coarsely with a fork. leave some texture. heat the oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, add the asafoetida and half the crushed garlic and fry 30 seconds until it smells sweet, not brown. add the onion and cook over medium heat until soft and pale gold, about 6 minutes. stir in half the green chilli, the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder, then the tomato. cook 6-7 minutes until the tomato breaks down and the oil separates at the edges. fold in the mashed aubergine and salt. cook uncovered 8 minutes, mashing against the side of the pan, until it thickens and darkens. take it off the heat and stir through the remaining raw crushed garlic, the remaining green chilli and the lemon juice. rest 5 minutes, stir in the coriander and serve with hot bajra rotlo and a spoon of butter or a raw onion.

entries.title: Sev Tameta nu Shaak
entries.snippet: soupy sweet-sharp tomato curry finished with crisp gram flour sev
entries.text: sev tameta nu shaak gujarati soupy sweet-sharp tomato curry finished with crisp gram flour sev vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tomato besan (gram flour) onion garlic green chilli neutral oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder jaggery water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and asafoetida. add the onion and garlic and fry 5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent, not browned. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder off the heat for 10 seconds so they bloom without burning. tip in the tomatoes, green chilli and salt and cook 8 minutes, pressing them down, until they collapse and the oil beads at the edges. add the jaggery and the water and simmer 6 minutes into a loose, pourable gravy. taste and balance: it wants to land sweet first, then sour, then hot. ladle into bowls, pile the sev over the top and scatter the coriander. serve at once with rotli or bhakri, while the sev is still crunchy.

entries.title: Shrikhand
entries.snippet: hung yogurt whipped with sugar, saffron and cardamom into a thick tart cream
entries.text: shrikhand gujarati hung yogurt whipped with sugar, saffron and cardamom into a thick tart cream vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi sugar saffron milk green cardamom pistachios almonds nutmeg crush the saffron between your fingers into the warm milk and leave it to steep 15 minutes until the milk is deep orange. tip the hung yogurt into a bowl and add the sugar. beat with a whisk for 4-5 minutes until the sugar has fully dissolved and the mixture is glossy and smooth. pass it through a fine sieve, pressing with a spatula, for a properly silken texture. fold in the saffron milk, ground cardamom and nutmeg. taste and adjust the sugar; it should be tart first and sweet second. chill at least 3 hours, until set firm enough to hold a peak. spoon into bowls, scatter the pistachios and almonds over and serve with hot puris.

entries.title: Sukhdi
entries.snippet: wheat flour toasted in ghee and set with jaggery, crumbly and warming
entries.text: sukhdi gujarati wheat flour toasted in ghee and set with jaggery, crumbly and warming vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) ghee jaggery dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom melt the ghee in a heavy kadhai over low heat. add the atta and stir continuously with a flat spatula, keeping the flour moving across the base. roast 12-15 minutes over low heat until the flour turns the colour of wet sand and smells like biscuits. stir in the dry ginger powder and cardamom and cook 20 seconds. take the pan completely off the heat and let it stand 60 seconds to cool slightly. add all the jaggery at once and stir hard until it melts into the flour and the mixture turns glossy and pourable, about 45 seconds. tip immediately into the greased tray and level the top with the back of a greased steel bowl. score into diamonds while still hot, after about 3 minutes, then leave to set completely for 30 minutes. break along the score lines and serve at room temperature.

entries.title: Undhiyu
entries.snippet: Surat's winter casserole of root vegetables and methi dumplings, cooked upside down
entries.text: undhiyu gujarati surat's winter casserole of root vegetables and methi dumplings, cooked upside down vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier yam (suran) sweet potato raw banana / plantain potato eggplant / brinjal cluster beans (guar) dried white peas (safed matar) besan (gram flour) fenugreek leaves (methi) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) green chilli ginger sesame seeds peanuts carom seeds (ajwain) asafoetida (hing) jaggery lemon / lime groundnut oil salt blend the coconut, coriander, green chilli, ginger, sesame, peanut, jaggery, lemon and salt to a coarse green masala. make muthiya: knead the besan with chopped methi, a spoon of the masala, ajwain and a little water into a stiff dough; shape small dumplings and shallow fry until golden. set aside. stuff the slit eggplants and any halved potatoes with the green masala. in a heavy pot, heat the oil with asafoetida, then layer the vegetables hardest-first: yam and sweet potato at the bottom, then banana and potato, then beans and peas, stuffed eggplant on top. spoon over the remaining masala and a splash of water, cover tightly and cook on low heat 35-40 minutes. add the muthiya for the last 10 minutes so they soften without dissolving. fold once, very gently, at the end.

entries.title: Vagharelo Bhaat
entries.snippet: yesterday's rice fried up with mustard seeds, potato and peas into a proper meal
entries.text: vagharelo bhaat gujarati yesterday's rice fried up with mustard seeds, potato and peas into a proper meal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) neutral oil mustard seeds cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) curry leaves green chilli onion potato peas turmeric powder red chilli powder sugar salt lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, asafoetida, curry leaves and slit chillies. add the onion and cook 4 minutes over medium-high heat until the edges colour. add the diced potato, turn to coat, cover and cook 6-7 minutes until a piece gives easily to a fork. stir in the peas, turmeric and chilli powder and cook 2 minutes. add the cold rice, salt and sugar and fold gently with a flat spatula until every grain is yellow. raise the heat and leave the rice undisturbed for 2 minutes so the bottom layer catches slightly, then fold once. cook 2 minutes more until the rice is hot all the way through and smells toasted. off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and coriander and serve with plain yogurt or chaas.

entries.title: Arsa
entries.snippet: deep-fried rice flour and jaggery cakes, crisp at the rim and chewy in the middle
entries.text: arsa himachali/pahari deep-fried rice flour and jaggery cakes, crisp at the rim and chewy in the middle vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour jaggery water sesame seeds fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom neutral oil salt melt the jaggery with 120ml water over low heat, stirring, until it dissolves, then strain out the grit through a fine sieve. return the syrup to the pan and boil until it reaches one-thread consistency — a drop lifted between finger and thumb pulls a single strand, about 6 minutes. pour the hot syrup over the rice flour in a wide bowl, add the sesame, fennel, cardamom and salt, and mix with a wooden spoon. once it is cool enough to handle, knead 4-5 minutes into a soft, sticky dough that just holds together. cover and rest at room temperature overnight, 8-10 hours. next day, wet your palms and shape walnut-sized pieces into flat discs about 6cm across and 1cm thick. heat the oil in a kadhai to medium-low, about 160c — a scrap of dough should rise slowly after 4 seconds. slide in 3-4 discs at a time and fry 6-8 minutes, spooning hot oil over them and turning once, until deep reddish brown. lift onto a rack and press each one gently with a slotted spoon to squeeze out oil. cool completely before eating — they firm up as they sit.

entries.title: Auriya Kaddu
entries.snippet: pumpkin in a sharp ground-mustard and yogurt gravy, the tangy course of a dham
entries.text: auriya kaddu himachali/pahari pumpkin in a sharp ground-mustard and yogurt gravy, the tangy course of a dham vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic pumpkin mustard seeds yogurt / dahi ghee mustard oil fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies turmeric powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) sugar water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the ghee and mustard oil together until the mustard oil stops smelling raw, about 1 minute. crackle the fenugreek seeds and broken red chillies for 20 seconds, then add the hing. add the pumpkin cubes and toss over medium heat 5 minutes until the edges catch a little colour. take the pan off the heat for a minute so it cools, then pour in the whisked spiced yogurt and stir continuously. return to a low flame and cook, stirring in one direction, until the yogurt loses its raw smell and thickens slightly, about 4 minutes. stir in the ground mustard paste, 200ml water and salt. simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the pumpkin is tender at a knifepoint but not falling apart. add the amchur and sugar, cook 2 minutes more and taste. it should be sour, mustardy and only faintly sweet. rest 5 minutes off the heat and serve with rice as part of a dham.

entries.title: Babru
entries.snippet: shimla-style fried breads packed with spiced ground urad dal, crisp outside and savoury through
entries.text: babru himachali/pahari shimla-style fried breads packed with spiced ground urad dal, crisp outside and savoury through vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) plain flour (maida) urad dal (black gram) neutral oil mustard oil cumin seeds carom seeds (ajwain) asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) fennel seeds (saunf) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water mix the atta, maida, 1 tsp salt and the mustard oil, then add water gradually to a firm, smooth dough. knead 6 minutes. cover and rest 30 minutes. the dough should press back slowly when poked. grind the drained urad dal with the green chillies and ginger to a coarse, dry paste, using at most 2 tbsp water. heat 2 tbsp of the frying oil in a pan, crackle the cumin, ajwain and asafoetida, then add the dal paste. cook the dal on medium for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking up lumps, until it dries out and comes away from the pan in a single crumbly mass. stir in the coriander powder, chilli powder, amchur, crushed fennel, garam masala, salt and coriander leaves. cook 2 minutes, then cool completely. divide the dough into 10 balls. flatten each in your palm, cup it, put in a heaped tablespoon of cold filling, gather the edges over the top and pinch shut. press flat. roll each stuffed ball gently to about 10cm across, working from the centre out with light pressure. heat the oil to 175c. slide in two babrus at a time and press the centre lightly with a slotted spoon so they puff. fry 2 minutes a side until deep golden and blistered. drain and serve hot with kaddu ka khatta or a tamarind chutney.

entries.title: Bhatt Ki Churkani
entries.snippet: kumaoni black beans roasted in mustard oil and simmered into a dark, smoky, rice-thickened gravy
entries.text: bhatt ki churkani himachali/pahari kumaoni black beans roasted in mustard oil and simmered into a dark, smoky, rice-thickened gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier whole urad (sabut urad) rice flour mustard oil garlic ginger green chilli dried red chillies cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a heavy pan until it smokes, then cool it 20 seconds. add the drained beans and roast them on medium for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring, until the skins wrinkle and blister. transfer the beans to a pressure cooker with 800ml water and 1 tsp salt. cook for 6 whistles and let the pressure fall naturally. heat the remaining 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking, then cool briefly. crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds and the broken red chillies, 20 seconds. add the asafoetida, then the crushed garlic, and fry 1 minute to pale gold. stir in the ginger and green chillies, then the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder. fry 30 seconds. tip in the cooked beans with all their liquid and bring to a boil. stir the rice flour slurry once more and pour it in slowly while stirring hard. the gravy will thicken visibly within a minute. simmer uncovered on low for 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the gravy turns glossy and dark and coats a spoon thickly. check the salt, scatter over the coriander leaves and serve with plain rice and a spoon of raw mustard oil on top if you like it sharp.

entries.title: Chana Dal Dham
entries.snippet: sweet-sour chana dal from the dham feast, no onion or garlic anywhere in it
entries.text: chana dal dham himachali/pahari sweet-sour chana dal from the dham feast, no onion or garlic anywhere in it vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder dry ginger powder (saunth) tamarind jaggery anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) garam masala water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) pressure cook the drained dal with 750ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 2 whistles, then lower the flame and give it 6 minutes more. heat the ghee in a heavy pan until it thins and shimmers, then add the cumin. it should crackle within 3 seconds. drop in the hing and count to five. it will foam and smell nutty, not acrid. stir in the coriander powder, chilli powder and dry ginger powder off the heat for 20 seconds so they bloom without burning. pour in the cooked dal with its liquid and bring to a simmer, 5 minutes. add the tamarind pulp and the jaggery and simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. crush in the anardana and the garam masala, simmer 3 minutes more, then check the salt. rest the pot off the heat for 10 minutes before serving. scatter the coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Chana Madra
entries.snippet: chickpeas simmered slowly in whisked yogurt until the gravy is silky, faintly sour and heavy with whole spice
entries.text: chana madra himachali/pahari chickpeas simmered slowly in whisked yogurt until the gravy is silky, faintly sour and heavy with whole spice vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic healthier chickpeas (kabuli chana) yogurt / dahi ghee besan (gram flour) cumin seeds cinnamon black cardamom green cardamom cloves bay leaf asafoetida (hing) coriander powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala almonds raisins (kishmish) salt water pressure cook the drained chickpeas with 500ml water and 1 tsp salt for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself. they should crush easily between finger and thumb but still hold their shape. heat the ghee in a heavy kadhai until it thins and shimmers. add the cumin, cinnamon, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves and bay leaves and let them swell and crackle, about 40 seconds. add the asafoetida, count to five, then take the pan off the heat entirely and let it cool for a full minute. pour in the whisked yogurt, return to the lowest possible flame and stir continuously in one direction for 8 to 10 minutes, until the yogurt loses its raw smell and thickens to the consistency of pouring cream. stir in the coriander powder, fennel powder, dry ginger, turmeric and kashmiri chilli. cook 3 minutes more - the gravy will turn glossy and the ghee will start to bead at the edges. add the drained chickpeas along with 150ml of their cooking water. season with salt. simmer uncovered on low for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon and a clear rim of ghee sits around the edge of the pan. fold in the almonds and raisins and cook 3 minutes so the raisins plump. finish with the garam masala, cover and rest off the heat for 10 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Kaapa
entries.snippet: garhwali spinach thickened with gram flour, garlicky and eaten by the bowl with rice
entries.text: kaapa himachali/pahari garhwali spinach thickened with gram flour, garlicky and eaten by the bowl with rice vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free spinach besan (gram flour) mustard oil garlic ginger green chilli cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies turmeric powder coriander powder water salt lemon / lime blanch the spinach in boiling water for 90 seconds, drain and plunge into cold water to fix the colour. squeeze out the excess water and either chop it fine or pulse it briefly in a blender to a coarse puree. heat the mustard oil until it smokes, cut the flame for a minute, then crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds for 20 seconds. add the hing, red chillies, garlic, ginger and green chillies and fry 2 minutes until the garlic is golden. stir in the turmeric and coriander powder, then pour in the smooth besan slurry, whisking continuously. cook the besan mixture on a low flame for 6-8 minutes until it thickens and stops smelling of raw flour. add the spinach, the remaining 200ml water and salt. simmer uncovered 10 minutes until it is thick enough to hold a ridge from the spoon. finish with the lemon juice off the heat and serve with hot rice.

entries.title: Kaddu Ka Khatta
entries.snippet: pumpkin cooked down with tamarind, pomegranate seed and jaggery into the sharp sour dish that cuts a dham
entries.text: kaddu ka khatta himachali/pahari pumpkin cooked down with tamarind, pomegranate seed and jaggery into the sharp sour dish that cuts a dham vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic pumpkin mustard oil fenugreek seeds (methi) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) tamarind anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) jaggery turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder dry ginger powder (saunth) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly and the sharp smell drops away, about 2 minutes. take it off the heat for 20 seconds to cool slightly. add the fenugreek seeds and let them darken to a nut brown, no more than 15 seconds, then the cumin. stir in the asafoetida, then immediately add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and dry ginger. fry 20 seconds. tip in the pumpkin and toss to coat every piece in the spiced oil. fry on medium for 5 minutes until the edges start to catch. pour in 300ml water, add salt, cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes until a knife slides into a cube with no resistance. add the tamarind pulp, the ground anardana and the jaggery. stir gently - from here on you want the cubes intact. simmer uncovered 8 to 10 minutes, mashing four or five pieces against the side of the pan, until the gravy thickens to a loose chutney that clings to the pumpkin. finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. serve at room temperature alongside rice and madra.

entries.title: Khatta Meat
entries.snippet: chamba mutton curry made sour with pomegranate seed and dried mango, thin and fiercely spiced
entries.text: khatta meat himachali/pahari chamba mutton curry made sour with pomegranate seed and dried mango, thin and fiercely spiced gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb mustard oil onion ginger garlic anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) amchur (dry mango powder) coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder cumin seeds black cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf garam masala jaggery water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil until it smokes, cut the flame for 60 seconds, then return it to medium. crackle the cumin, black cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaf for 30 seconds until the cardamom smells smoky. add the sliced onion and fry 10-12 minutes to a deep even brown, stirring often. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell lifts. add the mutton and brown it hard over high heat for 8 minutes, stirring so every piece takes colour. lower the heat, add the turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt, and fry 4 minutes until oil beads at the edges. pour in 600ml water, bring to a boil, then pressure cook 4 whistles and rest until the pressure drops on its own, about 20 minutes. open the cooker, stir in the ground anardana and the amchur, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes. the gravy stays deliberately thin. add the jaggery and garam masala, simmer 3 minutes, taste for salt and sourness. rest 10 minutes off the heat, scatter the coriander and serve with steamed rice.

entries.title: Kullu Trout
entries.snippet: whole river trout crisped in mustard oil with ajwain and a hard squeeze of lemon
entries.text: kullu trout himachali/pahari whole river trout crisped in mustard oil with ajwain and a hard squeeze of lemon pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard oil carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder ginger garlic black pepper lemon / lime rice flour salt coriander leaves (cilantro) mix the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, ajwain, black pepper, ginger, garlic, lemon juice and salt into a thick paste. rub the paste over the fish and well into the slashes and the cavity. rest 20 minutes. dust each fish lightly with rice flour on both sides and shake off the excess. heat the mustard oil on a heavy tawa until it smokes, then cut the heat to medium for a minute. lay the fish in away from you and fry undisturbed for 5 minutes. turn once with a wide spatula and fry the second side 4-5 minutes until the thickest part flakes at a fork. lift onto a warm plate, rest 2 minutes, scatter coriander and serve with lemon wedges and hot rice.

entries.title: Mash Ki Dal
entries.snippet: whole black urad cooked down thick and buttery over a mustard oil base, the everyday hill dal
entries.text: mash ki dal himachali/pahari whole black urad cooked down thick and buttery over a mustard oil base, the everyday hill dal vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier whole urad (sabut urad) chana dal mustard oil ghee onion garlic ginger tomato green chilli cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder dry ginger powder (saunth) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water pressure cook the drained dals with 900ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 5 whistles, then 15 minutes on the lowest flame. let the pressure drop naturally. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes lightly, then cool it 20 seconds off the flame. crackle the cumin, add the asafoetida, then the garlic. fry 40 seconds until it just turns pale gold. add the onion and cook on medium, stirring, for 10 to 12 minutes until it is properly brown at the edges and sweet-smelling. stir in the ginger and green chillies, then the coriander powder, chilli powder and dry ginger. fry 30 seconds. add the tomatoes and cook 6 to 8 minutes, pressing them down, until they break completely and the oil pulls away to the sides. pour the cooked dal into the masala. simmer uncovered 15 to 20 minutes on low, stirring and mashing against the pan, until it thickens enough to hold a furrow behind the spoon. check the salt, sprinkle over the garam masala and take off the heat. stir in the raw ghee and the coriander leaves and cover for 5 minutes before serving with rice or a hot roti.

entries.title: Mittha
entries.snippet: saffron sweet rice studded with raisin, almond and apricot, the dish that closes every dham
entries.text: mittha himachali/pahari saffron sweet rice studded with raisin, almond and apricot, the dish that closes every dham vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice sugar ghee saffron green cardamom cloves cinnamon raisins (kishmish) almonds dried apricots (khubani) dried coconut (copra) salt water heat 4 tbsp of the ghee in a heavy pot. fry the almonds until pale gold, about 90 seconds, then the raisins until they puff, 20 seconds. lift both out and set aside. into the same ghee add the cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the drained rice and fry gently for 3 minutes, turning with a flat spoon, until every grain is glossy and a few have turned opaque white. pour in 550ml water with the pinch of salt and half the saffron liquid. bring to a hard boil. drop the heat to low, cover and cook 10 minutes until the water is absorbed and the rice is about three-quarters done - still firm at the core. sprinkle the sugar evenly over the surface, add the apricots, and do not stir. cover and cook on the lowest heat 8 minutes - the sugar will melt and be drawn down through the rice. uncover, drizzle over the last tablespoon of ghee and the remaining saffron water, and fold through once with a fork. fold in the fried almonds, raisins and the coconut slivers. cover and rest off the heat 10 minutes. fluff once more with a fork and serve warm, in small portions - it is richer than it looks.

entries.title: Patrode
entries.snippet: colocasia leaves layered with spiced gram flour, steamed into rolls and fried in slices
entries.text: patrode himachali/pahari colocasia leaves layered with spiced gram flour, steamed into rolls and fried in slices vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free colocasia (arbi) besan (gram flour) rice flour tamarind jaggery carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) asafoetida (hing) mustard oil mustard seeds sesame seeds water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) wipe the leaves clean and shave down the raised central ribs so each leaf lies flat. whisk the besan, rice flour, tamarind pulp, jaggery, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, hing and salt with enough water to make a thick spreadable paste, about the consistency of peanut butter. lay a leaf shiny side down, spread a thin even layer of paste over it, and lay a second leaf on top facing the opposite way. build stacks of 4 leaves. fold the two long sides of each stack inward, spread a little more paste on the folds, then roll up tightly from the base into a firm log. steam the rolls seam side down for 25-30 minutes, until a knife pushed into the centre comes out clean. cool the rolls completely, at least 2 hours, then cut into 1.5cm thick slices. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, cut the heat for a minute, then pop the mustard seeds and sesame. lay the slices in a single layer and shallow fry 3 minutes a side until crisp and browned at the edges. drain, scatter with coriander leaves and serve hot with tea, or with rice and dal as part of a meal.

entries.title: Rajma Madra
entries.snippet: red kidney beans in a thick soured-yogurt gravy, the dham version that eats richer than chana madra
entries.text: rajma madra himachali/pahari red kidney beans in a thick soured-yogurt gravy, the dham version that eats richer than chana madra vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier rajma (kidney beans) yogurt / dahi ghee besan (gram flour) cumin seeds black cardamom green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf asafoetida (hing) coriander powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala salt water pressure cook the drained rajma with 700ml fresh water and 1 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles, then let the pressure fall naturally. a bean should collapse when pressed, with the skin still intact. heat the ghee in a heavy pan until it shimmers. add cumin, black cardamom, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves; they will foam and smell sweet within 30 to 40 seconds. add the asafoetida, then pull the pan off the flame and let it cool a full minute. return the pan to the lowest heat and pour in the yogurt, stirring without pause for 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens and the raw sourness cooks off. stir in the coriander, fennel, dry ginger, turmeric and kashmiri chilli. cook 3 minutes until the gravy turns a deep ochre and glossy. tip in the rajma with about 200ml of its cooking liquor and season with salt. crush a small ladleful of the beans against the side of the pan and stir back in - this thickens the gravy without flour. simmer uncovered 25 minutes on low, stirring often, until the ghee separates and rises in a clear rim. sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with steamed rice.

entries.title: Sepu Vadi
entries.snippet: fried urad dal dumplings soaked soft in a spinach and yogurt gravy, the dish that marks a proper kangra dham
entries.text: sepu vadi himachali/pahari fried urad dal dumplings soaked soft in a spinach and yogurt gravy, the dish that marks a proper kangra dham vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic urad dal (black gram) spinach yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) ghee neutral oil cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) green chilli ginger coriander powder turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water grind the drained urad dal to a thick, coarse paste with the green chillies and grated ginger, using no more than 3 tbsp water. beat the paste vigorously for 4 to 5 minutes with salt until it lightens in colour and passes the float test. heat the frying oil to 170c. drop in flat spoonfuls of the batter, four or five at a time, and fry 4 to 5 minutes until deep gold and firm. drain on paper. cut each fried vadi in half through its thickness. this is what lets it drink up the gravy. boil the spinach in 200ml water for 4 minutes, then blend it to a smooth green puree with its liquid. heat the ghee in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, add the asafoetida and take the pan off the heat for a minute to cool. on the lowest flame pour in the yogurt-besan mixture and stir continuously for 8 minutes until it thickens and stops smelling raw. stir in the coriander powder, turmeric, kashmiri chilli, fennel and dry ginger, then the spinach puree and 200ml water. season and simmer 8 minutes. slide in the halved vadis, cover and simmer very gently 10 minutes until they swell and turn spongy but still hold together. finish with garam masala and coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Siddu
entries.snippet: steamed wheat buns risen slow and stuffed with crushed walnut and poppy seed, eaten swimming in ghee
entries.text: siddu himachali/pahari steamed wheat buns risen slow and stuffed with crushed walnut and poppy seed, eaten swimming in ghee vegetarian atta (wholewheat flour) yogurt / dahi baking soda ghee walnuts poppy seeds (khus khus) mustard oil green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) carom seeds (ajwain) cumin powder (jeera) red chilli powder black pepper salt water mix the atta, baking soda and 1 tsp salt. work in the yogurt, then the lukewarm water a little at a time, to a soft dough slightly stickier than roti dough. knead 8 minutes. oil the surface, cover with a damp cloth and leave in a warm spot for 3 hours. it should look puffed and feel airy, not doubled like bread. meanwhile mix the crushed walnuts, roasted poppy seeds, mustard oil, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, ajwain, cumin powder, chilli powder, black pepper and salt into a damp, crumbly filling. knock the dough back gently and divide into 8 balls. do not knead it hard again. roll each ball into a 12cm disc. put 2 heaped tbsp of filling on one half, fold over into a half moon and press the curved edge firmly, then pleat it shut with your fingers. rest the shaped siddus, covered, for 15 minutes while the steamer comes up to a rolling boil. grease the steamer plate, arrange the siddus with 2cm between them and steam on high for 18 to 20 minutes. test with a skewer through the thickest part: it should come out clean and dry. give them 3 more minutes if not. take them out, split the tops slightly and pour a tablespoon of melted ghee over each. serve hot with mash dal or a chutney.

entries.title: Tudkiya Bhath
entries.snippet: chamba pahari rice cooked through with chana dal, potato and yogurt until every grain carries the masala
entries.text: tudkiya bhath himachali/pahari chamba pahari rice cooked through with chana dal, potato and yogurt until every grain carries the masala vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier basmati rice chana dal potato yogurt / dahi ghee mustard oil onion garlic ginger tomato green chilli bay leaf black cardamom cinnamon cloves cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala mint coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the ghee and mustard oil together in a heavy pot until shimmering. add the bay leaves, black cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and cumin and let them crackle for 30 seconds. add the sliced onion and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes until brown at the edges and shrunken to a third of its volume. stir in the garlic, ginger and green chillies and fry 1 minute until the raw smell goes. add the turmeric, coriander powder and kashmiri chilli, then the tomato. cook 5 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil beads at the edge. take the pot off the heat for 30 seconds, then pour in the whisked yogurt on low and stir constantly for 4 minutes until it thickens and stops looking curdled. add the drained chana dal and potato cubes with 150ml water. cover and simmer 10 minutes - the dal should be half done, still with a bite. fold in the drained rice as gently as you can and fry 2 minutes so each grain is coated. pour in 450ml hot water, add salt generously and the mint, and bring to a hard boil. taste the water - it should be a shade saltier than you want the finished rice. cover tight, drop to the lowest flame and cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid. rest off the heat 10 minutes, then fork through with the garam masala and coriander leaves. serve with plain yogurt.

entries.title: Bagara Baingan
entries.snippet: small aubergines stewed whole in a sesame-peanut gravy sharp with tamarind
entries.text: bagara baingan hyderabadi small aubergines stewed whole in a sesame-peanut gravy sharp with tamarind vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier eggplant / brinjal peanuts sesame seeds dried coconut (copra) poppy seeds (khus khus) onion tamarind ginger garlic green chilli curry leaves cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the peanuts 5 minutes until blistered, then rub off the skins. roast the sesame, coconut and poppy seeds separately, each for about a minute, and cool everything. grind the roasted lot to a smooth paste with 120ml water. heat half the oil in a kadhai and fry the drained aubergines over medium heat for 6-7 minutes, turning, until the skins are blistered and the flesh has softened. lift out. in the same oil fry the sliced onion until deep golden, about 10 minutes, then cool and grind to a paste. add the remaining oil, crackle the mustard, cumin and fenugreek, then add the curry leaves and green chillies. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes, cook 1 minute, then add the onion paste with the turmeric, chilli, coriander and cumin powders. fry 3 minutes. add the ground nut-and-seed paste and cook on medium-low for 8 minutes until it thickens, darkens by a shade and oil beads at the edges. pour in the tamarind water and the rest of the water, season with salt and simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon. lower the aubergines in, spoon gravy over them, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes until a knife slides through with no resistance. rest off the heat for 10 minutes and finish with coriander leaves. serve with bagara rice.

entries.title: Bagara Khana
entries.snippet: everyday whole-spice rice, the plain partner to salan and dalcha
entries.text: bagara khana hyderabadi everyday whole-spice rice, the plain partner to salan and dalcha vegetarian gluten-free nut-free basmati rice ghee onion ginger garlic green chilli cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon cloves green cardamom black cardamom star anise stone flower (dagad phool) curry leaves mint water salt heat the ghee in a heavy pot and add the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black cardamom, star anise and stone flower. let them sizzle 30 seconds until fragrant. add the curry leaves and sliced onion and fry 7-8 minutes until light golden and just beginning to crisp at the edges. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the slit green chillies and cook 1 minute. add the drained rice and turn it gently through the ghee for 2 minutes until every grain is glossy. pour in the water, add the salt and the mint, and bring to a full rolling boil. boil uncovered until the water level drops to the surface of the rice and craters appear, about 5 minutes. cover tightly, drop the heat to the lowest setting and cook 10 minutes without lifting the lid. rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork from the edges inwards and serve.

entries.title: Baghara Tamatar
entries.snippet: whole tomatoes simmered in the peanut, sesame and coconut gravy of the salan family
entries.text: baghara tamatar hyderabadi whole tomatoes simmered in the peanut, sesame and coconut gravy of the salan family vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier tomato peanuts sesame seeds dried coconut (copra) onion tamarind ginger garlic green chilli mustard seeds cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) fenugreek seeds (methi) curry leaves red chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder jaggery neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the peanuts over medium heat 5 minutes, until the skins blister. cool and rub off most of the skins. toast the sesame 2 minutes until it pops, then the coconut 1 minute until golden. cool everything. fry the sliced onion in 2 tbsp of the oil until golden, 10 minutes, then cool. grind the peanuts, sesame, coconut and fried onion with 150ml water to a smooth, thick paste. heat the remaining oil in a kadhai and pop the mustard seeds, cumin, nigella and fenugreek, 20 seconds. add the curry leaves and green chillies. add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 1 minute, then the whole tomatoes, and roll them in the oil for 3 minutes. lift the tomatoes out and set aside. add the ground paste with the chilli powder, turmeric and coriander powder, and fry over medium heat 8 minutes. pour in the strained tamarind water and 250ml plain water, add the salt and jaggery, and bring to a simmer. return the tomatoes, cover, and simmer on low 12 minutes, spooning gravy over them twice, until they are soft but still whole. uncover and simmer 5 minutes more, until a slick of red oil separates on top. scatter the coriander and rest 10 minutes before serving with bagara rice.

entries.title: Dalcha
entries.snippet: mutton and chana dal simmered with bottle gourd and a firm sour edge
entries.text: dalcha hyderabadi mutton and chana dal simmered with bottle gourd and a firm sour edge gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb chana dal bottle gourd (lauki) onion tomato tamarind ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala curry leaves cumin seeds mustard seeds dried red chillies neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) heat 2 tbsp oil in the pressure cooker and brown the sliced onion for 8 minutes until golden at the edges. add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 1 minute, then the mutton. sear on high for 5 minutes until the pieces lose their raw pink. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt, add the tomatoes, and cook 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down. add the drained chana dal and 1 litre of water. pressure cook 4 whistles, about 20 minutes, then let the pressure drop naturally. open, add the bottle gourd and the remaining water, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the gourd is translucent and yields to a spoon. pour in the tamarind water and the garam masala. simmer 10 minutes more, mashing some of the dal against the side of the pot to thicken it. taste for salt and sour; the balance should make you sit up. adjust with a little more tamarind water or a splash of plain water. for the tempering, heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a small pan and crackle the mustard and cumin seeds, then add the dried red chillies and curry leaves and let them spit for 10 seconds. pour the tempering over the dalcha, stir once, and scatter with coriander leaves. rest 5 minutes before serving with bagara rice.

entries.title: Double ka Meetha
entries.snippet: fried bread soaked in saffron milk and cardamom syrup, the wedding-feast pudding
entries.text: double ka meetha hyderabadi fried bread soaked in saffron milk and cardamom syrup, the wedding-feast pudding vegetarian sliced bread ghee milk sugar water khoya / mawa condensed milk green cardamom saffron almonds cashews pistachios raisins (kishmish) boil the milk in a heavy pan and simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until reduced to about 450ml and noticeably thickened. stir the khoya, or the condensed milk, into the reduced milk along with half the saffron milk. take off the heat. in a separate pan, dissolve the sugar in the water and boil 5 minutes to a thin one-string syrup, then add the crushed cardamom and the rest of the saffron milk. heat the ghee in a kadhai and fry the nuts and raisins briefly until golden. remove and set aside. fry the bread triangles in the same ghee over medium heat, a few at a time, for about 2 minutes a side until evenly deep golden and crisp right through. drain the fried bread on a rack for a minute so the surface ghee runs off. dip each piece into the warm syrup for 5 seconds only, then arrange in a single overlapping layer in a serving dish. pour the warm thickened milk evenly over the bread and leave it to soak for 15 minutes. scatter the fried nuts and raisins over the top and serve warm or at room temperature.

entries.title: Dum Ka Murgh
entries.snippet: chicken sealed and slow-cooked in a pale almond and fried-onion gravy
