entries.text: dum ka murgh hyderabadi chicken sealed and slow-cooked in a pale almond and fried-onion gravy gluten-free chicken yogurt / dahi onion almonds poppy seeds (khus khus) melon seeds (magaz) ginger garlic green chilli green cardamom black pepper mace (javitri) nutmeg saffron kewra water ghee neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) mint salt fry the sliced onion in the oil over medium heat until deep gold and crisp, 15 minutes. drain on paper, cool completely, then crush to a coarse paste. grind the soaked almonds, poppy seeds and melon seeds with 3 tbsp water to a completely smooth paste. rub a little between your fingers; any grit means keep grinding. mix the hung yogurt, birista paste, nut paste, ginger and garlic pastes, green chilli paste, cardamom, pepper, mace, nutmeg and salt into a marinade. coat the chicken thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate at least 3 hours. heat the ghee in a heavy pan, tip in the whole marinated chicken with all its marinade, and cook uncovered over medium heat 8 minutes, stirring gently. lower the heat to minimum, cover with a tight lid, and cook 30 minutes without lifting the lid. uncover, stir once from the bottom, and check the gravy: it should be thick, pale and clinging, with ghee pooling at the edges. stir in the saffron milk and kewra water and cook uncovered 5 minutes more to tighten the gravy. rest off the heat, covered, 10 minutes, then scatter over the coriander and mint and serve with sheermal or bagara rice.

entries.title: Gil-e-Firdaus
entries.snippet: bottle gourd cooked down in thickened milk with sago, a wedding-table pudding
entries.text: gil-e-firdaus hyderabadi bottle gourd cooked down in thickened milk with sago, a wedding-table pudding vegetarian gluten-free bottle gourd (lauki) milk sabudana (tapioca pearls) condensed milk sugar khoya / mawa green cardamom saffron almonds pistachios ghee rose water fry the grated bottle gourd in the ghee over medium heat 8 minutes, until it loses its raw smell and the volume halves. pour in the milk and any reserved gourd juice, bring to a boil, then lower to a steady simmer. simmer uncovered 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the base and sides, until the milk has reduced by about a third. add the drained sabudana and cook 10 minutes, stirring often, until the pearls are translucent with no white dot in the centre. stir in the condensed milk and sugar and cook 5 minutes, until dissolved and slightly thickened. fold in the grated khoya and cook 3 minutes, until melted and the pudding coats the back of a spoon. take off the heat and stir in the ground cardamom, saffron milk and rose water. stir in half the slivered almonds and pistachios and cool 20 minutes. chill at least 3 hours, then serve cold in small bowls scattered with the remaining nuts. it thickens as it chills.

entries.title: Haleem
entries.snippet: Wheat, lentils and mutton pounded together for hours into a smooth, savoury porridge
entries.text: haleem hyderabadi wheat, lentils and mutton pounded together for hours into a smooth, savoury porridge nut-free healthier dalia (broken wheat) mutton / lamb chana dal masoor dal (red lentil) moong dal urad dal (black gram) onion ginger garlic red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala mint lemon / lime ghee salt pressure cook the soaked dalia and the mixed dals with turmeric and plenty of water until collapsing, about 5 whistles. separately, cook the mutton with ginger, garlic, chilli powder, half the birista and salt until it falls off the bone. reserve the stock. pick the meat off the bones and shred it finely; discard the bones but keep every drop of stock. combine meat, grain and stock in a wide heavy pot. now beat and mash over low heat for 45-60 minutes, adding ghee in stages. when it pulls away from the sides of the pot in a single mass, stir in garam masala and mint. serve topped with birista, fried mint, ginger julienne and a lot of lemon.

entries.title: Hyderabadi Chicken 65
entries.snippet: twice-fried chilli chicken finished in a spitting curry-leaf and yogurt tempering
entries.text: hyderabadi chicken 65 hyderabadi twice-fried chilli chicken finished in a spitting curry-leaf and yogurt tempering gluten-free nut-free chicken yogurt / dahi ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder rice flour besan (gram flour) eggs garam masala black pepper lemon / lime curry leaves green chilli neutral oil salt coriander leaves (cilantro) mix the chicken with the 4 tbsp yogurt, ginger and garlic pastes, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, garam masala, black pepper, lemon juice and salt. refrigerate at least 2 hours. half an hour before cooking, work the rice flour, besan and beaten egg into the marinade. it should coat each piece in a thin paste, not a batter. heat the frying oil in a kadhai to 170c. a cube of chicken should sizzle steadily and rise within 3 seconds. fry in three batches, 4-5 minutes each, until pale gold and just cooked through. drain on a rack, not paper. raise the oil to 190c and return all the chicken for a second fry of 1-2 minutes until deep red-gold and crisp at the edges. drain. pour off the frying oil, leaving 2 tbsp in the pan. drop in the curry leaves and slit green chillies and let them crackle for 20 seconds. whisk the remaining 3 tbsp yogurt smooth, take the pan off the heat and stir it in. return the pan to a low flame, add the fried chicken and toss for 1 minute until every piece is coated and the yogurt has almost dried onto it. finish with coriander leaves and serve hot with raw onion rings and lemon.

entries.title: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
entries.snippet: Kachchi biryani: raw marinated mutton layered under rice and sealed from the start
entries.text: hyderabadi dum biryani hyderabadi kachchi biryani: raw marinated mutton layered under rice and sealed from the start gluten-free healthier mutton / lamb basmati rice yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala mint coriander leaves (cilantro) saffron lemon / lime green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf ghee atta (wholewheat flour) salt marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger, garlic, chilli, turmeric, garam masala, half the birista, half the herbs, lemon juice and salt. refrigerate 6 hours or overnight. bring the marinated meat to room temperature and spread it in a heavy pot with 3 tbsp ghee. boil the rice in well-salted water with the whole spices until 70% done, then drain immediately. layer the rice over the raw meat. top with the remaining birista, herbs, saffron milk and ghee. seal with a dough rope or tight foil. cook on high for 5 minutes to build steam, then on the lowest heat for 45 minutes. rest 15 minutes before opening. serve with mirchi ka salan and dahi chutney.

entries.title: Hyderabadi Kheema
entries.snippet: minced mutton with peas, dry and heavily spiced, the weeknight standby
entries.text: hyderabadi kheema hyderabadi minced mutton with peas, dry and heavily spiced, the weeknight standby gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb peas potato onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala cumin seeds mint coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime neutral oil water salt heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 15 seconds. add the chopped onion and fry over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden brown and shrunk to a third of its volume. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the green chillies and cook 1 minute until the raw smell lifts. add the mince and break it apart with the back of a spoon. fry on high for 6-7 minutes until it is uniformly brown with no clumps. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder and salt and fry 2 minutes. add the chopped tomatoes and cook 6-7 minutes until they melt down and oil beads at the edges of the pan. pour in the water, add the diced potato if using, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes. add the peas, cover and cook 8 minutes more until the mince is tender and the liquid has almost gone. uncover and fry on medium for 4 minutes, stirring, until the kheema is dry and glistening rather than saucy. stir in the garam masala, mint, coriander and lemon juice and rest 5 minutes before serving with roti or pav.

entries.title: Hyderabadi Khichdi
entries.snippet: loose rice and moong dal cooked with whole spices, the city's breakfast plate
entries.text: hyderabadi khichdi hyderabadi loose rice and moong dal cooked with whole spices, the city's breakfast plate vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) moong dal onion green chilli ginger cumin seeds green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf black pepper turmeric powder ghee water salt heat the ghee in a pressure cooker and crackle the cumin, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, peppercorns and bay leaf for 40 seconds. add the sliced onion and fry over medium heat 8 minutes, until light golden. add the ginger and green chillies and fry 1 minute. stir in the drained rice and dal and fry 3 minutes, until the grains look glossy and smell nutty. add the turmeric, salt and 900ml water, and stir once. close the cooker and cook on medium for 2 whistles, then turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally, about 10 minutes. open up and fluff with a fork. the grains should be soft and just holding their shape, with no free liquid at the bottom. rest covered 5 minutes, then serve hot with khichdi ka khatta and a spoon of extra ghee.

entries.title: Khatti Dal
entries.snippet: everyday toor dal made unapologetically sour with tamarind
entries.text: khatti dal hyderabadi everyday toor dal made unapologetically sour with tamarind vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) tamarind tomato green chilli onion garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) pressure cook the dal with the turmeric, chopped tomato, green chillies and 700ml water for 4 whistles, about 12 minutes. let the pressure fall on its own, then whisk the dal hard for 30 seconds until it is smooth and creamy with no whole lentils left. return the pan to a low flame, add the remaining water and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer. stir in the tamarind water and simmer 8 minutes, until the raw sour smell has cooked off and the dal has thickened slightly. heat the oil in a small pan for the tempering. crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin and fenugreek. add the crushed garlic and fry until it turns golden, about 1 minute, then the dried red chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida. it will spit hard. if using onion, add it to the tempering and fry 3 minutes until soft and translucent. pour the tempering into the dal, cover immediately for a minute to trap the aroma, then stir through. finish with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice and a wedge of lime.

entries.title: Khichdi Ka Khatta
entries.snippet: thin, sharp tamarind sauce poured over khichdi, sour first and sweet after
entries.text: khichdi ka khatta hyderabadi thin, sharp tamarind sauce poured over khichdi, sour first and sweet after vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tamarind garlic green chilli curry leaves mustard seeds cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder jaggery neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt squeeze the soaked tamarind hard in its water, strain through a sieve, and press the pulp to get everything out. discard the fibres. heat the oil in a pan and pop the mustard seeds, 20 seconds, until they stop jumping. add the cumin, fenugreek seeds and dried red chillies and fry 15 seconds, no longer. add the asafoetida, curry leaves, crushed garlic and green chillies and fry 1 minute, until the garlic is pale gold and the leaves are crisp. stir in the turmeric and chilli powder off the heat for 10 seconds so they bloom without scorching. pour in the strained tamarind water and 200ml plain water, add the salt, and bring to a boil. simmer uncovered 12 minutes, until the raw edge of the tamarind has gone and the sauce smells rounded rather than sharp. stir in the jaggery and simmer 3 minutes more, until dissolved. taste: sour should lead, sweet should follow. slacken with hot water if it has thickened past pouring consistency, scatter the coriander, and serve hot over khichdi.

entries.title: Lukhmi
entries.snippet: square flaky pastries filled with spiced mutton mince, the classic wedding starter
entries.text: lukhmi hyderabadi square flaky pastries filled with spiced mutton mince, the classic wedding starter nut-free plain flour (maida) ghee water mutton / lamb onion ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala black pepper lemon / lime mint coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt rub the melted ghee into the maida with your fingertips for 3 minutes until the flour holds its shape when squeezed in a fist. add the salt and cold water a little at a time and bring together into a firm, tight dough — firmer than a chapati dough. knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes. for the filling, heat 2 tbsp oil and fry the chopped onion for 8 minutes until golden. add the ginger and garlic pastes and green chillies, cook 1 minute, then the mince. break it up with the back of a spoon and fry on high for 5 minutes until it loses its pink. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and cook on medium for 12 minutes, stirring, until the mince is dry and the fat has separated out. stir in the garam masala, black pepper, lemon juice, mint and coriander. spread on a plate and cool completely. divide the dough into 12. roll each into a 12cm square about 2mm thick, keeping the rest covered. put 1.5 tbsp of filling on one half of each square, brush the edges with water, fold into a rectangle and press the edges firmly, then crimp with a fork. heat the frying oil to 160c. it should be moderate, not fierce: a scrap of dough should rise slowly over 4-5 seconds. fry 4 at a time for 6-7 minutes, turning once, until pale biscuit-gold and blistered. drain on a rack. serve hot with sliced onion and lemon.

entries.title: Marag
entries.snippet: thin white mutton soup enriched with cashew and yogurt, drunk before a biryani
entries.text: marag hyderabadi thin white mutton soup enriched with cashew and yogurt, drunk before a biryani gluten-free healthier mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi cashews almonds poppy seeds (khus khus) onion ginger garlic green chilli black pepper green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf mace (javitri) mint coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime ghee cream water salt heat the ghee in a pressure cooker and add the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf and mace. let them puff for 30 seconds. add the sliced onion and cook 8 minutes until soft and pale gold — stop before it browns, or the broth loses its whiteness. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the slit green chillies and cook 1 minute. add the mutton and sear on high for 5 minutes until the outside is sealed and no pink shows. take the pot off the heat, wait a minute, then fold in the whisked yogurt in three additions, stirring continuously. return to a low flame and cook 5 minutes until the yogurt tightens around the meat and no longer smells raw. add the water, salt and half the mint. pressure cook for 5 whistles, about 25 minutes, and let the pressure fall on its own. open, and stir in the ground cashew and almond paste. simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the broth thickens just enough to coat a spoon. add the crushed black pepper and the cream, if using, and simmer 3 minutes more. marag should stay drinkable, not stew-thick; loosen with hot water if needed. finish with the remaining mint and the coriander leaves, and serve in cups with lemon wedges to squeeze in.

entries.title: Methi Murgh
entries.snippet: chicken braised with fresh fenugreek, bitter-sweet and thick rather than soupy
entries.text: methi murgh hyderabadi chicken braised with fresh fenugreek, bitter-sweet and thick rather than soupy gluten-free nut-free healthier chicken fenugreek leaves (methi) onion yogurt / dahi ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) neutral oil ghee coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the sliced onion over medium heat until evenly golden brown, 12-14 minutes. add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes and the oil looks clear at the edges. add the chicken and green chillies and sear over high heat 5 minutes, until the pieces are opaque all over. lower the heat, stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powders with 2 tbsp water, and fry 3 minutes until the oil separates. take the pan off the heat for 30 seconds, whisk in the yogurt a spoonful at a time, then return to low heat and cook 5 minutes. fold in the squeezed methi leaves and salt, and cook uncovered 8 minutes, until the leaves collapse and darken. cover and simmer on low 12 minutes, stirring twice, until the chicken is tender and the gravy clings to the pieces. uncover and cook off any watery liquid over medium heat, 3-4 minutes. methi murgh should be thick enough to scoop, not ladle. sprinkle over the garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, spoon on the ghee, and rest covered 5 minutes off the heat. finish with coriander leaves and lemon juice, and serve with rumali roti or plain rice.

entries.title: Mirchi ka Salan
entries.snippet: long green chillies in a thick peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy
entries.text: mirchi ka salan hyderabadi long green chillies in a thick peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free green chilli peanuts sesame seeds dried coconut (copra) tamarind onion ginger garlic cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) nigella seeds (kalonji) curry leaves turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder jaggery neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the peanuts in a kadhai over medium heat for 5 minutes until the skins blister and loosen, then rub off the skins in a cloth. roast the sesame in the same pan for 1 minute until it pops, then the dried coconut for 1 minute until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. cool completely. grind the peanuts, sesame and coconut with 150ml water to a fine, smooth paste. set aside. heat 3 tbsp of the oil and fry the slit chillies for 2-3 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and go khaki. lift them out and reserve. in the same oil, fry the chopped onion until soft and light brown, about 8 minutes, then cool and grind to a paste. add the rest of the oil to the pan and crackle the cumin, mustard, fenugreek and nigella, then throw in the curry leaves. add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 1 minute until the raw smell goes, then the onion paste, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder. cook 3 minutes. stir in the ground peanut-sesame paste and fry on medium-low for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the mixture darkens and oil rises around the edges. pour in the tamarind water and the remaining water, add salt and the jaggery, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes until glossy and the thickness of pouring cream. slide the fried chillies back in, cover and simmer 5 minutes more, then rest off the heat 10 minutes and scatter with coriander leaves.

entries.title: Murgh do Pyaza
entries.snippet: chicken cooked with onions twice over, once browned to a paste and once in chunks
entries.text: murgh do pyaza hyderabadi chicken cooked with onions twice over, once browned to a paste and once in chunks gluten-free nut-free healthier chicken onion yogurt / dahi ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala black pepper cinnamon cloves green cardamom bay leaf neutral oil mint coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water heat 3 tbsp oil and fry the sliced onions over medium heat for 12-14 minutes until evenly deep brown. lift out half and reserve for the finish. cool the remaining browned onions and grind to a paste with a splash of water. in the same pan, add the whole spices — cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf — and let them puff for 30 seconds. add the remaining ginger and garlic pastes and cook 1 minute until the raw edge disappears. add the marinated chicken and sear on high for 6 minutes, turning, until the yogurt has tightened around the pieces and the base looks dry. stir in the browned onion paste, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder. fry on medium for 6-8 minutes until oil separates at the sides. pour in the water, add the green chillies, cover and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken is tender and pulling from the bone. heat the last 2 tbsp oil in a separate pan and sear the onion petals on high for 3 minutes until charred at the edges but still crunchy inside. fold the seared petals, the reserved browned onions, garam masala and black pepper into the curry and cook uncovered 3 minutes to thicken. take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, mint and coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving with roti.

entries.title: Mutton Do Pyaza
entries.snippet: mutton with onion twice over, once melted into the gravy and once in soft wedges
entries.text: mutton do pyaza hyderabadi mutton with onion twice over, once melted into the gravy and once in soft wedges gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb onion yogurt / dahi tomato ginger garlic green chilli red chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the oil in a pressure cooker and crackle the cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds, until fragrant. add the sliced onion and fry over medium heat until deep golden brown, 14 minutes. this lot is meant to disappear into the gravy. tip in the marinated mutton and sear over high heat 6 minutes, until the pieces have coloured and the yogurt has dried onto them. add the chilli powder, coriander and cumin powders and fry 3 minutes, until the oil separates and the masala smells toasted rather than raw. add the tomatoes and green chillies and cook 5 minutes, until the tomatoes break down completely. pour in 250ml water, close the cooker and cook on high for 5 whistles, then on low for 10 minutes. let the pressure drop on its own. open up, taste for salt, and boil uncovered 5 minutes to reduce the gravy to a coating consistency. in a separate pan, fry the onion petals in 1 tbsp of the oil skimmed from the curry over high heat, 3 minutes, until browned at the edges but still firm. fold the petals into the curry, sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest off the heat 5 minutes. scatter with coriander leaves and serve with roti or khatti dal and rice.

entries.title: Patthar Ka Gosht
entries.snippet: thin mutton slices seared hard and fast, smoky at the edges and still juicy
entries.text: patthar ka gosht hyderabadi thin mutton slices seared hard and fast, smoky at the edges and still juicy gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb raw green papaya yogurt / dahi ginger garlic green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) mint black pepper garam masala cumin powder (jeera) red chilli powder lemon / lime ghee salt grind the green chillies, coriander leaves and mint with 1 tbsp water to a coarse green paste. mix the papaya paste, yogurt, ginger and garlic pastes, green paste, pepper, garam masala, cumin, chilli powder, juice of half a lemon and salt. coat the flattened mutton slices in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate 2 hours. heat a heavy tawa or cast-iron griddle over high heat for a full 5 minutes, until a drop of water skitters and vanishes. brush the griddle with ghee and lay on the slices in a single layer, shaking off excess marinade. do not crowd the pan. sear 2 minutes without moving them, until the underside is browned and lifts cleanly. flip, dot with a little more ghee, and cook 2 minutes more. the slices should feel springy, not firm. move the cooked slices to a warm plate and repeat with the rest, wiping the griddle between batches. rest 3 minutes, then squeeze over the remaining lemon and serve hot with sliced onion and mint chutney.

entries.title: Qubani ka Meetha
entries.snippet: Dried apricots stewed to a glossy compote, served with cream and blanched kernels
entries.text: qubani ka meetha hyderabadi dried apricots stewed to a glossy compote, served with cream and blanched kernels vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free dried apricots (khubani) sugar green cardamom lemon / lime cream almonds water soak the apricots in water overnight until plump. keep the soaking water. pit them, reserving the stones. crack the stones and blanch the kernels; the skins slip off. simmer the fruit in its soaking water with the sugar and cardamom over low heat, 30-40 minutes, until it collapses into a thick glossy compote. sharpen with lemon if the apricots were very sweet. cool. serve at room temperature or chilled, topped with cream and the blanched kernels.

entries.title: Sheer Khurma
entries.snippet: eid morning milk pudding heavy with dates, roasted vermicelli and nuts
entries.text: sheer khurma hyderabadi eid morning milk pudding heavy with dates, roasted vermicelli and nuts vegetarian milk vermicelli (semiya) dates dried apricots (khubani) sugar ghee almonds pistachios cashews raisins (kishmish) khoya / mawa green cardamom saffron rose water melt the ghee in a heavy pan and fry the almonds, pistachios and cashews for 2 minutes until golden. lift them out with a slotted spoon. add the raisins to the same ghee and fry 20 seconds until they swell and turn glossy, then remove. add the broken vermicelli to the remaining ghee and roast on low for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until evenly reddish-brown and fragrant. pour in the milk and bring to a gentle boil, stirring to keep the vermicelli from clumping on the base. simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until the milk has reduced by about a quarter and coats the spoon. add the sugar and stir until fully dissolved, about 2 minutes. stir in the soaked dates with their milk, the apricots and the grated khoya. simmer 5 minutes until the khoya melts in with no lumps. add the saffron milk and crushed cardamom and cook 2 minutes more; the pudding should be pourable, a little looser than you want it. take off the heat, stir in the rose water, and fold through most of the fried nuts and raisins. rest 10 minutes and serve warm in small bowls, scattered with the remaining nuts. it is equally good chilled.

entries.title: Shikampuri Kebab
entries.snippet: soft mince patties with a cool hung-curd filling hidden inside
entries.text: shikampuri kebab hyderabadi soft mince patties with a cool hung-curd filling hidden inside gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb chana dal yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic green chilli mint coriander leaves (cilantro) black pepper garam masala cumin seeds green cardamom cloves cinnamon dried red chillies lemon / lime ghee salt put the mince, drained chana dal, sliced onion, ginger and garlic pastes, dried red chillies, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, cumin seeds, salt and 250ml water in a pan. bring to a boil, then simmer covered 30 minutes, until the dal is soft and the mince is cooked through. uncover and cook over medium heat, stirring, until every trace of liquid has gone and the mixture squeaks against the pan, about 8 minutes. cool completely. grind the cooled mixture to a smooth, stiff paste with no added water. mix in the black pepper, garam masala and lemon juice, and check the salt. make the filling: mash the hung curd with the finely chopped raw onion, green chillies, mint, coriander and a pinch of salt. divide the mince into 12. flatten a portion in your palm, place a teaspoon of filling in the centre, and draw the edges over to seal completely. press gently into a disc 6cm across and 1.5cm thick. repeat with the rest and chill 30 minutes. heat 2 tbsp ghee on a tawa over medium-low heat and fry the kebabs in batches, 3 minutes a side, until deep brown and crusted. drain briefly on paper and serve hot with onion rings and lemon.

entries.title: Tala Hua Gosht
entries.snippet: mutton boiled tender then fried dry with black pepper until the masala clings
entries.text: tala hua gosht hyderabadi mutton boiled tender then fried dry with black pepper until the masala clings gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb onion ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala black pepper curry leaves cinnamon cloves green cardamom lemon / lime neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) pressure cook the marinated mutton with 1 sliced onion, the whole spices and 400ml water for 5 whistles, about 25 minutes. let the pressure fall naturally, then check: the meat should give completely to a fork. if not, cook 5 minutes more. strain, keeping the stock. boil the stock down separately to about 100ml of concentrated liquid. heat the oil in a wide kadhai and fry the remaining sliced onions for 10 minutes until deep golden brown. add the green chillies and curry leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds. add the coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 30 seconds, then tip in the drained mutton pieces. fry on medium-high for 12-15 minutes, turning the pieces every couple of minutes, until they are browned on all sides and the masala has dried onto them. pour in the reduced stock a spoon at a time, letting each addition dry off before adding the next, until the pan is dry and glossy. add the crushed black pepper and garam masala and toss for 2 minutes off the direct heat. finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves and serve with roti or bagara khana.

entries.title: Til Ki Chutney
entries.snippet: toasted sesame and coconut ground with tamarind into a thick, nutty relish
entries.text: til ki chutney hyderabadi toasted sesame and coconut ground with tamarind into a thick, nutty relish vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free sesame seeds dried coconut (copra) dried red chillies tamarind garlic cumin seeds coriander leaves (cilantro) curry leaves mustard seeds neutral oil water salt dry-toast the sesame over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, 3-4 minutes, until the seeds turn one shade darker and start popping. in the same pan, toast the grated dried coconut 1 minute, until fragrant and just golden. set aside. add 1 tsp of the oil and fry the dried red chillies, garlic and cumin over medium heat 1 minute, until the chillies darken slightly. cool all the toasted ingredients completely, about 10 minutes. grind the sesame alone first to a coarse powder, then add the coconut, chillies, garlic, cumin, soaked tamarind with its water and salt. grind to a thick paste, adding the water 1 tbsp at a time. stop while it still has a little grain — this is a chutney, not a puree. heat the remaining oil, pop the mustard seeds and crisp the curry leaves, 20 seconds, and pour over the chutney. fold in the coriander leaves and serve with rice and ghee, or as a side to biryani.

entries.title: Tomato Kut
entries.snippet: thick sour-hot tomato gravy thickened with gram flour and eggs poached in it
entries.text: tomato kut hyderabadi thick sour-hot tomato gravy thickened with gram flour and eggs poached in it vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier tomato besan (gram flour) eggs tamarind garlic green chilli curry leaves dried red chillies cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder asafoetida (hing) neutral oil water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) simmer the tomatoes with 350ml water and the turmeric for 15 minutes until completely collapsed and pulpy. cool slightly, blend smooth, then push through a sieve to leave the skins and seeds behind. heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pan, crackle the mustard, cumin and fenugreek, then add the curry leaves, dried red chillies and green chillies. add the crushed garlic and fry 1 minute until it smells sweet and turns pale gold, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the asafoetida. return to the heat, add the chilli powder and coriander powder, and fry 20 seconds before pouring in the sieved tomato. whisk the standing besan slurry once more and pour it in slowly, stirring constantly. simmer 12 minutes until the gravy is thick, glossy and no longer tastes of raw flour. add the tamarind water and salt and simmer 5 minutes more; it should be thick enough to hold a channel behind the spoon. crack the eggs one at a time onto the surface, spacing them apart. cover and poach on low for 6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft. heat the last 2 tbsp oil, sizzle a few extra curry leaves in it, and pour it over the top. scatter with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Akki Rotti
entries.snippet: rice-flour flatbread patted straight onto the tawa with onion, dill and coconut
entries.text: akki rotti karnataka rice-flour flatbread patted straight onto the tawa with onion, dill and coconut vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour onion carrot dill (suva) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli curry leaves cumin seeds coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water coconut oil combine the rice flour, onion, carrot, dill, coconut, green chilli, curry leaves, cumin and salt in a wide bowl and rub together with your fingers for a minute. add hot water a little at a time, mixing to a soft dough just past the point of stickiness — softer than a chapati dough. smear 1/2 tbsp coconut oil over a cold tawa and place a lemon-sized ball of dough in the centre. with wet fingers, pat the dough outward into a thin 8-inch round with an even edge. make 3 small holes in it with your finger. drizzle a few drops of oil into the holes, cover with a lid and set the tawa over medium heat. cook covered 4 minutes until the surface loses its wet sheen and brown spots appear underneath. uncover, loosen the edges with a spatula, flip and cook 2 minutes more until crisp and golden in patches. slide off and repeat, letting the tawa cool for a minute under running water before patting the next one.

entries.title: Badanekayi Ennegayi
entries.snippet: small eggplants stuffed with a dark peanut-sesame masala and stewed in tamarind
entries.text: badanekayi ennegayi karnataka small eggplants stuffed with a dark peanut-sesame masala and stewed in tamarind vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier eggplant / brinjal peanuts sesame seeds dried coconut (copra) dried red chillies coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder jaggery tamarind onion garlic groundnut oil mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water dry-roast the peanuts over medium heat 5 minutes until the skins blister and loosen, then rub off the skins in a cloth. in the same pan roast the sesame 1 minute until it pops, then the dried coconut 2 minutes until sandy brown, then the red chillies 30 seconds. grind the roasted peanut, sesame, coconut and chillies with the garlic, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, jaggery, 2 tbsp of the tamarind pulp and 1 tsp salt to a thick, coarse paste using splashes of water. drain and pat the eggplants dry, then push a heaped teaspoon of the masala into each one, working it into all four slits. reserve the leftover masala. heat the groundnut oil in a kadhai, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves and hing. add the onion and fry 6 minutes until soft and pale gold at the edges. lay the stuffed eggplants in a single layer, cover and cook 8 minutes on low, turning them gently twice so each side takes colour. stir the reserved masala and the remaining tamarind pulp into 1 cup water and pour it around, not over, the eggplants. cover and simmer 15 minutes on low until the eggplants are collapsing-soft when pressed and the gravy has darkened and thickened, with oil pooling at the edges. taste for salt and sour, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with jolada rotti.

entries.title: Hesarubele Payasa
entries.snippet: soft moong dal pudding sweetened with jaggery and finished in coconut milk
entries.text: hesarubele payasa karnataka soft moong dal pudding sweetened with jaggery and finished in coconut milk vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic moong dal jaggery coconut milk ghee green cardamom cashews raisins (kishmish) dried coconut (copra) water salt dry-roast the moong dal over medium heat 4 minutes, stirring, until it is a shade darker and smells like roasted nuts. rinse the roasted dal, then pressure-cook it with 2 cups water for 3 whistles, or simmer covered 25 minutes, until completely soft and mashable. mash the cooked dal lightly against the side of the pot, leaving some texture, and keep it on low heat. melt the grated jaggery with 1/4 cup water in a separate pan over low heat, then strain it through a fine sieve into the dal. simmer the dal and jaggery together 8 minutes, stirring, until the mixture thickens and takes on a glossy amber colour. take the pot off the heat and stir in the coconut milk, crushed cardamom and the pinch of salt. return to the very lowest heat for 2 minutes to warm through, without letting it bubble. heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cashews 1 minute until golden, then the coconut slices 30 seconds, then the raisins until they swell. pour the ghee and its fried garnish over the payasa, stir once and serve warm.

entries.title: Jolada Rotti
entries.snippet: thin unleavened jowar bread from north Karnataka, dry-toasted until it puffs
entries.text: jolada rotti karnataka thin unleavened jowar bread from north karnataka, dry-toasted until it puffs vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic jowar (sorghum) flour water salt boil the water with the salt. tip in the jowar flour all at once and stir with a wooden spoon until no dry flour remains. cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat so the flour drinks the water. turn out while still warm and knead 6 to 8 minutes with the heel of your hand until the dough is smooth, warm and slightly tacky, not crumbly. divide into 8 balls and keep them under a damp cloth. dust the work surface generously with dry jowar flour. flatten one ball and pat it outward with flat fingertips, rotating as you go, into a 7-inch round about 2mm thick. brush the excess flour off the round and lift it onto a hot tawa over medium heat. cook 40 seconds until the surface dulls, then flip. wipe a wet hand lightly over the top surface. cook the second side 1 minute, then lift the rotti onto a direct flame or press it with a cloth on the tawa until it puffs into a dome, about 20 seconds. stack the finished rottis in a cloth-lined basket and repeat with the rest.

entries.title: Koli Saaru
entries.snippet: peppery kannadiga chicken curry in a roasted coconut and poppy seed gravy
entries.text: koli saaru karnataka peppery kannadiga chicken curry in a roasted coconut and poppy seed gravy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken onion tomato coconut (fresh or desiccated) poppy seeds (khus khus) dried red chillies black pepper coriander powder cumin seeds cinnamon cloves garlic ginger turmeric powder curry leaves coconut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water heat 1 tbsp of the coconut oil and fry the sliced onion 6 minutes until browned at the edges. set aside. in the same pan roast the red chillies, black pepper, cumin, cinnamon and cloves 1 minute until they smell sharp, then add the poppy seeds for 30 seconds. add the grated coconut and roast 4 minutes over medium-low, stirring constantly, until it turns an even golden brown and smells toasted. cool, then grind the roasted spices, coconut, browned onion, garlic, ginger and coriander powder with 3/4 cup water to a very smooth dark paste. heat the remaining 3 tbsp coconut oil in a kadhai, add the curry leaves and the chopped onion and fry 8 minutes until soft and deep gold. add the tomato and remaining turmeric and cook 5 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil beads at the edges. add the chicken and fry on high 6 minutes, turning the pieces, until they are opaque all over and lightly seared. stir in the ground masala and cook 6 minutes on medium, scraping the base, until it darkens by a shade and the oil separates. pour in 1 1/4 cups hot water and salt to taste, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 20 minutes on low until the chicken is falling off the bone and the gravy is the thickness of pouring cream. finish with the lemon juice and coriander leaves, rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with ragi mudde or akki rotti.

entries.title: Kosambari
entries.snippet: crunchy soaked moong dal salad with cucumber, coconut and lemon
entries.text: kosambari karnataka crunchy soaked moong dal salad with cucumber, coconut and lemon vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier moong dal cucumber carrot coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) coconut oil mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) salt drain the soaked moong dal thoroughly and spread it on a cloth for 5 minutes to shed surface water. tip it into a wide bowl with the drained cucumber, grated carrot, coconut, green chilli and coriander leaves. heat the coconut oil in a small pan until it shimmers, add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, about 30 seconds. add the curry leaves and hing, swirl for 10 seconds until the leaves go crisp, then take the pan off the heat. pour the tempering over the salad and fold it through. just before serving, add the lemon juice and salt to taste and toss once more.

entries.title: Maddur Vada
entries.snippet: flat, shatteringly crisp onion fritters from the railway platform at maddur
entries.text: maddur vada karnataka flat, shatteringly crisp onion fritters from the railway platform at maddur vegetarian nut-free rice flour rava / sooji (semolina) plain flour (maida) onion green chilli curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) ghee neutral oil salt water combine the rice flour, rava, maida, salt, hing and cumin in a wide bowl. pour over the hot ghee and rub it through the flour with your fingertips for a minute, until the mix holds its shape when squeezed in a fist. add the onion, green chilli, curry leaves and coriander leaves and mix with your hands, crushing the onion slightly. add water a tablespoon at a time to a stiff, barely-together dough. it should be firmer than a chapati dough. heat the oil in a kadhai to medium — a pinch of dough should rise steadily in about 5 seconds, not shoot to the surface. take a lime-sized ball, place it on an oiled sheet of plastic or a wet palm, and press it flat into a thin 9cm disc. peel it off and slide it into the oil. fry 3 to 4 vadas at a time for 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the bubbling has almost stopped. lift onto paper and repeat with the rest, letting the oil come back to temperature between batches. serve hot with coconut chutney and filter coffee.

entries.title: Majjige Huli
entries.snippet: gentle udupi buttermilk curry with ash gourd in a coconut-cumin paste
entries.text: majjige huli karnataka gentle udupi buttermilk curry with ash gourd in a coconut-cumin paste vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier ash gourd (petha) yogurt / dahi coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds toor dal (pigeon pea) turmeric powder coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water simmer the ash gourd with the turmeric, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water for 10 minutes until a knife slides through but the cubes still hold shape. meanwhile grind the coconut, green chillies, cumin seeds and drained toor dal with 1/2 cup water to a very smooth, thick paste. stir the paste into the cooked gourd and simmer 5 minutes on medium, stirring often, until the raw coconut smell is gone and the gravy coats the spoon. take the pot off the heat and let it stop bubbling, about 2 minutes. pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring continuously, then return to the lowest heat. warm through 3 minutes without letting it boil — the surface should barely tremble. check the salt. heat the coconut oil in a small pan, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and hing and fry 10 seconds. pour the tempering over the curry, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot with plain rice.

entries.title: Ragi Mudde
entries.snippet: smooth finger-millet balls, the everyday staple of the southern Karnataka plate
entries.text: ragi mudde karnataka smooth finger-millet balls, the everyday staple of the southern karnataka plate vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic ragi (finger millet) flour water salt bring 4 cups water to a hard rolling boil with the salt in a heavy-bottomed pot. stir in the cold ragi slurry and let it boil 3 minutes until the water turns opaque brown and thickens slightly. lower the heat to minimum and tip in the remaining ragi flour all at once, in a mound in the centre. do not stir. cover and let it steam 5 minutes — the mound cooks through from the sides in. uncover and beat hard with the wooden spatula, pressing the dough against the side of the pot, for 4 to 5 minutes until it is one glossy, uniform mass with no pale flecks. cook another 3 minutes on low, folding the mass over itself, until it pulls cleanly away from the pot. wet your hands in the cold water, scoop out a fistful and roll it into a smooth ball the size of a small orange. serve immediately with hot saaru or bassaru, swallowing the pieces rather than chewing them.

entries.title: Vangi Bath
entries.snippet: mysore-style eggplant rice with a roasted coconut and stone-flower masala
entries.text: vangi bath karnataka mysore-style eggplant rice with a roasted coconut and stone-flower masala vegetarian gluten-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) eggplant / brinjal onion dried red chillies chana dal urad dal (black gram) coriander powder dried coconut (copra) sesame seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) cinnamon cloves stone flower (dagad phool) tamarind jaggery turmeric powder ghee groundnut oil mustard seeds peanuts curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the chana dal and urad dal over medium heat 4 minutes until reddish gold and fragrant, then tip onto a plate. in the same pan roast the red chillies, cinnamon, cloves and stone flower 1 minute, then the sesame and poppy seeds 30 seconds, then the dried coconut 2 minutes until sandy brown. cool completely, add the coriander powder and grind everything to a fine powder. you should have about 6 tbsp of vangi bath masala. heat the groundnut oil and 1 tbsp of the ghee in a kadhai. crackle the mustard seeds, add the peanuts and fry 2 minutes until they colour. add the curry leaves and sliced onion and fry 5 minutes until the onion is translucent and just catching gold. add the drained eggplant batons and the turmeric, toss to coat, then cover and cook 8 minutes on medium, stirring twice, until the flesh is tender and the skin blistered. stir in the tamarind pulp, jaggery, 1 tsp salt and 4 tbsp of the ground masala. simmer 6 minutes until the mixture is thick, glossy and pulling away from the sides. fold in the cooled rice a third at a time, lifting rather than stirring, until every grain is evenly coloured. drizzle over the remaining 2 tbsp ghee, cover and let it sit on the lowest heat 5 minutes. check the salt and sour, scatter the coriander leaves and serve warm with plain yogurt.

entries.title: Aab Gosht
entries.snippet: mutton chops poached in fennel-scented milk, pale and delicate
entries.text: aab gosht kashmiri mutton chops poached in fennel-scented milk, pale and delicate gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb milk ghee garlic fennel seeds (saunf) fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom black cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf white pepper water salt bring the chops, water, garlic, bay leaf, both cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, the muslin bag of fennel seeds and 1 tsp salt to a boil, then skim off the foam. simmer covered 45 minutes, until the meat is tender and pulling from the bone, then uncover and boil the liquid down to about 150ml. remove the muslin bag and squeeze it out into the pan. add the milk in three additions, letting each come back to a bare simmer before the next goes in. stir in the fennel powder, dry ginger and white pepper. simmer uncovered on low for 25 minutes, stirring the base every few minutes with a flat spoon, until the gravy thinly coats the back of it. heat the ghee separately until it is nut-brown and pour it over the pan, giving it one stir. check the salt, rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with plain rice or with a girda.

entries.title: Al Yakhni
entries.snippet: bottle gourd simmered in a pale, fennel-scented yogurt gravy
entries.text: al yakhni kashmiri bottle gourd simmered in a pale, fennel-scented yogurt gravy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic bottle gourd (lauki) yogurt / dahi ghee fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) green cardamom cloves bay leaf kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) black pepper salt water whisk the fennel powder, dry ginger powder and salt into the yogurt and keep it beside the stove. heat the ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat and add the cardamom, cloves and bay leaf; they should sizzle and perfume the fat within 20 seconds. add the asafoetida, count to three, then add the bottle gourd batons. turn the gourd in the ghee for 4 minutes until the edges look glassy. lower the heat right down, pour in the spiced yogurt and stir continuously in one direction until it comes to a bare simmer, about 5 minutes. add the water, bring back to a simmer and cook uncovered for 12 minutes, until the gourd is tender but still holds its shape. crush the kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and add the black pepper. simmer 3 minutes more until the gravy coats the back of a spoon thinly, then taste for salt. rest off the heat for 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Chaman Qaliya
entries.snippet: fried paneer in a thin turmeric-yellow gravy, mild and milky
entries.text: chaman qaliya kashmiri fried paneer in a thin turmeric-yellow gravy, mild and milky vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic paneer mustard oil milk water turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf black pepper ghee salt heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, then take it off the flame for 30 seconds to settle. fry the paneer in batches over medium heat, 2 minutes a side, to a pale gold — no darker. slip each fried piece into the warm salted water and leave it there while you make the gravy. pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil, add the hing, bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and cardamom and let them crackle for 20 seconds. off the heat, stir in the turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger. add the water and 1 tsp salt, bring to a boil and let it bubble 5 minutes so the spices lose their raw edge. lower the heat, pour in the milk and let it come back to a bare simmer. drain the paneer and slide it in. simmer 8 minutes, until the gravy is the thickness of pouring cream and pale yellow. finish with the black pepper and the spoon of ghee, and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Choek Wangun
entries.snippet: fried aubergine in a sharp tamarind gravy, sour before it is hot
entries.text: choek wangun kashmiri fried aubergine in a sharp tamarind gravy, sour before it is hot vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic eggplant / brinjal mustard oil tamarind kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) cumin seeds jaggery water salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then drop the flame to medium. fry the aubergine quarters in batches, 4 minutes a side, until the skin is blistered and the flesh is collapsing. lift out onto paper. pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil, add the cumin seeds and let them crackle for 15 seconds. add the hing, wait 10 seconds for it to foam, then take the pan off the heat. stir in the chilli powder, turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger off the flame for 20 seconds. return to low heat, add the water, tamarind pulp, jaggery and 1 tsp salt, and simmer 6 minutes until the gravy darkens and thickens slightly. slide the fried aubergine back in and simmer uncovered 6 minutes, spooning gravy over rather than stirring. rest 10 minutes off the heat — it is better warm than hot — and serve with rice.

entries.title: Gushtaba
entries.snippet: pounded mutton meatballs poached in a white yogurt gravy, the closing course of wazwan
entries.text: gushtaba kashmiri pounded mutton meatballs poached in a white yogurt gravy, the closing course of wazwan gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb shallots (small red onions) yogurt / dahi ghee fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom black cardamom cloves cinnamon black pepper mint baking soda milk water salt work the mince with 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp of the fennel powder, 1/2 tsp dry ginger, the ground green cardamom, black pepper, baking soda and 1 tsp salt for a full 10 minutes, until it turns pale, tacky and springy. chill the mix 20 minutes, then wet your palms and roll 8 balls the size of a small orange, smoothing away every crack. heat the remaining ghee in a wide pan and cook the shallot on low for 6 minutes until soft and translucent. add the black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon, then the remaining fennel powder and dry ginger, and stir for 30 seconds. off the heat, whisk in the yogurt and the water, then return to a low flame and stir constantly until it reaches a bare simmer, about 8 minutes. slide the meatballs in one at a time. do not stir for the first 10 minutes — swirl the pan by its handle instead. simmer uncovered on low for 40 minutes, spooning gravy over the balls now and then, until they are firm and the gravy is the thickness of single cream. stir in the milk and crushed mint, season, and give it 5 minutes more. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve one gushtaba per person with plain rice.

entries.title: Haak
entries.snippet: kashmiri greens boiled whole in mustard oil, chilli and hing, served in their own broth
entries.text: haak kashmiri kashmiri greens boiled whole in mustard oil, chilli and hing, served in their own broth vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic mustard greens (sarson) mustard oil green chilli asafoetida (hing) water dry ginger powder (saunth) baking soda salt heat the mustard oil in a wide pan until it just begins to smoke, then take it off the heat for 20 seconds. add the hing and the slit chillies and let them sizzle for 15 seconds. pour in the water, add the salt and dry ginger, and bring to a hard boil. push the leaves in a handful at a time, letting each batch wilt before the next goes in, about 2 minutes in all. boil uncovered on high for 12 minutes, stirring twice, until the leaves are tender but still hold their shape. stir in the baking soda if using, and taste — the broth should be well salted, since it is eaten with rice. serve immediately in a deep bowl with plenty of its broth, alongside plain rice.

entries.title: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
entries.snippet: Fried baby potatoes finished in a yogurt gravy with fennel and dry ginger, no onion or garlic
entries.text: kashmiri dum aloo kashmiri fried baby potatoes finished in a yogurt gravy with fennel and dry ginger, no onion or garlic vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato yogurt / dahi kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) green cardamom black cardamom cinnamon cloves asafoetida (hing) ghee neutral oil salt fry the pricked potatoes in hot oil until deep golden and crusted all over, 8-10 minutes. drain. they should be cooked through but firm. whisk the yogurt with the kashmiri chilli, fennel powder and dry ginger until there are no lumps. keep it beside the stove. heat the ghee in a heavy pan, add the asafoetida, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, and let them bloom for 20 seconds. take the pan off the heat. pour in the yogurt mixture, stirring without stopping. return to low heat and keep stirring until it comes to a bare simmer and thickens slightly, about 5 minutes. add the potatoes and salt with about half a cup of hot water. cover tightly and cook on the lowest possible heat for 15-20 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally. uncover; the gravy should cling to the potatoes and the fat should show at the edges. rest 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Kashmiri Pulav
entries.snippet: Mildly sweet saffron rice with fruit and nuts, served alongside the wazwan
entries.text: kashmiri pulav kashmiri mildly sweet saffron rice with fruit and nuts, served alongside the wazwan vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice milk saffron green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf fennel powder almonds cashews raisins (kishmish) pomegranate sugar ghee salt warm the milk and steep the saffron in it. fry the nuts and raisins in ghee until the nuts colour and the raisins puff. lift out and reserve. in the same ghee, bloom the whole spices, then add the drained rice and turn it gently for 2 minutes. add the saffron milk, 2.5 cups water, sugar and salt. bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat 12 minutes. rest, covered and off the heat, a further 10 minutes before lifting the lid. fork through the fried nuts and raisins and scatter pomegranate over the top.

entries.title: Kashmiri Rajma
entries.snippet: small dark kidney beans simmered with fennel and dry ginger, without an onion in sight
entries.text: kashmiri rajma kashmiri small dark kidney beans simmered with fennel and dry ginger, without an onion in sight vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier rajma (kidney beans) mustard oil kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder black cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf garam masala water salt boil the drained beans in the water with the bay leaf, black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon. simmer covered 60 minutes, or pressure-cook 20 minutes at full pressure, until a bean crushes to paste between finger and thumb. heat the mustard oil in a second pan until it just smokes, then lower the flame. add the hing and let it foam for 10 seconds. off the heat, stir in the chilli paste, turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger, then return to low heat and fry for 2 minutes until the oil separates at the edges. pour the tempering into the beans along with their cooking liquid and add salt to taste. crush a ladleful of the beans against the side of the pot and stir them back in to thicken the gravy. simmer uncovered 15 minutes, until the gravy is red-brown and coats the beans rather than pooling around them. stir in the garam masala, rest 5 minutes and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Marchwangan Korma
entries.snippet: fiery wazwan mutton stained deep red with kashmiri chilli
entries.text: marchwangan korma kashmiri fiery wazwan mutton stained deep red with kashmiri chilli gluten-free nut-free mutton / lamb kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder mustard oil shallots (small red onions) garlic ginger yogurt / dahi fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) cloves black cardamom cinnamon bay leaf garam masala ghee salt water heat the mustard oil until it stops smoking and the sharp raw smell fades, about 3 minutes, then let it cool for 30 seconds. fry the whole shallots in the hot oil until they collapse and turn a soft brown, 6 to 7 minutes, then lift them out and set aside. slide in the mutton with the cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf and sear over high heat until the pieces are browned all over, about 10 minutes. add the crushed garlic and ginger and fry for 2 minutes until the raw edge is gone. pull the pan off the heat, wait a minute, then stir in the whisked yogurt in three additions, stirring constantly in one direction as it comes back to a bare simmer. stir in the chilli paste, fennel powder, dry ginger powder and salt and fry over medium heat until the oil separates and floats red on the surface, 8 to 10 minutes. return the fried shallots, pour in the hot water and bring to a simmer. pressure cook for 4 whistles and rest until the pressure drops on its own, or cover and simmer on the lowest flame for 60 minutes until the meat pulls from the bone. uncover and reduce over medium heat until the gravy clings to the meat and a slick of red oil pools on top, about 10 minutes. sprinkle over the garam masala, swirl in the ghee and stand covered for 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Methi Maaz
entries.snippet: slow-cooked mutton dried down with fenugreek leaves until dark and crumbly
entries.text: methi maaz kashmiri slow-cooked mutton dried down with fenugreek leaves until dark and crumbly gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier mutton / lamb fenugreek leaves (methi) mustard oil asafoetida (hing) fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder cloves green chilli salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then take it off the flame for 30 seconds. drop in the asafoetida and cloves; the hing will foam and smell nutty within 5 seconds. add the mutton at once and fry over high heat, stirring, until the pieces are browned and the pan is dry, about 12 minutes. lower the heat, add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, fennel powder, dry ginger powder and salt and fry 2 minutes until the spices coat the meat and smell toasted. pour in the water, cover and simmer on the lowest flame for 35 minutes, until the mutton gives easily under a spoon. uncover, raise the heat and boil off nearly all the liquid, about 6 minutes, until only fat and a thick masala remain. stir in the squeezed fenugreek leaves and the green chillies and fry over medium heat for 10 minutes, scraping the base as they wilt and darken. cook another 5 minutes until the mixture looks dry and crumbly and the oil glistens at the edges, then taste for salt. stand covered for 5 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Modur Pulav
entries.snippet: sweet saffron rice with milk, ghee and dried fruit, made for pandit feast days
entries.text: modur pulav kashmiri sweet saffron rice with milk, ghee and dried fruit, made for pandit feast days vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice ghee milk water sugar saffron green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf almonds cashews raisins (kishmish) dried apricots (khubani) salt heat 3 tbsp of the ghee and fry the almonds and cashews until pale gold, about 90 seconds, then lift them out. fry the raisins in the same ghee for 15 seconds, until they puff up, and lift them out too. add the remaining ghee, then the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and bay leaf, and let them scent the fat for 30 seconds. tip in the drained rice and turn it gently for 2 minutes, until every grain is coated and looks glassy at the edges. pour in the water, milk, salt and the saffron milk, and bring to a boil. as soon as it boils, lower the flame to its minimum, cover tightly and cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid. uncover, scatter over the sugar, fried nuts, raisins and apricot, and fold through with two strokes. cover again and leave on the lowest heat for 5 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 before serving warm.

entries.title: Mujh Chetin
entries.snippet: cold grated radish and walnut relish sharpened with yogurt and green chilli
entries.text: mujh chetin kashmiri cold grated radish and walnut relish sharpened with yogurt and green chilli vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic radish (mooli) walnuts yogurt / dahi green chilli kashmiri chilli powder mustard oil salt water squeeze the salted radish hard between your palms and discard the liquid that runs out. blitz the walnuts and green chillies with the 2 tbsp water to a coarse, damp paste, stopping before it turns oily. tip the paste into a bowl and fold in the squeezed radish. whisk the yogurt separately until it is smooth and pourable, then fold it in a spoonful at a time. season with the remaining salt and taste; it should be sharp, nutty and only faintly hot. sprinkle over the kashmiri chilli and trickle the raw mustard oil across the surface without stirring it in. chill for 20 minutes before serving with tehar, rice or nadru monje.

entries.title: Muji Gaad
entries.snippet: winter fish and radish in a red chilli gravy, sour and warming
entries.text: muji gaad kashmiri winter fish and radish in a red chilli gravy, sour and warming pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) radish (mooli) mustard oil kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) water salt heat the mustard oil in a wide pan until it smokes, then lower the flame to medium. fry the fish steaks in a single layer, 3 minutes a side, until crusted and deep gold. lift them out and set aside. add the radish batons to the same oil and fry 5 minutes, until the edges brown and the sharp raw smell fades. add the hing and let it foam for 10 seconds. off the heat, stir in the chilli paste, remaining turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger. pour in the water, add 1 tsp salt, and simmer covered 12 minutes until the radish is tender and the gravy has turned deep red. return the fish, add the crushed anardana, and simmer uncovered 8 minutes, spooning gravy over rather than stirring. rest 5 minutes off the heat and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Mutton Yakhni
entries.snippet: pale yogurt and fennel mutton curry, aromatic rather than hot
entries.text: mutton yakhni kashmiri pale yogurt and fennel mutton curry, aromatic rather than hot gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi ghee fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mint black pepper water salt bring the mutton, water, bay leaves, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and 1 tsp salt to a boil, then skim off every bit of grey foam. cover and simmer 40 minutes, until the meat gives easily to a fork. lift the pieces out and keep the strained stock. heat the ghee in a heavy pan and add the hing — it foams and smells sharp for about 10 seconds. pull the pan off the heat and stir in the fennel powder and dry ginger for 20 seconds. return to a low flame, add the drained mutton and turn it in the spiced ghee for 3 minutes until every piece is glossy. take the pan off the heat again, pour in the whisked yogurt and stir without stopping for 2 minutes before setting it back on the lowest flame. add 450ml of the reserved stock, the crushed mint and the black pepper, and simmer uncovered 20 minutes until the gravy thinly coats a spoon. crush the green cardamom over the top, check the salt and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Nadru Monje
entries.snippet: crisp lotus stem fritters in a spiced gram and rice flour batter
entries.text: nadru monje kashmiri crisp lotus stem fritters in a spiced gram and rice flour batter vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic lotus stem (nadru/bhee) besan (gram flour) rice flour kashmiri chilli powder dry ginger powder (saunth) fennel powder asafoetida (hing) baking soda mustard oil salt water boil the lotus stem rounds in salted water for 8 minutes, until a knife tip goes in with slight resistance, then drain and spread out to dry completely. whisk the besan, rice flour, kashmiri chilli, dry ginger powder, fennel powder, asafoetida, baking soda and salt together. add the water a little at a time, whisking to a thick batter that coats the back of a spoon and drips slowly. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the heat and bring it back to about 180c — a drop of batter should rise and sizzle within 3 seconds. dip the rounds one by one into the batter, let the excess run off, and lower them into the oil in batches of six or seven. fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until the coating is set, deep gold and audibly crisp when tapped. lift onto a rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp, and salt them lightly while hot. repeat with the remaining rounds, letting the oil come back up to temperature between batches. serve immediately, with a bowl of mujh chetin alongside.

entries.title: Nadru Yakhni
entries.snippet: lotus stem rounds in a gentle fennel and yogurt gravy, the meatless yakhni
entries.text: nadru yakhni kashmiri lotus stem rounds in a gentle fennel and yogurt gravy, the meatless yakhni vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic lotus stem (nadru/bhee) yogurt / dahi ghee fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf mint black pepper water salt boil the rounds in the water with the bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and 1/2 tsp salt for 12 minutes, until a knife goes in with slight resistance. drain, keeping every drop of the cooking water. heat the ghee in a heavy pan and add the hing, letting it foam for 10 seconds. off the heat, stir in the fennel powder and dry ginger for 20 seconds. return to low heat, add the drained rounds and turn them for 3 minutes until coated. take the pan off the heat, pour in the yogurt and stir continuously for 2 minutes before setting it back on the lowest flame. add 350ml of the reserved cooking water, the cardamom, mint and black pepper, and simmer uncovered 15 minutes until the gravy just coats the rounds. check the salt and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Phirni
entries.snippet: chilled ground-rice pudding set in earthenware, scented with cardamom and rose
entries.text: phirni kashmiri chilled ground-rice pudding set in earthenware, scented with cardamom and rose vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice milk sugar green cardamom saffron rose water kewra water pistachios almonds bring the milk to a boil in a heavy-based pan, then lower the heat to a bare simmer. mix the ground rice with 4 tbsp cold milk to a smooth slurry with no lumps. pour the slurry into the simmering milk in a thin stream, whisking the whole time. cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring constantly and scraping the base and corners, until the mixture coats the back of a spoon and the rice has no bite left. add the sugar and cook 5 minutes more, until it thickens again to the consistency of pouring cream. stir in the saffron milk and the ground cardamom, and take the pan off the heat. let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the rose water or kewra. pour into the chilled bowls while still pourable; it thickens a great deal as it sets. scatter with the slivered pistachios and almonds and refrigerate at least 4 hours until firm and cold.

entries.title: Rista
entries.snippet: the red twin of gushtaba, meatballs poached in a chilli and fennel gravy
entries.text: rista kashmiri the red twin of gushtaba, meatballs poached in a chilli and fennel gravy gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier mutton / lamb ghee kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf black pepper baking soda water salt work the mince with 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp fennel powder, 1/2 tsp dry ginger, the ground green cardamom, black pepper, baking soda and 1 tsp salt for 10 minutes until pale and springy. wet your palms and roll 8 smooth balls, slightly flattened, then chill them 20 minutes. heat the remaining ghee in a wide pan, add the hing and let it foam for 10 seconds. add the bay leaf, black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them crackle for 30 seconds. off the heat, stir in the soaked chilli paste along with the rest of the fennel powder and dry ginger. pour in the water, add 1 tsp salt and bring to a gentle boil, then let it bubble 5 minutes so the raw chilli taste cooks out. lower the balls in one by one and leave the pan alone for 10 minutes, swirling rather than stirring. simmer uncovered on low for 35 minutes, basting the balls with gravy, until the fat rises red on the surface and the gravy has reduced by a third. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Rogan Josh
entries.snippet: Kashmiri lamb in a red gravy coloured by ratan jot and Kashmiri chilli, without onion or garlic
entries.text: rogan josh kashmiri kashmiri lamb in a red gravy coloured by ratan jot and kashmiri chilli, without onion or garlic gluten-free no-onion-garlic healthier mutton / lamb yogurt / dahi kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cinnamon cloves bay leaf ghee salt heat the ghee and bloom the asafoetida and whole spices until fragrant. add the mutton and sear over high heat until browned on all sides. take the pan off the heat. stir the kashmiri chilli, fennel and dry ginger into the whisked yogurt, then add it to the meat, stirring constantly. return to low heat and cook, stirring, until the gravy thickens and the fat begins to show, about 10 minutes. add a cup of hot water and salt, cover, and simmer 60-70 minutes until the meat is tender and the gravy is deep red and glossy. rest 15 minutes. serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Roth
entries.snippet: thick sweet fried bread studded with poppy seeds, made for pann
entries.text: roth kashmiri thick sweet fried bread studded with poppy seeds, made for pann vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) sugar ghee milk poppy seeds (khus khus) green cardamom fennel seeds (saunf) salt neutral oil rub the warm ghee thoroughly into the maida and salt with your fingertips for 4 minutes, until the flour looks like damp breadcrumbs. add the crushed cardamom and fennel seeds, then pour in the sweetened milk a little at a time. bring it together into a stiff dough and knead just 2 minutes, no more. cover and rest 20 minutes. divide into 6 balls, flatten each into a disc about 12cm across and 1cm thick, and press poppy seeds generously over both sides. prick each disc all over with a fork, right through. heat the oil in a kadhai to about 160c — a scrap of dough should take a full 10 seconds to rise. slide in one or two discs and fry for 4 to 5 minutes a side, turning once, until they are a deep even biscuit-brown and firm to the touch. lift onto a rack and let them cool completely; they crisp as they cool. repeat with the rest, letting the oil settle back to temperature between batches.

entries.title: Ruwangan Chaman
entries.snippet: fried paneer fingers in a bright, sour tomato gravy, pandit style
entries.text: ruwangan chaman kashmiri fried paneer fingers in a bright, sour tomato gravy, pandit style vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic paneer tomato mustard oil asafoetida (hing) fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder green cardamom cloves green chilli sugar salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the heat and let it settle for 30 seconds. pat the paneer fingers dry and fry them in batches until pale gold on two sides, about 3 minutes a batch, then lift out onto a plate. into the same oil add the cardamom, cloves and then the asafoetida; count to three as it foams. pour in the tomato puree, stand back from the spitting, and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until it darkens and pulls away from the sides. add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, fennel powder, dry ginger powder and salt and fry 3 minutes until the oil separates and rims the pan red. pour in the water and bring to a simmer, adding the sugar if the gravy tastes harsh. slide in the fried paneer and the slit green chillies and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes so the fingers drink up the gravy. take off the heat when the gravy is loose enough to pour but coats the paneer, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Shufta
entries.snippet: warm wedding sweet of fried paneer and dried fruit in a peppery cardamom syrup
entries.text: shufta kashmiri warm wedding sweet of fried paneer and dried fruit in a peppery cardamom syrup vegetarian gluten-free paneer ghee almonds cashews walnuts pistachios raisins (kishmish) dried apricots (khubani) dates sugar water green cardamom cinnamon black pepper dry ginger powder (saunth) saffron milk kewra water heat 3 tbsp of the ghee in a kadhai over medium heat and fry the paneer cubes until pale gold on all sides, about 4 minutes. lift the paneer out and drop it straight into a bowl of warm water for 5 minutes, then drain. add the remaining ghee to the pan and fry the almonds and cashews until they turn a shade darker, about 2 minutes. add the walnuts, pistachios, apricots and dates and toss for 1 minute, then add the raisins and take the pan off the heat as they swell. in a separate pan, dissolve the sugar in the water and boil for 6 to 7 minutes to a syrup of one-thread consistency — a drop between finger and thumb should pull a single short thread. stir the crushed cardamom, cinnamon, cracked black pepper and dry ginger powder into the syrup and simmer 2 minutes. pour the spiced syrup over the fruit and nuts, return to low heat and simmer 4 minutes until the syrup clings. fold in the drained paneer and the saffron milk and cook 2 minutes more, turning gently. take off the heat, stir in the kewra water and rest 10 minutes. serve warm, in small bowls — it is very rich.

entries.title: Syun Olav
entries.snippet: everyday mutton and potato curry in a thin, red, chilli-warm gravy
entries.text: syun olav kashmiri everyday mutton and potato curry in a thin, red, chilli-warm gravy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb potato onion garlic ginger mustard oil kashmiri chilli powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) turmeric powder black cardamom cloves cinnamon garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil to smoking point in a pressure cooker, then reduce the heat. fry the drained potato halves until golden on the cut sides, about 6 minutes, and lift them out. add the sliced onion and fry until deep gold, 10 to 12 minutes, stirring so the edges do not blacken. stir in the garlic and ginger and fry 2 minutes. add the mutton with the black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and brown over high heat for 8 minutes until the pieces have colour on every side. lower the heat, add the chilli paste, fennel powder, dry ginger powder, turmeric and salt and fry until the oil separates, about 6 minutes. pour in the hot water, close the cooker and cook for 4 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own. open, add the fried potatoes and simmer uncovered for 12 minutes until they are tender to a knife tip and the gravy has thickened slightly. taste for salt, scatter over the garam masala and coriander leaves and take off the heat.

entries.title: Tabak Maaz
entries.snippet: lamb ribs simmered soft in spiced milk, then fried crisp in ghee
