entries.text: tabak maaz kashmiri lamb ribs simmered soft in spiced milk, then fried crisp in ghee gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic mutton / lamb milk water ghee turmeric powder fennel powder dry ginger powder (saunth) asafoetida (hing) black cardamom green cardamom cloves cinnamon bay leaf black pepper salt put the ribs in a wide pan with the milk, water, turmeric, fennel powder, dry ginger, hing, both cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf and 1 tsp salt. bring to a bare simmer and hold it there, uncovered, for about 60 minutes. the ribs are ready when the meat has shrunk back from the bone ends and almost all the liquid has gone, leaving a thick coating. lift the ribs onto a rack and leave them to cool and dry for at least 30 minutes. heat the ghee in a heavy frying pan over medium heat until it shimmers. fry the ribs in a single layer, 4 minutes on the first side, until the edges are deep gold and audibly crisp. turn once and give them 3 minutes on the second side, pressing lightly with a spatula so the whole face colours. drain on paper, scatter with salt and the black pepper, and serve hot as a starter with green chutney or plain.

entries.title: Tehar
entries.snippet: turmeric-yellow rice scented with hing and whole spices, the pandit festival plate
entries.text: tehar kashmiri turmeric-yellow rice scented with hing and whole spices, the pandit festival plate vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice ghee turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) cumin seeds cloves black cardamom cinnamon bay leaf dried red chillies salt water heat the ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds, cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf. add the broken red chillies and then the asafoetida; it will foam and smell savoury almost at once. stir in the turmeric off the heat so it blooms in the ghee without scorching, about 10 seconds. add the drained rice and turn it gently in the yellow ghee for 2 minutes until every grain is coated and glossy. pour in the water, add the salt and bring to a hard boil. as soon as the surface water has been absorbed and craters appear, about 6 minutes, turn the heat to its lowest setting. cover tightly and cook undisturbed for 12 minutes. take off the heat and stand covered for a further 10 minutes. fluff with a fork, lifting from the base, and serve hot with yogurt or a dry mutton dish.

entries.title: Ada Pradhaman
entries.snippet: rice ada simmered in jaggery and thick coconut milk, the sadya finale
entries.text: ada pradhaman kerala rice ada simmered in jaggery and thick coconut milk, the sadya finale vegetarian gluten-free rice flour jaggery coconut milk ghee green cardamom dry ginger powder (saunth) cumin powder (jeera) cashews raisins (kishmish) coconut (fresh or desiccated) water salt boil the ada squares in plenty of water for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. drain and rinse in cold water. heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the cashews until golden, then the raisins until they puff, then the coconut slivers until brown. lift each out separately. in the same pan pour in the strained jaggery syrup and boil 4 minutes until it thickens and coats a spoon. add the drained ada and cook in the syrup on low for 10 minutes, stirring, until each piece is glossy and has darkened to the colour of the jaggery. pour in the thin coconut milk and simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until it reduces by about a quarter. stir in the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and cook 3 minutes more. add the powdered cardamom, dry ginger, cumin powder and the pinch of salt. take the pan off the heat and stir in the thick coconut milk. do not return it to the boil. scatter over the fried cashews, raisins and coconut slivers and serve warm.

entries.title: Appam
entries.snippet: Lacy fermented rice pancakes with a soft, thick centre
entries.text: appam kerala lacy fermented rice pancakes with a soft, thick centre vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut milk rice (short/medium grain) sugar salt coconut oil grind the soaked rice with the grated coconut, cooked rice and enough water to make a smooth, pourable batter. add sugar, cover, and leave to ferment 8-10 hours until risen and faintly sour. stir in the coconut milk and salt. the batter should be thinner than dosa batter — like single cream. heat the appachatti, wipe with coconut oil, pour a ladle into the middle, then immediately lift the pan and swirl it once so batter climbs the sides. cover and cook 2-3 minutes on low. do not flip. lift out when the edges lift away on their own. serve with stew, kadala curry or sweetened coconut milk.

entries.title: Avial
entries.snippet: Mixed vegetables bound in coconut, cumin and yogurt, finished with raw coconut oil
entries.text: avial kerala mixed vegetables bound in coconut, cumin and yogurt, finished with raw coconut oil vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier raw banana / plantain yam (suran) drumstick (moringa pod) carrot french beans ash gourd (petha) cucumber coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli turmeric powder yogurt / dahi curry leaves coconut oil salt cook the vegetables hardest-first in a wide pan with turmeric, salt and just enough water — yam and banana first, softer vegetables after. coarsely grind the coconut with cumin and green chilli. do not make it a smooth paste. fold the coconut mixture through the cooked vegetables and simmer 5 minutes. take the pan off the heat, then stir in the whisked yogurt. return briefly to very low heat but do not let it boil. crush the curry leaves between your palms and stir them in with the raw coconut oil. rest 10 minutes before serving. avial is served warm, not hot.

entries.title: Beef Ularthiyathu
entries.snippet: slow-fried beef in dark pepper masala with coconut slivers and a raft of curry leaves
entries.text: beef ularthiyathu kerala slow-fried beef in dark pepper masala with coconut slivers and a raft of curry leaves gluten-free dairy-free nut-free beef coconut (fresh or desiccated) shallots (small red onions) ginger garlic green chilli black pepper coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder fennel powder garam masala cloves cinnamon vinegar curry leaves coconut oil salt pressure cook the marinated beef with 1/2 cup water and the whole cloves and cinnamon for 4 whistles, then 15 minutes on low. release naturally. meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a wide kadhai and fry the coconut slivers over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden. lift out and set aside. in the same oil add the shallots, ginger, garlic and green chillies. cook 8 minutes until the shallots are deep brown at the edges. add the fennel powder, garam masala and remaining pepper and fry 1 minute until the oil smells of fennel. tip in the cooked beef along with any liquid from the cooker. raise the heat and boil hard, stirring, for 8-10 minutes until the liquid has gone. add the remaining 2 tbsp coconut oil and turn the heat to medium-low. now fry the beef, stirring every couple of minutes, for 20-25 minutes. scrape the crust off the base of the pan back into the meat every few minutes — that is where the flavour is. throw in all four sprigs of curry leaves and the fried coconut slivers. fry 2 minutes more until the leaves crisp and shatter. rest off the heat 5 minutes and serve with kappa or porotta.

entries.title: Cabbage Thoran
entries.snippet: shredded cabbage tossed with crushed coconut, mustard and curry leaves
entries.text: cabbage thoran kerala shredded cabbage tossed with crushed coconut, mustard and curry leaves vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free cabbage coconut (fresh or desiccated) shallots (small red onions) green chilli garlic cumin seeds turmeric powder coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt heat the coconut oil in a kadhai over medium heat until it thins and shimmers. add the mustard seeds and let them pop, about 30 seconds, then add the broken red chillies and curry leaves. stir in the chopped shallot and remaining slit chillies. cook 3 minutes until the shallot turns translucent and smells sweet. tip in the cabbage and salt. toss to coat in the oil. cover and cook on low for 5 minutes. the cabbage will release its own water — do not add any. uncover, raise the heat and stir-fry 2 minutes to drive off the moisture at the bottom of the pan. add the crushed coconut mixture and toss through for 2 minutes, until the coconut smells toasty and looks dry. taste for salt and take it off the heat while the cabbage still has bite.

entries.title: Cheera Thoran
entries.snippet: amaranth greens tossed dry with coconut, garlic and cumin
entries.text: cheera thoran kerala amaranth greens tossed dry with coconut, garlic and cumin vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free amaranth greens (chaulai) coconut (fresh or desiccated) shallots (small red onions) garlic green chilli cumin seeds turmeric powder mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves coconut oil salt pound the coconut, garlic, green chilli, cumin seeds and turmeric together to a coarse, fragrant crumble. do not make it a paste. heat the coconut oil in a wide kadhai over medium-high and crackle the mustard seeds until they pop, about 30 seconds. add the dried red chillies and curry leaves and let them sizzle for 10 seconds. add the sliced shallots and fry 3-4 minutes until soft and just turning gold at the edges. tip in the chopped greens and the salt, raise the heat, and toss for 2 minutes until they collapse to a third of their volume. cook uncovered 4-5 minutes, tossing occasionally, until the water the greens threw off has completely evaporated and the pan looks dry. scatter over the coconut mixture and toss through for 3 minutes until the coconut is heated and smells toasty. taste for salt, take off the heat and serve warm alongside rice.

entries.title: Chemmeen Manga Curry
entries.snippet: prawns and raw mango in a sharp red coconut gravy from the backwaters
entries.text: chemmeen manga curry kerala prawns and raw mango in a sharp red coconut gravy from the backwaters pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier prawns raw green mango coconut milk shallots (small red onions) ginger garlic green chilli kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds curry leaves coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and pop the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. add the fenugreek seeds and let them darken for 15 seconds only. add the shallots, ginger, garlic, green chillies and 2 sprigs of curry leaves. cook 6 minutes until the shallots are soft and just starting to colour. turn the heat to low, add the kashmiri chilli and turmeric and fry 45 seconds until the oil runs red. add the mango slices, the thin coconut milk and salt. simmer 8 minutes until the mango is tender but still holding together. slide in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes, just until they turn opaque and curl into loose c shapes. stir in the thick coconut milk and the last sprig of curry leaves. warm through 1 minute without boiling. take off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes so the mango sourness spreads through the gravy.

entries.title: Duck Mappas
entries.snippet: slow-braised duck in spiced coconut milk with potatoes
entries.text: duck mappas kerala slow-braised duck in spiced coconut milk with potatoes gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier duck coconut milk shallots (small red onions) onion ginger garlic green chilli potato coriander powder turmeric powder black pepper fennel powder garam masala cinnamon cloves green cardamom star anise vinegar curry leaves coconut oil water salt heat the coconut oil in a heavy pan and brown the duck pieces skin-side down over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until the skin is golden and a pool of fat has rendered out, then lift the pieces aside. pour off all but 2 tbsp of the rendered fat and keep it — it is the best cooking fat in the kitchen. fry the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and star anise in the reserved fat for 30 seconds until they perfume the pan. add the shallots and onion and cook over medium heat 12-14 minutes until soft and pale gold, not brown. add the ginger, garlic and green chillies and cook 3 minutes. stir in the coriander powder, remaining black pepper and fennel powder and fry 1 minute with a splash of water so nothing catches. return the duck with 2 sprigs of curry leaves, the thin coconut milk, 300ml water and the salt. cover and simmer very gently for 50-60 minutes, turning the pieces twice, until a skewer slides into the thigh without resistance. add the potatoes and cook a further 15 minutes uncovered until tender and the gravy has reduced by about a third. turn the heat to its lowest, pour in the thick coconut milk and the garam masala, and swirl the pan. heat through 3-4 minutes without letting it boil, until the gravy is glossy and coats the duck. finish with the last sprig of curry leaves, rest 10 minutes covered, and serve with appam or vellayappam.

entries.title: Fish Molee
entries.snippet: gentle coconut milk fish stew, pale and peppery rather than hot
entries.text: fish molee kerala gentle coconut milk fish stew, pale and peppery rather than hot pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut milk onion shallots (small red onions) ginger garlic green chilli tomato turmeric powder black pepper cloves cinnamon green cardamom curry leaves lemon / lime coconut oil salt heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a wide shallow pan and sear the marinated fish for 1 minute a side, just to firm the surface, then lift it out. add the remaining oil and fry the cloves, cinnamon and cardamom for 20 seconds until fragrant. add the sliced onion, shallot, ginger, garlic and green chillies and cook over medium-low heat 8-10 minutes until completely soft but still pale. sprinkle in the remaining turmeric and the black pepper and stir for 30 seconds. pour in the thin coconut milk with 1 sprig of curry leaves and the salt and simmer 6-8 minutes until slightly reduced. slide the fish back in along with the tomato rounds and simmer very gently 4 minutes, spooning gravy over the pieces rather than stirring. lower the heat to its minimum, pour in the thick coconut milk and swirl the pan to combine. heat through for 2-3 minutes until the surface just trembles and the fish flakes when nudged with a spoon. add the second sprig of curry leaves, taste for salt and pepper, and take off the heat. rest 5 minutes before serving with appam or plain rice.

entries.title: Idiyappam
entries.snippet: steamed rice string hoppers, soft and threadlike, served with coconut milk
entries.text: idiyappam kerala steamed rice string hoppers, soft and threadlike, served with coconut milk vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour water coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil salt bring the water to a full rolling boil with the salt and 1 tsp of the coconut oil. pour the boiling water over the rice flour all at once, stirring hard with a wooden spoon until it comes together as a shaggy mass. cover and rest 5 minutes so the flour absorbs fully. oil your palms and knead the warm dough for 3-4 minutes until it is completely smooth, soft and non-sticky — like fresh play dough. grease the idiyappam plates and scatter a teaspoon of grated coconut on each. load the press and squeeze the dough onto the plates in tight overlapping spirals, about 1cm thick. scatter a little more coconut on top and stack the plates in a steamer over rapidly boiling water. steam 6-8 minutes, until the strings look glossy and set and no longer taste of raw flour. lift off and let them cool for 2 minutes before easing them off the plate, or they will tear.

entries.title: Kaalan
entries.snippet: thick sour yogurt curry with yam and raw banana, heavy with pepper
entries.text: kaalan kerala thick sour yogurt curry with yam and raw banana, heavy with pepper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier yam (suran) raw banana / plantain yogurt / dahi coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds turmeric powder black pepper fenugreek seeds (methi) curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies coconut oil water salt boil the yam and raw banana with the turmeric, black pepper, green chillies, salt and 400ml water in an open pan for 15-18 minutes until the pieces are tender but still hold their shape on a spoon. meanwhile grind the coconut with the cumin seeds and 100ml water to a fine, smooth paste. whisk the yogurt in a bowl until completely smooth and pourable. stir the coconut paste into the simmering vegetables and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the raw coconut smell has gone. turn the heat to its lowest setting and pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring continuously in one direction. cook 8-10 minutes on low, stirring often, until the curry thickens visibly and clings to the vegetables. stir in a pinch of the roasted fenugreek powder and take the pan off the heat. heat the coconut oil in a small pan, crackle the mustard seeds, add the dried chillies and curry leaves and let them crisp for 10 seconds. pour the tempering over the kaalan, cover, and leave 10 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Kadala Curry
entries.snippet: black chickpeas in dark roasted coconut gravy, the breakfast partner to puttu
entries.text: kadala curry kerala black chickpeas in dark roasted coconut gravy, the breakfast partner to puttu vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier kala chana (brown chickpeas) coconut (fresh or desiccated) shallots (small red onions) onion ginger garlic coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder fennel seeds (saunf) garam masala coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with 3 cups water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 5 whistles, then 10 minutes on low. release naturally and keep the cooking liquid. heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a heavy pan and fry the sliced shallots for 4 minutes until browning at the edges. add the grated coconut and roast on medium-low, stirring constantly, for 10-12 minutes until it is a deep chocolate brown. add the coriander powder, chilli powder and fennel seeds and roast 1 minute more, until the spices darken and smell toasted. cool slightly, then blend with 1/2 cup water to a fine dark paste. in the same pan heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the broken red chillies, curry leaves, chopped onion, ginger and garlic. cook 6 minutes until the onion is soft and gold. stir in the ground coconut paste and fry 4 minutes until the oil begins to separate at the edges. add the cooked chickpeas with their liquid and the garam masala. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. taste for salt and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with puttu or appam.

entries.title: Kerala Meen Curry
entries.snippet: Fish simmered in coconut milk and kokum, tempered with curry leaves and coconut oil
entries.text: kerala meen curry kerala fish simmered in coconut milk and kokum, tempered with curry leaves and coconut oil gluten-free dairy-free nut-free pescatarian healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut milk kokum shallots (small red onions) ginger garlic green chilli curry leaves turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil. splutter the mustard seeds and fenugreek, then add the curry leaves, shallots, ginger, garlic and green chillies. fry until the shallots soften and turn pale gold. lower the heat, add the turmeric and kashmiri chilli and stir for 30 seconds only. powdered chilli scorches fast and turns bitter. add the soaked kokum with its water, the thin part of the coconut milk and salt. simmer 8 minutes to build the base. slide in the fish in a single layer. do not stir; shake the pan instead so the pieces stay whole. simmer 6-8 minutes until just opaque. pour in the thick coconut milk, swirl the pan and heat through without letting it boil. take it off the heat as soon as it steams. rest at least an hour before eating. this curry is markedly better after resting, and better still the next day.

entries.title: Koottu Curry
entries.snippet: yam, plantain and chana dal in a sweet-peppery roasted coconut gravy
entries.text: koottu curry kerala yam, plantain and chana dal in a sweet-peppery roasted coconut gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chana dal yam (suran) raw banana / plantain coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds black pepper turmeric powder red chilli powder green chilli jaggery curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies coconut oil water salt pressure-cook the drained chana dal with 250ml water and 1/4 tsp turmeric for 3 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. the dal should be soft but not collapsed. in a separate pot, boil the yam and plantain with the remaining turmeric, black pepper, green chillies, salt and 250ml water for 12-15 minutes until just tender. grind half the coconut with the cumin seeds and 100ml water to a coarse, thick paste — a few seconds only, this should stay slightly textured. add the cooked dal with its liquid to the vegetables and simmer 5 minutes so the two come together. stir in the ground coconut and the jaggery, and cook 8 minutes on medium-low until the gravy is thick and barely runs off a spoon. taste and adjust salt, pepper and jaggery — it should read sweet first, then peppery. in a kadhai heat the coconut oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the dried red chillies and curry leaves. add the remaining grated coconut to the tempering and roast over medium heat 6-8 minutes, stirring, until it is a deep golden brown and smells toasted. tip the whole tempering, coconut and all, over the curry and fold it through. rest 10 minutes covered before serving as part of a sadya or with plain rice.

entries.title: Kozhi Porichathu
entries.snippet: crisp fried chicken in a pepper-and-fennel masala with fried curry leaves
entries.text: kozhi porichathu kerala crisp fried chicken in a pepper-and-fennel masala with fried curry leaves gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder black pepper fennel powder garam masala lemon / lime rice flour curry leaves green chilli shallots (small red onions) coconut oil salt crush the ginger and garlic to a rough paste with a little salt. mix the paste with the kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, turmeric, black pepper, fennel powder, garam masala, lemon juice and salt into a thick marinade. rub it into the slashed chicken, working it into the cuts, cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours. just before frying, sprinkle the rice flour over the chicken and toss so each piece wears a thin, even dusting. heat the coconut oil in a kadhai to about 170c — a pinch of rice flour should sizzle steadily, not violently. slide in the chicken in a single uncrowded layer and fry over medium heat 7-8 minutes on the first side without moving it. turn and fry 6-7 minutes on the second side until deep red-brown and the juices at the thickest part run clear. lift onto a rack, not paper, and let the pieces drain while you fry the rest. drop the curry leaves, slit green chillies and sliced shallots into the hot oil for 20-30 seconds until the leaves stop spluttering and turn glassy. scatter the fried aromatics over the chicken, squeeze over a little more lemon and serve hot.

entries.title: Kozhukatta
entries.snippet: steamed rice dumplings filled with jaggery and coconut
entries.text: kozhukatta kerala steamed rice dumplings filled with jaggery and coconut vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour water coconut (fresh or desiccated) jaggery green cardamom cumin seeds coconut oil salt make the filling first: melt the jaggery with 3 tbsp water in a pan over medium heat until it dissolves into a syrup, about 4 minutes, then strain out any grit. return the syrup to the pan, add the grated coconut, crushed cardamom and cumin seeds, and cook 6-8 minutes, stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides and holds its shape when pressed. spread the filling on a plate to cool completely. bring the 400ml water to a full boil with the salt and 1 tbsp coconut oil. take the pan off the heat and tip in the rice flour all at once, stirring hard with a wooden spoon until no dry flour remains and the mass comes together. cover and leave 5 minutes, then knead the warm dough with oiled palms for 3-4 minutes until it is completely smooth and does not crack when you press a ball flat. divide the dough into 14-16 balls, keeping the rest covered with a damp cloth while you work. flatten each ball into a 7cm disc in your oiled palm, place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle, and gather the edges up over it, sealing and rolling into a smooth ball. arrange the dumplings in a greased steamer basket with space between them. steam over rapidly boiling water for 10-12 minutes, until the surface turns glossy and slightly translucent. rest 5 minutes before lifting them out — straight from the steamer they tear.

entries.title: Meen Varuthathu
entries.snippet: chilli-and-pepper crusted fish shallow fried in coconut oil until the edges blister
entries.text: meen varuthathu kerala chilli-and-pepper crusted fish shallow fried in coconut oil until the edges blister pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder black pepper ginger garlic lemon / lime rice flour curry leaves coconut oil salt bring the marinated fish back to room temperature for 15 minutes if it has been in the fridge. dust each piece lightly with rice flour on both sides and shake off the excess. heat the coconut oil in a heavy tawa over medium-high until a pinch of flour dropped in sizzles instantly. slide in the fish, laying it away from you, and do not touch it for 4 minutes. turn once and fry the second side 3-4 minutes until the crust is deep brick red and the flesh at the slash is opaque. throw the curry leaves into the hot oil around the fish for the last 30 seconds until they crisp. lift onto a plate, scatter the crisped leaves over, and serve within minutes with rice and a wedge of lemon.

entries.title: Mutta Roast
entries.snippet: boiled eggs in a dark slow-fried onion masala, breakfast alongside appam
entries.text: mutta roast kerala boiled eggs in a dark slow-fried onion masala, breakfast alongside appam vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free eggs onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder garam masala fennel powder black pepper curry leaves coconut oil salt heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a kadhai and fry the scored eggs with a pinch of turmeric and salt for 2 minutes, turning, until blistered and gold. lift out. add the remaining oil, then the sliced onions, ginger, garlic, green chillies and 2 sprigs of curry leaves with a pinch of salt. cook on medium-low for 20-25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the onions collapse to about a fifth of their volume and turn a deep glossy brown. add the chilli powder, kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, turmeric and pepper. fry 90 seconds with a splash of water so the spices do not catch. stir in the tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until they break down completely and the oil pools at the edges. add 1/4 cup water, the garam masala and fennel powder, and simmer 3 minutes into a thick clinging masala. return the fried eggs, roll them in the masala and cook 3 minutes on low so they take on the colour. scatter over the last sprig of curry leaves, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with appam or bread.

entries.title: Nadan Chicken Stew
entries.snippet: pale peppery chicken and potato stew in coconut milk, the classic appam partner
entries.text: nadan chicken stew kerala pale peppery chicken and potato stew in coconut milk, the classic appam partner gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken potato carrot onion ginger garlic green chilli black pepper cinnamon cloves green cardamom coconut milk curry leaves coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil in a heavy pot over medium-low and add the cinnamon, cloves and cardamom. fry 30 seconds until fragrant. add the onion, ginger, garlic and green chillies with a pinch of salt. cook 6-8 minutes until soft and glassy. stir in the crushed pepper and fry 30 seconds. add the chicken and turn it in the aromatics for 3 minutes until the flesh turns opaque white. pour in the thin coconut milk, add the potato, carrot, curry leaves and salt, and bring to a bare simmer. cover and cook on low for 25 minutes, until the chicken pulls easily from the bone and the potato is soft at the centre. uncover and stir in the thick coconut milk. warm through for 2 minutes without letting it boil. taste for salt and pepper, then rest covered for 10 minutes off the heat before serving with appam.

entries.title: Nadan Mutton Curry
entries.snippet: slow-cooked mutton in a dark roasted-coconut and fennel gravy
entries.text: nadan mutton curry kerala slow-cooked mutton in a dark roasted-coconut and fennel gravy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb shallots (small red onions) onion ginger garlic green chilli tomato coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder fennel powder black pepper garam masala cinnamon cloves green cardamom curry leaves coconut oil water salt dry-roast the grated coconut in a heavy kadhai over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring, until it is chocolate brown and smells nutty, then cool and grind with 100ml water to a smooth dark paste. heat 3 tbsp coconut oil in a pressure cooker and fry the whole cinnamon, cloves and cardamom for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the sliced shallots and onion and fry over medium heat for 15 minutes until deeply browned and sweet — this is the longest active step and it cannot be shortened. add the ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 3 minutes until the raw smell lifts. lower the heat, add the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, remaining chilli powder, fennel powder and black pepper and fry 90 seconds, sprinkling in a tablespoon of water if the spices catch. add the tomatoes and 2 sprigs of curry leaves and cook 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down and oil shows at the edges. stir in the marinated mutton and fry over high heat for 6-8 minutes until every piece is coated and the meat has tightened and browned. add 400ml water and the salt, close the cooker and cook on medium for 5 whistles, then let the pressure fall naturally, around 15 minutes. open the cooker, stir in the roasted coconut paste and simmer uncovered 15-20 minutes until the gravy is thick, dark and clings to the meat. stir in the garam masala, taste for salt, and take off the heat. heat the last tablespoon of coconut oil in a small pan, fry the remaining curry leaf sprig for 10 seconds and pour it over the curry. rest 15 minutes covered before serving with appam, kappa or rice.

entries.title: Neyyappam
entries.snippet: dark ghee-fried rice and jaggery fritters, crisp outside and soft within
entries.text: neyyappam kerala dark ghee-fried rice and jaggery fritters, crisp outside and soft within vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) jaggery coconut (fresh or desiccated) green cardamom dry ginger powder (saunth) sesame seeds ghee baking soda water salt melt the jaggery with 100ml water over medium heat until dissolved, about 5 minutes, then strain through a sieve and cool to lukewarm. grind the drained rice with the cooled jaggery syrup and the remaining 50ml water to a thick, smooth batter — thicker than dosa batter, roughly the consistency of cake batter. beat in the crushed cardamom, dry ginger powder and salt, then cover and rest the batter 2-3 hours at room temperature. heat 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan and fry the coconut slivers for 3-4 minutes until golden at the edges, then fry the sesame for 20 seconds. fold the fried coconut, sesame and all the ghee from that pan into the rested batter. stir in the baking soda if using, right before frying, and do not let the batter sit after this. heat the remaining ghee in a kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter rises to the surface within 3 seconds without browning instantly. drop in tablespoons of batter, 4-5 at a time, and fry 3 minutes until the undersides are deep mahogany. flip each one and fry a further 2-3 minutes until puffed, dark and firm at the edges. lift onto a rack to drain and cool, and let the ghee come back to temperature between batches. serve at room temperature, when the outside has crisped and the inside stays soft.

entries.title: Olan
entries.snippet: ash gourd and cowpeas simmered in thin coconut milk, barely spiced on purpose
entries.text: olan kerala ash gourd and cowpeas simmered in thin coconut milk, barely spiced on purpose vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier ash gourd (petha) lobia (black-eyed peas) coconut milk green chilli curry leaves coconut oil salt boil the soaked cowpeas in 2 cups of water for 20-25 minutes until soft but still holding their shape. drain, keeping a little of the cooking water. put the ash gourd slices in a wide pan with the slit chillies, salt and just enough water to come halfway up. simmer uncovered 8 minutes until the gourd turns translucent at the edges and a knife slides through without resistance. add the cooked cowpeas and the thin coconut milk. bring to a bare simmer. cook 5 minutes on low, shaking the pan rather than stirring so the gourd slices stay whole. pour in the thick coconut milk and the curry leaves. warm through for 1 minute only. take off the heat, stir in the raw coconut oil and cover for 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Parippu Curry
entries.snippet: soft moong dal in coconut and cumin, the first course of a sadya
entries.text: parippu curry kerala soft moong dal in coconut and cumin, the first course of a sadya vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier moong dal coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds garlic turmeric powder shallots (small red onions) coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt pressure cook the rinsed dal with 2.5 cups water and the turmeric for 3 whistles, then rest until the pressure drops. whisk the cooked dal smooth with a ladle, adding hot water until it is the consistency of thin cream. stir in the ground coconut paste and the salt. simmer on low for 6-8 minutes, stirring often, until the raw coconut smell disappears and it thickens slightly. heat the coconut oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. add the sliced shallots, broken red chillies and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes until the shallots brown. pour the tempering over the dal and cover for 5 minutes so the curry leaf aroma settles in. serve over hot rice as the first course of the meal, with a papadam crushed over the top.

entries.title: Pazham Pori
entries.snippet: ripe plantain slices in a turmeric-gold batter, the four o'clock teashop snack
entries.text: pazham pori kerala ripe plantain slices in a turmeric-gold batter, the four o'clock teashop snack vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free raw banana / plantain plain flour (maida) rice flour turmeric powder sugar salt water cumin seeds coconut oil whisk the maida, rice flour, turmeric, sugar, salt and crushed cumin together in a bowl. add the water gradually, whisking, until you have a smooth lump-free batter. rest 10 minutes. peel the plantains and slice each lengthwise into 3-4 flat strips about 8mm thick. heat the oil in a kadhai to 175c — a drop of batter should rise and sizzle within 3 seconds without browning instantly. dip a strip into the batter, let the excess run off, and lower it gently into the oil. fry 3-4 at a time for 2 minutes, until the underside is set and pale gold. turn and fry a further 2 minutes until both sides are deep gold and the surface has stopped bubbling hard. lift onto a rack, not paper, so the underside stays crisp. repeat with the rest. serve hot with strong black tea.

entries.title: Pulissery
entries.snippet: soured yogurt and coconut curry, gently spiced and never boiled
entries.text: pulissery kerala soured yogurt and coconut curry, gently spiced and never boiled vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi ash gourd (petha) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds turmeric powder coconut oil mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves salt cook the ash gourd with the salt and 1/2 cup water in a wide pan, covered, for 8 minutes until soft and translucent. stir in the ground coconut paste and simmer 4 minutes on low, until the raw coconut smell has gone. take the pan off the heat completely and let it cool for 3 minutes. pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring as you go. return to the lowest possible heat and warm, stirring constantly, for 3-4 minutes until it just steams and thickens slightly. taste for salt and set aside covered. heat the coconut oil in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds, then add the fenugreek seeds, broken red chillies and curry leaves and fry 20 seconds. pour the tempering over the curry and cover for 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Pumpkin Erissery
entries.snippet: mashed pumpkin and cowpeas under a lid of dark roasted coconut
entries.text: pumpkin erissery kerala mashed pumpkin and cowpeas under a lid of dark roasted coconut vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pumpkin lobia (black-eyed peas) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green chilli cumin seeds turmeric powder red chilli powder garlic coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves salt boil the soaked cowpeas in 2 cups water for 20 minutes until tender. do not drain. add the pumpkin cubes, chilli powder and salt to the same pan with a little more water if needed. cook covered 10 minutes until the pumpkin is soft enough to crush against the side of the pan. mash roughly with the back of a ladle, leaving some cubes whole for texture. stir in the ground coconut paste and simmer 5 minutes on low until it loses its raw smell and thickens. in a separate kadhai, heat the coconut oil and pop the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and the remaining cumin seeds and fry 20 seconds. add the reserved grated coconut and roast on medium-low, stirring constantly, for 5-6 minutes until it is a deep even brown and smells nutty. pour the roasted coconut tempering over the pumpkin, stir once, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Puttu
entries.snippet: steamed cylinders of rice flour layered with coconut, eaten hot with kadala curry
entries.text: puttu kerala steamed cylinders of rice flour layered with coconut, eaten hot with kadala curry vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour coconut (fresh or desiccated) water salt dissolve the salt in the warm water. sprinkle the salted water over the rice flour a tablespoon at a time, rubbing it through with your fingertips after each addition. stop when the flour feels like damp sand and holds a shape in your fist. you may not need all the water. pass the whole lot through a coarse sieve or break the lumps by rubbing between your palms, then rest 10 minutes. bring water to a rolling boil in the base of the puttu maker or steamer. load the mould: a tablespoon of grated coconut at the bottom, then loose flour to two-thirds, then coconut, then flour, finishing with coconut. do not press down. steam 7-8 minutes from when a steady plume comes out of the top. push the puttu out onto a plate with the handle of a wooden spoon and serve immediately with kadala curry or ripe banana.

entries.title: Sambharam
entries.snippet: spiced buttermilk cooler with crushed ginger, chilli and curry leaf
entries.text: sambharam kerala spiced buttermilk cooler with crushed ginger, chilli and curry leaf vegetarian gluten-free nut-free yogurt / dahi water shallots (small red onions) ginger green chilli curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime asafoetida (hing) salt crush the shallot, ginger, green chilli and curry leaves together with the salt into a rough, wet paste. whisk the yogurt in a wide bowl for about 1 minute until it is completely smooth and pourable, with no lumps clinging to the whisk. pour in the chilled water in three additions, whisking between each, until you have a thin, milky liquid. stir the crushed paste through the buttermilk along with the chopped coriander leaves. add the pinch of asafoetida if using and stir once. leave to stand 10 minutes at room temperature so the ginger and chilli bleed into the liquid. taste and correct the salt, adding the lemon juice only if the drink tastes flat. strain through a coarse sieve into a jug and serve over ice, or pour unstrained for a rougher, more rustic glass.

entries.title: Semiya Payasam
entries.snippet: quick vermicelli milk pudding with ghee-fried cashews and raisins
entries.text: semiya payasam kerala quick vermicelli milk pudding with ghee-fried cashews and raisins vegetarian vermicelli (semiya) milk sugar condensed milk ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) green cardamom coconut (fresh or desiccated) heat the ghee in a heavy pan and fry the cashews over medium heat for 2 minutes until pale gold, then lift them out with a slotted spoon. fry the raisins in the same ghee for 20 seconds until they swell and puff, then lift them out. fry the coconut slivers, if using, for 2 minutes until golden and set aside with the nuts. break the vermicelli into 3cm lengths, add to the remaining ghee and roast over medium-low heat for 4-5 minutes until evenly light brown. pour in the milk, raise the heat and bring to a gentle boil, stirring so nothing sticks to the base. lower the heat and simmer 12-15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the vermicelli is soft and the milk has thickened and turned faintly cream-coloured. stir in the sugar and the condensed milk and cook a further 5 minutes until fully dissolved. add the crushed cardamom, stir once and take the pan off the heat. fold through most of the fried cashews, raisins and coconut, keeping some back for the top. rest 10 minutes — it thickens considerably as it stands — then scatter over the reserved nuts and serve warm or chilled.

entries.title: Ulli Theeyal
entries.snippet: dark roasted-coconut and shallot curry, sour with tamarind
entries.text: ulli theeyal kerala dark roasted-coconut and shallot curry, sour with tamarind vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free shallots (small red onions) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder fenugreek seeds (methi) black pepper tamarind curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies jaggery coconut oil water salt heat 1 tbsp of the coconut oil in a heavy pan and roast the grated coconut over medium-low heat, stirring almost constantly, for 12-15 minutes until it is a deep even brown and smells nutty. add the fenugreek seeds and roast 30 seconds more, then take the pan off the heat. stir the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder and turmeric into the hot coconut off the heat and let the residual warmth cook them for 1 minute. cool completely, then grind with 150ml water to a very smooth, dark paste — a full 3-4 minutes in the blender. heat the remaining 2 tbsp coconut oil in the same pan and fry the whole shallots over medium heat for 8 minutes until browned at the edges and softened. pour in the strained tamarind water and 350ml water, add the salt, and simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the shallots are tender to a knife tip. stir in the ground coconut paste, rinse the blender with a splash of water and add that too. simmer gently 12-15 minutes, uncovered, until the gravy darkens and thickens enough to coat a spoon and oil beads at the surface. stir in the jaggery and cracked pepper, taste, and correct salt and sourness. in a small pan heat a teaspoon of coconut oil, crackle the mustard seeds, add the dried chillies and curry leaves, and pour the tempering over the curry. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Baimbale Curry
entries.snippet: tender monsoon bamboo shoot in coconut gravy, sour and faintly bitter
entries.text: baimbale curry karnataka tender monsoon bamboo shoot in coconut gravy, sour and faintly bitter vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli turmeric powder onion garlic curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies coriander powder black pepper coconut oil vinegar salt water boil the chopped bamboo shoot in plenty of water for 10 minutes, drain, and repeat twice with fresh water each time. grind the coconut, cumin and green chilli with 150 ml water to a smooth paste and set aside. heat the coconut oil in a heavy pan, add the mustard seeds and let them pop, about 30 seconds. add the dried red chilli and curry leaves and crackle for 10 seconds. add the onion and garlic and fry until the onion is soft and gold at the edges, about 8 minutes. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and crushed pepper and fry 1 minute. add the drained bamboo shoot and fry 5 minutes, stirring, until it smells sweet rather than sharp. pour in 200 ml water and 1 tsp salt, cover and simmer 12 minutes until the shoot is tender to the bite. stir in the ground coconut paste and simmer very gently 8 minutes; the gravy should thicken and turn glossy. take the pan off the heat, stir in the vinegar, cover and rest 5 minutes. serve with hot rice.

entries.title: Chekke Curry
entries.snippet: raw jackfruit simmered soft in a mild ground coconut masala
entries.text: chekke curry karnataka raw jackfruit simmered soft in a mild ground coconut masala vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier raw jackfruit (kathal) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli garlic turmeric powder coriander powder black pepper coconut oil mustard seeds dried red chillies curry leaves onion vinegar salt water pressure-cook the jackfruit with 250 ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 3 whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself. grind the coconut, cumin, green chilli and garlic with 150 ml water to a smooth paste. heat the coconut oil in a pan, add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, about 30 seconds. add the dried red chilli and curry leaves and let them crackle for 10 seconds. add the onion and fry until soft and pale gold, about 7 minutes. stir in the coriander powder and crushed black pepper and fry 1 minute. tip in the cooked jackfruit along with its liquid and simmer 5 minutes. add the ground coconut paste, bring to a bare simmer and cook 8 minutes, stirring often. check the salt, take the pan off the heat and stir in the vinegar if using. rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Kadambuttu
entries.snippet: soft steamed rice dumplings, the standing partner to pandi curry
entries.text: kadambuttu karnataka soft steamed rice dumplings, the standing partner to pandi curry vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour water coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil salt bring the water to a full boil with the salt and coconut oil in a wide heavy pan. lower the heat to minimum and add the rice flour all at once, stirring hard with a wooden spoon. keep stirring 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides in a single rough mass with no dry flour left. cover the pan and leave it on the lowest heat for 5 minutes so the flour steams through. tip the dough onto a plate, scatter over the grated coconut and let it cool just enough to handle, about 3 minutes. knead the hot dough with wet hands for 3 minutes until it is completely smooth and slightly shiny. break off lime-sized pieces and roll each between wet palms into a smooth ball with no seams or cracks. arrange the balls in a greased steamer plate, leaving a finger's gap between them. steam over rapidly boiling water for 12 minutes, until the surfaces look matt and set rather than wet. turn off the heat and leave them in the covered steamer 5 minutes before lifting them out.

entries.title: Koli Curry
entries.snippet: Kodava chicken curry in a roasted coconut and pepper gravy
entries.text: koli curry karnataka kodava chicken curry in a roasted coconut and pepper gravy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper dried red chillies fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds onion garlic ginger green chilli curry leaves turmeric powder coconut oil vinegar coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water dry-roast the coriander powder, cumin, dried red chilli, fenugreek and mustard seeds in a small pan over low heat for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty and the mustard begins to pop. add the grated coconut to the same pan and roast, stirring constantly, 6 to 8 minutes until it is an even reddish brown. grind the roasted coconut and spices with 150 ml water to a smooth, thick paste and set aside. heat the coconut oil in a heavy pan and fry the onion until soft and gold, about 8 minutes. add the garlic, ginger, green chilli and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes, until the raw garlic smell is gone. add the chicken and fry on medium-high for 6 minutes, turning the pieces, until the flesh is opaque and lightly coloured. stir in the ground coconut masala and fry 4 minutes until the oil separates at the edges and the paste darkens a shade. pour in the remaining 150 ml water and the crushed black pepper, cover and simmer on low 20 minutes until the chicken is tender at the bone. uncover and simmer 5 minutes more to thicken, then check the salt. off the heat, stir in the vinegar and the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Kumm Curry
entries.snippet: quick hill mushroom curry heavy with black pepper and coconut
entries.text: kumm curry karnataka quick hill mushroom curry heavy with black pepper and coconut vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mushrooms onion garlic ginger green chilli curry leaves black pepper coriander powder turmeric powder coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and fry the onion over medium heat until soft and gold, about 7 minutes. add the garlic, ginger, green chilli and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes until fragrant. turn the heat high, add the mushrooms and cook without stirring for 3 minutes so they colour on one side. stir and cook 4 minutes more, until the water the mushrooms release has boiled away. lower the heat, add the turmeric, coriander powder and half the crushed pepper and fry 1 minute. add the grated coconut and fry 2 minutes, until it smells toasted and looks dry. pour in the water with 3/4 tsp salt, cover and simmer 6 minutes. uncover, stir in the rest of the pepper and cook 3 minutes until the gravy is thick enough to coat the mushrooms. check the salt, scatter over the coriander leaves and serve with rice or otti.

entries.title: Otti
entries.snippet: thin rice flatbread pressed by hand and cooked on a griddle
entries.text: otti karnataka thin rice flatbread pressed by hand and cooked on a griddle vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour water coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil salt bring the water to a boil with the salt and 1 tsp of the coconut oil. turn the heat to its lowest, add the rice flour all at once and stir hard until no dry flour is visible, about 2 minutes. cover and cook on the lowest heat for 4 minutes, then turn the dough out onto a plate. add the grated coconut and knead the hot dough with oiled hands for 3 minutes until smooth and pliable, like soft clay. divide into 8 balls and keep them under a damp cloth. place a ball on an oiled sheet and pat it out with your palm and fingertips into a 15 cm round, turning as you go. lift the roti onto a hot griddle and cook 90 seconds, until the underside shows brown freckles. flip and cook the second side 90 seconds, pressing the edges down with a cloth so it puffs slightly. brush with a little coconut oil, stack in a covered box and repeat with the rest.

entries.title: Pandi Curry
entries.snippet: the Coorg pork curry, black with pepper and sharpened with kachampuli
entries.text: pandi curry karnataka the coorg pork curry, black with pepper and sharpened with kachampuli gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork turmeric powder black pepper onion garlic ginger green chilli curry leaves coriander powder cumin seeds red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder cinnamon cloves vinegar coconut oil salt water put the pork, turmeric, 1 tsp of the crushed pepper and 1 tsp salt in a heavy pot over medium heat, with no oil and no water. cover and cook 20 minutes, stirring twice; the pork throws off a lot of cloudy grey liquid. uncover, raise the heat and boil that liquid away until the fat starts spitting and the cubes catch gold at the edges, about 15 minutes. push the meat to one side and add the onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli and curry leaves to the rendered fat. fry the aromatics until the onion is soft and evenly gold, about 10 minutes, then stir everything together. add the coriander powder, crushed cumin, chilli powder, kashmiri chilli, cinnamon and cloves and fry 3 minutes until the pot smells toasted. pour in the hot water, scrape the base clean, cover and simmer on low 45 minutes until the pork cuts with the side of a spoon. stir in the remaining crushed black pepper and simmer uncovered 10 minutes, until the gravy is dark and clings to the meat. take the pot off the heat, stir in the vinegar, cover and leave it 10 minutes before serving. taste and correct salt and sourness, adding vinegar a half teaspoon at a time. serve with kadambuttu or otti.

entries.title: Thambuttu
entries.snippet: roasted ragi pressed with jaggery, coconut and sesame into soft sweet rounds
entries.text: thambuttu karnataka roasted ragi pressed with jaggery, coconut and sesame into soft sweet rounds vegetarian gluten-free nut-free ragi (finger millet) flour dates jaggery coconut (fresh or desiccated) sesame seeds ghee green cardamom honey salt dry-roast the ragi flour in a heavy pan over low heat, stirring constantly, for 8 minutes until it darkens slightly and smells nutty. tip the flour onto a plate to stop it cooking and spread it out to cool for 5 minutes. in the same pan, toast the sesame seeds for 90 seconds until they pop and turn one shade darker. put the warm ragi flour, mashed dates, grated jaggery, coconut, sesame and salt in a wide bowl. rub everything together with your fingertips for 2 minutes until the jaggery is no longer visible as lumps. pour over the melted ghee and the cardamom and work it in until the mixture darkens and starts holding its shape when squeezed. take a fistful and squeeze it firmly in your closed hand, then press it into a rough round about 5 cm across. repeat with the rest of the mixture; you should get 8 to 10 rounds. serve at room temperature, with a drizzle of honey over each if you like.

entries.title: Alu Vadi
entries.snippet: colocasia leaves rolled with sweet-sour gram flour paste, steamed and sliced
entries.text: alu vadi maharashtrian colocasia leaves rolled with sweet-sour gram flour paste, steamed and sliced vegetarian vegan dairy-free gluten-free nut-free colocasia (arbi) besan (gram flour) rice flour tamarind jaggery red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) sesame seeds water groundnut oil mustard seeds coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt mix the besan, rice flour, tamarind pulp, jaggery, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, asafoetida, 1 tbsp sesame and salt into a thick, spreadable paste, adding water a teaspoon at a time only if it is too stiff. lay a leaf shiny side down, tip pointing away from you, and spread a thin, even layer of paste over the whole surface. lay a second leaf on top facing the opposite way, spread again, and repeat until you have a stack of 3 leaves. fold in both long sides by 3cm, spread paste on the folded edges, then roll from the wide end into a tight cylinder. seal the end with paste. make 4 rolls. steam the rolls over rolling water 25-30 minutes, until a knife goes through cleanly and the outside is a dull olive green. cool completely, 30 minutes, then cut into 1.5cm slices with a sharp thin knife. heat 4 tbsp oil in a kadhai and shallow-fry the slices in batches, 2 minutes a side, until the edges crisp and brown. heat the remaining oil, pop the mustard seeds with the remaining sesame, and pour over the fried slices. finish with fresh coconut and coriander and eat warm.

entries.title: Amti
entries.snippet: toor dal made sweet, sour and dark with goda masala, tamarind and jaggery
entries.text: amti maharashtrian toor dal made sweet, sour and dark with goda masala, tamarind and jaggery vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free toor dal (pigeon pea) garam masala tamarind jaggery coconut (fresh or desiccated) groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the soaked dal with the turmeric and 300ml water for 4 whistles until completely soft, then whisk it smooth. heat the oil in a pan, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing and let them sizzle 10 seconds. add the kashmiri chilli and chilli powder and stir for 10 seconds off the heat so they bloom without burning. pour in the whisked dal and the remaining 200ml water and bring to a simmer. stir in the goda masala, tamarind pulp, jaggery and salt. simmer uncovered 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the amti darkens and thins slightly and a skin no longer forms on top. taste and adjust: more jaggery if it bites, more tamarind if it tastes flat. finish with the grated coconut and coriander and serve with rice.

entries.title: Basundi
entries.snippet: milk cooked down by half until it is thick, grainy and the colour of ivory
entries.text: basundi maharashtrian milk cooked down by half until it is thick, grainy and the colour of ivory vegetarian gluten-free milk sugar green cardamom saffron nutmeg almonds pistachios bring the milk to a boil in a wide heavy pan, then drop the heat to a steady low simmer. simmer 45-55 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes and scraping the base and the sides with a flat spatula. keep going until the milk has reduced by half and coats the back of a spoon in a thick ivory layer. stir in the sugar and simmer 8 more minutes — the milk will loosen at first and then thicken again. add the crushed cardamom, the saffron milk and the scraping of nutmeg and simmer 2 minutes. take off the heat and cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally to stop a skin forming. chill at least 3 hours; it thickens noticeably as it cools. serve cold in small bowls, scattered with the slivered almonds and pistachios, with hot puris alongside if it is a festival day.

entries.title: Batata Bhaji
entries.snippet: soft turmeric-yellow potatoes with mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chilli
entries.text: batata bhaji maharashtrian soft turmeric-yellow potatoes with mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier potato onion green chilli groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) sugar water lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt boil the potatoes whole in their skins until a knife goes through easily, about 20 minutes, then cool, peel and break into rough 3cm pieces. heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the green chilli and sliced onion and cook 5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent. stir in the turmeric and let it cook 20 seconds in the oil. add the potato, salt and sugar and turn everything over gently until the pieces are evenly yellow. pour in the water, cover and steam on low heat for 5 minutes. squeeze over the lemon, fold through the coriander and serve with pooris, chapati or as the filling for vada pav.

entries.title: Bharli Vangi
entries.snippet: baby aubergines stuffed with roasted peanut, coconut and goda masala, simmered in their own gravy
entries.text: bharli vangi maharashtrian baby aubergines stuffed with roasted peanut, coconut and goda masala, simmered in their own gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier eggplant / brinjal peanuts dried coconut (copra) sesame seeds onion garlic ginger garam masala coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder tamarind jaggery groundnut oil water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the grated dried coconut over low heat for 4 minutes until it is a deep golden brown, then tip it straight out of the pan. grind the roasted coconut, peanut and sesame with one chopped onion, the garlic and the ginger to a coarse, thick masala using 3 tbsp water. mix the masala with the goda masala, coriander powder, chilli powder, turmeric, half the tamarind pulp, the jaggery and salt. drain the aubergines, pat dry and pack about a tablespoon of masala into each slit, keeping the fruit whole. reserve the leftover masala. heat the oil in a wide pan and lay the stuffed aubergines in a single layer. fry 6 minutes, turning them by shaking the pan, until the skins blister and dull. lift the aubergines out, add the second onion, sliced, and cook 5 minutes until soft. stir in the reserved masala and fry 4 minutes until it darkens and oil separates at the edges. add the water and the remaining tamarind, return the aubergines to the pan, cover and simmer 20 minutes over low heat. check that a knife slides into an aubergine without resistance, and that the gravy is thick and rust-coloured with oil floating on top. scatter with coriander and rest 10 minutes before serving with bhakri or rice.

entries.title: Bombil Fry
entries.snippet: koli-style bombay duck, rava-crusted outside and custard-soft within
entries.text: bombil fry maharashtrian koli-style bombay duck, rava-crusted outside and custard-soft within pescatarian dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) rava / sooji (semolina) rice flour kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder garlic ginger lemon / lime groundnut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt press the cleaned bombil between kitchen paper for 20 minutes to draw out as much water as possible. rub the fish with the garlic and ginger pastes, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, turmeric, salt and the juice of half a lemon. leave 15 minutes. mix the rava and rice flour on a wide plate with a pinch of salt. heat 3 tbsp oil in a flat pan over medium-high until a pinch of rava sizzles at once. press each fish into the rava on both sides, patting it on firmly, and lay it straight into the pan. fry 3-4 minutes on the first side without touching it, until the crust is set and deep gold at the edges. turn once with a wide spatula and fry 2-3 minutes more, adding the remaining oil around the edges of the pan. drain briefly on paper, squeeze over the remaining lemon, scatter with coriander and eat immediately with rice and dal.

entries.title: Dadpe Pohe
entries.snippet: no-cook flattened rice tossed with coconut, raw onion and a hot tempering
entries.text: dadpe pohe maharashtrian no-cook flattened rice tossed with coconut, raw onion and a hot tempering vegetarian vegan dairy-free gluten-free nut-free poha (flattened rice) coconut (fresh or desiccated) onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime sugar groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) curry leaves dried red chillies salt pick over the thin poha and sieve out the powdery bits, but do not wash it. spread the poha in a wide bowl and layer the coconut, onion, green chilli and coriander over it without mixing. sprinkle over the sugar, salt and the juice of the whole lemon. heat the oil until it shimmers. pop the mustard seeds, add cumin seeds, curry leaves, dried red chillies and asafoetida, and take it off the heat as the curry leaves stop spluttering. stir the turmeric into the hot oil off the heat, then pour the whole tempering over the untouched layers. cover the bowl with a plate and leave it undisturbed 15 minutes — this pressing down is what dadpe means. toss everything together lightly with your fingers, taste for salt and lemon, and eat within the hour.

entries.title: Hirvi Mirchi Cha Thecha
entries.snippet: pounded green chilli and garlic relish, fierce and smoky, eaten with bhakri
entries.text: hirvi mirchi cha thecha maharashtrian pounded green chilli and garlic relish, fierce and smoky, eaten with bhakri vegetarian vegan dairy-free gluten-free nut-free green chilli garlic cumin seeds groundnut oil coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt heat 1 tbsp oil in a flat pan and add the whole chillies and garlic cloves. roast over medium heat 6-8 minutes, turning often, until the chilli skins blister and blacken in patches and the garlic is soft and browned. add the cumin seeds in the last 30 seconds, just to warm them through. cool for 5 minutes, then pound in a mortar with the salt to a coarse, uneven paste — visible flecks of chilli skin, not a smooth puree. work in the coriander with a few more pounds. heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil until it just smokes, pour it over the thecha and stir it through. squeeze in the lemon if using, taste for salt, and serve alongside jowar bhakri, plain rice or dal.

entries.title: Jowar Bhakri
entries.snippet: an unleavened sorghum flatbread patted out by hand, nutty and slightly coarse
entries.text: jowar bhakri maharashtrian an unleavened sorghum flatbread patted out by hand, nutty and slightly coarse vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic jowar (sorghum) flour water salt rice flour bring the water to a rolling boil with the salt. put the flour in a wide bowl and pour in about three quarters of the boiling water, mixing with the handle of a wooden spoon until it comes together in a shaggy mass. as soon as it is cool enough to touch, knead firmly for 5 minutes with the heel of your hand until the dough is smooth and shows no cracks when you press it. divide into 6 balls and keep them covered with a damp cloth. dust the counter with jowar flour, flatten a ball with your palm, then pat it out into a 15cm disc by pressing and rotating with the flat of your fingers. brush the loose flour off, lift the bhakri on your palm and lay it onto the hot tawa. smear the top surface with water using your fingers and cook 1 minute, until the wet film dries and the underside shows pale brown patches. flip and cook the second side 1 minute, then flip once more and press around the edges with a folded cloth until it puffs up like a balloon. stack the finished bhakris in a cloth-lined basket and serve hot with zunka, pithla or usal.

entries.title: Kanda Poha
entries.snippet: flattened rice steamed soft with onion, peanuts and curry leaves, breakfast in fifteen minutes
entries.text: kanda poha maharashtrian flattened rice steamed soft with onion, peanuts and curry leaves, breakfast in fifteen minutes vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free poha (flattened rice) onion peanuts groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds green chilli curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) sugar potato lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) coconut (fresh or desiccated) salt rinse the poha in a colander until the grains soften, then leave it to drain and swell for 10 minutes. toss the drained poha with the turmeric, sugar and salt so every grain turns yellow. do this with your fingertips, not a spoon. fry the peanuts in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until they darken and smell toasted, then lift them out. into the same oil add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, then the cumin, green chilli, curry leaves and hing. add the diced potato, if using, cover and cook 6 minutes until tender. add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned. fold in the poha and the fried peanuts, lower the heat, cover and steam 3 minutes. turn off the heat, squeeze over the lemon and scatter with coriander and grated coconut. serve at once.

entries.title: Katachi Amti
entries.snippet: thin, hot-sour chana dal broth made from the water left over from puran
entries.text: katachi amti maharashtrian thin, hot-sour chana dal broth made from the water left over from puran vegetarian vegan dairy-free gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal water dried coconut (copra) sesame seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) stone flower (dagad phool) cinnamon cloves coriander powder groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder tamarind jaggery coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the soaked chana dal with 5 cups water for 4 whistles, or simmer covered 40 minutes, until soft. strain, keeping every drop of the cloudy water. this is the kat. set the dal aside for puran or another use. dry-roast the dried coconut, sesame, poppy seeds, stone flower, cinnamon and cloves over low heat 4 minutes, until the coconut is golden. cool and grind with the coriander powder to a coarse powder. heat the oil in a pan. pop the mustard seeds, then add cumin seeds, dried red chillies, curry leaves and a generous pinch of asafoetida. add the turmeric and chilli powder, count to five, and pour in the kat immediately so the spices do not burn. stir in the ground masala, tamarind pulp, jaggery and salt, and top up with up to 2 cups water — the amti should be thin enough to drink. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes, until a light froth forms on top and the raw tamarind edge softens. finish with the chopped coriander and serve alongside puran poli with a spoon of ghee, or over plain rice.

entries.title: Kolambi Bhaat
entries.snippet: konkani prawn rice, red with coconut masala and eaten straight from the pot
entries.text: kolambi bhaat maharashtrian konkani prawn rice, red with coconut masala and eaten straight from the pot pescatarian dairy-free gluten-free nut-free healthier prawns rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) dried coconut (copra) onion garlic ginger green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) black pepper turmeric powder cloves cinnamon coconut oil kokum water lemon / lime salt toss the prawns with turmeric, salt and lemon and set aside 15 minutes, refrigerated. dry-roast the dried coconut over low heat for 3 minutes until it smells toasted, then grind it with the fresh coconut, one chopped onion, garlic, ginger, half the coriander leaves and 4 tbsp water to a thick, smooth paste. heat the coconut oil in a heavy pan. add cloves and cinnamon, then the sliced onion and green chillies, and fry 6 minutes until the onion is soft and browning at the tips. add the ground paste and cook on medium 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and oil beads at the edges. stir in the kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, cumin powder, black pepper and remaining turmeric and fry 1 minute. add the prawns and cook 2 minutes only, until they just turn opaque and curl. lift them out onto a plate. add the drained rice to the masala and fold 3 minutes until each grain is coated and glossy. pour in the hot water with the kokum and its soaking liquid, and salt. bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat 12 minutes. scatter the prawns over the rice, cover again and cook 3 more minutes, then rest off the heat 10 minutes. fork through the remaining coriander and serve with lemon wedges.

entries.title: Kolhapuri Chicken Rassa
entries.snippet: thin, fiery red chicken curry built on roasted coconut and dagad phool
entries.text: kolhapuri chicken rassa maharashtrian thin, fiery red chicken curry built on roasted coconut and dagad phool gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken onion dried coconut (copra) coconut (fresh or desiccated) garlic ginger kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder stone flower (dagad phool) poppy seeds (khus khus) sesame seeds coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon black cardamom bay leaf turmeric powder groundnut oil water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt grind the ginger and garlic to a paste and rub half of it into the chicken with the turmeric and salt. leave 30 minutes. dry-roast the grated dried coconut over low heat for 5 minutes until it is dark brown and smells toasted, then tip it out immediately. in the same pan, dry-roast the cumin, black pepper, cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom, stone flower, poppy seeds and sesame for 2 minutes until fragrant. cool completely. fry 2 sliced onions in 2 tbsp of the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until deep brown, then cool. grind the roasted coconut, roasted spices, fried onion, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder and coriander powder with 100ml water to a smooth dark masala. heat the remaining oil in a heavy pan with the bay leaf, add the last onion, finely chopped, and cook 8 minutes until golden. add the remaining ginger-garlic paste, fry 1 minute, then add the chicken and sear over high heat for 5 minutes until the pieces are opaque all over. stir in the ground masala and fry over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, scraping the base, until it darkens and oil pools at the sides. pour in the water, season with salt, bring to a boil then simmer uncovered 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and a red film of oil floats on the surface. stir in the fresh coconut, if using, check the salt and finish with coriander. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with bhakri or chapati and raw onion.

entries.title: Kothimbir Vadi
entries.snippet: steamed coriander and gram flour squares, fried crisp and tempered with sesame
entries.text: kothimbir vadi maharashtrian steamed coriander and gram flour squares, fried crisp and tempered with sesame vegetarian vegan dairy-free gluten-free coriander leaves (cilantro) besan (gram flour) rice flour peanuts sesame seeds green chilli ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder asafoetida (hing) sugar water groundnut oil mustard seeds curry leaves lemon / lime salt chop the coriander finely, stems included, and squeeze it in your fist — it should feel dry, not release green water. mix the coriander with the besan, rice flour, crushed peanut, 1 tbsp sesame, green chilli, ginger, garlic, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, asafoetida, sugar and salt. add water a little at a time to make a thick batter that drops slowly off the spoon — about 1/2 cup. it should be stiffer than pakora batter. stir in 1 tbsp oil, scrape into a greased 15cm tin and level the top. steam over rolling water 20-22 minutes, until a knife inserted in the centre comes out clean and the surface is matte, not tacky. cool completely, 30 minutes at least, then turn out and cut into 4cm squares or diamonds. heat 4 tbsp oil in a kadhai and shallow-fry the squares in batches, 2-3 minutes a side, until the edges are brown and crisp. in the same pan, heat the last tablespoon of oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the remaining sesame and curry leaves and pour it over the fried vadi. squeeze over the lemon and serve hot with green chutney and tea.

entries.title: Masale Bhat
entries.snippet: one-pot spiced rice with vegetables, goda masala spices and a slick of ghee
entries.text: masale bhat maharashtrian one-pot spiced rice with vegetables, goda masala spices and a slick of ghee vegetarian gluten-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) ghee onion peas cauliflower capsicum / bell pepper dried coconut (copra) sesame seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) stone flower (dagad phool) cinnamon cloves bay leaf coriander powder cumin seeds mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder jaggery water salt cashews coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) wash the rice through three changes of water until it runs clear, then leave it to drain 20 minutes. dry-roast the dried coconut, sesame, poppy seeds, stone flower, cinnamon and cloves over low heat for 4-5 minutes, until the coconut turns one shade darker and smells nutty. cool completely, then grind with the coriander powder to a coarse powder. heat the ghee in a heavy pan. crackle the mustard seeds, then add cumin seeds, curry leaves, bay leaf and asafoetida. add the onion and fry 5 minutes, until soft and pale gold at the edges. stir in the cauliflower, capsicum and peas with turmeric, kashmiri chilli and chilli powder. cook 3 minutes so the vegetables take on the fat. add the drained rice and fold gently for 3-4 minutes, until every grain is glossy and the edges look translucent. pour in the hot water, then add the ground masala, jaggery and salt. taste the water — it should read slightly saltier than you want the finished rice. bring to a rolling boil, cover, drop to the lowest heat and cook 12-14 minutes, until the water is gone and small steam craters appear on the surface. rest covered off the heat for 10 minutes, then fork through the fresh coconut, coriander and fried cashews.

entries.title: Matki Usal
entries.snippet: sprouted moth beans in a thin dark gravy of onion, roasted coconut and goda masala
entries.text: matki usal maharashtrian sprouted moth beans in a thin dark gravy of onion, roasted coconut and goda masala vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier sprouted moth/matki beans onion garlic ginger dried coconut (copra) garam masala red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) jaggery tamarind groundnut oil water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt grind the roasted dried coconut with half the onion, the garlic and the ginger to a coarse paste with 3 tbsp water. heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the remaining chopped onion and cook 6 minutes until golden at the edges. stir in the coconut paste and fry 5 minutes over medium heat until it darkens and stops smelling raw. add the chilli powder, kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, turmeric and goda masala and fry 1 minute. tip in the sprouts, turn them through the masala and cook 3 minutes. add the water, salt, jaggery and tamarind, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 18 minutes until the beans are soft but still hold their shape. uncover and check the gravy: it should be thin, dark and slick with red oil on top. loosen with hot water if it has tightened. finish with coriander and serve with bhakri, or with pav and chopped onion.

entries.title: Misal Pav
entries.snippet: Sprouted beans under a fiery kat, topped with farsan and eaten with pav
