entries.text: misal pav maharashtrian sprouted beans under a fiery kat, topped with farsan and eaten with pav vegetarian vegan dairy-free healthier sprouted moth/matki beans onion tomato coconut (fresh or desiccated) garlic ginger red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder garam masala mustard seeds curry leaves peanuts sesame seeds pav / soft bread rolls lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) groundnut oil salt pressure cook the sprouts with turmeric and salt until just tender, 2 whistles. they should hold their shape. for the kat masala, dry roast the coconut, peanut and sesame until deep brown, then blend with two onions, tomato, garlic and ginger to a paste. heat oil, splutter the mustard seeds and curry leaves, add the remaining chopped onion, then the ground paste. fry until the oil separates. add the chilli powder, coriander, cumin and garam masala and cook a further 2 minutes. add 3 cups of hot water and simmer 15 minutes. the kat should be thin and carry a visible layer of red oil. to serve, spoon the usal into bowls, ladle the kat over, and top with farsan, raw onion, coriander and lemon. pav alongside.

entries.title: Patodi Rassa
entries.snippet: vidarbha besan cakes cut into diamonds and floated in a fiery red gravy
entries.text: patodi rassa maharashtrian vidarbha besan cakes cut into diamonds and floated in a fiery red gravy vegetarian vegan dairy-free gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) water carom seeds (ajwain) groundnut oil onion dried coconut (copra) garlic ginger kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon bay leaf turmeric powder sesame seeds coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan into 4 cups cold water with 1/2 tsp turmeric, the ajwain and 1 tsp salt until completely smooth, with no dry pockets. pour into a heavy pan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly with a flat spatula, 12-15 minutes, until the mixture pulls away from the sides in one mass and no longer tastes raw. spread it 1.5cm thick on an oiled tray, smooth the top with an oiled palm and leave to set 30 minutes. for the rassa, dry-roast the dried coconut and sesame until deep gold, 4-5 minutes, then blend with 2 roughly chopped onions, the garlic and ginger and 4 tbsp water to a thick paste. heat 4 tbsp oil in a kadhai. add cumin seeds, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf and black pepper and let them foam for 30 seconds. add the chopped onion and fry 8 minutes to a proper brown, then add the ground paste and cook 10-12 minutes on medium, stirring, until it darkens and oil pools at the edges. stir in the kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, coriander powder and remaining turmeric, fry 1 minute, then pour in 2.5 cups hot water and salt. simmer uncovered 12 minutes, until a red-orange tarri floats on top. cut the set patodi into 4cm diamonds. shallow-fry them in the remaining 2 tbsp oil for 2 minutes a side until lightly crusted, if you want them to hold up better. slide the patodi into the rassa, simmer 3 minutes only, scatter with coriander and serve with jowar bhakri.

entries.title: Pav Bhaji
entries.snippet: mashed vegetables cooked down red and buttery, eaten with griddled pav
entries.text: pav bhaji maharashtrian mashed vegetables cooked down red and buttery, eaten with griddled pav vegetarian nut-free healthier potato cauliflower peas capsicum / bell pepper tomato onion garlic ginger kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder garam masala coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder amchur (dry mango powder) butter pav / soft bread rolls water lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt boil the potato, cauliflower and peas in salted water until completely soft, about 15 minutes, then drain and keep the pan warm. melt 40g of the butter on a large tawa or wide pan and cook the chopped onion over medium heat until soft and translucent, about 6 minutes. add the garlic and ginger and fry 1 minute, until the raw edge disappears. stir in the capsicum and cook 3 minutes, just until it loses its squeak. add the tomato and cook down for 10 minutes, pressing it against the pan, until the mass darkens and oil beads at the edges. add the kashmiri chilli, garam masala, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, amchur and chilli powder and fry 1 minute. tip in the drained vegetables and mash them straight into the pan with a potato masher until no lumps remain. pour in the water, season with salt, and simmer 10 minutes, mashing and stirring, until the bhaji is thick and glossy and a spoon leaves a trail. stir 20g of butter through the bhaji off the heat and scatter with coriander. split the pav, griddle them cut side down in the remaining butter with a pinch of the masala until the edges are crisp and red, about 2 minutes. serve the bhaji with the hot pav, raw chopped onion and lemon wedges.

entries.title: Pithla
entries.snippet: loose gram flour curry slackened with sour buttermilk, garlicky and made in ten minutes
entries.text: pithla maharashtrian loose gram flour curry slackened with sour buttermilk, garlicky and made in ten minutes vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) buttermilk (chaas) garlic green chilli onion groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan into the cold buttermilk with the turmeric and salt until completely smooth, then whisk in the water. heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute until the garlic smells sweet but has not coloured. add the onion, if using, and cook 4 minutes until soft. pour in the besan slurry in a slow stream, stirring continuously. bring to a gentle boil and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and the raw besan smell is gone. check the salt, fold through the coriander and pour into bowls. serve immediately with hot jowar bhakri, raw onion and a green chilli.

entries.title: Puran Poli
entries.snippet: a soft flatbread stuffed with sweet chana dal and jaggery, scented with cardamom and nutmeg
entries.text: puran poli maharashtrian a soft flatbread stuffed with sweet chana dal and jaggery, scented with cardamom and nutmeg vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic chana dal jaggery green cardamom nutmeg atta (wholewheat flour) plain flour (maida) turmeric powder ghee rice flour water salt knead the atta, maida, turmeric, salt, 2 tbsp ghee and enough water into a very soft, sticky dough, working it for 8 minutes until it stretches without tearing. coat the dough with a spoon of ghee, cover and rest at least 1 hour. pressure cook the soaked chana dal with 500ml water for 4 whistles until soft but not disintegrating, then drain it thoroughly in a colander for 10 minutes. mash or pass the drained dal through a sieve until completely smooth. cook the mashed dal with the jaggery in a heavy pan over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture pulls away from the sides and holds a line when you drag a spoon through it. stir in the cardamom and nutmeg and let the puran cool completely — it should be firm enough to roll into balls. divide both dough and puran into 8 portions each, with the puran balls slightly larger than the dough balls. flatten a dough ball in your palm, sit a puran ball in the middle, gather the edges over the top and pinch them shut, then flatten gently. dust with rice flour and roll out very gently to about 18cm, turning often and using almost no pressure. cook on a medium-hot tawa for about 1 minute a side until pale brown spots appear, smearing each side with ghee as you turn it. serve warm with a spoon of ghee poured over, and katachi amti alongside.

entries.title: Sabudana Khichdi
entries.snippet: tapioca pearls turned glassy in ghee with crushed peanuts and green chilli, the fasting-day standby
entries.text: sabudana khichdi maharashtrian tapioca pearls turned glassy in ghee with crushed peanuts and green chilli, the fasting-day standby vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic sabudana (tapioca pearls) peanuts potato ghee cumin seeds green chilli curry leaves sugar lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt check the soaked pearls: one should crush to a smooth paste between thumb and finger with no hard white centre. drain in a colander for 10 minutes. toss the drained sabudana with the ground peanut, sugar and salt until every pearl is coated and the mix looks dry and loose. heat the ghee, add the cumin and let it darken for 20 seconds, then add the green chilli and curry leaves. add the diced potato and fry 2 minutes until the edges catch a little gold. tip in the sabudana, stir once to combine, then cook over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes, turning it over gently every minute. cover, take the pan off the heat and let it stand 2 minutes. squeeze over the lemon, fold through the coriander and serve hot, with a spoonful of plain yogurt alongside if you are not fasting.

entries.title: Sabudana Vada
entries.snippet: crisp fasting fritters of sago and crushed peanut with a soft potato middle
entries.text: sabudana vada maharashtrian crisp fasting fritters of sago and crushed peanut with a soft potato middle vegetarian vegan dairy-free gluten-free sabudana (tapioca pearls) potato peanuts green chilli ginger cumin seeds coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime sugar groundnut oil salt check the soaked sabudana: press a pearl between your fingers. it should flatten completely with no opaque core. combine the drained sabudana, mashed potato, ground peanut, green chilli, ginger, cumin seeds, coriander, lemon juice, sugar and salt with your hands. squeeze a handful — it should hold together without cracking. if it crumbles, mash in a little more potato; if it is sticky, add 2 tbsp more ground peanut. divide into 12 balls and flatten each into a 6cm disc about 1.5cm thick, smoothing the edges so there are no cracks. heat the oil to medium — a pinch of the mixture should rise steadily in about 4 seconds, not instantly. fry 3 or 4 vada at a time for 4-5 minutes, turning once, until deep gold and hard-crisp on the outside. drain on paper and rest 2 minutes — they crisp further as they cool slightly. serve hot with peanut chutney or plain yogurt (yogurt makes it non-vegan).

entries.title: Saoji Mutton
entries.snippet: nagpur's black, oil-slicked mutton curry, hot enough to make your scalp sweat
entries.text: saoji mutton maharashtrian nagpur's black, oil-slicked mutton curry, hot enough to make your scalp sweat gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb onion dried coconut (copra) poppy seeds (khus khus) stone flower (dagad phool) dried red chillies black pepper cloves cinnamon bay leaf coriander powder cumin seeds garlic ginger turmeric powder red chilli powder groundnut oil water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the dried coconut, poppy seeds, stone flower, dried red chillies, black pepper, cloves and cinnamon over low heat for 6-7 minutes, until the coconut is dark gold and the chillies smell smoky. cool completely, then grind the roasted spices with the coriander powder and cumin seeds to a fine dark powder. blend 2 roughly chopped onions with the garlic and ginger and 3 tbsp water to a smooth paste. heat 6 tbsp oil in a heavy pan. fry the sliced onions over medium heat 12-14 minutes until deep brown, not black. add the onion-garlic-ginger paste and fry 8 minutes, until it stops smelling raw and the oil comes back to the surface. add the mutton, turmeric, chilli powder and 2 tsp salt. fry on high 8-10 minutes, until the pieces are seared on all sides and no water is pooling. stir in the ground saoji masala and fry 3 minutes on low so it toasts in the oil without catching. pour in the hot water, bring to a boil, then pressure cook 4-5 whistles, or simmer covered 60-70 minutes until the meat pulls from the bone. open, add the remaining 2 tbsp oil and boil uncovered 8-10 minutes until a dark red tarri rises and floats on the surface. rest 10 minutes off the heat, scatter with coriander, and serve with bhakri or plain rice and raw onion.

entries.title: Sol Kadhi
entries.snippet: pink kokum and coconut milk drink, sour and cooling, drunk at the end of a coastal meal
entries.text: sol kadhi maharashtrian pink kokum and coconut milk drink, sour and cooling, drunk at the end of a coastal meal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free kokum coconut milk garlic green chilli cumin seeds water coriander leaves (cilantro) sugar salt soak the kokum in the warm water 20 minutes, squeezing the petals every few minutes, until the water is a deep pink. squeeze the petals dry and discard them, keeping the pink extract. crush the garlic, green chilli and cumin to a rough paste with a pinch of salt. whisk the coconut milk with the remaining 300ml water until completely smooth and lump-free. stir the kokum extract into the coconut milk a little at a time, tasting as you go, until it is as sour as you want and a pale rose colour. stir in the crushed garlic paste, salt and sugar, and let it stand 10 minutes for the garlic to bloom. chill 30 minutes, stir, scatter with coriander and serve in glasses, or poured over plain rice at the end of the meal.

entries.title: Thalipeeth
entries.snippet: a savoury multigrain flatbread patted out by hand, spiced through and eaten with white butter
entries.text: thalipeeth maharashtrian a savoury multigrain flatbread patted out by hand, spiced through and eaten with white butter vegetarian nut-free jowar (sorghum) flour bajra (pearl millet) flour besan (gram flour) rice flour atta (wholewheat flour) onion coriander leaves (cilantro) green chilli ginger garlic cumin seeds coriander powder turmeric powder red chilli powder carom seeds (ajwain) sesame seeds groundnut oil water butter yogurt / dahi salt combine the jowar, bajra, besan, rice flour and atta in a wide bowl with the salt. add the onion, coriander, green chilli, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander powder, turmeric, chilli powder, ajwain and sesame and rub everything through the flour. pour in the warm water a little at a time and bring it together into a soft dough, softer than chapati dough and only just short of sticky. cover and rest the dough 10 minutes, then divide into 6 balls. oil a square of parchment lightly, put a ball on it and pat it out with wet fingertips into a disc about 15cm across and 5mm thick. poke a hole through the middle with your finger and two or three smaller ones around it. invert the disc onto a hot tawa, peel away the parchment, and drizzle a teaspoon of oil into the centre hole and around the rim. cover and cook 3 minutes over medium heat, then flip and cook a further 3 minutes uncovered until both sides carry dark brown spots. serve hot off the tawa with a lump of white butter melting on top and thick yogurt on the side.

entries.title: Ukadiche Modak
entries.snippet: Steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coconut and jaggery, made for Ganpati
entries.text: ukadiche modak maharashtrian steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coconut and jaggery, made for ganpati vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice flour coconut (fresh or desiccated) jaggery green cardamom nutmeg poppy seeds (khus khus) ghee water salt for the filling, cook the coconut and jaggery together over medium heat until the jaggery melts and the mixture comes together but is still moist, 8-10 minutes. add cardamom, nutmeg and poppy seeds. cool. boil the water with a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of ghee. take it off the heat, tip in the rice flour all at once and stir hard until no dry flour remains. cover 5 minutes. turn out and knead while hot, greasing your palm with ghee, until completely smooth. take a lime-sized ball, flatten into a cup with your fingers, pleat the edge into 9-11 folds, fill, then gather the pleats to a point and seal. steam 10-12 minutes until the shells turn glossy and translucent. serve warm with a spoon of ghee over the top.

entries.title: Vada Pav
entries.snippet: Mumbai's potato fritter in a bun, with garlic chutney and fried chillies
entries.text: vada pav maharashtrian mumbai's potato fritter in a bun, with garlic chutney and fried chillies vegetarian nut-free potato besan (gram flour) pav / soft bread rolls garlic green chilli ginger mustard seeds turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) peanuts red chilli powder coconut (fresh or desiccated) lemon / lime neutral oil salt for the dry chutney, dry roast the peanuts, coconut and 6 garlic cloves separately until fragrant, then grind coarsely with the chilli powder and salt. set aside. crush the remaining garlic, the green chillies and ginger to a coarse paste. heat 2 tbsp oil, splutter the mustard seeds, add the asafoetida and curry leaves, then the garlic-chilli paste. fry 1 minute, add the turmeric, then fold through the mashed potato, coriander, lemon and salt. cool and shape into 8 balls. whisk the besan with a pinch of turmeric, salt and enough water to make a thick, smooth coating batter. rest it 10 minutes. heat the frying oil to 180c. dip each ball in batter, let the excess drip off and lower it in. fry 4-5 minutes until pale gold and crisp, turning once. drain on a rack, not paper. split the pav without cutting all the way through, spread the dry chutney generously inside, press in a hot vada and serve at once with the fried chillies.

entries.title: Varan Bhaat
entries.snippet: plain toor dal with ghee and a touch of jaggery over hot rice, the first course of every festive meal
entries.text: varan bhaat maharashtrian plain toor dal with ghee and a touch of jaggery over hot rice, the first course of every festive meal vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) rice (short/medium grain) turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) ghee jaggery cumin seeds lemon / lime water salt rinse and soak the toor dal 20 minutes, then drain. pressure cook the dal with 500ml water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, or simmer covered 40 minutes, until it collapses at a touch. cook the rice in the remaining water until soft, about 15 minutes, and keep it covered and hot. open the cooker and whisk the dal smooth with a ladle, adding the remaining 200ml water until it pours easily. bring it back to a simmer with the salt, jaggery and hing and cook 5 minutes. heat the ghee, crackle the cumin seeds if using, and pour it into the dal. squeeze in the lemon off the heat and taste for salt. serve a ladle of varan over a mound of hot rice with a spoon of raw ghee on top, and eat it first, before anything else on the plate.

entries.title: Zunka
entries.snippet: dry crumbled gram flour cooked with onion and garlic, sharp with green chilli
entries.text: zunka maharashtrian dry crumbled gram flour cooked with onion and garlic, sharp with green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free besan (gram flour) onion garlic green chilli groundnut oil mustard seeds cumin seeds curry leaves turmeric powder red chilli powder asafoetida (hing) water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt dry-roast the besan in the pan over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it turns a shade darker and smells nutty. tip it out and let it cool. heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, then the cumin, curry leaves and hing. add the onion and cook 5 minutes over medium heat until soft and translucent — soft, not browned. stir in the garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute. add the turmeric, chilli powder and salt, then pour in the hot water and bring it to a boil. lower the heat and sprinkle the roasted besan over the surface in a thin stream with one hand while stirring hard with the other. cover and cook on the lowest heat for 5 minutes without stirring, then take the lid off and break the mass up with a fork into a coarse crumble. drizzle over a spoonful of raw oil, fold through the coriander and serve with jowar bhakri and raw onion.

entries.title: Chana Gashi
entries.snippet: konkani saraswat black chickpeas and sweet potato in a roasted coconut gravy
entries.text: chana gashi karnataka konkani saraswat black chickpeas and sweet potato in a roasted coconut gravy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier kala chana (brown chickpeas) coconut (fresh or desiccated) kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder tamarind turmeric powder sweet potato jaggery coconut oil mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) water salt drain the chickpeas and pressure cook them with 2 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt for 5 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. warm 1 tsp coconut oil in a small pan and roast the chillies over low heat for 90 seconds until they darken slightly. add the coriander powder, roast 30 seconds more and take it off the heat. grind the roasted chillies and coriander with the coconut, turmeric, tamarind pulp and 3/4 cup water to a smooth, fine paste. tip the ground masala into the cooked chickpeas along with their cooking liquid and the sweet potato. add the jaggery, salt and enough water to make a pourable gravy, and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sweet potato is tender. heat the remaining coconut oil in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds, add the curry leaves and the hing, and pour the whole thing over the curry. cover and stand 10 minutes off the heat before serving with rice or neer dosa.

entries.title: Dali Thoy
entries.snippet: the everyday konkani toor dal, thin and clean, finished with hing and green chilli
entries.text: dali thoy karnataka the everyday konkani toor dal, thin and clean, finished with hing and green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) turmeric powder green chilli ginger coconut oil mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) curry leaves dried red chillies coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt pressure cook the dal with 2 1/2 cups water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own. open the cooker and whisk the dal smooth, adding up to 1/2 cup hot water — thoy should pour like thin cream, not sit in a mound. add the green chillies, crushed ginger and salt and simmer 5 minutes on low. taste and check the salt now, while there is still time for it to dissolve evenly. heat the coconut oil in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the mustard seeds and let them pop fully, about 20 seconds. take the pan off the flame, add the broken red chilli, curry leaves and hing, and let them foam in the residual heat for 5 seconds. pour the tempering into the dal, cover immediately and leave it 2 minutes to trap the aroma. stir through the coriander leaves and serve hot over rice with a spoon of coconut oil and a piece of pickle.

entries.title: Halbai
entries.snippet: set rice and coconut milk pudding sweetened with jaggery and cut into soft diamonds
entries.text: halbai karnataka set rice and coconut milk pudding sweetened with jaggery and cut into soft diamonds vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) coconut milk jaggery green cardamom ghee coconut (fresh or desiccated) water salt drain the rice and grind it with 1 cup of the coconut milk to a completely smooth, pourable batter. strain the batter through a fine sieve into a heavy-bottomed pan, pushing through with the back of a ladle. stir in the strained jaggery syrup, the remaining coconut milk and the salt. cook over low heat, stirring continuously with a flat wooden spoon, for about 20 minutes. the mixture will thin first, then thicken and start to gloss and pull away from the sides of the pan. add the ghee a tablespoon at a time, letting each one be absorbed before the next goes in, about 8 minutes more. stir in the crushed cardamom and cook 1 minute more. pour into the greased tray, level the top with a ghee-smeared spatula and scatter the grated coconut over. cool at room temperature for 3 to 4 hours until firm, then cut into diamonds with a greased knife.

entries.title: Kane Rava Fry
entries.snippet: ladyfish rubbed in red chilli paste and shallow fried in a sandy semolina crust
entries.text: kane rava fry karnataka ladyfish rubbed in red chilli paste and shallow fried in a sandy semolina crust pescatarian dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) kashmiri chilli powder garlic ginger tamarind turmeric powder black pepper lemon / lime rava / sooji (semolina) rice flour coconut oil curry leaves salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, tamarind, turmeric and pepper with 2 tbsp of the soaking water to a thick paste. mix in the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt, then rub the paste into the fish, working it into the slits. marinate 30 minutes in the fridge while you get the pan and the rava plate ready. stir the rice flour into the rava on a wide plate. heat 3 tbsp coconut oil in a flat tawa until a pinch of rava dropped in sizzles immediately. press each fish into the rava on both sides, shake off the loose grains and lay it straight into the pan. fry 4 minutes on the first side without touching it, until the crust is set and deep red-gold at the edges. flip once and fry 3 minutes on the second side, adding the remaining oil around the edge of the pan as needed. fry the curry leaves in the last of the hot oil for 15 seconds and scatter them over the fish. drain on a rack, not on paper, and serve hot with raw onion and lemon.

entries.title: Kori Rotti
entries.snippet: bunt chicken curry poured over crisp rice wafers that soften as you eat
entries.text: kori rotti karnataka bunt chicken curry poured over crisp rice wafers that soften as you eat gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken rice flour coconut (fresh or desiccated) kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) black pepper turmeric powder garlic ginger onion tamarind coconut oil curry leaves coconut milk water salt roast the kashmiri and hot chillies in 1 tsp of the coconut oil over low heat until they darken a shade and smell toasty, about 2 minutes. in the same pan roast the coriander powder, cumin, fenugreek and pepper for 1 minute until fragrant, then tip everything onto a plate to cool. fry the sliced onion, garlic and ginger in 1 tbsp coconut oil until the onion is soft and edged with brown, about 8 minutes. grind the cooled spices, the fried onion mixture and the grated coconut with 1/2 cup water to a very smooth, deep red paste. heat the remaining coconut oil in a kadhai, crackle the curry leaves and cook the chopped onion until translucent, about 4 minutes. add the chicken and turmeric and turn it over high heat for 5 minutes, until the pieces stiffen and the surface goes opaque. stir in the ground masala and fry it down for 8 minutes, until it darkens and oil beads at the edge of the pan. pour in 2 cups water and the tamarind extract, salt it, and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy just coats a spoon. stir in the thick coconut milk, warm it through for 1 minute and take the pan off the heat. break the rotti wafers into wide bowls and ladle the hot curry over them at the table.

entries.title: Kundapur Chicken Ghee Roast
entries.snippet: chicken cloaked in a dark tangy byadgi masala fried down in a serious amount of ghee
entries.text: kundapur chicken ghee roast karnataka chicken cloaked in a dark tangy byadgi masala fried down in a serious amount of ghee gluten-free nut-free chicken yogurt / dahi lemon / lime turmeric powder ghee kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) black pepper garlic tamarind jaggery curry leaves water salt drain the soaked chillies and grind them with the garlic, coriander powder, cumin, fenugreek, pepper and tamarind pulp to a thick, smooth paste using as little water as possible. melt 3 tbsp ghee in a kadhai and fry the marinated chicken over high heat for 6 minutes, until the pieces are sealed and patched with brown. lift the chicken out onto a plate, leaving the ghee and any juices behind. add the remaining ghee to the same pan and fry the ground masala on a low flame for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often. stir in the jaggery and 1/2 tsp salt and cook another minute. return the chicken with its juices, toss to coat every piece, add 1/2 cup water and cover. cook on low for 15 minutes, turning the pieces twice, until the chicken is done and the masala clings to it with almost no gravy left. throw in the curry leaves, let them crisp in the hot ghee for 30 seconds, and take it off the heat. rest 5 minutes before serving with neer dosa or plain rice.

entries.title: Meen Gassi
entries.snippet: coastal fish curry in a roasted coconut gravy soured with kokum
entries.text: meen gassi karnataka coastal fish curry in a roasted coconut gravy soured with kokum pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut (fresh or desiccated) kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) black pepper turmeric powder garlic onion kokum coconut oil mustard seeds curry leaves water salt warm 1 tsp coconut oil in a pan and roast the chillies over low heat for 1 minute until they puff slightly and smell toasted. add the coriander powder, cumin, fenugreek and pepper and roast 45 seconds more, then take the pan off the heat. grind the roasted spices with the grated coconut, garlic and the remaining turmeric and 3/4 cup water into a smooth, thick orange paste. heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a wide pan, pop the mustard seeds and add the curry leaves. cook the onion until soft and just turning gold at the edges, about 6 minutes. pour in the ground masala and 1 1/4 cups water, add the kokum with its soaking liquid and salt, and bring it to a gentle simmer. simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the raw coconut smell is gone and the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. slide the fish steaks in in a single layer, spoon gravy over them and cook 7 to 8 minutes without stirring. drizzle over the last 1 tsp raw coconut oil, cover and let it stand 10 minutes off the heat before serving with red rice.

entries.title: Pork Bafat
entries.snippet: catholic wedding-table pork stewed in bafat masala and sharpened with vinegar
entries.text: pork bafat karnataka catholic wedding-table pork stewed in bafat masala and sharpened with vinegar gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies coriander powder cumin seeds black pepper cloves cinnamon mustard seeds turmeric powder garlic ginger onion vinegar potato neutral oil water salt dry roast the chillies, coriander powder, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon and mustard seeds separately over low heat until each smells toasted, 1 to 2 minutes each. cool completely and grind to a fine powder — this is your bafat masala. heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onion over medium heat for 12 minutes, until soft and evenly gold. add the crushed garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes more, until the raw edge is gone. stir in 4 tbsp of the bafat masala and fry for 2 minutes with a splash of water so it does not catch. add the marinated pork and turn it over high heat for 8 minutes, until the cubes are sealed and coated. pour in 2 cups water, cover and simmer on low for 50 minutes, or pressure cook for 4 whistles and let the pressure fall on its own. add the potatoes and cook uncovered 15 minutes, until they are tender and the gravy has thickened around them. stir in the remaining 3 tbsp vinegar, check the salt, and simmer 5 minutes more. rest the pot off the heat for 20 minutes before serving with sanna or plain rice.

entries.title: Pundi Gatti
entries.snippet: steamed tulu rice dumplings speckled with coconut and mustard, eaten with curry or chutney
entries.text: pundi gatti karnataka steamed tulu rice dumplings speckled with coconut and mustard, eaten with curry or chutney vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) urad dal (black gram) mustard seeds green chilli curry leaves coconut oil water salt drain the soaked rice well and grind it coarse with 1/2 cup water — aim for the texture of wet rava, not a smooth batter. heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a heavy pan, pop the mustard seeds and fry the urad dal until it turns light gold, about 1 minute. add the green chilli and curry leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds. pour in 1 cup water with the salt and bring it to a rolling boil. tip in the ground rice and the grated coconut all at once and stir hard over low heat. keep stirring for 6 to 8 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides in one lump and no longer sticks to the spoon. cover the pan and let the dough cool for 10 minutes, until it is warm enough to handle but not cold. with wet palms roll the dough into 12 smooth balls the size of a lime, pressing out any cracks. steam them in a single layer for 12 to 15 minutes, until they are glossy and a skewer comes out clean. rest 5 minutes off the heat before lifting them out, and serve hot with chicken curry, chana gashi or coconut chutney.

entries.title: Aloo Pitika
entries.snippet: mashed potato sharpened with raw mustard oil and onion, the plate-partner to every assamese meal
entries.text: aloo pitika northeast indian mashed potato sharpened with raw mustard oil and onion, the plate-partner to every assamese meal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier potato mustard oil onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water boil the whole potatoes in well-salted water 20 minutes, until a knife slides to the centre with no push. drain and peel them while still hot — the skins slip off between your fingers. mash with your hand or a fork while warm, leaving a little texture. do not use a blender. pour the raw mustard oil straight over the warm mash and work it in until the mash looks glossy and smells sharp. fold in the onion, green chilli, coriander and salt. add the lemon juice, taste, and correct the salt — it needs more than you think against the plain rice it is eaten with. shape into a low mound on the plate and let it stand 5 minutes so the onion softens into the potato.

entries.title: Axone Pork
entries.snippet: naga pork belly stewed to spoon-softness with fermented funk and raw chilli heat
entries.text: axone pork northeast indian naga pork belly stewed to spoon-softness with fermented funk and raw chilli heat gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork dried fish dried red chillies green chilli ginger garlic onion tomato bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) spring onion salt water put the pork cubes in a heavy dry pot over medium heat with 2 tbsp of the water and cook 10 minutes, turning, until the fat has rendered and the cubes are browning in their own fat. add the onion, garlic and half the ginger and fry 5 minutes in the rendered fat, until the onion has gone soft and translucent. stir in the torn dried chillies and the roasted dried fish and fry 2 minutes, until the whole pot smells sharp and savoury. add the tomato, if using, and cook 3 minutes until it breaks down. pour in the rest of the water, add salt, cover and simmer very gently 45 minutes. check at 30 minutes and add a splash if it looks dry. add the bamboo shoot and the green chillies and simmer uncovered 10 minutes more. the pork is ready when a piece of skin gives completely under a spoon and the gravy has reduced to a thick, glossy few centimetres in the base. stir in the remaining ginger julienne and the spring onion, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and serve with plain sticky rice.

entries.title: Bai
entries.snippet: the mizo pot of greens and pumpkin, barely seasoned and softened with an alkaline pinch
entries.text: bai northeast indian the mizo pot of greens and pumpkin, barely seasoned and softened with an alkaline pinch vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier mustard greens (sarson) pumpkin french beans bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) colocasia (arbi) baking soda green chilli ginger salt water bring the water to a boil in a wide pot with the salt, slit chillies and ginger. add the colocasia, if using, and boil 10 minutes — it takes longer than everything else and must be cooked right through. add the pumpkin and boil 6 minutes, until the edges have just started to soften. add the beans and bamboo shoot and cook 4 minutes. pile in the mustard greens, push them under the liquid and cook 4 minutes, until they have collapsed and turned dark. stir in the baking soda and simmer 3 minutes more. the greens will soften noticeably and the broth thickens a little. crush a few pieces of pumpkin against the side of the pot to thicken the liquid, taste for salt, and serve hot with rice and a chilli chutney.

entries.title: Bilahi Pitika
entries.snippet: fire-roasted tomatoes mashed with raw mustard oil, onion and green chilli
entries.text: bilahi pitika northeast indian fire-roasted tomatoes mashed with raw mustard oil, onion and green chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier tomato mustard oil onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) salt lemon / lime set the tomatoes directly on a gas flame over medium heat and turn them with tongs every couple of minutes, 8-10 minutes in all, until the skins blister black and split and the flesh sags. drop the hot tomatoes into a bowl and cover it for 5 minutes. peel away and discard the skins, tipping every drop of juice back into the bowl. mash with a fork or your fingers to a coarse, lumpy pulp. fold in the raw mustard oil and salt and leave it 2 minutes. stir in the onion, green chilli and coriander. taste, and add the lemon juice only if it tastes flat. serve at room temperature in a heap beside plain rice, with dal poured over the rice.

entries.title: Chakhwi
entries.snippet: Tripuri bamboo shoot stew with raw papaya and a low, savoury note of dried fish
entries.text: chakhwi northeast indian tripuri bamboo shoot stew with raw papaya and a low, savoury note of dried fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) raw green papaya dried fish potato green chilli garlic ginger turmeric powder water salt rice flour french beans neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-toast the dried fish over low heat for 3 minutes until brittle and strongly fragrant, then crumble it. warm the oil in a deep pan and fry the garlic and ginger for 1 minute until they smell sweet. add the bamboo shoot and cook 4 minutes, until the sharp raw smell softens. stir in the crumbled fish and the turmeric and cook 1 minute. add the papaya, potato and water, bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered 20 minutes until the papaya turns translucent at the edges. add the beans and green chillies and simmer 6 minutes more. stir in the slaked rice flour and cook 2 minutes, until the broth thickens just enough to leave a film on the spoon. season with salt — the dried fish has done much of the work — scatter the coriander and serve with rice.

entries.title: Chamthong
entries.snippet: the manipuri everyday vegetable stew, clear and light and lifted by fermented fish
entries.text: chamthong northeast indian the manipuri everyday vegetable stew, clear and light and lifted by fermented fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pumpkin potato french beans cabbage amaranth greens (chaulai) dried fish onion ginger green chilli spring onion neutral oil salt water dry-roast the dried fish 3 minutes over low heat until brittle and toasty, then break it into rough pieces. bring the water to a boil in a wide pot with the onion, ginger, green chillies, roasted fish and salt. boil 5 minutes. add the potato and pumpkin and boil 8 minutes, uncovered, until the potato is nearly done. add the beans and cook 4 minutes. add the cabbage and cook 3 minutes, until it has just wilted but still has a bite. stir in the amaranth greens and the tablespoon of oil and cook 2 minutes more. taste for salt, scatter over the spring onion and serve hot in bowls alongside rice.

entries.title: Doh Khleh
entries.snippet: khasi pork salad — boiled meat tossed hot with onion, chilli and a lot of lemon
entries.text: doh khleh northeast indian khasi pork salad — boiled meat tossed hot with onion, chilli and a lot of lemon gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork onion green chilli ginger lemon / lime black pepper sesame seeds coriander leaves (cilantro) bay leaf salt water bring the water to a boil with the bay leaf and a generous tablespoon of salt, lower in the pork and simmer 35 minutes. test it with a skewer — it should go in easily but the meat should still hold together, not shred. meanwhile toss the sliced onion with a big pinch of salt and leave it in a bowl for 20 minutes. roast the sesame in a dry pan 2 minutes, until it pops and smells toasted, then grind it coarsely. lift the pork out, rest it 5 minutes, then cut it into 1.5cm dice, fat and all. while it is still warm, toss the pork with the onion and any liquid in its bowl, the ginger, green chilli and crushed black pepper. add the lemon juice and check the salt — the boiling water has seasoned the meat already, so taste before adding more. fold in the ground sesame and coriander and serve at room temperature, on its own or with plain rice.

entries.title: Doh Neiiong
entries.snippet: Khasi pork stewed in ground black sesame until the gravy turns dark and nutty
entries.text: doh neiiong northeast indian khasi pork stewed in ground black sesame until the gravy turns dark and nutty gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork sesame seeds onion ginger garlic black pepper turmeric powder green chilli neutral oil water salt bay leaf dry-roast the sesame seeds in a heavy pan over low heat for 4-5 minutes, shaking constantly, until they start to pop and smell strongly nutty. cool the seeds completely, then blend with the chopped onion and 4 tbsp water to a thick, slightly coarse paste. put the pork in a pan with the turmeric, 1 tsp salt, the bay leaf and 300ml of the water. bring to a boil and simmer covered 20 minutes, skimming the grey foam off the top. heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the sliced onion for 8 minutes until deep gold and shrunken. add the ginger and garlic and cook 2 minutes until the raw smell is gone. lift the pork out of its liquor into the kadhai, keeping the liquor. add the cracked pepper and fry hard for 8 minutes, turning, until the cubes take on brown edges and the pan looks dry. stir in the sesame paste and cook 3 minutes, then add the reserved pork liquor and the remaining 200ml water. simmer uncovered 20-25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the gravy darkens, thickens enough to coat the pork, and fat beads at the rim. add the green chillies, check the salt, and simmer 5 minutes more. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Eromba
entries.snippet: manipuri mash of boiled vegetables, fierce chilli and fermented fish, eaten with rice
entries.text: eromba northeast indian manipuri mash of boiled vegetables, fierce chilli and fermented fish, eaten with rice pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier potato eggplant / brinjal french beans dried fish dried red chillies spring onion coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water dry-roast the dried fish in a small pan over low heat for 3 minutes, turning, until it smells toasty and goes brittle. crumble it and set aside. roast the dried red chillies in the same pan 40 seconds a side, until they darken and puff slightly. pound them to a coarse paste with a pinch of salt. boil the potato in the water for 8 minutes. add the eggplant and beans and boil 8 minutes more, until everything is completely tender and the potato is starting to fall apart. drain, keeping about 100ml of the cooking water. mash the vegetables roughly in the pot with the back of a ladle, leaving some lumps. work in the crumbled fish, the chilli paste and salt, adding the reserved water a spoon at a time until it is thick and scoopable. fold in the spring onion and coriander off the heat and serve at room temperature with hot rice.

entries.title: Galho
entries.snippet: Naga one-pot of rice cooked down with smoked pork and bitter greens into a soft porridge
entries.text: galho northeast indian naga one-pot of rice cooked down with smoked pork and bitter greens into a soft porridge gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) pork mustard greens (sarson) garlic ginger onion dried red chillies black pepper water salt colocasia (arbi) put the pork, onion, garlic, ginger, dried chillies and 800ml of the water in a pressure cooker and cook for 15 minutes at pressure, or simmer covered for 45 minutes. release the pressure, open up, and skim off any heavy fat sitting on the surface, leaving a thin slick behind. add the rinsed rice, the colocasia and the remaining 700ml water. bring back to a boil. simmer uncovered on low for 20 minutes, stirring every 4 or 5 minutes and scraping the base, until the grains have burst and swollen. stir in the greens a handful at a time. they will look like far too much and will collapse within 2 minutes. cook another 8 minutes until the greens are tender and the whole thing is the consistency of loose porridge. add the cracked pepper and salt to taste. remember the smoked pork has already salted it. take it off the heat, cover, and let it sit 5 minutes — it thickens noticeably. loosen with hot water and serve in bowls.

entries.title: Gundruk ko Jhol
entries.snippet: sour Sikkimese greens broth, thin and hot, drunk alongside a plate of rice
entries.text: gundruk ko jhol northeast indian sour sikkimese greens broth, thin and hot, drunk alongside a plate of rice vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mustard greens (sarson) vinegar potato tomato garlic ginger onion turmeric powder fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies mustard oil water salt heat the mustard oil until it smokes, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds. add the fenugreek seeds and dried chillies and fry for 15 seconds only, until the seeds turn one shade darker. add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook 3 minutes until the onion is translucent. stir in the chopped greens and cook 4 minutes, pressing them down, until they have wilted right down and turned dark. add the tomato and turmeric and cook 3 minutes until the tomato has slumped. add the potato and the water, bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the potato is soft enough to crush against the side. crush 3 or 4 pieces of potato into the broth to give it the faintest body, and season with salt. take the pan off the heat, stir in the vinegar, and stand 2 minutes before ladling out.

entries.title: Hanhor Mangkho
entries.snippet: assamese duck stewed slowly with ash gourd, peppery and lean rather than creamy
entries.text: hanhor mangkho northeast indian assamese duck stewed slowly with ash gourd, peppery and lean rather than creamy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier duck ash gourd (petha) mustard oil onion ginger garlic black pepper bay leaf cinnamon cloves black cardamom turmeric powder green chilli salt water put the duck pieces in a dry heavy pot over medium heat and cook 6 minutes, turning, until fat pools in the base. pour that fat off and set the duck aside. heat the mustard oil in the same pot until it smokes, cool it a minute, then fry the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and black cardamom for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the sliced onion and cook 12 minutes over medium heat, until deep gold and shrunk to a third of its volume. stir in the ginger and garlic paste and fry 3 minutes, until the raw smell goes and the oil starts to separate at the edges. add the turmeric and crushed black pepper, stir for 20 seconds, then return the duck and toss to coat every piece. fry the duck in the masala 8 minutes, scraping the base as it catches, until the pieces are browned all over. pour in the hot water, add salt, cover and simmer very gently 45 minutes, until a skewer goes into the thigh with no resistance. add the ash gourd and green chillies and simmer uncovered 15 minutes more, until the gourd is translucent and the gravy has reduced to a coating consistency. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Jadoh
entries.snippet: khasi rice cooked through with pork, ginger and black pepper, meghalaya's one-pot meal
entries.text: jadoh northeast indian khasi rice cooked through with pork, ginger and black pepper, meghalaya's one-pot meal gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) pork onion ginger garlic black pepper turmeric powder bay leaf green chilli neutral oil spring onion salt water heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the diced pork over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, until it has rendered its fat and the edges are browned and crisp. add the bay leaves and sliced onion and cook 8 minutes in the pork fat, until the onion is gold and sticky. stir in the ginger and garlic and fry 2 minutes, until the raw edge has gone. add the turmeric and crushed black pepper and stir for 30 seconds. tip in the drained rice and toss gently for 3 minutes, until every grain is coated and glossy and the rice smells toasted. pour in the hot water, add the green chillies and salt, and bring to a fast boil. as soon as the water level drops to the surface of the rice, cover tightly, drop the heat to its lowest and cook 12 minutes undisturbed. take it off the heat and rest, still covered, 10 minutes. fluff with a fork, scatter over the spring onion and serve.

entries.title: Masor Jhol
entries.snippet: the everyday Assamese fish curry, thin and turmeric-yellow with potato and tomato
entries.text: masor jhol northeast indian the everyday assamese fish curry, thin and turmeric-yellow with potato and tomato pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) turmeric powder mustard oil potato tomato onion ginger garlic green chilli panch phoron coriander powder water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) rub the fish with 1/2 tsp of the turmeric and 1 tsp salt and set it aside for 10 minutes. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes and the sharp smell fades, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds. fry the fish in the hot oil, 2 minutes a side, until the edges are set and pale gold. lift out onto a plate. in the same oil, fry the potato quarters for 4 minutes until the cut faces are gold. lift them out too. drop the panch phoron into the oil and let it crackle for about 20 seconds until the fennel seeds turn a shade darker. add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft and just gold, then the ginger and garlic for 1 minute more, until the raw garlic smell goes. stir in the tomato, the remaining 1 tsp turmeric and the coriander powder, and mash it about for 4 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil beads at the edge of the pan. pour in the water, return the potato, bring to a boil and simmer 10 minutes until a knife goes into the potato without resistance. slide the fish back in with the green chillies and simmer uncovered 5 minutes. do not stir — shake the pan by the handle instead. take it off the heat, rest 5 minutes, scatter the coriander leaves and serve with hot rice.

entries.title: Masor Tenga
entries.snippet: assam's daily sour fish curry, thin and lemon-bright rather than rich
entries.text: masor tenga northeast indian assam's daily sour fish curry, thin and lemon-bright rather than rich pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard oil tomato fenugreek seeds (methi) turmeric powder green chilli potato lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a wide pan until it smokes, take it off the heat for a minute, then fry the fish steaks 2 minutes a side until the edges are golden. lift them out onto a plate. in the same oil, crackle the fenugreek seeds for about 10 seconds, until they darken a shade and smell nutty. slide in the potato wedges and fry 4 minutes, until the cut edges look translucent. add the tomato, the rest of the turmeric, the slit chillies and salt. cook 5 minutes, pressing the tomato with the back of the spoon, until it slumps and gives up its water. pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 minutes uncovered, until the potato gives easily to a knife. slide the fish back in, spoon broth over each piece and simmer 4 minutes more. shake the pan rather than stirring. take the pan off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and coriander, and let it sit 5 minutes before serving over plain rice.

entries.title: Momos
entries.snippet: Steamed dumplings with a juicy filling, eaten with a fiery tomato-chilli chutney
entries.text: momos northeast indian steamed dumplings with a juicy filling, eaten with a fiery tomato-chilli chutney dairy-free nut-free plain flour (maida) chicken cabbage onion spring onion garlic ginger black pepper dried red chillies tomato neutral oil salt knead the flour with water and a pinch of salt into a firm, smooth dough. rest 30 minutes covered. mix the filling ingredients with the oil and pepper. salt it only when you are ready to fill. roll the dough very thin and cut 8cm rounds, keeping the edges thinner than the centre. place a spoon of filling in each, then pleat and seal into a half-moon or a gathered purse. steam in a greased steamer for 10-12 minutes. the wrappers turn translucent and stop looking floury. for the chutney, boil the tomatoes and dried chillies, then blend with garlic and salt. serve alongside.

entries.title: Muya Awandru
entries.snippet: tripura's oil-free bamboo shoot pot, thickened with rice flour and pungent with dried fish
entries.text: muya awandru northeast indian tripura's oil-free bamboo shoot pot, thickened with rice flour and pungent with dried fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) dried fish rice flour potato french beans green chilli ginger garlic coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water rinse the bamboo shoot twice, cover with fresh water, boil 5 minutes and drain. dry-roast the dried fish in a small pan over low heat 3 minutes, until brittle and toasty, then break it into pieces. bring the 800ml of water to a boil with the crushed ginger, garlic, green chillies, roasted fish and salt. boil 5 minutes so the broth takes on the flavours. add the drained bamboo shoot and the potato and simmer 12 minutes, uncovered. add the beans and cook 5 minutes, until the potato is soft enough to break with a spoon. stir the rice flour into 4 tbsp cold water until completely smooth, with no dry specks. pour the slurry into the simmering pot in a thin stream, stirring the whole time, and cook 4 minutes until the liquid turns glossy and coats the back of a spoon. taste for salt and heat, stir in the coriander and serve hot with plain rice.

entries.title: Naga Smoked Pork with Bamboo Shoot
entries.snippet: Smoked pork simmered with fermented bamboo shoot and raja mircha
entries.text: naga smoked pork with bamboo shoot northeast indian smoked pork simmered with fermented bamboo shoot and raja mircha gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier pork bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) green chilli ginger garlic onion tomato coriander leaves (cilantro) salt rinse the fermented bamboo shoot in two changes of water and drain. put the smoked pork in a pot with the ginger, garlic, chillies and just enough water to cover. bring to a boil. simmer covered 45-60 minutes until the pork is tender and the water has reduced by half. add the bamboo shoot and the onion and tomato if using, and cook a further 15 minutes. season with salt only at the end; smoked pork is already salty. serve with plain rice and a raw chilli on the side.

entries.title: Nga Thongba
entries.snippet: Manipuri fish curry, thin and ginger-sharp, built on a small hit of fermented fish
entries.text: nga thongba northeast indian manipuri fish curry, thin and ginger-sharp, built on a small hit of fermented fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) dried fish mustard oil onion garlic ginger turmeric powder green chilli tomato spring onion water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-toast the dried fish in a small pan over low heat for 3 minutes, until it is brittle and smells strongly nutty. crumble it and set it aside. rub the fish pieces with 1/2 tsp of the turmeric and 1 tsp salt and leave them while you prepare the rest. heat the mustard oil until it smokes, rest it off the heat 30 seconds, then fry the fish 90 seconds a side just to set the surface. lift it out. in the same oil cook the onion 4 minutes until translucent, then add the garlic and half the ginger for 1 minute. add the tomato and the remaining 1/2 tsp turmeric and cook 4 minutes, pressing the tomato until it breaks down. stir in the crumbled toasted fish and cook 1 minute — the smell should turn savoury rather than sharp. pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer 8 minutes uncovered so it stays thin but tastes concentrated. slide the fish back in with the green chillies and the rest of the ginger. simmer 5 minutes without stirring, tilting the pan instead. off the heat, scatter the spring onion and coriander and stand 3 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Omita Khar
entries.snippet: the alkaline assamese opener — raw papaya simmered soft, plain and cleansing
entries.text: omita khar northeast indian the alkaline assamese opener — raw papaya simmered soft, plain and cleansing vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free raw green papaya baking soda mustard oil whole urad (sabut urad) green chilli turmeric powder coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a heavy pan until it smokes, then let it cool for a minute. fry the drained urad 2 minutes until deep gold and lift it out with a slotted spoon. keep it for the end. drop in the slit chillies and let them blister 30 seconds. add the papaya, turmeric and salt and toss 3 minutes, until the cut edges look glassy. pour in the water, cover and simmer 12 minutes, until a fork goes through a cube with no resistance. stir in the baking soda and simmer uncovered 5 minutes. it will foam up and settle, and the liquid turns faintly silky. crush four or five cubes against the side of the pan to thicken the broth, then scatter over the fried urad and coriander and serve at once.

entries.title: Ooti
entries.snippet: Manipuri dried peas simmered soft with bamboo shoot and finished with burnt chilli oil
entries.text: ooti northeast indian manipuri dried peas simmered soft with bamboo shoot and finished with burnt chilli oil vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier dried white peas (safed matar) baking soda bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) spring onion green chilli mustard oil dried red chillies water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) drain the soaked peas and pressure cook them with 800ml of the water, the baking soda and 1 tsp salt — 5 whistles, or about 20 minutes at pressure. let the pressure drop on its own, open up, and crush about a quarter of the peas against the side of the pan. add the bamboo shoot and the remaining 400ml water and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes. the sourness sharpens as it reduces. stir in the spring onion whites and the green chillies and simmer another 10 minutes, until the stew coats the back of a spoon. check the consistency: it should pour thickly, not sit in a mound. loosen with hot water if it has gone too far. in a small pan heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off the heat for 20 seconds, then drop in the dried red chillies for 20 seconds until they darken and smell toasty. pour the chilli oil over the ooti and stir it through once, leaving streaks. scatter the spring onion greens and coriander, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and serve with rice.

entries.title: Pika Pila
entries.snippet: Apatani bamboo shoot pickle, fiercely sour and hot, eaten a spoonful at a time
entries.text: pika pila northeast indian apatani bamboo shoot pickle, fiercely sour and hot, eaten a spoonful at a time gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier bamboo shoot (fermented or fresh) pork dried red chillies ginger garlic turmeric powder mustard oil lemon / lime salt render the diced pork fat in a dry pan over low heat for about 12 minutes, until the pieces are shrunken and gold and swimming in clear fat. lift the crisp pieces out with a slotted spoon and set them aside, leaving the fat in the pan. fry the dried chillies in the fat for 30 seconds until they darken and the kitchen makes you cough. add the ginger and garlic and cook 2 minutes until pale gold. stir in the squeezed bamboo shoot, turmeric and salt and cook 8 minutes over medium heat, stirring often, until the liquid has dried off and it no longer smells raw. return the crackling, pour in the raw mustard oil, the lemon juice and the reserved bamboo liquor, and cook 2 minutes more. taste for salt and sourness. it should be sharp enough to make you flinch. cool completely, uncovered, before spooning into the jar and pressing down so the oil covers the surface.

entries.title: Poita Bhat
entries.snippet: cooked rice soaked overnight until faintly sour, eaten cold with mustard oil and onion
entries.text: poita bhat northeast indian cooked rice soaked overnight until faintly sour, eaten cold with mustard oil and onion vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) water mustard oil onion green chilli salt potato coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime boil the rice in the 1.5 litres of water for 15-18 minutes, until the grains are soft and just past the point you would normally stop. drain and spread the rice in a wide bowl. leave it uncovered until it is completely cool to the touch, about 30 minutes. pour in cold water to cover the rice by about 3cm, cover the bowl loosely and leave it overnight. next morning the water should smell faintly sour and clean, a little like buttermilk. pour off most of it, keeping 3-4 tbsp in the bowl. break the clumped rice up with your fingers until it is loose again. fold through the raw mustard oil and salt. stir in the onion, green chilli and coriander, and squeeze over the lemon. serve cold, with the mashed potato and a green chilli on the side.

entries.title: Sanpiau
entries.snippet: Mizo rice porridge under a drift of toasted rice powder, coriander and black pepper
entries.text: sanpiau northeast indian mizo rice porridge under a drift of toasted rice powder, coriander and black pepper vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) rice flour coriander leaves (cilantro) spring onion black pepper dried red chillies lemon / lime water salt bring the rice and water to a boil, then turn the heat right down. simmer 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the base, until the grains have burst and the whole thing is a loose porridge the consistency of thin oatmeal. season with salt and keep it hot on the lowest heat. meanwhile dry-roast the rice flour in a small pan over low heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring without stopping, until it is sandy brown and smells like popcorn. tip the toasted flour onto a cold plate and spread it out to cool — it only stays loose and powdery once cold. dry-roast the chillies in the same pan for 40 seconds until brittle, then crush them coarsely. ladle the porridge into bowls, loosening it with hot water if it has thickened while standing. top each bowl with a heaped teaspoon of the toasted rice powder, then a thick layer of coriander, the spring onion, the pepper and a pinch of crushed chilli. serve with a lemon wedge to squeeze over at the table.

entries.title: Sel Roti
entries.snippet: crisp-edged ring of fried fermented rice batter, lightly sweet and cardamom-scented
entries.text: sel roti northeast indian crisp-edged ring of fried fermented rice batter, lightly sweet and cardamom-scented vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) sugar ghee green cardamom milk water salt neutral oil cloves drain the soaked rice thoroughly and spread it on a cloth for 15 minutes until the surface looks dry. grind the rice in batches with the milk and only as much of the water as it takes to move the blades, to a thick, completely smooth batter. beat in the sugar, melted ghee, ground cardamom, cloves and salt, then beat by hand for a good 5 minutes. cover and leave in a warm place for 3-4 hours, until the batter has risen slightly and smells faintly sweet and sour. heat the oil in a kadhai to about 170c — a drop of batter should sink briefly, then rise within 3 seconds. pour the batter into a squeeze bottle or a piping bag. working quickly, pipe a 12cm ring onto the surface of the oil, joining the ends. let it fry undisturbed 1 minute, until it floats free and the top loses its shine. turn it with a skewer through the hole and fry another 2 minutes until both sides are a deep reddish gold. drain on a wire rack, not paper, and fry the rest one or two at a time. cool at least 10 minutes before eating — the crispness only arrives as they cool.

entries.title: Singju
entries.snippet: manipur's raw-vegetable salad bound with roasted gram flour and loud with chilli
entries.text: singju northeast indian manipur's raw-vegetable salad bound with roasted gram flour and loud with chilli pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier cabbage radish (mooli) spring onion besan (gram flour) sesame seeds dried fish dried red chillies coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt dry-roast the besan over low heat for 4 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns a shade darker and smells nutty. tip it straight out of the pan. roast the sesame in the same pan 2 minutes until the seeds start popping, then grind them coarsely. roast the dried red chillies 40 seconds a side until they darken, and pound them coarse. roast the dried fish 3 minutes over low heat until brittle, then crumble it fine. toss the cabbage, radish and spring onion in a wide bowl with the salt and leave 5 minutes. squeeze the vegetables gently with your hands and pour off any water that has come out. scatter over the roasted besan, ground sesame, crumbled fish and pounded chilli, and mix with your fingers until every shred is coated and the flour has stopped looking powdery. add the lemon juice and coriander, toss once more and serve immediately as a side or an evening snack.

entries.title: Thukpa
entries.snippet: sikkim's hand-torn noodle soup, chicken broth thick with vegetables and pepper
entries.text: thukpa northeast indian sikkim's hand-torn noodle soup, chicken broth thick with vegetables and pepper dairy-free nut-free plain flour (maida) chicken onion garlic ginger tomato carrot cabbage spinach spring onion black pepper turmeric powder red chilli powder neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water mix the maida with 1/2 tsp salt and enough water — about 120ml — to make a firm, slightly stiff dough. knead 8 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest 30 minutes. heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onion, garlic and ginger 5 minutes over medium heat, until the onion is soft and the garlic smells sweet. add the chicken strips and fry 5 minutes, until they have lost their pink and picked up a little colour at the edges. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and crushed black pepper for 20 seconds, then add the tomato and cook 5 minutes until it collapses. pour in the 1.2 litres of water, add salt, and simmer 15 minutes with the lid ajar. while it simmers, roll the rested dough out to about 2mm and cut or tear it into ribbons roughly 2cm wide and 10cm long. dust them with flour and keep them separate. add the carrot to the simmering broth and cook 3 minutes. drop the noodles in a few at a time, stirring so they do not clump, and boil 4 minutes until they float and turn from chalky to translucent. add the cabbage and spinach and cook 2 minutes more, until the spinach has just wilted. taste for salt and pepper, ladle into deep bowls and finish with spring onion and coriander.

entries.title: Aloo Potala Rasa
entries.snippet: potato and pointed gourd in a thin, cumin-scented tomato gravy, made without onion or garlic
entries.text: aloo potala rasa odia potato and pointed gourd in a thin, cumin-scented tomato gravy, made without onion or garlic vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier pointed gourd (parwal) potato tomato ginger green chilli cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. fry the halved pointed gourd on medium for 5 minutes, turning, until blistered and lightly browned. lift out and set aside. in the same oil add the bay leaf and cumin seeds and let them sizzle 15 seconds. add the grated ginger and slit green chillies and fry 1 minute. add the potato quarters and fry 4 minutes until the edges are golden. pour in the tomato puree with the turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt. fry 6-8 minutes until the oil beads at the edges. add the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender. return the fried pointed gourd and simmer uncovered 5 minutes. the gravy should stay thin — this is a rasa, not a thick curry. stir in the garam masala, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Arisa Pitha
entries.snippet: deep-fried jaggery and rice flour discs crusted with sesame, chewy in the middle
entries.text: arisa pitha odia deep-fried jaggery and rice flour discs crusted with sesame, chewy in the middle vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice flour jaggery water sesame seeds green cardamom neutral oil salt melt the jaggery with the water in a pan over medium heat, stirring until dissolved, then strain out any grit. boil the syrup 5 to 6 minutes until a drop pressed between finger and thumb pulls a single short thread as they part. take the syrup off the heat, add the pinch of salt and the cardamom, and let it cool 2 minutes. pour the hot syrup over the roasted rice flour in a wide bowl and mix with a spoon until it comes together as a shaggy mass. when it is cool enough to handle, knead 5 minutes with oiled hands into a smooth dough the softness of an earlobe. cover and rest at least 4 hours or overnight at room temperature. divide into 14 balls, flatten each between oiled palms into a 7cm disc, and press one side firmly into the sesame seeds. heat the oil in a kadhai to medium — a scrap of dough should rise slowly and sizzle steadily, not fizz violently. slide in 2 or 3 discs sesame-side down and fry 3 minutes a side, spooning oil over, until deep reddish brown. lift onto a rack, not paper, and let them cool completely; they firm from soft to chewy as they cool.

entries.title: Badi Chura
entries.snippet: crushed fried lentil dumplings pounded with raw onion, chilli and mustard oil
entries.text: badi chura odia crushed fried lentil dumplings pounded with raw onion, chilli and mustard oil vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free urad dal (black gram) mustard oil onion garlic green chilli salt coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime heat the mustard oil in a small kadhai over medium until it shimmers and smells sharp. fry the badi, turning often, for 4 to 5 minutes until they are deep chestnut brown all over and float lightly. lift them out onto paper and let them cool for 5 minutes — they crisp as they cool, not in the pan. pound the garlic and green chillies with 1/4 tsp of the salt into a rough, wet paste. break the cooled badi into the mortar and crush to coarse gravel, leaving a few pea-sized pieces for bite. tip the crushed badi into a bowl with the chopped onion, the garlic-chilli paste and the remaining salt. pour over 1 tbsp of the warm frying oil straight from the pan and rub everything together with your fingers. squeeze in the lemon, fold through the coriander, taste for salt and serve at once alongside pakhala or plain rice.

entries.title: Besara
entries.snippet: mixed vegetables in a sharp ground-mustard gravy, pungent enough to make your eyes water
entries.text: besara odia mixed vegetables in a sharp ground-mustard gravy, pungent enough to make your eyes water vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mustard seeds garlic green chilli potato eggplant / brinjal pumpkin raw banana / plantain drumstick (moringa pod) panch phoron dried red chillies turmeric powder mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked mustard seeds, garlic, 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste with 4 tbsp water. set aside. heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the panch phoron and broken dried red chillies. when the seeds pop and the chillies darken, about 20 seconds, add the slit green chilli. add the potato and raw banana and fry 3 minutes, stirring, until the surfaces turn matte. add the pumpkin, eggplant and drumstick with the turmeric and salt. fry 2 minutes more. pour in the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is nearly tender. lower the flame to its weakest setting and stir in the mustard paste. do not let it boil hard from here on. simmer uncovered on low for 6-8 minutes, until the raw smell of the mustard has gone and the gravy coats a spoon. taste for salt, stir in the coriander leaves and take off the heat. rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Chakuli Pitha
entries.snippet: soft fermented rice and urad pancakes, thicker and paler than a dosa
entries.text: chakuli pitha odia soft fermented rice and urad pancakes, thicker and paler than a dosa vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) sugar neutral oil water salt stir the salt into the fermented batter and let it down with water until it is the consistency of thick cream, thicker than dosa batter. heat a flat tawa over medium until a drop of water skitters and vanishes in about 2 seconds. rub the surface with half an onion or a scrunched paper towel dipped in oil and wipe off the excess. pour a ladleful into the centre and spread it with the back of the ladle in one slow spiral to about 15cm — chakuli is meant to be thick and soft, not lace-thin. drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the rim and cook 2 minutes, until the top loses its shine and small holes open across the surface. flip and cook the second side 1 minute, until it is set and speckled pale gold. slide it off and repeat, wiping and re-oiling the tawa between each one and dropping the heat a notch if they start browning too fast. stack them under a cloth as you go so they steam each other soft, and serve hot with ghuguni or a mustardy vegetable curry.

entries.title: Chhatu Rai
entries.snippet: mushrooms simmered in a hot mustard and poppy seed gravy, a monsoon favourite
entries.text: chhatu rai odia mushrooms simmered in a hot mustard and poppy seed gravy, a monsoon favourite vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mushrooms mustard seeds poppy seeds (khus khus) garlic ginger green chilli tomato mustard oil panch phoron turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes lightly, then lower to medium-high. add the mushrooms with 1/2 tsp salt and fry hard for 6 to 7 minutes, without stirring much, until they have given up their water and the edges are browned. scoop the mushrooms out and set aside, leaving the oil in the pan. crackle the panch-phoron in the same oil for 20 seconds until it pops and smells nutty. add the crushed garlic and ginger and fry for 2 minutes until the raw edge goes and the paste turns straw coloured. stir in the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and cumin powder and cook for 5 minutes, pressing with the spoon, until the tomato breaks down and oil beads at the sides. return the mushrooms, pour in the water, and simmer uncovered for 6 minutes. drop the heat to its lowest, stir in the mustard-poppy paste and the remaining slit green chilli, and cook 4 minutes at a bare simmer. taste for salt, take off the heat and finish with the coriander and a teaspoon of raw mustard oil.

entries.title: Chhena Poda
entries.snippet: Odisha's baked cheesecake: fresh chhena and sugar caramelised until the top is almost burnt
entries.text: chhena poda odia odisha's baked cheesecake: fresh chhena and sugar caramelised until the top is almost burnt vegetarian milk lemon / lime sugar rava / sooji (semolina) green cardamom cashews raisins (kishmish) ghee sugar curdle the milk with lemon juice, strain through muslin and rinse briefly. hang only 20 minutes — it should stay moist. knead the chhena smooth, then work in the sugar, rava, cardamom, nuts and raisins. rest 15 minutes so the rava swells. caramelise the 2 tbsp sugar in a ghee-greased tin and let it set at the bottom. pour in the batter and bake at 180c for 50-60 minutes, until the top is deep brown to nearly black and a skewer comes out clean. cool completely in the tin — at least 2 hours — before turning out. serve at room temperature in wedges.

entries.title: Chhena Tarkari
entries.snippet: soft fresh cheese in a light gingered tomato gravy, no onion, no garlic, straight out of the temple kitchen
entries.text: chhena tarkari odia soft fresh cheese in a light gingered tomato gravy, no onion, no garlic, straight out of the temple kitchen vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier paneer tomato ginger green chilli cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala ghee milk sugar salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the ghee in a kadhai and add the bay leaf and cumin seeds. they should sizzle on contact and smell toasty in about 15 seconds. add the grated ginger and slit green chillies and fry 1 minute, until the raw ginger smell lifts. pour in the tomato puree with the turmeric, cumin powder and coriander powder. stand back — it will spit. fry the puree on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens to brick red and the ghee separates at the edges. add the water and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes. slide in the paneer cubes, add the sugar, and simmer very gently for 6 minutes, spooning gravy over them. stir in the milk and the garam masala and warm through for 1 minute without boiling. take off the heat, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or roti.

entries.title: Chingudi Tarkari
entries.snippet: everyday prawn and potato curry, thin-gravied and heavy on mustard oil
