entries.text: chingudi tarkari odia everyday prawn and potato curry, thin-gravied and heavy on mustard oil pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier prawns potato onion garlic ginger tomato mustard oil bay leaf cumin seeds turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala green chilli water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower to medium and let it settle for 30 seconds. fry the prawns for 90 seconds, just until they turn opaque pink and curl loosely, then lift them straight out. add the potato cubes to the same oil and fry 5 minutes until patched with gold, then set them aside too. crackle the bay leaf and cumin seeds in the remaining oil for 20 seconds. add the onion and cook 7 to 8 minutes over medium heat until it is soft and properly browned at the edges. stir in the garlic and ginger and fry 90 seconds until the raw smell is gone. add the tomato with the remaining turmeric, chilli powder, cumin powder and coriander powder and cook 6 minutes, until the mixture pulls together and oil beads at the edges. return the potato, pour in the hot water with 1 tsp salt, cover and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender to a knife tip. slide the prawns back in with the slit green chillies and simmer just 3 minutes. stir in the garam masala, take off the heat, scatter the coriander and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Chungdi Malai
entries.snippet: prawns simmered in coconut milk, mildly spiced and faintly sweet, Odisha's most coaxing curry
entries.text: chungdi malai odia prawns simmered in coconut milk, mildly spiced and faintly sweet, odisha's most coaxing curry pescatarian gluten-free nut-free healthier prawns coconut milk onion ginger garlic ghee bay leaf cinnamon green cardamom cloves turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala green chilli sugar salt heat 1 tbsp ghee in a kadhai and sear the prawns on high for 45 seconds a side, until they just turn pink. lift them out at once. add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and drop in the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves. fry 30 seconds until fragrant. add the onion paste and fry on medium for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it turns pale gold and stops smelling raw. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes more. add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli and salt with 2 tbsp water and fry 1 minute so the spices do not scorch. lower the flame and pour in the coconut milk. add the sugar and slit green chillies. simmer gently, uncovered, for 6-8 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. return the prawns with any juices, add the garam masala, and simmer 2 minutes only. take off the heat and rest 5 minutes covered before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Dahi Baigana
entries.snippet: fried eggplant rounds folded into cool tempered yogurt, sharp with mustard oil
entries.text: dahi baigana odia fried eggplant rounds folded into cool tempered yogurt, sharp with mustard oil vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic nut-free eggplant / brinjal yogurt / dahi mustard oil turmeric powder sugar mustard seeds cumin seeds dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat 3 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it just begins to smoke, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds to lose the raw pungency. fry the eggplant in a single layer over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes a side, until bronzed and collapsing at the centre. drain the rounds on paper and leave them to cool to room temperature. whisk the yogurt with the sugar and 1/4 tsp salt until it pours off the spoon in a smooth ribbon. wipe the pan, heat the remaining 1 tbsp mustard oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin, about 20 seconds. add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida and stand back — they spit for 10 seconds, then go quiet. take the pan off the heat and let the tempering cool for 2 minutes until it stops sizzling. stir the green chilli and ginger into the yogurt, then pour in the warm tempering and fold once or twice. lay the eggplant in a shallow dish, spoon the yogurt over, and rest 15 minutes so the rounds drink it up. scatter the coriander and serve at room temperature with rice or pakhala.

entries.title: Dahi Pakhala
entries.snippet: Odia fermented rice in water with yogurt, eaten cold in the hot months
entries.text: dahi pakhala odia odia fermented rice in water with yogurt, eaten cold in the hot months vegetarian gluten-free nut-free rice (short/medium grain) yogurt / dahi water ginger green chilli curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt put the cooled rice in a bowl, add the water and lightly crush some of the grains with your fingers to cloud the liquid. for the traditional version, this is where you leave it overnight. whisk the yogurt smooth and stir it through with salt, the ginger and green chilli. it should be soupy, not thick; add more water if needed. heat the oil in a small pan. splutter the mustard seeds, then add the dried chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida. pour the tempering over the pakhala, add a squeeze of lemon and scatter with coriander. chill at least 30 minutes before eating. serve with something fried and salty alongside; fried fish, badi chura or a simple potato bharta are the usual partners.

entries.title: Dalma
entries.snippet: Odia lentils simmered with vegetables, finished with roasted cumin and coconut
entries.text: dalma odia odia lentils simmered with vegetables, finished with roasted cumin and coconut vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) raw banana / plantain pumpkin potato drumstick (moringa pod) tomato turmeric powder cumin seeds dried red chillies ginger coconut (fresh or desiccated) bay leaf ghee salt pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric, the ginger and 3 cups of water for 3 whistles, or simmer covered in a pot for about 35 minutes until completely soft. add the potato, raw banana, pumpkin and drumstick with a little more hot water and salt. cook a further 2 whistles, or 12-15 minutes in a pot, until the vegetables are tender but not collapsing. meanwhile, dry roast half the cumin seeds and one dried chilli in a small pan over medium heat until the cumin darkens a shade and smells toasty, about 90 seconds. cool, then grind to a coarse powder. heat the ghee in a small pan. add the bay leaf, the remaining cumin seeds and the remaining dried chilli. when the cumin sizzles and turns fragrant, pour the whole tempering into the dal. stir in the grated coconut and the roasted cumin powder. simmer 2 minutes so the flavours settle, then taste and adjust salt.

entries.title: Ghanta Tarkari
entries.snippet: a big pot of mixed vegetables and chana dal with coconut, cooked for festivals without onion or garlic
entries.text: ghanta tarkari odia a big pot of mixed vegetables and chana dal with coconut, cooked for festivals without onion or garlic vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier chana dal pumpkin yam (suran) raw banana / plantain potato colocasia (arbi) drumstick (moringa pod) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds panch phoron ginger green chilli bay leaf turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala ghee salt water boil the soaked chana dal in 400ml water with 1/2 tsp turmeric for 15 minutes, until it is just tender but still holds its shape. do not drain. meanwhile heat the ghee in a large kadhai and add the bay leaves, whole cumin seeds and panch phoron. let them crackle 20 seconds. add the remaining grated ginger and the slit green chillies and fry 1 minute. add the yam, colocasia and potato and fry 4 minutes until the cut faces turn golden. add the pumpkin, raw banana and drumstick with the remaining turmeric, the cumin powder and salt. toss 2 minutes. pour in the remaining 500ml water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 15 minutes. tip in the boiled chana dal with its water and the coconut-cumin paste. stir gently from the bottom. simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and the yam is completely soft. mash a few pieces of pumpkin against the pan to bind the gravy, then stir in the garam masala. scatter the reserved fresh coconut over the top and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

entries.title: Kanika
entries.snippet: fragrant sweet ghee rice from the Jagannath temple kitchen, studded with cashew and raisin
entries.text: kanika odia fragrant sweet ghee rice from the jagannath temple kitchen, studded with cashew and raisin vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic basmati rice ghee sugar water cashews raisins (kishmish) bay leaf cinnamon cloves green cardamom black pepper turmeric powder nutmeg salt heat 3 tbsp of the ghee in a heavy pan over medium and add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and peppercorns; they should swell and smell sweet in about 30 seconds. add the cashew halves and raisins and fry for 1 minute, until the cashews are pale gold and the raisins puff up. lift the cashews and raisins out with a slotted spoon onto a plate, leaving the whole spices behind. tip in the drained rice and the turmeric and toast gently for 3 to 4 minutes, until every grain looks glassy and slicked with ghee. pour in the hot water, add the salt, and bring to a rolling boil. cover, drop to the lowest heat and cook undisturbed for 12 minutes, until the water is gone and the top grains are just tender. scatter the sugar evenly over the surface without stirring, put the lid back on and leave for 3 minutes so it melts into the steam. fold the sugar through with a fork along with the fried cashews and raisins, the remaining 1 tbsp ghee and the grated nutmeg. rest covered off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve warm.

entries.title: Khaja
entries.snippet: layered flaky pastry fried and dipped in sugar syrup, sold in stacks outside the Puri temple
entries.text: khaja odia layered flaky pastry fried and dipped in sugar syrup, sold in stacks outside the puri temple vegetarian plain flour (maida) ghee rice flour sugar water green cardamom salt neutral oil rub the melted ghee and salt into the maida for 3 minutes, then add the 150ml water a little at a time to make a firm, tight dough. knead 6 minutes. cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. beat the 3 tbsp ghee with the rice flour to a smooth, spreadable white paste. divide the dough in two. roll each half into a thin rectangle about 2mm thick and spread the sata paste evenly right to the edges. roll each rectangle up tightly into a log, pressing as you go to expel air pockets. cut each log into 2cm slices. lay each slice cut-side up and press it flat with your palm, then roll very lightly into an oval about 8cm long — you should see the spiral of layers on the face. boil the 350g sugar with 200ml water and the cardamom for 8-10 minutes to a one-thread syrup, then keep it warm on the lowest flame. heat the oil in a kadhai to low-medium — a scrap of dough should take a full 30 seconds to float up. fry the khaja in small batches for 7-9 minutes, turning often, until they are pale gold and the layers have visibly fanned open. drain briefly, then dip each hot khaja in the warm syrup for 30 seconds, turning once, and lift onto a rack. leave to set for 30 minutes until the syrup coating turns matte and crisp.

entries.title: Macha Besara
entries.snippet: rohu steaks in a hot, sour ground-mustard gravy, the Sunday fish curry of coastal Odisha
entries.text: macha besara odia rohu steaks in a hot, sour ground-mustard gravy, the sunday fish curry of coastal odisha pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) mustard seeds garlic green chilli tomato panch phoron turmeric powder red chilli powder mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) grind the soaked mustard, garlic, green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste with 4 tbsp water. set aside. heat 4 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes. fry the turmeric-rubbed fish in one layer, 3 minutes a side, until a light crust forms. lift the fish out onto a plate. pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the oil. add the panch phoron to the hot oil and let it crackle 20 seconds, then add the sliced garlic and 2 slit green chillies. add the chopped tomato with 1/2 tsp turmeric, the chilli powder and salt. cook 6 minutes, mashing, until the tomato collapses and the oil separates. pour in the water and bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes. drop the flame to its lowest and stir in the mustard paste. simmer uncovered 5 minutes without letting it boil. slide the fried fish back in, spoon gravy over each piece, and simmer 4 minutes more. take off the heat, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 10 minutes before serving. the fish keeps absorbing gravy as it stands.

entries.title: Machha Ghanta
entries.snippet: fish head cooked down with roasted moong dal and mixed vegetables into a thick one-pot stew
entries.text: machha ghanta odia fish head cooked down with roasted moong dal and mixed vegetables into a thick one-pot stew pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) moong dal potato pumpkin raw banana / plantain eggplant / brinjal mustard oil panch phoron bay leaf dried red chillies garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat 3 tbsp mustard oil until smoking, drop to medium and fry the fish pieces 2 minutes a side until the skin is set and golden. lift the fish out, and when it is cool enough to handle break the head into large pieces and flake the collar meat off the bone. add the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the same pan and crackle the panch-phoron, bay leaves and red chillies for 20 seconds. stir in the garlic and ginger and fry 90 seconds until the raw smell lifts. add the potato, raw banana and pumpkin with the turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder and 1 tsp salt, and fry 5 minutes until the pieces are coated and glossy. tip in the roasted moong dal and stir for 2 minutes so each grain takes on oil. pour in the hot water, add the eggplant and the slit green chillies, bring to a boil then cover and simmer 20 minutes. uncover and check: the dal should be soft but still holding shape and the liquid reduced by about half. fold the flaked fish and head pieces back in and simmer 5 minutes more, stirring gently so the fish stays in pieces. take off the heat, scatter the coriander and rest 10 minutes before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Mahura
entries.snippet: yam, pumpkin and colocasia in mustard with crumbled badi, the festival curry of western Odisha
entries.text: mahura odia yam, pumpkin and colocasia in mustard with crumbled badi, the festival curry of western odisha vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier yam (suran) pumpkin colocasia (arbi) raw banana / plantain potato urad dal (black gram) mustard seeds green chilli cumin seeds panch phoron turmeric powder jaggery mustard oil salt water heat 1 tbsp mustard oil and fry the crushed badi over medium heat for 2 minutes until deep brown and smelling nutty. lift out and reserve. add the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the same kadhai and heat until it smokes, then lower the flame. add the panch phoron and let it crackle 20 seconds. add the yam, colocasia, potato and raw banana. fry 4 minutes, turning, until the cut faces are lightly golden. add the pumpkin, slit green chilli, turmeric and salt and toss for 2 minutes. pour in the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 15 minutes until the yam is tender to a knife. turn the flame to its lowest, stir in the mustard paste and the jaggery, and simmer uncovered 8 minutes. return the fried badi, stir once and simmer 3 minutes more so they drink up the gravy but keep their bite. rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

entries.title: Mudhi Mansa
entries.snippet: Baripada's peppery mutton curry eaten by the fistful with puffed rice
entries.text: mudhi mansa odia baripada's peppery mutton curry eaten by the fistful with puffed rice gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb murmura (puffed rice) onion garlic ginger tomato potato mustard oil bay leaf cinnamon green cardamom cloves black pepper turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala water coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the mustard oil in a pressure cooker until it smokes, then lower to medium and add the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves for 30 seconds. add the sliced onion and fry 12 to 14 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and shrunk to a third of its volume. stir in the remaining garlic and fry 1 minute, then add the tomato and cook 5 minutes until it collapses. add the chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder with 3 tbsp water and fry 3 minutes until oil separates at the edges. tip in the marinated mutton and brown it over high heat for 8 minutes, turning the pieces so every side catches. add the potato halves, the crushed black pepper and 1/2 tsp salt and stir for 2 minutes. pour in the hot water, close the cooker and cook on high for 4 whistles, then on low for 12 minutes. let the pressure drop naturally, open, and check that the meat pulls from the bone with light pressure; if not, simmer uncovered 10 minutes more. simmer uncovered 5 to 8 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon but is still loose enough to soak into puffed rice. stir in the garam masala and coriander, rest 10 minutes, and serve in bowls with the puffed rice heaped alongside for crushing in by hand.

entries.title: Rasabali
entries.snippet: fried chhena discs soaked in thick cardamom milk, the offering sweet of Kendrapara
entries.text: rasabali odia fried chhena discs soaked in thick cardamom milk, the offering sweet of kendrapara vegetarian nut-free paneer milk sugar rava / sooji (semolina) green cardamom black pepper ghee water saffron reduce the 1.5 litres of milk in a heavy pan over medium-low heat, scraping the sides down, for about 30 minutes until it has halved and thickened to a pourable rabri. stir 100g sugar, the crushed cardamom, the pepper and the saffron milk into the reduced milk. simmer 3 minutes and take off the heat. separately dissolve 50g sugar in 300ml water and bring to a boil to make a thin syrup. keep it warm. knead the crumbled paneer with the rava for 8 minutes until smooth and dough-like, with no grains visible. rest 10 minutes covered. divide into 12 balls and flatten each into a disc about 5cm across and 1cm thick, with smooth unbroken edges. heat the ghee in a kadhai to medium-low — a scrap of dough should rise slowly and take 20 seconds to colour. fry the discs in batches, 4-5 minutes, turning once, until they are an even deep reddish-brown. they will puff slightly. drop each fried disc straight into the warm syrup and leave 10 minutes to soften and swell. lift the discs out, squeeze them very gently against the side of the bowl to shed excess syrup, and slide them into the warm rabri. rest at least 2 hours so the discs drink the milk all the way through. serve cool, not chilled.

entries.title: Saga Bhaja
entries.snippet: amaranth greens stir-fried hard in mustard oil with garlic and dried chilli, done in ten minutes
entries.text: saga bhaja odia amaranth greens stir-fried hard in mustard oil with garlic and dried chilli, done in ten minutes vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free amaranth greens (chaulai) garlic dried red chillies green chilli mustard seeds turmeric powder mustard oil salt heat the mustard oil in a wide kadhai until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the mustard seeds and let them pop, about 15 seconds. add the sliced garlic and broken red chillies and fry until the garlic is pale gold at the edges, about 1 minute. throw in the chopped stems and the slit green chillies and fry 2 minutes on high. add the leaves in two handfuls, letting the first wilt before the second goes in. keep the flame high. add the turmeric and stir-fry 4-5 minutes uncovered, tossing often, until the water the leaves throw off has cooked away. salt to taste, toss once more and take off the heat immediately.

entries.title: Saja Pakhala
entries.snippet: same-day watered rice with lemon, ginger and a mustard tempering, eaten cool on the hottest afternoons
entries.text: saja pakhala odia same-day watered rice with lemon, ginger and a mustard tempering, eaten cool on the hottest afternoons vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) water lemon / lime ginger green chilli curry leaves mustard seeds cumin seeds mustard oil salt coriander leaves (cilantro) boil the washed rice in 1.5 litres of water for 12-14 minutes, uncovered, until the grains are soft and just starting to swell open. drain off the excess starch water into a bowl and keep it. spread the rice in a wide dish. let the rice cool to room temperature, about 40 minutes. do not rush it in the fridge. add 700ml cold water plus the reserved starch water to the rice, along with the salt. it should be soupy, with the grains floating loose. stir in the lemon juice, half the julienned ginger and the slit green chillies. heat the mustard oil in a small pan until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds and curry leaves. when the mustard pops and the leaves crisp, about 20 seconds, pour the whole tempering over the rice. stir once, scatter over the remaining ginger and the coriander leaves, and let it sit 15 minutes before eating.

entries.title: Sajana Chhuin Rai
entries.snippet: drumsticks and potato in a pale, pungent ground-mustard gravy with no onion or garlic
entries.text: sajana chhuin rai odia drumsticks and potato in a pale, pungent ground-mustard gravy with no onion or garlic vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier drumstick (moringa pod) potato mustard seeds green chilli mustard oil panch phoron dried red chillies turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) sugar water salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then bring it down to medium. crackle the panch-phoron and broken red chillies for about 20 seconds, until the fenugreek in the mix darkens a shade. add the potato, turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and fry for 4 minutes until the cut edges take on gold patches. add the drumstick pieces and toss for 2 minutes so they pick up the oil. pour in the water, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until a spoon scrapes the drumstick flesh out cleanly and the potato yields to a fork. turn the heat right down until the surface is barely moving, then stir in the ground mustard paste, the sugar and the cumin powder. hold at a bare simmer for 4 minutes; the gravy thickens slightly and loses its raw, nose-tingling smell. drop in the two slit green chillies and simmer 2 minutes more. take off the heat, stir through 1 tsp of raw mustard oil, and let it sit 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Santula
entries.snippet: barely-spiced mixed vegetables stewed in their own water, the plainest good thing in an Odia kitchen
entries.text: santula odia barely-spiced mixed vegetables stewed in their own water, the plainest good thing in an odia kitchen vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier potato eggplant / brinjal pumpkin raw banana / plantain drumstick (moringa pod) raw green papaya tomato green chilli panch phoron turmeric powder mustard oil salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it just smokes, then lower the flame and let it settle for 30 seconds. add the panch phoron and let it crackle for about 20 seconds, until the fenugreek darkens a shade. add the slit green chillies and the potato and raw banana. stir 2 minutes until the edges look chalky. add the pumpkin, eggplant, papaya, drumstick and tomato with the turmeric and salt. toss to coat. pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes. uncover and check the potato with a knife tip; it should give with no resistance. simmer uncovered 5 minutes more to thicken. mash three or four pieces of pumpkin against the side of the pan and stir through. that is what makes the broth cling. take off the heat, stir in the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Tomato Khajuri Khatta
entries.snippet: sweet-sour tomato and date relish tempered with panch phoron, served at the end of every Odia meal
entries.text: tomato khajuri khatta odia sweet-sour tomato and date relish tempered with panch phoron, served at the end of every odia meal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic tomato dates raisins (kishmish) jaggery panch phoron dried red chillies turmeric powder mustard oil salt water lemon / lime heat the mustard oil in a small pan until it smokes, then lower the flame for 30 seconds. add the panch phoron and the broken red chillies. let them crackle for 20 seconds until the fenugreek turns tan. tip in the chopped tomato with the turmeric and salt. stir once and cover. cook covered on medium for 8 minutes, until the tomatoes have completely collapsed. add the dates, raisins and water. simmer uncovered 6 minutes so the dates plump and soften. stir in the jaggery and cook 6-8 minutes more, stirring now and then, until the mixture is glossy and a spoon dragged through leaves a track that closes slowly. taste. add the lemon juice if it needs sharpening, and adjust salt. cool to room temperature before serving alongside rice and dal.

entries.title: Akuri
entries.snippet: soft-scrambled eggs loose with onion, chilli and coriander, eaten on buttered pav
entries.text: akuri parsi soft-scrambled eggs loose with onion, chilli and coriander, eaten on buttered pav vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier eggs onion tomato green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) butter milk turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) black pepper salt beat the eggs with the milk, black pepper and salt just until streaky — about 15 strokes. melt the butter in a small kadhai over medium-low heat until it foams but does not brown. add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft and translucent, with no colour on it at all. stir in the ginger and green chilli and cook 1 minute until fragrant. add the turmeric and cumin powder, then the tomato, and cook 2 minutes until the tomato slumps but still holds shape. drop the heat to its lowest setting and pour in the eggs. push the eggs slowly from the edges to the centre with a flat spoon for 3 to 4 minutes, forming large soft curds. fold through the coriander leaves off the heat and serve immediately on buttered pav or toast.

entries.title: Berry Pulao
entries.snippet: saffron rice layered over spiced chicken, studded with sharp sour-sweet dried fruit
entries.text: berry pulao parsi saffron rice layered over spiced chicken, studded with sharp sour-sweet dried fruit gluten-free healthier basmati rice chicken yogurt / dahi onion ginger garlic green chilli mint coriander leaves (cilantro) garam masala cinnamon cloves green cardamom bay leaf black pepper saffron milk ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) dried apricots (khubani) lemon / lime salt water fry the sliced onion in 4 tbsp ghee over medium heat for 15 minutes until dark brown and crisp, drain on paper, and set a third aside for the garnish. fry the cashews in the same ghee for 1 minute until golden and set aside. add the marinated chicken to the pan with two thirds of the fried onion and cook uncovered 20 minutes over medium heat until the yogurt tightens around the meat. stir in half the mint and coriander and cook 3 minutes more, then set the chicken aside off the heat. bring 3 litres of water to a rolling boil with the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf, black pepper and 2 tbsp salt. add the drained rice and boil 4 to 5 minutes, until a grain crushes between your fingers but still has a hard white core. drain the rice immediately and spread it on a tray to stop the cooking. layer the chicken in a heavy pot, then the rice, then the lemon-soaked raisins and apricots, the reserved fried onion, cashews and the rest of the herbs. drizzle over the saffron milk and the remaining 1 tbsp ghee, seal the pot with a tight lid or foil, and cook on the lowest heat 20 minutes, or in a 160c oven for 25. rest 10 minutes sealed, then open and lift the pulao from the sides with a flat spoon so the layers stay visible.

entries.title: Bhida Par Eeda
entries.snippet: okra fried dry with onion and eggs cracked over the top
entries.text: bhida par eeda parsi okra fried dry with onion and eggs cracked over the top vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free okra / bhindi eggs onion green chilli garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil black pepper salt heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai and fry the okra over high heat, undisturbed for the first 3 minutes so it sears rather than steams. keep frying 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pieces are browned at the edges and no longer sticky. lift them out onto a plate. add the last tbsp of oil and fry the onion until golden, 8 minutes. add the garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute. stir in turmeric, chilli powder, cumin and coriander powder for 30 seconds. return the okra with salt, toss 2 minutes to coat, then spread it into an even layer. make four hollows and crack in the eggs. season with salt and black pepper. cover and cook on low 7-9 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still run. squeeze over the lemon, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot with rotli.

entries.title: Dar Ni Pori
entries.snippet: flaky ghee pastry packed with sweet lentil paste, made for Navroze and weddings
entries.text: dar ni pori parsi flaky ghee pastry packed with sweet lentil paste, made for navroze and weddings vegetarian plain flour (maida) ghee toor dal (pigeon pea) sugar almonds pistachios khoya / mawa green cardamom nutmeg rose water salt water pressure cook the toor dal with 500ml water for 4 whistles, until completely soft, then drain off every drop of liquid. blend or mash the dal to a smooth paste while still warm. cook the dal paste with the sugar and 2 tbsp ghee over low heat, stirring, 15-18 minutes, until it pulls away from the pan in one mass. take it off the heat and fold in the ground almonds, pistachios, khoya, cardamom, nutmeg and rose water. cool completely, then divide into 8 balls. for the dough, rub 60g melted ghee and the salt into the maida until it clumps when squeezed, then add the water a little at a time to make a firm, smooth dough. knead 5 minutes, coat with a spoon of ghee, cover and rest 30 minutes. divide the dough into 8, roll each into a 12cm disc, place a filling ball in the centre and gather the edges over the top, pinching them shut. flatten each parcel gently and roll it out to about 18cm, sealed side down, using light even pressure. cook on a medium tawa 2-3 minutes a side until pale gold flecks appear. spoon a tablespoon of ghee around each pori and fry 1-2 minutes more per side until deep golden and crisp. cool on a rack. they crisp as they cool and are traditionally cut into wedges.

entries.title: Dhansak
entries.snippet: sunday mutton simmered into a purée of four dals and gourds, sour and gently hot
entries.text: dhansak parsi sunday mutton simmered into a purée of four dals and gourds, sour and gently hot gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb toor dal (pigeon pea) masoor dal (red lentil) chana dal moong dal pumpkin eggplant / brinjal fenugreek leaves (methi) onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder red chilli powder garam masala cinnamon cloves green cardamom black pepper tamarind jaggery mint coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt water pressure cook the drained dals with the pumpkin, eggplant, methi leaves, chopped onion, tomato, turmeric and 1 litre of water for 5 whistles, about 20 minutes. meanwhile heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pan and brown the mutton in two batches over high heat, 5 minutes a batch. pound the garlic, ginger and green chilli to a coarse paste and fry it in the same pan for 2 minutes, until the raw smell lifts. add the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black pepper, coriander powder, cumin powder, chilli powder and garam masala and fry 90 seconds, splashing in 2 tbsp water when it catches. return the mutton, add 200ml water, cover and simmer 45 minutes until a knife slides into the meat with no resistance. cool the dal mixture slightly, fish out any large spice pieces, and blend to a smooth, pourable purée. pour the purée over the mutton, add the tamarind extract, jaggery and salt, and simmer uncovered 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes. taste and balance — it should land sour first, then sweet, then hot. add tamarind or jaggery a teaspoon at a time. fry the sliced onion in the remaining 2 tbsp oil until dark brown and crisp, about 10 minutes over medium heat. rest the dhansak 10 minutes off the heat, then top with the fried onion, mint and coriander leaves.

entries.title: Jardaloo Ma Gosht
entries.snippet: mutton braised with dried apricots until the gravy turns sweet, sour and dark
entries.text: jardaloo ma gosht parsi mutton braised with dried apricots until the gravy turns sweet, sour and dark gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb dried apricots (khubani) onion ginger garlic tomato red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala cinnamon cloves jaggery vinegar potato neutral oil salt water heat the oil in a heavy pan and fry the cinnamon and cloves for 30 seconds, until the cloves swell. add the sliced onion and cook over medium heat until deep brown, 18-20 minutes, stirring so the edges do not catch. stir in the ginger and garlic paste and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes. add turmeric, coriander, cumin, chilli powder and kashmiri chilli. fry 40 seconds with a splash of water so they do not scorch. add the mutton and brown it hard for 8 minutes, until the pieces are sealed and the oil separates at the edges. add the tomato and salt, cover, and cook 10 minutes until the tomato collapses into the masala. pour in the water, bring to a boil, then simmer covered 55-65 minutes until the mutton is tender. in a pressure cooker, 4 whistles then 10 minutes on low. add the soaked apricots with their water, the jaggery and the vinegar. simmer uncovered 12 minutes. taste and balance: it should read sweet first, then sour, then hot. adjust with a little more jaggery or vinegar. stir in the garam masala, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and pile the fried sali on top just before serving.

entries.title: Kheema Par Eeda
entries.snippet: spiced mutton mince with eggs baked into the surface, soft yolks over dry kheema
entries.text: kheema par eeda parsi spiced mutton mince with eggs baked into the surface, soft yolks over dry kheema gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb eggs onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) mint ghee black pepper salt water heat the ghee in a wide kadhai and fry the onion until golden brown, 12 minutes. add ginger, garlic and green chilli and fry 2 minutes. add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder, and fry 30 seconds. add the mince and break it up with the back of a spoon, frying 8 minutes until it loses all pinkness and starts to catch. add the tomato and salt and cook 6 minutes until the tomato disappears into the mince. add the water, cover, and simmer 12 minutes, then uncover and cook off every trace of liquid, about 5 minutes. stir through the garam masala, coriander leaves and mint, then level the surface and press four shallow wells with the back of a spoon. crack an egg into each well, season with salt and the coarse black pepper. cover and cook on the lowest heat 8-10 minutes, until the whites are opaque and the yolks still wobble. bring the pan to the table and serve with pav or rotli.

entries.title: Kolmi no Patio
entries.snippet: prawns in a thick red tamarind masala that is fiery, sour and sweet at once
entries.text: kolmi no patio parsi prawns in a thick red tamarind masala that is fiery, sour and sweet at once pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free prawns onion tomato garlic ginger dried red chillies kashmiri chilli powder cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder tamarind jaggery vinegar curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin seeds, kashmiri chilli and 2 tbsp of the soaking water to a smooth red paste. heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the curry leaves for 20 seconds until they crackle and go translucent. add the onion and cook 10 minutes over medium heat until soft and pale gold. add the ground masala and fry 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil pools around the edges and the raw garlic smell disappears. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and tomato and cook 6 minutes until the tomato has collapsed completely. add the tamarind extract, jaggery, vinegar and salt and simmer 5 minutes to a thick, glossy masala. taste and balance the three points — sour, sweet, hot. it should be assertive on all three, since the prawns will mute it. slide in the prawns, stir to coat, and cook 3 to 4 minutes only, until they curl and turn opaque. rest 5 minutes off the heat, scatter with coriander leaves, and serve with plain rice or rotli.

entries.title: Lagan nu Custard
entries.snippet: the dense baked wedding custard, caramel-topped and heavy with nutmeg and cardamom
entries.text: lagan nu custard parsi the dense baked wedding custard, caramel-topped and heavy with nutmeg and cardamom vegetarian gluten-free milk condensed milk eggs sugar green cardamom nutmeg rose water almonds pistachios ghee boil the milk in a wide heavy pan and simmer 30 minutes, stirring often, until reduced to about 600ml. stir in the condensed milk and sugar and simmer 5 minutes more, then take off the heat and cool to lukewarm. beat the eggs until just smooth, with no strands of white remaining. pour a ladle of the warm milk into the eggs while whisking, then repeat twice before adding the eggs back into the pan. whisk in the ground cardamom, nutmeg and rose water. strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a ghee-rubbed baking dish about 25cm across. scatter the slivered almonds and pistachios over the surface. bake at 160c for 45 to 55 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre wobbles like a soft jelly when nudged. if the top has not browned, run it under a hot grill for 2 minutes until patched with dark caramel spots. cool completely at room temperature, at least 3 hours, before cutting into squares.

entries.title: Machhi No Saas
entries.snippet: pomfret poached in a pale sweet-sour sauce thickened with egg and rice flour
entries.text: machhi no saas parsi pomfret poached in a pale sweet-sour sauce thickened with egg and rice flour pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) eggs rice flour onion garlic green chilli cumin seeds ginger sugar vinegar coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt water heat the oil and cook the onion gently until soft and translucent but not coloured, 8 minutes. add the ground garlic-chilli-cumin paste and fry 2 minutes, until it stops smelling raw. pour in the water with salt, bring to a simmer, and cook 5 minutes. stir in the slaked rice flour and simmer 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon lightly. slide in the fish steaks in a single layer and poach on low 8-10 minutes, spooning sauce over rather than turning them. lift the fish out onto a serving dish and keep it warm. beat the eggs with the vinegar until smooth. take the pan off the heat, wait a minute, then trickle in the egg-vinegar mixture in a thin stream while whisking hard. return to the lowest heat with the sugar and stir 2 minutes until the sauce thickens to a thin custard. it must not boil. taste for the sweet-sour balance, pour over the fish, scatter with coriander and serve with plain boiled rice.

entries.title: Margi Na Farcha
entries.snippet: chicken marinated overnight, dipped in beaten egg and fried crisp for wedding lunches
entries.text: margi na farcha parsi chicken marinated overnight, dipped in beaten egg and fried crisp for wedding lunches gluten-free dairy-free nut-free chicken eggs ginger garlic red chilli powder kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder garam masala black pepper vinegar lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt water mix the ginger and garlic paste, all the ground spices, the vinegar, lemon juice and salt into a thick marinade. rub it hard into the slashed chicken, working it into the cuts, and refrigerate overnight. tip the chicken with all its marinade into a wide pan, add the water, cover, and cook over medium heat 18-20 minutes, turning once. uncover and cook off the liquid until the pieces are coated in a thick, almost dry masala. cool completely on a plate. beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and the chopped coriander until pale and frothy. heat the oil in a kadhai to 175c — a drop of batter should rise and sizzle in 3 seconds. dip a chicken piece in the egg, let the excess drip for two seconds, and lower it into the oil away from you. fry 2-3 pieces at a time for 3-4 minutes, spooning egg over any bald patches, until the coating is golden and puffed. drain on a rack, not paper, so the underside stays crisp. serve hot with lemon wedges and a plate of rotli, or alongside pulao dal.

entries.title: Mutton Pulao Dal
entries.snippet: brown-rice mutton pulao served with a smooth toor dal, the Sunday lunch of Parsi homes
entries.text: mutton pulao dal parsi brown-rice mutton pulao served with a smooth toor dal, the sunday lunch of parsi homes nut-free healthier basmati rice mutton / lamb toor dal (pigeon pea) onion sugar ghee cinnamon cloves green cardamom black cardamom bay leaf black pepper ginger garlic tomato turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin seeds garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water for the dal, pressure cook the toor dal with the tomato, turmeric, half the chilli powder, salt and 700ml water for 5 whistles, then blend smooth and keep warm. heat 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the cumin seeds, add 1 sliced onion and fry to deep gold, then pour this over the dal. for the pulao, heat 4 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot and fry the remaining sliced onion until dark brown, 20 minutes. lift out half and reserve for the top. add cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black cardamom, bay leaves and peppercorns to the pot and fry 1 minute. add the ginger and garlic paste, fry 2 minutes, then add the mutton and brown it 8 minutes. add the rest of the chilli powder, salt and 700ml water. pressure cook 4 whistles, or simmer covered 60 minutes, until the mutton is tender. strain the meat from the stock. measure the stock and make it up with water to 900ml — this is what the rice will drink. bring the stock to a boil with the caramel, the garam masala and salt. it should taste slightly too salty on its own. stir in the drained rice and the mutton, boil hard 4 minutes until craters appear on the surface, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat 15 minutes. rest, still covered, for 10 minutes off the heat before opening. fork the rice through gently, scatter the reserved brown onion and coriander over, and serve with the hot dal in a bowl alongside.

entries.title: Papeta Ma Gosht
entries.snippet: everyday mutton and potato stew, gently spiced and thickened by the potatoes themselves
entries.text: papeta ma gosht parsi everyday mutton and potato stew, gently spiced and thickened by the potatoes themselves gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb potato onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime neutral oil salt water heat the oil and fry the chopped onion over medium heat until soft and pale gold, about 10 minutes. add ginger and garlic paste with the slit green chillies and fry 2 minutes. add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder. fry 30 seconds. add the mutton and brown 6 minutes, turning the pieces so each face colours. add the tomato and salt and cook 8 minutes until the tomato has broken down and the oil rises. pour in the water and simmer covered 45 minutes, or pressure cook 3 whistles and release naturally. add the potatoes, cover, and cook 20 minutes more until a knife slides through them with no resistance. stir in the garam masala and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to reduce to a pouring consistency. finish with coriander leaves and the lemon juice, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rotli or plain rice.

entries.title: Papeta par Eeda
entries.snippet: eggs baked on a bed of soft spiced potatoes, the everyday parsi supper
entries.text: papeta par eeda parsi eggs baked on a bed of soft spiced potatoes, the everyday parsi supper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier potato eggs onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) turmeric powder cumin powder (jeera) red chilli powder black pepper ghee salt water heat the ghee in a wide kadhai and fry the sliced onion 6 minutes until soft and lightly golden. add the green chilli and cook 1 minute. stir in the turmeric, cumin powder and chilli powder and fry 30 seconds. add the potato matchsticks with 1 tsp salt and toss until every strand is coated yellow. sprinkle over 3 tbsp water, cover, and cook 12 to 14 minutes on low, shaking the pan every few minutes. uncover and check — a matchstick should give completely under a spoon but the mass should still be loose, not sticky. fold in half the coriander leaves, then flatten the potato into an even bed and make five shallow wells with the back of a spoon. crack one egg into each well, season with salt and black pepper, cover, and cook on the lowest heat 6 to 8 minutes. scatter the remaining coriander over and bring the pan straight to the table with pav or rotli.

entries.title: Patra ni Machhi
entries.snippet: pomfret packed in green coconut chutney and steamed in a leaf until it flakes
entries.text: patra ni machhi parsi pomfret packed in green coconut chutney and steamed in a leaf until it flakes pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier fish (firm fillets or steaks) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) mint green chilli garlic cumin seeds sugar lemon / lime vinegar turmeric powder salt blend the coconut, coriander, mint, green chilli, garlic, cumin seeds, sugar, turmeric, remaining lemon juice, vinegar and salt to a thick paste. taste the chutney and correct it now — it should be sharp, sweet and hot all at once, and it will taste milder once steamed. cut the softened banana leaf into rectangles roughly twice the size of each fillet. spread a spoon of chutney on the leaf, lay the fish on it, then blanket the fish with a thick layer of chutney on top and sides. fold the leaf over into a snug parcel and tie with kitchen string or secure with a toothpick. set the parcels in a steamer over rapidly boiling water, cover, and steam 12 minutes for fillets or 18 for whole fish. open one parcel at the edge and press the thickest part — the flesh should part into flakes with no translucent centre. rest the parcels 3 minutes off the heat, then serve them closed so each person opens their own.

entries.title: Ravo
entries.snippet: birthday-morning semolina pudding, soft and milky with cardamom and fried raisins
entries.text: ravo parsi birthday-morning semolina pudding, soft and milky with cardamom and fried raisins vegetarian rava / sooji (semolina) milk ghee sugar eggs green cardamom nutmeg raisins (kishmish) almonds rose water salt heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the raisins for 30 seconds until they puff, then lift them out. fry the slivered almonds in the same ghee for 45 seconds until pale gold and set them aside with the raisins. add the remaining ghee and the semolina and roast over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and turns the colour of pale sand. pour in the hot milk in a thin stream, whisking hard the whole time. add the pinch of salt and simmer 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the semolina swells and the mixture coats the back of a spoon. stir in the sugar and cook 3 minutes more; it will loosen at first and then thicken again. take the pan off the heat, let it cool for 2 minutes, then whisk in the beaten egg quickly and return to very low heat for 2 minutes. stir in the cardamom, nutmeg and rose water, and thin with a splash of hot milk if it has gone past pourable. spoon into bowls, top with the fried raisins and almonds, and serve warm.

entries.title: Sali Boti
entries.snippet: mutton in a sweet-sour tomato gravy under a haystack of crisp potato straws
entries.text: sali boti parsi mutton in a sweet-sour tomato gravy under a haystack of crisp potato straws gluten-free dairy-free nut-free mutton / lamb onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala vinegar jaggery dried apricots (khubani) potato neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water pound the ginger and garlic to a smooth paste and use half for the marinade, keeping half for the pan. heat 4 tbsp oil and fry the sliced onion over medium heat for 15 minutes until evenly deep brown. add the reserved ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and fry 2 minutes. stir in the kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 1 minute until the oil takes on colour. tip in the tomato purée and cook 12 minutes until the oil separates and pools at the edges. add the marinated mutton and sear 6 minutes, stirring, until every cube is coated and no pink shows. pour in 400ml water, cover, and simmer 45 minutes, or pressure cook 4 whistles, until the mutton is tender. stir in the jaggery, remaining vinegar, garam masala, soaked apricots and salt and simmer uncovered 10 minutes. drain and dry the potato straws thoroughly, then fry in 500ml hot oil in two batches for 3 minutes each until pale gold and crisp. drain the sali on paper, salt lightly, and pile over the mutton just before serving.

entries.title: Salli Marghi
entries.snippet: chicken in a tangy tomato-onion gravy crowned with matchstick potatoes
entries.text: salli marghi parsi chicken in a tangy tomato-onion gravy crowned with matchstick potatoes gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chicken onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala cinnamon cloves vinegar jaggery potato neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat 3 tbsp oil with the cinnamon and cloves until the spices swell, about 40 seconds. add the sliced onion and fry 12 minutes over medium heat to a deep even brown. add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and fry 2 minutes until the raw edge is gone. stir in the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 45 seconds. add the tomato and cook 10 minutes, mashing with the spoon, until it breaks down and the oil separates. add the marinated chicken and turn it in the masala over high heat for 5 minutes until it is sealed all over. pour in 300ml water, cover, and simmer 20 minutes until the chicken pulls easily from the bone. stir in the jaggery, remaining vinegar, garam masala and salt and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to a gravy that just coats a spoon. fry the dried potato matchsticks in 500ml hot oil in two batches, 3 minutes each, until pale gold, then drain and salt. scatter the coriander leaves over the chicken and heap the salli on top at the table.

entries.title: Sev
entries.snippet: vermicelli fried in ghee and sweetened with raisins, almonds and cardamom for birthday mornings
entries.text: sev parsi vermicelli fried in ghee and sweetened with raisins, almonds and cardamom for birthday mornings vegetarian vermicelli (semiya) ghee sugar water raisins (kishmish) almonds pistachios green cardamom nutmeg rose water saffron salt melt the ghee over medium-low heat and fry the almonds and pistachios for 1 minute until they just colour. lift them out. fry the drained raisins in the same ghee for 30 seconds, until they swell. lift them out too. add the broken vermicelli and roast, stirring constantly, 5-7 minutes until it is an even reddish brown and smells nutty. pour in the hot water with the pinch of salt. it will hiss violently. stir once. cover and cook on low 6 minutes, until the vermicelli is soft and almost all the water has gone. add the sugar and stir. the mixture will loosen again as the sugar melts. cook uncovered 6-8 minutes, stirring gently, until the syrup has been absorbed and the sev is glossy and just moist. stir in the crushed cardamom, nutmeg, saffron water and rose water, then fold back the nuts and raisins. rest covered 5 minutes off the heat and serve warm, with plain yogurt on the side.

entries.title: Tamota Par Eeda
entries.snippet: eggs set over sweet-sour stewed tomatoes, a fifteen-minute Parsi supper
entries.text: tamota par eeda parsi eggs set over sweet-sour stewed tomatoes, a fifteen-minute parsi supper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier tomato eggs onion green chilli ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder cumin powder (jeera) sugar coriander leaves (cilantro) ghee black pepper salt heat the ghee and fry the onion over medium heat until soft and just golden, 8 minutes. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant. stir in turmeric, chilli powder and cumin powder for 20 seconds. add the tomato, sugar and salt. cook uncovered 10-12 minutes, mashing occasionally, until the mixture is jammy and no watery liquid pools at the edge. stir in half the coriander leaves and level the surface. make four wells and slip in the eggs, then season them with salt and the black pepper. cover and cook on the lowest heat 6-8 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks are still soft. scatter the remaining coriander over and serve straight from the pan with buttered pav or rotli.

entries.title: Aloo Gobi
entries.snippet: dry-cooked potato and cauliflower, browned at the edges and heavy on ginger
entries.text: aloo gobi punjabi dry-cooked potato and cauliflower, browned at the edges and heavy on ginger vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier cauliflower potato onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli mustard oil cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai until it shimmers and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. fry the potato cubes on medium-high for 6 minutes, undisturbed for the first 3, until they are gold on several faces, then lift them out. add the cauliflower to the same pan with the remaining oil and fry 6 minutes until browned in patches. push the cauliflower aside, add the onion, and fry 5 minutes until soft and gold. stir in the grated ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 90 seconds. add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir 20 seconds, then add the tomato and 1 tsp salt. cook 6 minutes until the tomato has broken down into a coating masala rather than a gravy. return the potatoes, stir to coat everything, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 10 minutes, shaking the pan every few minutes. check that a knife slides into both potato and stalk with no resistance; give it 5 minutes more if not. uncover, stir in the amchur and garam masala, and cook 2 minutes to dry it off. finish with the julienned ginger and coriander and serve with roti.

entries.title: Aloo Methi
entries.snippet: cubed potato and fresh fenugreek fried dry, bitter and sweet in the same mouthful
entries.text: aloo methi punjabi cubed potato and fresh fenugreek fried dry, bitter and sweet in the same mouthful vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fenugreek leaves (methi) potato onion garlic green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) salt heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 15 seconds. add the sliced garlic and fry 40 seconds until it just turns pale gold. add the onion and green chilli and fry 4 minutes until soft and translucent. tip in the potato cubes, turmeric and salt and toss to coat. spread them into a single layer. fry uncovered on medium for 10-12 minutes, turning only every 3 minutes, until the cubes are browned on several faces and nearly tender. add the chilli powder and coriander powder and toss for 1 minute. add the methi leaves in handfuls, letting each batch wilt before the next goes in. this takes about 3 minutes. raise the heat and stir-fry 5 minutes more until the leaves have darkened and the pan is dry, with no green liquid pooling. sprinkle over the amchur, toss once and take off the heat. serve hot with phulka.

entries.title: Aloo Paratha
entries.snippet: wholewheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and griddled in ghee
entries.text: aloo paratha punjabi wholewheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and griddled in ghee vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) water potato onion green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) amchur (dry mango powder) cumin seeds red chilli powder garam masala carom seeds (ajwain) ghee butter salt mix the atta with 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tbsp ghee, then add the water gradually and knead 8 minutes to a soft, smooth dough. cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. mash the cold potatoes and mix in the onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, amchur, crushed cumin, chilli powder, garam masala, ajwain and 1 tsp salt. taste the filling and correct the salt and sour — it should taste slightly over-seasoned on its own. divide dough and filling into 8 each, and roll both into balls. flatten a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, cup it in your palm, place a filling ball in the middle, and gather the edges over the top, pinching them shut. press the sealed ball flat, dust with flour, and roll gently to a 7-inch disc, working from the centre outward and turning as you go. lay it on a hot tawa and cook 60 seconds until the surface bubbles and the underside has pale spots. flip, brush the cooked side with ghee, and cook 60 seconds. flip once more, brush again, and press the edges down with a cloth until both sides are freckled deep brown, about 45 seconds. stack in a covered dish and serve hot with butter, yogurt and pickle.

entries.title: Amritsari Fish
entries.snippet: ajwain-spiked gram flour batter fried crisp around soft white fish
entries.text: amritsari fish punjabi ajwain-spiked gram flour batter fried crisp around soft white fish pescatarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free fish (firm fillets or steaks) besan (gram flour) rice flour ginger garlic carom seeds (ajwain) kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder black pepper lemon / lime salt water neutral oil chaat masala rub the fish pieces with the lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt and the turmeric, and set aside 10 minutes. whisk the besan, rice flour, ginger, garlic, crushed ajwain, kashmiri chilli, black pepper and remaining salt in a bowl. add the water a tablespoon at a time until you have a batter the thickness of double cream. fold the fish through the batter, cover, and rest 30 minutes in the fridge. heat the oil in a kadhai to 170c — a drop of batter should sink briefly, then rise and sizzle steadily. lower in 4 or 5 pieces at a time, without crowding, and fry 4 minutes until pale gold. lift onto the rack and let all the fish rest 5 minutes. raise the oil to 190c and fry the pieces a second time for 60 to 90 seconds until deep gold and crackling. drain on the rack, dust with chaat masala, and serve at once with lemon wedges and sliced onion.

entries.title: Amritsari Kulcha
entries.snippet: crisp-bottomed stuffed maida bread, blistered and crushed under a spoonful of butter
entries.text: amritsari kulcha punjabi crisp-bottomed stuffed maida bread, blistered and crushed under a spoonful of butter vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) yogurt / dahi baking soda sugar ghee water potato onion green chilli ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) amchur (dry mango powder) chaat masala coriander powder cumin seeds red chilli powder nigella seeds (kalonji) butter salt mix the maida, baking soda, sugar and salt. rub in the ghee, then work in the yogurt and enough lukewarm water to make a soft, slightly tacky dough. knead 8 minutes until smooth. oil the surface of the dough, cover with a damp cloth and rest 2 hours in a warm spot. it should feel puffy and slack, not springy. grate the cold potatoes coarsely — do not mash. mix with the onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, anardana, amchur, chaat masala, coriander powder, crushed cumin, chilli powder and salt. divide the dough and the filling into 6 each. flatten a dough ball in your palm, cup a portion of filling inside, gather the edges over it and pinch shut. rest the sealed balls 10 minutes, seam down. roll each ball out to a 15cm oval, using dry maida, pressing outwards from the centre with even weight and stopping if the filling threatens to break through. press nigella seeds and a little chopped coriander into the top surface, then flip and wet the underside with water using your palm. slap the wet side onto the screaming-hot tray or upturned tawa. it will stick. bake or cook 3-4 minutes until the top blisters and browns in patches. if using a tawa, invert the tawa over the flame for 40 seconds to char the top directly. prise the kulcha off with a spatula, brush hard with softened butter, then crush it once between both palms so it cracks open. serve immediately with pindi chole and sliced onion.

entries.title: Atte Ka Halwa
entries.snippet: wholewheat flour roasted in ghee until nutty, then swelled with hot sugar syrup
entries.text: atte ka halwa punjabi wholewheat flour roasted in ghee until nutty, then swelled with hot sugar syrup vegetarian atta (wholewheat flour) ghee sugar water milk green cardamom almonds raisins (kishmish) saffron boil the water, milk and sugar together in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, then keep it on the lowest heat. melt the ghee in a heavy kadhai over low-medium heat and add the atta all at once. stir constantly for 15-18 minutes. the mixture goes from pale and pasty, to loose and sandy, to a deep reddish-brown that smells like biscuits. watch for the ghee to separate and pool around the edges of the mass — that is the signal the flour is done. add the almonds and raisins and stir 1 minute so they toast in the ghee. take the kadhai off the flame, stand back, and pour in the hot syrup in three additions, stirring hard between each. return to low heat and stir until the halwa thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan, about 5 minutes. stir in the crushed cardamom and the saffron milk, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat. serve warm, spooned into bowls, with the surface ghee left glistening on top.

entries.title: Baingan Bharta
entries.snippet: fire-roasted aubergine mashed rough with onion and tomato, smoky throughout
entries.text: baingan bharta punjabi fire-roasted aubergine mashed rough with onion and tomato, smoky throughout vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier eggplant / brinjal onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli mustard oil cumin seeds turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt set the aubergines directly on a medium gas flame and roast 15 to 20 minutes, turning every few minutes with tongs. if you have no gas flame, roast at 240c for 45 minutes, turning twice, then blacken briefly under the grill. put the roasted aubergines in a covered bowl for 10 minutes — the steam loosens the skin. peel off every scrap of charred skin, then chop and mash the flesh roughly with a fork. heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes until deep gold. stir in the ginger, minced garlic and green chillies and fry 2 minutes. add the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, and cook 10 minutes until the tomato disappears into a thick masala and oil separates. fold in the mashed aubergine and cook 8 minutes on medium, pressing and stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan. stir in the garam masala and most of the coriander, taste for salt, and finish with the rest of the coriander.

entries.title: Bharwa Karela
entries.snippet: bitter gourds stuffed with sharp onion masala and cooked down slow until the skins wrinkle
entries.text: bharwa karela punjabi bitter gourds stuffed with sharp onion masala and cooked down slow until the skins wrinkle vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier bitter gourd (karela) onion mustard oil fennel powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) amchur (dry mango powder) turmeric powder red chilli powder garam masala fenugreek seeds (methi) mustard seeds green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) salt scrape the ridged skin off each karela with a knife, reserving the scrapings. slit each one lengthways down one side without cutting through, and scoop out the seeds. rub the gourds inside and out with 2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric and leave in a colander for 1-3 hours. squeeze out the brown liquid and rinse once. heat 3 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, cool for 30 seconds, then crackle the mustard seeds and crushed fenugreek. add the onion and the reserved scrapings and fry 10-12 minutes on medium until golden and dry. stir in the fennel, coriander, cumin, remaining turmeric, chilli powder, amchur, garam masala, green chilli and salt. fry 3 minutes until the mixture smells toasted and looks dry. cool the masala, fold in the coriander leaves, then pack it firmly into each karela and tie shut with string. heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan and lay the gourds in a single layer. cook uncovered on low for 25-30 minutes, turning every 5 minutes, until the skins are wrinkled, blistered and dark in patches. press one with a spoon — it should give completely. rest 5 minutes, snip the strings and serve with dal and roti.

entries.title: Bhindi Masala
entries.snippet: sliced okra fried dry until it loses all its slime, then tossed with onion and amchur
entries.text: bhindi masala punjabi sliced okra fried dry until it loses all its slime, then tossed with onion and amchur vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free okra / bhindi onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) garam masala salt coriander leaves (cilantro) heat 4 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai until it shimmers. add the okra in a single layer and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes, stirring only every 2 or 3 minutes. keep frying until the pieces are browned in patches and no thread follows the spoon, about 4 minutes more. lift the okra out onto a plate and set aside. add the last tablespoon of oil to the pan and crackle the cumin and crushed fennel for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry 7 minutes on medium-high until soft with brown edges. stir in the ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 90 seconds. add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir 20 seconds, then add the tomato wedges and 1 tsp salt. cook 5 minutes, just until the tomato softens but still holds its shape. return the okra, fold everything together gently, and cook 3 minutes uncovered. stir in the amchur and garam masala, scatter the coriander, and serve immediately.

entries.title: Butter Chicken
entries.snippet: Murgh makhani: charred chicken in a tomato and cream gravy, mild and fenugreek-scented
entries.text: butter chicken punjabi murgh makhani: charred chicken in a tomato and cream gravy, mild and fenugreek-scented gluten-free nut-free chicken yogurt / dahi ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder garam masala tomato butter cream kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) green cardamom cashews sugar lemon / lime salt marinate the chicken with the yogurt, half the ginger and garlic, the kashmiri chilli, 1 tsp garam masala, lemon juice and salt. leave at least 30 minutes, ideally 4 hours refrigerated. grill, broil or pan-sear the chicken in a very hot pan until the edges char in places and it is just cooked. do not cook it through to dryness; it finishes in the sauce. set aside with any resting juices. simmer the tomatoes with the remaining ginger and garlic, the cardamom and a splash of water, covered, for 20 minutes until completely collapsed. blend the tomato mixture smooth with the soaked cashews if using, then pass it through a sieve. the sieve is what separates a silky makhani from a rustic curry. return the puree to the pan with the butter and cook 10 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring, until it darkens and thickens and the butter shows at the edges. add the chicken with its juices, the cream, the sugar and the remaining garam masala. simmer 5 minutes. crush the kasuri methi between your palms and stir it through. taste for salt and lemon.

entries.title: Chana Masala
entries.snippet: everyday chickpeas in a dark, sour-edged onion-tomato masala
entries.text: chana masala punjabi everyday chickpeas in a dark, sour-edged onion-tomato masala vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chickpeas (kabuli chana) water onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds bay leaf black cardamom coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) turmeric powder red chilli powder garam masala anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) amchur (dry mango powder) asafoetida (hing) salt coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime drain the soaked chickpeas and pressure cook with 5 cups fresh water, the black cardamom and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes at full pressure. heat the oil in a heavy pan, crackle the cumin seeds and bay leaf for 20 seconds, then add the asafoetida. add the onion and fry on medium for 14 minutes, stirring often, until uniformly dark brown. stir in the garlic, grated ginger and green chillies and fry 2 minutes. add the coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 20 seconds. pour in the tomato puree and cook 12 minutes until the masala is thick, glossy and pulling away from the pan with oil at the edges. add the cooked chickpeas with 2 cups of their cooking liquid and simmer uncovered 20 minutes. mash a ladleful of chickpeas against the side of the pan and stir them back in to thicken the gravy. stir in the crushed anardana, amchur and garam masala, and simmer 5 minutes more. taste and push the sour and salt until it makes you sit up, then top with julienned ginger, coriander and lemon wedges.

entries.title: Chole
entries.snippet: Punjabi chickpea curry, dark and tangy with pomegranate and dried mango
entries.text: chole punjabi punjabi chickpea curry, dark and tangy with pomegranate and dried mango vegetarian vegan gluten-free nut-free dairy-free healthier chickpeas (kabuli chana) onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala cumin seeds bay leaf black cardamom lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with salt and the black cardamom in fresh water for 5-6 whistles, until a chickpea crushes easily between finger and thumb. reserve the cooking liquid. heat the oil in a heavy pan. add the cumin seeds and bay leaf, and when the cumin sizzles, add the onion. fry patiently over medium heat until genuinely brown, 10-12 minutes; this is most of the flavour. add the ginger and garlic and cook for a minute until the raw smell goes, then add the tomato puree, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder. cook the masala down until the oil separates and pools at the edges of the pan, 8-10 minutes. do not rush this. add the drained chickpeas with a cup of the reserved cooking liquid. simmer uncovered 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy. stir in the garam masala, a good squeeze of lemon and the coriander leaves. rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving; chole improves noticeably in that time.

entries.title: Dahi Bhalla
entries.snippet: feather-light urad dal dumplings drowned in sweetened yogurt with tamarind and roasted cumin
entries.text: dahi bhalla punjabi feather-light urad dal dumplings drowned in sweetened yogurt with tamarind and roasted cumin vegetarian gluten-free nut-free urad dal (black gram) moong dal ginger green chilli asafoetida (hing) raisins (kishmish) baking soda neutral oil yogurt / dahi sugar tamarind jaggery cumin powder (jeera) black salt (kala namak) red chilli powder chaat masala coriander leaves (cilantro) mint pomegranate salt water grind the drained dals to a thick, smooth paste with 3-4 tbsp water only. the batter should hold a peak on the spoon. beat the batter hard with your hand or a whisk for 5 minutes, adding the asafoetida, ginger, green chilli, baking soda and salt. drop a teaspoonful into a bowl of water — it should float within seconds. heat the oil to 170c. wet your palm, take a spoon of batter, press a raisin into the centre and slide it in. fry 5-6 at a time. fry 4-5 minutes, turning, to an even pale gold — not brown. drain on paper. drop the hot bhalle straight into 2 litres of warm salted water and leave them 20 minutes. they will swell and go soft. meanwhile soak the tamarind in 200ml hot water for 15 minutes, squeeze out the pulp, strain, and simmer with the jaggery, 1/2 tsp of the roasted cumin and a pinch of black salt for 8 minutes until it coats a spoon. whisk the yogurt with the sugar and 1/2 tsp salt until it is smooth and pourable, like thin cream. chill. lift each bhalla out of the water and press it flat between your palms to squeeze out the water. be firm but do not tear it. arrange the pressed bhalle in a shallow dish and pour the chilled yogurt over to cover. rest 20 minutes in the fridge. drizzle with the tamarind chutney, then dust with the remaining roasted cumin, black salt, chilli powder and chaat masala. scatter coriander, mint and pomegranate over and serve cold.

entries.title: Dal Makhani
entries.snippet: black urad simmered for hours until it turns silky and smoky-sweet with butter
entries.text: dal makhani punjabi black urad simmered for hours until it turns silky and smoky-sweet with butter vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier whole urad (sabut urad) rajma (kidney beans) water tomato ginger garlic butter cream neutral oil kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) salt coriander leaves (cilantro) drain the soaked beans, put them in the pressure cooker with 5 cups water, half the crushed ginger and 1 tsp salt, and cook 25 minutes at full pressure. release the pressure and check: a bean should collapse to paste when pressed against the pot with a spoon. if not, give it another 10 minutes. heat the oil in a heavy pan, add the garlic paste and remaining crushed ginger and fry 90 seconds until the raw smell lifts. add the tomato puree, both chillies and 1/2 tsp salt, and fry on medium until the mixture darkens and oil beads at the edges, about 12 minutes. tip the cooked beans in with all their liquid and stir well to break some of them up against the side of the pan. simmer uncovered on the lowest heat for 45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the base. stir in half the butter, a cube at a time, letting each melt before the next goes in. add the cream, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, and simmer 10 minutes more until the dal coats a spoon thickly. taste for salt, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes so it thickens and settles. serve topped with the remaining butter, the julienned ginger and the coriander.

entries.title: Dal Tadka
entries.snippet: everyday yellow dal finished with a loud garlic and chilli tempering
entries.text: dal tadka punjabi everyday yellow dal finished with a loud garlic and chilli tempering vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) moong dal water turmeric powder tomato onion ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) kashmiri chilli powder garam masala lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dals with 3.5 cups water, the turmeric, half the chopped tomato and 1/2 tsp salt for 8 minutes at full pressure. let the pressure drop naturally, then whisk the dal briskly for 30 seconds until it is smooth and pourable. keep the dal on the lowest simmer while you make the tempering. heat the ghee in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the cumin seeds and let them crackle and darken, about 20 seconds. add the sliced garlic and fry 60 seconds until the slices are gold at the edges. add the onion and fry 5 minutes until soft and browning. add the ginger, green chillies, broken red chillies and asafoetida and fry 30 seconds. add the remaining tomato and cook 4 minutes until it slumps and the ghee separates. take the pan off the heat, stir in the kashmiri chilli, and immediately pour the whole thing over the dal. stir once, add the garam masala, lemon juice and coriander, and taste for salt. cover and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

entries.title: Gajar ka Halwa
entries.snippet: grated winter carrots cooked down in milk and ghee until dark, dense and cardamom-scented
entries.text: gajar ka halwa punjabi grated winter carrots cooked down in milk and ghee until dark, dense and cardamom-scented vegetarian gluten-free carrot milk sugar ghee khoya / mawa green cardamom cashews almonds raisins (kishmish) pistachios fry the cashews, almonds and raisins in 1 tbsp of the ghee for 2 minutes until the nuts are gold and the raisins puff, then lift them out. add 2 tbsp ghee to the pan and fry the grated carrot on medium for 10 minutes until it darkens and smells sweet. pour in the milk and bring to a boil, then drop to medium-low. simmer uncovered 40 to 45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the base and sides. keep going until the milk is almost entirely gone and the mass pulls together when you draw the spoon through it. add the sugar and stir — the mixture will go loose again as the sugar melts. cook 10 minutes more on medium until that liquid has gone too. stir in the crumbled khoya and the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and cook 8 minutes until the halwa is glossy and leaves the sides of the pan. fold in the crushed cardamom and most of the fried nuts and raisins. take off the heat, rest 10 minutes, and serve warm topped with the pistachios and remaining nuts.

entries.title: Ghar Da Chicken Curry
entries.snippet: the plain everyday punjabi chicken curry, onion-heavy and thin enough to eat with roti
