entries.text: ghar da chicken curry punjabi the plain everyday punjabi chicken curry, onion-heavy and thin enough to eat with roti gluten-free nut-free healthier chicken onion tomato yogurt / dahi ginger garlic green chilli mustard oil cumin seeds bay leaf black cardamom cinnamon cloves turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then take it off the flame for 30 seconds to settle. return to medium heat, crackle the cumin, then add the bay, black cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 20 seconds. add the sliced onion and a pinch of salt and fry 15-18 minutes to a deep brown, stirring every minute or so. add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and the green chillies and fry 2 minutes. add the kashmiri chilli, coriander and cumin powders with 2 tbsp water and cook 1 minute so they do not scorch. add the tomato puree and cook 10 minutes on medium, until the mixture pulls together into a mass and oil rims the edge. add the marinated chicken with all its yogurt and fry on high for 6-7 minutes, until the pieces are sealed and coated and the yogurt has tightened. pour in 500ml hot water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes. uncover and simmer 6-8 minutes more until the gravy coats a spoon thinly and the chicken pulls from the bone. crush in the kasuri methi, add the garam masala, cover and rest 5 minutes. finish with coriander leaves and serve with roti.

entries.title: Keema Matar
entries.snippet: minced mutton browned hard with peas, the sunday lunch of a punjabi kitchen
entries.text: keema matar punjabi minced mutton browned hard with peas, the sunday lunch of a punjabi kitchen gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb peas onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds bay leaf black cardamom cinnamon cloves turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) yogurt / dahi coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, then add the bay, black cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 20 seconds. add the onion and cook on medium for 12-14 minutes to a deep even gold, stirring often. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the green chillies and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powders with a splash of water and cook 1 minute. add the tomatoes and salt and cook 8-10 minutes until they collapse and the ghee separates at the edge of the pan. turn the heat high, add the mince and break it up constantly for 8 minutes until no pink remains and the grains are separate and browned. lower the heat, beat in the whisked yogurt a spoon at a time, and fry 3 minutes more. add 250ml water, close the cooker and cook 3 whistles, then 10 minutes on low. rest until the pressure drops. open, stir in the peas and simmer uncovered 8 minutes, until the peas are tender and the keema is moist but not soupy. crush in the kasuri methi, add the garam masala, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat. finish with coriander leaves.

entries.title: Lauki Kofta
entries.snippet: grated bottle gourd dumplings bound with besan, sitting in a plain onion-tomato gravy
entries.text: lauki kofta punjabi grated bottle gourd dumplings bound with besan, sitting in a plain onion-tomato gravy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free bottle gourd (lauki) besan (gram flour) rice flour ginger green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil onion tomato garlic yogurt / dahi cream cumin seeds turmeric powder kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) salt water squeeze the salted grated lauki hard, reserving the liquid. mix the pulp with the besan, rice flour, half the grated ginger, the green chillies, 3 tbsp coriander leaves and salt into a mix that just holds a ball. heat the frying oil to 170c. test with one kofta: it should sink, then rise in about 20 seconds without falling apart. roll walnut-sized balls and fry 6-7 at a time for 4-5 minutes to a deep even brown. drain on paper. blend the onion, garlic and remaining ginger to a coarse paste, and separately blend the tomatoes to a puree. heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, then add the onion paste and fry 12 minutes on medium until it is golden and no longer smells raw. add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, coriander and cumin powders and fry 1 minute with a splash of water. add the tomato puree and salt and cook 10-12 minutes until it thickens and the oil separates cleanly. lower the heat, beat in the whisked yogurt spoon by spoon, then cook 3 minutes. add the reserved lauki liquid made up to 400ml with hot water. simmer 8 minutes until the gravy is smooth and coats a spoon. stir in the cream, crushed kasuri methi and garam masala. slide the koftas in, cover and let them sit off the heat for 8 minutes to soak. scatter the remaining coriander over and serve with roti or jeera rice.

entries.title: Mah Di Dal
entries.snippet: whole black urad simmered for hours with ginger and ghee, no cream and no tomato
entries.text: mah di dal punjabi whole black urad simmered for hours with ginger and ghee, no cream and no tomato vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier whole urad (sabut urad) chana dal ginger garlic green chilli onion ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water drain the soaked dals and pressure cook with 1.2 litres water, the turmeric, half the crushed ginger, half the garlic and 1 tsp salt for 6 whistles, then 25 minutes on low. let the pressure drop naturally and open. the grains should be soft enough to crush against the side of the pot with a spoon. mash about a third of the dal against the pot with the back of a ladle to thicken the liquid. simmer uncovered on the lowest heat for 35-40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and topping up with hot water when it gets too thick. in a small pan heat the ghee, add the cumin and asafoetida and let them foam for 15 seconds. add the onion and fry 8 minutes to a deep gold. add the remaining crushed garlic and the slit green chillies and fry 1 minute more. off the heat, stir in the chilli powder and coriander powder so they bloom in the residual heat without burning. pour the tadka into the dal, stir once, and simmer together 10 minutes. check the salt, add the garam masala and finish with the ginger matchsticks and coriander leaves. serve with makki di roti or plain rice.

entries.title: Makki di Roti
entries.snippet: coarse, crumbly winter flatbread patted out by hand and eaten hot with saag
entries.text: makki di roti punjabi coarse, crumbly winter flatbread patted out by hand and eaten hot with saag vegetarian gluten-free nut-free maize flour (makki ka atta) water salt carom seeds (ajwain) ghee butter mix the flour, salt and ajwain in a wide bowl. pour in the hot water a little at a time, mixing with a spoon at first, then knead 5 minutes with the heel of your hand into a smooth, pliable dough. cover and rest 10 minutes. divide into 8 balls. roll one between your palms until it has no cracks on the surface. flatten it between two sheets of paper, pressing outward with your fingertips to a rough disc 5 inches across and about 5mm thick. heat the tawa on medium until a drop of water skitters across it. peel the top sheet off, invert the roti onto your palm, and lay it on the tawa. cook 90 seconds until the underside has pale brown freckles. flip and cook the second side 90 seconds, pressing the edges down with a cloth so it puffs slightly. smear generously with ghee, flip once more for 20 seconds, and stack in a covered dish while you make the rest. serve immediately with butter melting on top and a bowl of saag.

entries.title: Matar Paneer
entries.snippet: peas and paneer in a straightforward onion-tomato gravy, the weeknight standard
entries.text: matar paneer punjabi peas and paneer in a straightforward onion-tomato gravy, the weeknight standard vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier paneer peas onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder coriander powder kashmiri chilli powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) sugar salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) blend the onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and green chillies to a smooth paste with 2 tbsp water. heat the ghee in a kadhai, add the bay leaf and cumin seeds, and let them crackle 20 seconds. pour in the blended paste — stand back, it spits — and cook on medium for 15 minutes. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and kashmiri chilli and fry 1 minute. add 1.5 cups water, 1 tsp salt and the sugar, and bring to a simmer. add the peas and simmer 8 minutes for fresh, 4 minutes for frozen, until tender. slide in the paneer cubes and simmer 4 minutes on low. crush in the kasuri methi and add the garam masala. rest off the heat 5 minutes so the paneer takes up the gravy, then taste for salt. scatter the coriander and serve with roti or rice.

entries.title: Methi Malai Matar
entries.snippet: bitter fenugreek leaves and sweet peas in a mild white cream gravy
entries.text: methi malai matar punjabi bitter fenugreek leaves and sweet peas in a mild white cream gravy vegetarian gluten-free healthier fenugreek leaves (methi) peas cashews onion ginger garlic green chilli cream milk ghee cumin seeds green cardamom white pepper garam masala sugar salt water salt, rest and squeeze the methi leaves as in the prep notes, then chop them roughly. boil the onion, ginger, garlic and green chillies in 1 cup water for 8 minutes until soft. blend the boiled mixture with the drained cashews to a completely smooth paste. heat the ghee in a kadhai and fry the cumin seeds and cardamom for 30 seconds until fragrant. add the chopped methi and fry on medium for 6 minutes until it darkens and the raw green smell turns nutty. stir in the cashew-onion paste and cook 8 minutes on low, stirring constantly so it does not catch. add the peas, milk, white pepper, sugar and 1 tsp salt, and simmer 8 minutes until the peas are tender. turn the heat off and stir in the cream and garam masala. rest 5 minutes covered, taste for salt and sugar, and serve with naan or paratha.

entries.title: Missi Roti
entries.snippet: gram flour and wheat flatbread with onion and ajwain, coarse and savoury off the tawa
entries.text: missi roti punjabi gram flour and wheat flatbread with onion and ajwain, coarse and savoury off the tawa vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) besan (gram flour) onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) turmeric powder red chilli powder ghee water salt mix the atta, besan, salt, ajwain, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder in a wide bowl. rub in 2 tbsp ghee until the flour holds its shape when squeezed in your fist. add the onion, green chilli, coriander leaves and crushed kasuri methi and toss through. add the lukewarm water a little at a time and knead 6-8 minutes to a soft, pliable dough, slightly stiffer than chapati dough. cover with a damp cloth and rest 20 minutes. divide into 8, roll each into a ball and dust well with dry atta. roll out to 16cm discs, a little thicker than a chapati. lay a roti on the hot tawa. when small bubbles appear across the surface, about 45 seconds, flip it. cook the second side 1 minute until brown spots form, pressing the edges down with a folded cloth so it puffs. flip once more, smear with ghee and cook 20 seconds a side until crisp at the rim. stack in a cloth-lined box and serve hot with white butter, dahi and pickle.

entries.title: Palak Paneer
entries.snippet: soft paneer in a bright green spinach gravy, mild and creamy
entries.text: palak paneer punjabi soft paneer in a bright green spinach gravy, mild and creamy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier spinach paneer onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds coriander powder turmeric powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) cream salt water boil a large pan of water, drop in the spinach and green chillies, and blanch for exactly 90 seconds. lift the spinach straight into the iced water, leave 1 minute, then drain and squeeze out most of the liquid. blend the spinach and chillies to a coarse puree with 2 tbsp water and set aside. heat the ghee in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry 8 minutes until soft and light gold at the edges. stir in the ginger and garlic and fry 90 seconds until fragrant. add the tomato, coriander powder, turmeric and 3/4 tsp salt, and cook 8 minutes until the tomato breaks down and oil shows at the edges. pour in the spinach puree with 1/2 cup water and simmer just 5 minutes. slide in the paneer cubes, stir gently, and simmer 3 minutes so they warm through and take on the seasoning. crush in the kasuri methi, add the garam masala, and swirl in the cream off the heat. taste for salt and serve hot with roti or jeera rice.

entries.title: Paneer Bhurji
entries.snippet: crumbled paneer scrambled with onion, tomato and capsicum in under twenty minutes
entries.text: paneer bhurji punjabi crumbled paneer scrambled with onion, tomato and capsicum in under twenty minutes vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier paneer onion tomato capsicum / bell pepper ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt heat the ghee in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 15 seconds. add the onion and fry 6 minutes on medium until soft and lightly golden at the edges. add the ginger, garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant. add the capsicum and fry 2 minutes; it should stay slightly crunchy. add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and cook 4-5 minutes until the tomato collapses and the oil shows at the edges. fold in the crumbled paneer and toss gently for 2-3 minutes, just until it is hot and coated. crush in the kasuri methi and add the garam masala. take off the heat. squeeze over the lemon, scatter the coriander leaves and serve straight away with buttered pav or roti.

entries.title: Paneer Tikka
entries.snippet: charred cubes of paneer and capsicum off a skewer, smoky and sharp with chaat masala
entries.text: paneer tikka punjabi charred cubes of paneer and capsicum off a skewer, smoky and sharp with chaat masala vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier paneer yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) capsicum / bell pepper onion ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) chaat masala mustard oil lemon / lime salt dry-roast the besan in a small pan on low for 3 minutes until it smells like toasted nuts, then cool. whisk the hung yogurt with the roasted besan, ginger-garlic paste, kashmiri chilli, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, oil and salt into a thick paste. fold in the paneer, capsicum and onion petals, coating everything evenly, and refrigerate 1 hour. heat the oven to 230c with a rack in the upper third. thread the paneer and vegetables alternately onto skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces. set the skewers on a wire rack over a foil-lined tray and roast 12 minutes. turn the skewers and roast another 6 to 8 minutes, until the edges are blackened in patches and the marinade has set dry. rest 3 minutes, then dust with chaat masala and squeeze over lemon. serve hot with sliced onion and mint chutney.

entries.title: Pindi Chole
entries.snippet: dark, dry rawalpindi chickpeas soured with pomegranate seed and amchur, no onion or tomato
entries.text: pindi chole punjabi dark, dry rawalpindi chickpeas soured with pomegranate seed and amchur, no onion or tomato vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier chickpeas (kabuli chana) baking soda black cardamom cinnamon bay leaf cloves anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) amchur (dry mango powder) coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) black pepper dry ginger powder (saunth) carom seeds (ajwain) red chilli powder garam masala black salt (kala namak) asafoetida (hing) neutral oil ginger green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) pomegranate lemon / lime salt water tie the black cardamom, cinnamon, bay and cloves in a small muslin bundle. pressure cook the drained chickpeas with the bundle, the baking soda, salt and 1 litre of water for 5 whistles, then 15 minutes on low. lift out the spice bundle and squeeze it against the side of the pot. drain the chickpeas but keep 300ml of the black cooking liquor. dry-roast the ground anardana, coriander powder, cumin powder, crushed pepper, dry ginger and amchur in a kadhai over low heat for 90 seconds, until the pan smells sharp and toasty. tip onto a plate. heat the oil in the same kadhai, add the ajwain and asafoetida and let them foam for 10 seconds. add half the ginger matchsticks and the slit green chillies and fry 1 minute, until the ginger turns pale gold at the edges. return the roasted spice mix, add the chilli powder and black salt, and stir for 30 seconds. tip in the chickpeas and toss until every one is coated and dark. add 200ml of the reserved liquor. cook uncovered on medium for 12-15 minutes, mashing about a fifth of the chickpeas against the pan, until the liquid has gone and the mass is glossy and almost dry. sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest off the heat for 5 minutes. scatter the remaining ginger matchsticks, coriander and pomegranate seeds over the top and serve with lemon wedges and kulcha or bhatura.

entries.title: Punjabi Chana Dal
entries.snippet: nutty split gram dal cooked to just-holding grains under a garlic tadka
entries.text: punjabi chana dal punjabi nutty split gram dal cooked to just-holding grains under a garlic tadka vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier chana dal water onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt pressure cook the drained dal with 3 cups water and the turmeric for 12 minutes at full pressure, then let the pressure fall on its own. heat 2 tbsp of the ghee in a pan, add the cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then add the asafoetida. add the onion and fry 7 minutes until soft and gold at the edges. stir in the ginger, half the garlic and the green chillies, and fry 90 seconds. add the tomato, coriander powder, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, and cook 8 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil pools at the sides. tip in the cooked dal with its liquid, add 1/2 cup hot water, and simmer 12 minutes so the flavours settle in. stir in the garam masala and amchur and taste for salt. heat the last tablespoon of ghee in a small pan and fry the remaining garlic slices until deep gold, about 90 seconds. pour the garlic ghee over the dal, scatter the coriander, and serve with roti.

entries.title: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
entries.snippet: tangy yogurt and gram flour gravy simmered thick, with soft onion fritters dropped in
entries.text: punjabi kadhi pakora punjabi tangy yogurt and gram flour gravy simmered thick, with soft onion fritters dropped in vegetarian gluten-free nut-free yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) water onion green chilli ginger garlic turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder fenugreek seeds (methi) cumin seeds mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies ghee neutral oil kashmiri chilli powder salt coriander leaves (cilantro) whisk the sour yogurt with 6 tbsp besan, the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and 1 tsp salt until completely smooth, then whisk in 4 cups water. heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot, crackle the fenugreek and cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add the asafoetida, half the ginger, the garlic and half the green chillies. pour in the yogurt mixture and bring it to a boil on medium, stirring constantly in one direction. once it boils, drop to the lowest heat and simmer uncovered 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. meanwhile make the pakora batter: mix the remaining besan with the sliced onion, remaining ginger and chilli, 1/2 tsp salt and just enough water to bind, about 4 tbsp. heat the oil in a kadhai to 175c and drop in rough spoonfuls of batter, 6 at a time. fry 4 minutes, turning, until deep gold and firm, then drain on a rack. loose, craggy spoonfuls fry lighter than neat balls. slide the pakoras into the simmering kadhi and cook 8 minutes more so they drink up the gravy but keep their shape. taste for salt — sour kadhi needs a firm hand with it. for the final tempering, heat the last tablespoon of ghee, take it off the heat, stir in the kashmiri chilli and broken red chillies, and pour it over the kadhi. scatter the coriander and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Rajma Chawal
entries.snippet: soft kidney beans in a thick onion-tomato gravy, eaten over plain rice
entries.text: rajma chawal punjabi soft kidney beans in a thick onion-tomato gravy, eaten over plain rice vegan vegetarian gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rajma (kidney beans) basmati rice onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds bay leaf turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) salt water coriander leaves (cilantro) pressure cook the drained rajma with 4 cups fresh water, the bay leaf and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes at full pressure, then let the pressure fall naturally. while it cooks, heat the oil in a heavy pan and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry on medium-high, stirring often, until evenly deep brown — a full 12 to 14 minutes. stir in the ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 2 minutes until the sharpness goes. add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir for 20 seconds, then pour in the tomato puree. cook the masala down for 10 to 12 minutes until it darkens and oil separates at the sides. scoop out a ladle of cooked beans, mash them to a paste, and stir that back in with the rest of the beans and their liquid. simmer uncovered 20 minutes until the gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. add hot water if it tightens too far. meanwhile boil the rice in 3 cups water with 1/2 tsp salt, covered, on the lowest heat for 11 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat and fork through. finish the rajma with garam masala and amchur, taste for salt, and scatter over the coriander. serve the rajma ladled over the hot rice.

entries.title: Sarson ka Saag
entries.snippet: slow-cooked mustard greens, bitter and buttery, thickened with a little coarse flour
entries.text: sarson ka saag punjabi slow-cooked mustard greens, bitter and buttery, thickened with a little coarse flour vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier mustard greens (sarson) spinach fenugreek leaves (methi) maize flour (makki ka atta) ginger garlic green chilli onion ghee butter salt water put the mustard greens, spinach, methi, chopped ginger, garlic, green chillies, 1 tsp salt and 1.5 cups water in the pressure cooker and cook 15 minutes at full pressure. let the pressure drop, then uncover — the greens should be army-green and completely collapsed. blend to a coarse puree, or crush with a wooden masher for the traditional rough texture. return the puree to the pan and bring to a bare simmer. whisk in the flour slurry in a thin stream and cook 25 minutes on low, stirring every few minutes. meanwhile heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the chopped onion until golden brown, about 8 minutes. add the julienned ginger to the onion and fry 1 minute more. pour the tempering into the saag, scraping the pan clean, and simmer 10 minutes more. taste for salt — greens need more than you expect — and finish with the butter melting on top.

entries.title: Shahi Paneer
entries.snippet: paneer in a pale, mildly sweet cashew and cream gravy scented with cardamom
entries.text: shahi paneer punjabi paneer in a pale, mildly sweet cashew and cream gravy scented with cardamom vegetarian gluten-free healthier paneer cashews melon seeds (magaz) onion tomato ginger garlic green chilli ghee green cardamom cinnamon cloves black cardamom cream milk kashmiri chilli powder garam masala sugar kewra water salt water simmer the sliced onion, ginger, garlic and green chilli in 1 cup water for 10 minutes until completely soft, then cool slightly. blend the boiled onion mixture with the drained cashews and melon seeds to a silky paste, adding a little of the cooking water. blend the tomato separately to a puree and set aside. heat the ghee in a kadhai and fry the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and black cardamom for 40 seconds until fragrant. add the tomato puree and cook 8 minutes until it thickens and the ghee separates. stir in the cashew-onion paste and cook 10 minutes on low, stirring constantly. add the kashmiri chilli, sugar, 1 tsp salt and the milk, and simmer 5 minutes to a gravy that coats a spoon. slide in the paneer cubes and simmer 3 minutes on the lowest heat. turn off the heat, stir in the cream and garam masala, and add the kewra water. rest 5 minutes covered, then fish out the whole spices and serve with naan or pulao.

entries.title: Tandoori-Style Chicken
entries.snippet: yogurt and chilli marinated chicken charred hard at the edges, done in a home oven
entries.text: tandoori-style chicken punjabi yogurt and chilli marinated chicken charred hard at the edges, done in a home oven gluten-free nut-free healthier chicken yogurt / dahi ginger garlic kashmiri chilli powder red chilli powder garam masala cumin powder (jeera) coriander powder black salt (kala namak) kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) lemon / lime mustard oil salt butter rub the chicken with the lemon juice, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp of the kashmiri chilli, and leave 20 minutes. whisk the hung yogurt with the ginger-garlic paste, remaining chillies, garam masala, cumin, coriander, black salt, crushed kasuri methi, cooled mustard oil and remaining salt. coat the chicken thoroughly, working the marinade into every slash, then cover and refrigerate overnight. heat the oven to its maximum, at least 240c, with a rack set near the top and a tray of water on the floor of the oven. arrange the chicken on a wire rack over a foil-lined tray, shaking off pooled marinade. roast 20 minutes, until the surface is dry and starting to blacken at the edges. turn the pieces, baste with melted butter, and roast another 15 minutes. test the thickest thigh: the juices should run clear and the meat pull easily from the bone. rest 5 minutes, then finish under a hot grill for 3 minutes for extra char if you want it. serve with lemon wedges, raw onion rings and green chutney.

entries.title: Aam ki Launji
entries.snippet: raw mango cooked down with jaggery, fennel and nigella into a sweet-sour relish
entries.text: aam ki launji rajasthani raw mango cooked down with jaggery, fennel and nigella into a sweet-sour relish vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic raw green mango jaggery mustard oil fennel seeds (saunf) nigella seeds (kalonji) fenugreek seeds (methi) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder dried red chillies salt water heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it just smokes, then lower the heat and let it cool for 30 seconds. add the fenugreek seeds first and let them go one shade darker, then the fennel, nigella and cumin. they should sizzle and smell toasty within 20 seconds. add the hing and broken red chillies, stir once, then tip in the mango chunks. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and salt and toss the mango in the oil for 3 minutes until the edges look glossy. pour in 200ml water, cover, and cook on low heat 10 minutes until the mango is tender but the chunks still hold. add the jaggery and stir until it melts completely. uncover and simmer 8-10 minutes. cook until the syrup coats the back of a spoon and a line drawn through it on the pan base closes slowly. it thickens further as it cools, so stop while it still looks slightly loose. cool completely before jarring. serve alongside dal baati, puri or paratha.

entries.title: Aloo Pyaaz ki Sabzi
entries.snippet: everyday dry potato and onion stir-fry, sharp with amchur and hing
entries.text: aloo pyaaz ki sabzi rajasthani everyday dry potato and onion stir-fry, sharp with amchur and hing vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier potato onion neutral oil cumin seeds mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the oil until it shimmers, then crackle the mustard seeds, followed by the cumin. add the hing and slit green chillies and fry 15 seconds. tip in the sliced onion and cook 6-7 minutes over medium-high heat until the edges brown but the pieces still have bite. take the pan off the heat, add the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders, and stir for 10 seconds in the residual heat. return to the flame, add the cubed potato and salt, and toss to coat every piece. fry 8 minutes over medium heat, turning only every couple of minutes, until the potatoes take on crisp golden faces. crush in the kasuri methi and sprinkle over the amchur, then toss and cook 1 more minute. stir through the coriander leaves and serve hot with methi bajra puri or plain roti.

entries.title: Bajre ki Raab
entries.snippet: a thin savoury millet gruel loosened with buttermilk and warmed with dry ginger
entries.text: bajre ki raab rajasthani a thin savoury millet gruel loosened with buttermilk and warmed with dry ginger vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic bajra (pearl millet) flour buttermilk (chaas) ghee carom seeds (ajwain) dry ginger powder (saunth) turmeric powder jaggery salt water heat the ghee in a heavy pan on low and add the ajwain. it should sizzle gently, not pop, about 15 seconds. tip in the bajra flour and roast it on low heat 4-5 minutes, stirring continuously, until it darkens slightly and smells like toasted grain. pour in 400ml water a little at a time, whisking hard after each addition so the flour stays smooth. bring to a boil, then simmer on low 8 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens to a pourable gruel. take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 2 minutes. whisk the buttermilk smooth and stir it in gradually. return to the lowest heat for 3 minutes, stirring, and do not let it boil. season with salt, the dry ginger powder and the turmeric. stir in the jaggery now if you want the sweet version. serve hot in glasses. it thickens as it stands, so loosen with warm water if it sits.

entries.title: Bajre ki Roti
entries.snippet: thick hand-patted millet flatbread, nutty and earthy, eaten hot with ghee
entries.text: bajre ki roti rajasthani thick hand-patted millet flatbread, nutty and earthy, eaten hot with ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic bajra (pearl millet) flour water salt ghee mix the flour and salt, then pour in the hot water a little at a time, stirring with a spoon until too hot to handle comfortably. knead 4-5 minutes with the heel of your hand while it is still warm, until smooth and pliable with no cracks. divide into 6 balls and keep them covered with a damp cloth. flatten one ball between your palms, then pat it out on a greased sheet of plastic or a damp cloth, rotating as you go, into a 15cm disc about 5mm thick. lift it onto a medium-hot tawa and cook 2 minutes until the underside is speckled and dry. flip and cook the second side 2 minutes, pressing the edges gently with a cloth so it cooks evenly. lift the roti with tongs and hold it directly over the flame for 15-20 seconds a side until it puffs and chars in patches. smear with ghee and serve immediately with ker sangri, gatte ki sabzi or plain garlic chutney.

entries.title: Besan ki Chakki
entries.snippet: dense granular fudge of ghee-roasted gram flour, sweet and toasty
entries.text: besan ki chakki rajasthani dense granular fudge of ghee-roasted gram flour, sweet and toasty vegetarian gluten-free besan (gram flour) ghee sugar water milk green cardamom pistachios saffron boil the sugar and water together and cook 6-7 minutes to a one-string consistency — a drop between finger and thumb should pull a single short thread. keep it warm. in a heavy kadhai melt the ghee over low heat and add the besan. roast on low, stirring constantly, for 20-25 minutes. it will go from crumbly to pasty to loose and flowing, and turn the colour of peanut butter. when it smells strongly nutty, sprinkle over the warm milk — it will hiss and foam violently. keep stirring. keep roasting 5 more minutes as the mixture breaks into loose granules and the ghee visibly separates. take off the heat, wait 1 minute, then pour in the hot syrup in a thin stream, stirring hard. return to low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until the mixture thickens and starts pulling away from the sides of the pan. stir in the cardamom and saffron milk, pour into the greased tray and level the top with the back of a spoon. scatter the pistachios, press them in lightly, and cool 45 minutes before cutting into squares or diamonds.

entries.title: Dahi Wale Aloo
entries.snippet: boiled potatoes in a thin, tangy yogurt gravy with no onion or garlic
entries.text: dahi wale aloo rajasthani boiled potatoes in a thin, tangy yogurt gravy with no onion or garlic vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato yogurt / dahi besan (gram flour) ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder fennel powder garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the ghee in a kadhai over medium heat and crackle the cumin until it turns a shade darker, about 20 seconds. add the hing, then the grated ginger and slit chillies, and fry 40 seconds until fragrant. lower the heat, add the turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and fennel powder, and stir for 15 seconds only. pull the pan off the heat, count to ten, then pour in the yogurt-besan mixture in a steady stream while stirring hard. return to low heat and stir continuously in one direction until the gravy comes to a bare simmer, about 5 minutes. only now stop stirring. add the potatoes, the remaining 200ml water and salt. simmer uncovered 10 minutes; the gravy should stay pourable, not thick. crush a few potato pieces against the side of the pan to give the gravy body, then simmer 2 minutes more. finish with garam masala and coriander. serve hot with puri or plain rice.

entries.title: Dal Baati Churma
entries.snippet: Baked wheat balls drowned in ghee, with a five-lentil dal and sweet crushed churma
entries.text: dal baati churma rajasthani baked wheat balls drowned in ghee, with a five-lentil dal and sweet crushed churma vegetarian atta (wholewheat flour) rava / sooji (semolina) ghee carom seeds (ajwain) toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal moong dal urad dal (black gram) masoor dal (red lentil) onion tomato ginger garlic cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala jaggery green cardamom almonds salt make a stiff dough from atta, rava, ajwain, salt and 4 tbsp ghee with as little water as possible. rest 20 minutes. shape into balls, press a dimple into each, and bake at 200c for 35-40 minutes, turning once, until cracked and deep golden. meanwhile pressure cook the mixed dals with turmeric and salt until soft, 4 whistles. temper cumin and asafoetida in ghee, add ginger, garlic and onion, then tomato and the powdered spices. cook until the fat separates, then fold into the dal and simmer 10 minutes. for the churma, crush a few baatis coarsely and work in jaggery, cardamom, chopped almonds and hot ghee. to serve, dunk each hot baati in melted ghee, break it open into the dal, and eat with churma on the side.

entries.title: Gatta Pulao
entries.snippet: basmati layered with fried besan dumplings and whole spices, a marwari one-pot
entries.text: gatta pulao rajasthani basmati layered with fried besan dumplings and whole spices, a marwari one-pot vegetarian gluten-free nut-free basmati rice besan (gram flour) yogurt / dahi carom seeds (ajwain) neutral oil ghee cumin seeds bay leaf cloves cinnamon black cardamom onion green chilli ginger turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water rub the besan with 1 tbsp oil, the yogurt, ajwain, 1/4 tsp turmeric, half the chilli powder and salt, then knead into a stiff dough with a splash of water. rest 10 minutes. roll into 3 ropes about 1.5cm thick and drop them into 1 litre of boiling salted water. boil 10 minutes until they float and feel firm. lift out, cool, and cut into 2cm pieces. fry the pieces in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat until golden on all sides, about 5 minutes. drain and set aside. in a heavy pot heat the ghee and add the cumin, bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and black cardamom. wait for the cumin to darken and the spices to smell sweet, about 30 seconds. add the sliced onion and fry 8 minutes on medium until evenly golden brown at the edges. add the ginger and green chilli, fry 1 minute, then the remaining turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with 2 tbsp water. cook 2 minutes. tip in the drained rice and turn it gently in the masala for 2 minutes until every grain is coated and looks glassy at the edges. add 550ml hot water and salt. bring to a rolling boil, then scatter the fried gatte over the top without stirring them in. cover tightly, drop to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes. do not lift the lid. rest off the heat, still covered, 10 minutes. then fold through the coriander, garam masala and lemon juice with a fork.

entries.title: Gatte ki Sabzi
entries.snippet: steamed gram-flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yogurt gravy
entries.text: gatte ki sabzi rajasthani steamed gram-flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yogurt gravy vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) yogurt / dahi ghee carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder dried red chillies garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt knead the besan with 2 tbsp ghee, the ajwain, 1/2 tsp salt and about 4 tbsp yogurt into a stiff, smooth dough. it should feel like firm putty, not sticky. rest the dough 10 minutes, then roll into 4 ropes about 1.5cm thick. slide the ropes into rolling boiling water and cook 12-14 minutes, until they float and the surface looks matte rather than shiny. lift out, cool 5 minutes, and cut into 2cm pieces. save 250ml of the cooking water — it is the body of the gravy. heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the cumin, add the hing and broken red chilli, and let them darken for 10 seconds. pour in the spiced yogurt and stir continuously on low heat for 4-5 minutes until it stops looking grainy and a film of ghee shows at the edge. add the reserved cooking water and salt, and simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon. slip in the gatte and simmer another 5 minutes so they drink up the gravy. crush in the kasuri methi, sprinkle the garam masala and coriander leaves, and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Govind Gatte
entries.snippet: besan dumplings stuffed with khoya and nuts, simmered in a yogurt gravy
entries.text: govind gatte rajasthani besan dumplings stuffed with khoya and nuts, simmered in a yogurt gravy vegetarian gluten-free besan (gram flour) yogurt / dahi carom seeds (ajwain) baking soda khoya / mawa cashews raisins (kishmish) dried coconut (copra) black pepper onion ginger garlic neutral oil ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) kashmiri chilli powder coriander powder turmeric powder garam masala kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water rub the besan with 2 tbsp oil, the thick yogurt, ajwain, baking soda, 1/4 tsp turmeric and salt until it looks like coarse crumbs, then bring it together with a tablespoon or two of water into a stiff dough. knead 2 minutes and rest 10 minutes. mash the khoya with the cashew, raisins, dried coconut, cracked pepper and a pinch of salt into a coarse, sticky filling. chill it. divide the dough into 8. flatten each into a 7cm disc on your palm, place a teaspoon of filling in the centre, draw the edges over and roll into a smooth cylinder about 5cm long. seal any cracks with a wet fingertip. lower the cylinders into 1.2 litres of gently boiling salted water. cook 12 minutes — they will bob to the surface and firm up. lift out, cool 5 minutes, then cut each into 3 thick pieces. keep 300ml of the cooking water. fry the pieces in the remaining 2 tbsp oil over medium heat, turning, until they are freckled gold on the cut faces, about 4 minutes. set aside. in the same kadhai heat the ghee, crackle the cumin, add the hing, and one second later the onion paste. cook 8 minutes until it stops smelling raw and pulls away from the pan. add the ginger and garlic and fry 2 minutes, then the kashmiri chilli, coriander powder and remaining turmeric with a splash of water. bhuno until the oil separates and rims the masala, about 4 minutes. take the pan off the heat, wait 30 seconds, then pour in the whisked yogurt in a thin stream, stirring constantly. return to low heat and keep stirring until it comes to a bare simmer. add the reserved cooking water, salt and the fried gatte. simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon and darkens. finish with garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and scatter coriander over. serve with plain phulka or rice.

entries.title: Haldi ki Sabzi
entries.snippet: winter curry of fresh turmeric root and peas cooked down in yogurt and ghee
entries.text: haldi ki sabzi rajasthani winter curry of fresh turmeric root and peas cooked down in yogurt and ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic turmeric powder peas yogurt / dahi ghee ginger green chilli cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala cream coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt heat 4 tbsp ghee on low and add the grated turmeric. fry gently for 12-15 minutes, stirring often, until the raw earthy smell turns sweet and the ghee runs clear orange at the sides. push the turmeric aside, add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and crackle the cumin, then the hing, ginger and green chillies. stir in the coriander and chilli powders off the heat for 10 seconds. take the pan right off the flame, add the whisked yogurt, then return to the lowest heat and stir continuously 5-6 minutes until it thickens and the ghee separates. add the peas, salt and water, cover and simmer 10 minutes until the peas are tender and the gravy is thick. stir in the cream and garam masala and cook 2 more minutes. rest 5 minutes, scatter the coriander leaves and serve with bajre ki roti and a spoonful of jaggery on the side.

entries.title: Junglee Maas
entries.snippet: a hunter's mutton cooked with almost nothing but ghee, whole red chillies and salt
entries.text: junglee maas rajasthani a hunter's mutton cooked with almost nothing but ghee, whole red chillies and salt gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb ghee dried red chillies garlic salt water warm the ghee in a heavy pot over medium heat and add the whole red chillies. fry 40 seconds until they swell and darken, then lift them out and set aside. add the crushed garlic to the ghee and fry 1 minute until it is pale gold and perfumed. raise the heat, add the mutton in a single layer and let it sit undisturbed 4 minutes before turning. brown all over, about 12 minutes total. return the chillies to the pot with the salt and turn everything over the heat for 3 minutes so the ghee takes on the chilli colour. add 300ml water, bring to a boil, then cover and drop to the barest simmer. cook 55-65 minutes, turning the meat every 15 minutes, until it pulls away from the bone under a fork. uncover, raise the heat and cook off the remaining liquid, stirring, until the ghee separates out clear and red and clings to the meat, about 8 minutes. rest 10 minutes off the heat, then tilt the pot and spoon off any ghee you do not want. serve with bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Ker Sangri
entries.snippet: dry desert-style beans and berries, tart with amchur and hot with whole red chilli
entries.text: ker sangri rajasthani dry desert-style beans and berries, tart with amchur and hot with whole red chilli vegetarian gluten-free nut-free cluster beans (guar) raisins (kishmish) dried apricots (khubani) yogurt / dahi mustard oil dried red chillies cumin seeds carom seeds (ajwain) asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) water salt boil the cluster beans in salted water 8 minutes, until just yielding but still squeaky. drain well and pat dry. heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off the flame for 30 seconds, then return it to medium heat. crackle the cumin and ajwain, add the whole red chillies and hing, and fry 20 seconds until the chillies swell and darken. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder off the heat for 5 seconds so they bloom without burning. add the drained beans and toss over high heat 4-5 minutes until they take on brown blistered patches. fold in the raisins and apricot, add the water and salt, cover and cook 8 minutes on low. lower the heat right down, stir in the whisked yogurt and cook 4 minutes until it clings to the beans and no liquid pools at the base. finish with the amchur, toss once, and serve dry alongside bajre ki roti and a spoon of ghee.

entries.title: Khoba Roti
entries.snippet: a thick wheat flatbread pinched into ridges that hold pools of ghee
entries.text: khoba roti rajasthani a thick wheat flatbread pinched into ridges that hold pools of ghee vegetarian nut-free no-onion-garlic atta (wholewheat flour) ghee carom seeds (ajwain) salt water mix the atta with the salt, ajwain and 1 tbsp ghee, rubbing until it feels like breadcrumbs. add the warm water in stages and knead 8 minutes into a firm, smooth dough — noticeably stiffer than chapati dough. cover and rest 20 minutes. divide into 4. roll each into a thick disc about 15cm across and a full 1cm deep. do not roll it thin. working from the centre out, pinch the surface between thumb and forefinger to raise ridges, leaving a pattern of small pits across the whole disc. leave a 1cm plain border. heat a tawa on medium until a drop of water skitters. lay the roti pinched side up and cook 3 minutes until the base is set and pale brown in patches. flip and cook the pinched side 2 minutes, pressing only the plain border with a cloth so the ridges keep their shape. flip back and cook the base another 3-4 minutes on low, turning the roti a quarter turn twice so it cooks evenly. it should sound hollow when tapped. finish the pinched side directly over a low open flame for 30 seconds until the ridge tips char in spots. brush generously with the remaining ghee while hot so it runs into the pits. serve with lehsun ki chutney or ker sangri.

entries.title: Laal Maas
entries.snippet: fiery mutton curry stained deep red by whole chillies and slow-cooked in ghee
entries.text: laal maas rajasthani fiery mutton curry stained deep red by whole chillies and slow-cooked in ghee gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb kashmiri chilli powder dried red chillies yogurt / dahi ghee onion garlic ginger coriander powder turmeric powder cumin seeds cloves cinnamon black cardamom bay leaf garam masala water salt heat the ghee and fry the whole spices — cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom, bay leaf and cumin — for 30 seconds until they smell toasted. add the sliced onion and cook 12-14 minutes over medium heat until deep gold and collapsed. stir in the garlic and ginger pastes and fry 3 minutes until the raw smell goes. add the mutton and brown over high heat 8 minutes, turning the pieces so they seize on all sides. turn the heat to low, add the yogurt-and-chilli paste with the coriander powder and turmeric, and bhuno for 12-15 minutes, stirring, until the ghee separates and pools red at the edges. add the whole dried red chillies, salt and water, and pressure-cook 5 whistles, or cover and simmer 60 minutes, until the meat pulls off the bone. uncover and reduce 10 minutes until the gravy is glossy and clings to the meat. optional dhungar: set a small steel bowl in the pan, drop in a red-hot coal, pour a teaspoon of ghee over it and cover for 4 minutes to smoke the curry. sprinkle the garam masala, rest 10 minutes, and serve with bajre ki roti or plain rice.

entries.title: Lehsun ki Chutney
entries.snippet: a fierce red garlic and chilli chutney pounded with mustard oil and lemon
entries.text: lehsun ki chutney rajasthani a fierce red garlic and chilli chutney pounded with mustard oil and lemon vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free garlic dried red chillies kashmiri chilli powder mustard oil cumin seeds lemon / lime salt water heat the mustard oil until it smokes faintly, then take it off the heat and let it cool to warm, about 5 minutes. drain the soaked chillies, keeping 4 tbsp of the soaking water. grind the chillies, garlic, cumin and salt to a thick, coarse paste with the soaking water. stop while it still has some texture — this is not a smooth sauce. return 2 tbsp of the mustard oil to the pan on medium heat and fry the paste, stirring, for 6-8 minutes until it darkens and the raw garlic smell is gone. stir in the kashmiri chilli in the last minute for colour, then take the pan off the heat. cool completely, then beat in the lemon juice and the remaining tablespoon of mustard oil. taste for salt. it should be hot, sour, garlicky and just loose enough to spoon.

entries.title: Malpua
entries.snippet: fennel-scented pancakes fried in ghee and steeped in cardamom syrup
entries.text: malpua rajasthani fennel-scented pancakes fried in ghee and steeped in cardamom syrup vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) khoya / mawa milk rava / sooji (semolina) sugar water fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom ghee saffron boil the sugar and water 5-6 minutes to a sticky syrup just short of one string, add the saffron and cardamom, and keep warm. mash the grated khoya with 4 tbsp of the milk until lump-free. whisk in the maida, rava and crushed fennel, then the rest of the milk, a little at a time, into a smooth pouring batter. rest the batter 45 minutes, then check it — it should coat a spoon and drip in a ribbon. loosen with milk if needed. heat 2cm of ghee in a shallow kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter sizzles immediately. pour a small ladleful into the centre of the pan. do not spread it — let it settle into a 8cm disc with frilled edges. fry 2 minutes, spooning hot ghee over the top, until the edges are deep gold and lacy, then flip and fry 1 minute more. lift out, drain for a few seconds, and drop straight into the warm syrup. soak 3-4 minutes, then lift onto a plate. repeat with the rest of the batter, frying two at a time, and serve warm with rabri or on their own.

entries.title: Mangodi ki Sabzi
entries.snippet: sun-dried moong dal nuggets fried crisp and stewed in a tart tomato masala
entries.text: mangodi ki sabzi rajasthani sun-dried moong dal nuggets fried crisp and stewed in a tart tomato masala vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free moong dal neutral oil tomato garlic ginger green chilli cumin seeds mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai over medium heat and fry the mangodi in two batches, stirring constantly, until they turn a deep reddish brown and smell nutty, about 3 minutes a batch. drain on paper. tip out all but 2 tbsp of oil. crackle the cumin and mustard seeds, then add the hing and let it foam for a second. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 90 seconds until the garlic is pale gold at the edges. stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with 2 tbsp water so they do not scorch, then pour in the tomato puree. cook the masala on medium heat 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it thickens, darkens and the oil pools at the sides. add 600ml water and salt, bring to a boil, then slide in the fried mangodi. simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes until the mangodi have swollen to twice their size and are soft right through but still hold their shape. stir in the amchur and garam masala, simmer 2 minutes more, and finish with coriander. serve with bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Mawa Kachori
entries.snippet: jodhpur's sweet kachori — khoya and nuts in flaky pastry, drowned in syrup
entries.text: mawa kachori rajasthani jodhpur's sweet kachori — khoya and nuts in flaky pastry, drowned in syrup vegetarian plain flour (maida) ghee khoya / mawa sugar water green cardamom almonds cashews pistachios raisins (kishmish) dried coconut (copra) saffron salt rub the 60ml ghee into the maida with the pinch of salt for 3 minutes, then add water gradually to a soft dough. cover and rest 30 minutes. roast the grated khoya in a dry pan over low heat 6-8 minutes until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. spread on a plate and cool fully. mix the cold khoya with the powdered sugar, cardamom, almonds, cashew, half the pistachios, raisins and dried coconut. boil the 350g sugar with 175ml water 6 minutes to a one-string syrup, add the saffron, and keep it warm. divide the dough into 8. roll each into a 9cm disc, thicker in the middle than at the rim. place a heaped tablespoon of filling in the centre, gather the edges up over it, pinch tightly shut and twist off the excess dough. flatten each gently with your palm into a 7cm disc and rest them seam-down for 10 minutes. heat the frying ghee to a low 140c — a kachori should take a good 10 seconds to float up. fry 4 at a time for 12-14 minutes on low, spooning ghee over them, until blistered and pale gold all over. drain briefly, then dip each hot kachori in the warm syrup for 30 seconds and lift onto a plate. crack open the top, spoon a little extra syrup inside, scatter the remaining pistachios and serve warm.

entries.title: Methi Bajra Puri
entries.snippet: millet and fenugreek puris, crisp-edged and faintly bitter
entries.text: methi bajra puri rajasthani millet and fenugreek puris, crisp-edged and faintly bitter vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free bajra (pearl millet) flour atta (wholewheat flour) fenugreek leaves (methi) neutral oil carom seeds (ajwain) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder sesame seeds water salt squeeze the salted methi dry and put it in a bowl with both flours, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, sesame and salt. rub in the 2 tbsp oil, then add warm water a little at a time to make a stiff dough, firmer than chapati dough. knead 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest 15 minutes. divide into 16 balls and roll each into a 10cm disc on a lightly oiled surface, about 3mm thick. heat the oil to 180c. a scrap of dough should rise to the surface in about 2 seconds. slide in one puri, press it under with the back of a slotted spoon for 3 seconds until it puffs. flip and fry the second side 30-40 seconds until the edges are crisp and the colour is deep brown-green. drain upright in a colander so the oil runs off, and serve hot with aloo pyaaz ki sabzi or plain yogurt.

entries.title: Mirchi Vada
entries.snippet: jodhpur's fat green chillies stuffed with spiced potato and fried in gram-flour batter
entries.text: mirchi vada rajasthani jodhpur's fat green chillies stuffed with spiced potato and fried in gram-flour batter vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic green chilli potato besan (gram flour) neutral oil cumin seeds fennel seeds (saunf) asafoetida (hing) ginger turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) carom seeds (ajwain) baking soda water salt heat 2 tbsp oil, crackle the cumin and fennel, add the hing and grated ginger, and fry 30 seconds. add the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders off the heat, then fold in the mashed potato and salt. cook 4 minutes over medium heat, then stir in the amchur and coriander leaves and cool completely. whisk the besan with the ajwain, baking soda, a pinch of salt and enough water to make a batter that thickly coats a spoon and does not run off it. pack each chilli firmly through its slit with the potato filling and press the slit closed. heat the frying oil to 175c — a drop of batter should rise steadily and sizzle without browning instantly. dip each stuffed chilli in the batter, turning to coat completely including the ends, and lower it into the oil. fry 4-5 minutes, turning once, until the crust is pale gold and crisp. do no more than three at a time. drain on paper and serve hot with tamarind or mint chutney, or pushed into a soft bun as jodhpur does.

entries.title: Moong Dal Halwa
entries.snippet: a slow-roasted lentil halwa, grainy and deeply nutty, eaten in the cold months
entries.text: moong dal halwa rajasthani a slow-roasted lentil halwa, grainy and deeply nutty, eaten in the cold months vegetarian gluten-free moong dal ghee milk sugar water green cardamom saffron almonds cashews raisins (kishmish) grind the drained dal to a coarse, thick paste. it should hold a ridge when you drag a spoon through it. melt the ghee in a heavy kadhai over low-medium heat and add the dal paste. it will seize into a solid mass immediately — this is normal. roast, stirring and scraping constantly with a flat spatula, for 35-45 minutes. it moves through pale lumps, then a sandy crumble, then a loose glossy mass that smells like toasted besan and turns golden brown. fry the almonds, cashews and raisins in a spoonful of the separating ghee for 1 minute and lift them out. keep going until the ghee visibly separates and pools around the edges of the mass. do not move on before this happens. meanwhile bring the sugar and 200ml water to a boil in a small pan and simmer 3 minutes into a thin syrup. keep it hot. pour the hot milk into the roasted dal in three additions, stirring hard after each, and let it be absorbed before the next. add the hot syrup and the saffron milk. stir continuously 8-10 minutes until the halwa drinks it up and thickens. cook until the halwa comes together and slides as one mass, leaving a clean film of ghee on the pan, about 5 minutes more. fold in the crushed cardamom and the fried nuts and raisins. rest 5 minutes off the heat and serve hot.

entries.title: Panchmel Dal
entries.snippet: five lentils cooked together and finished with a ghee, hing and red chilli tadka
entries.text: panchmel dal rajasthani five lentils cooked together and finished with a ghee, hing and red chilli tadka vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal moong dal urad dal (black gram) masoor dal (red lentil) ghee cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies bay leaf cloves ginger green chilli tomato turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt drain the soaked dals and pressure-cook with the turmeric, 1 tbsp ghee and 900ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. whisk the cooked dal briefly — it should be soft but the chana dal still recognisable, not a puree. heat 2 tbsp ghee in a separate pan, crackle 1 tsp cumin with the bay leaf and cloves. add the ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant. stir in the coriander powder, chilli powder and half the hing off the heat for 10 seconds, then add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down. pour this into the dal with the salt and the remaining water, and simmer 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens to a pouring consistency. stir in the amchur and garam masala and taste for salt and sourness. for the final tadka, heat the last 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the remaining cumin, add the broken red chillies and the rest of the hing, and pour it over the dal while it is still foaming. scatter the coriander leaves and serve with baati or bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Pyaaz Kachori
entries.snippet: Flaky fried pastry with a spiced onion filling, from the sweet shops of Jodhpur
entries.text: pyaaz kachori rajasthani flaky fried pastry with a spiced onion filling, from the sweet shops of jodhpur vegetarian nut-free plain flour (maida) ghee onion besan (gram flour) fennel seeds (saunf) coriander powder cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) asafoetida (hing) neutral oil salt rub the ghee into the flour with salt until it holds together when squeezed, then add water a little at a time to make a firm dough. rest 30 minutes. fry the cumin, fennel, nigella and asafoetida, add the onion and cook until soft and just golden, not brown. add the besan and the powdered spices and cook 4-5 minutes until dry and crumbly. add amchur, cool completely. roll small dough balls into cups, fill, gather and seal, then flatten very gently to about 1cm. fry in oil kept at a low 130-140c for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until pale gold and covered in blisters. drain on a rack. serve warm with tamarind and coriander chutneys.

entries.title: Pyaaz Kachori
entries.snippet: flaky fried pastry packed with a dark, heavily spiced onion and besan filling
entries.text: pyaaz kachori rajasthani flaky fried pastry packed with a dark, heavily spiced onion and besan filling vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free plain flour (maida) neutral oil onion besan (gram flour) fennel seeds (saunf) cumin seeds coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder garam masala amchur (dry mango powder) asafoetida (hing) ginger green chilli nigella seeds (kalonji) water salt rub the 60ml oil into the maida with 1/2 tsp salt for 3 minutes, then add water a little at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. cover and rest 30 minutes. heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin, fennel and nigella, then add the hing. add the chopped onion and cook 12-15 minutes over medium heat until it loses all its water and turns light brown. stir in the ginger, green chilli and besan and roast 4 minutes until the besan smells nutty. add the ground spices, amchur and salt and bhuno 3 more minutes, then spread the filling on a plate to cool. divide the dough into 8, roll each into a ball, and flatten into a 8cm disc thicker at the centre than the edge. place a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle, gather the edges over it, pinch shut and pull off the excess knot of dough. flatten each stuffed ball gently with your palm into a 7cm disc. rest them 10 minutes, seam down. heat the frying oil to just 140c, low enough that a kachori dropped in takes 8-10 seconds to float. slide in 3 or 4. fry very slowly, 12-14 minutes, spooning oil over the tops, until they are covered in blisters and pale gold. raise the heat for the last 2 minutes to crisp them. drain and serve warm, cracked open with tamarind chutney poured in.

entries.title: Rajasthani Kadhi
entries.snippet: thin, sour buttermilk kadhi sharpened with a chilli and hing tempering
entries.text: rajasthani kadhi rajasthani thin, sour buttermilk kadhi sharpened with a chilli and hing tempering vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic besan (gram flour) buttermilk (chaas) ghee cumin seeds mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) dried red chillies green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) salt whisk the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt into the buttermilk until completely smooth. strain it if you can see any lumps. pour into a heavy pan and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction. as soon as it boils, drop the heat to low and simmer 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until it thickens slightly and loses its raw besan smell. add the slit green chillies and cook another 2 minutes. in a small pan heat the ghee, crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin, then the fenugreek seeds for 10 seconds. add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and hing, and pull off the heat the moment the chillies darken. pour the tempering over the kadhi, cover for 2 minutes to trap the aroma, then stir through with the coriander leaves. serve loose and pourable over steamed rice, or with bajre ki roti.

entries.title: Safed Maas
entries.snippet: pale, creamy mutton braised with cashew, yogurt and white pepper instead of red chilli
entries.text: safed maas rajasthani pale, creamy mutton braised with cashew, yogurt and white pepper instead of red chilli gluten-free healthier mutton / lamb cashews almonds poppy seeds (khus khus) melon seeds (magaz) yogurt / dahi cream ghee onion garlic ginger white pepper green chilli green cardamom cloves cinnamon mace (javitri) kewra water water salt heat the ghee on medium and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and mace 30 seconds, without letting them colour. add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes until the raw edge goes but no colour develops. stir in the boiled onion paste and cook 5 minutes on low, stirring, until it thickens and smells sweet. add the mutton and turn it in the paste 6 minutes over medium heat — sealing, not browning. take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt, then return to the lowest flame and cook 8 minutes until it thickens and the ghee edges out. add the nut paste, white pepper, green chillies, salt and water. pressure-cook 5 whistles, or cover and simmer 60 minutes until the meat is tender. uncover and simmer 8 minutes to reduce until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. stir in the cream and kewra water, warm through 2 minutes without boiling, and rest 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Aloo Tuk
entries.snippet: twice-fried smashed potatoes, crisp outside and floury within, dusted with amchur
entries.text: aloo tuk sindhi twice-fried smashed potatoes, crisp outside and floury within, dusted with amchur vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free potato neutral oil amchur (dry mango powder) chaat masala red chilli powder black salt (kala namak) black pepper salt heat the oil to medium — a potato piece dropped in should bubble steadily around the edges, not fizz furiously. fry the potatoes in two batches for 8-10 minutes each, until pale gold and a skewer slides in easily. they should be cooked through but not coloured much. lift them out onto a rack and let them cool for 10 minutes. flatten each piece with the heel of your hand or the flat of a knife to about 1.5cm, so the edges crack open. raise the oil to high, until a scrap of potato surfaces immediately. fry the flattened pieces again in batches, 3-4 minutes, until deep golden and audibly crisp when knocked against the ladle. drain on a rack rather than paper so the undersides do not steam soft. while still very hot, toss with the spice mix and taste for salt. serve at once, alongside sindhi kadhi and rice as tradition has it, or on their own with tea.

entries.title: Bhee Patata
entries.snippet: rhizome and potato braised down in a dry onion-tomato masala until the edges catch
entries.text: bhee patata sindhi rhizome and potato braised down in a dry onion-tomato masala until the edges catch vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier lotus stem (nadru/bhee) potato onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder cumin seeds amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil water salt heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds, about 20 seconds. fry the par-boiled lotus stem coins and the potato fingers on medium-high for 8 minutes, turning once or twice, until patched with gold. lift them out. in the same oil, fry the onion 8-10 minutes until properly brown at the edges, not merely soft. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute, until the raw garlic smell goes. stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook 6-8 minutes, until the mass darkens and oil pools at the sides. return the vegetables, turn them through the masala, add the water and cover. cook on low 12-15 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the potato is tender and almost no liquid remains. uncover, raise the heat and let it fry dry for 2-3 minutes so the underside catches and crusts. sprinkle over the amchur and coriander leaves, toss once and take it off the heat.

entries.title: Bhee ji Bhaji
entries.snippet: dry-cooked lotus stem, crisp at the edges and sharp with amchur
entries.text: bhee ji bhaji sindhi dry-cooked lotus stem, crisp at the edges and sharp with amchur vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier lotus stem (nadru/bhee) onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli neutral oil carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water pressure cook the lotus stem rounds with the water and 1/2 tsp salt for 8 minutes, about 2 whistles, then drain and reserve 1/4 cup of the cooking water. heat the oil in a heavy pan and crackle the ajwain and cumin for 30 seconds. add the asafoetida, then the crushed garlic, and fry 45 seconds until it turns pale gold. add the onion, ginger and green chilli, and fry 7 minutes until the onion is golden at the edges. add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder, and cook 6 minutes until the tomato collapses and the oil separates. tip in the drained lotus stem and toss to coat every round in masala. add the reserved cooking water, cover, and cook 8 minutes over low heat. uncover, raise the heat and fry 6-8 minutes without stirring much, until the rounds catch and brown in patches. sprinkle over the amchur and salt, toss once, and take off the heat. finish with coriander leaves and serve with phulka.

entries.title: Bhuga Chawal
entries.snippet: brown onion rice, sweet and savoury at once, the plate that sindhi kadhi is poured over
entries.text: bhuga chawal sindhi brown onion rice, sweet and savoury at once, the plate that sindhi kadhi is poured over vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free basmati rice onion neutral oil cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon cloves black pepper water salt heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onion over medium heat, stirring often. keep going 18-20 minutes. the onions will go translucent, then straw, then a deep mahogany brown and sticky-sweet. push the onions aside, add the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns and let them sizzle 20 seconds. add the drained rice and turn it gently through the onions and oil for 2 minutes, until every grain is glossy and faintly brown. pour in the hot water, add the salt and bring to a hard boil. as soon as the water level drops to the surface of the rice, about 5 minutes, cover tightly and drop the heat to its lowest setting. cook undisturbed 12 minutes, then take the pot off the heat and let it stand, still covered, 10 minutes. fluff with a fork from the edges inward and serve with sindhi kadhi ladled over.

entries.title: Dal Pakwan
entries.snippet: soft chana dal under a shower of chaat masala with crisp fried maida discs to break over it
entries.text: dal pakwan sindhi soft chana dal under a shower of chaat masala with crisp fried maida discs to break over it vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free chana dal turmeric powder plain flour (maida) rava / sooji (semolina) carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) green chilli ginger tomato red chilli powder amchur (dry mango powder) chaat masala black salt (kala namak) onion coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime neutral oil water salt knead the maida, rava, 1/2 tsp ajwain, 1/2 tsp salt and 4 tbsp oil with about 3/4 cup water into a firm, smooth dough. cover and rest 30 minutes. pressure cook the drained dal with the turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt and 4 cups water for 2 whistles, then 4 minutes on low. the grains should be soft but still separate, not a puree. heat 3 tbsp oil in a small pan, crackle the remaining cumin and ajwain, add the hing, green chilli and half the ginger. add the tomato, chilli powder and amchur and cook 3 minutes until the oil separates, then pour the whole tempering into the dal. simmer the dal 8-10 minutes, mashing a ladleful against the side to thicken it. it should be spoonable, like loose porridge. divide the dough into 12. roll each into a thin 12cm disc and prick it all over with a fork — 20 or 30 holes, right through. heat the frying oil to medium — a scrap of dough should rise slowly, not race to the top. fry each pakwan 2-3 minutes a side until pale gold and rigid. drain the pakwan upright in a colander so they stay crisp rather than steaming on kitchen paper. ladle the hot dal into bowls, top with chopped onion, remaining ginger, coriander, chaat masala and black salt, and squeeze over lemon. serve at once with the pakwan alongside, to be cracked and dipped.

entries.title: Koki
entries.snippet: thick crumbly onion flatbread cooked twice on the tawa, the Sindhi breakfast bread
entries.text: koki sindhi thick crumbly onion flatbread cooked twice on the tawa, the sindhi breakfast bread vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) carom seeds (ajwain) cumin seeds red chilli powder ghee water salt rub 4 tbsp ghee into the atta with your fingertips until the flour clumps when squeezed. this moyan is what makes koki crumbly rather than chewy. mix in the squeezed onion, green chilli, coriander, anardana, ajwain, cumin, chilli powder and salt. add water a spoonful at a time and knead to a stiff, tight dough. cover and rest 15 minutes. divide into 4 balls. roll each one about 1cm thick and 12cm across — much thicker than a roti. cook the first side on a medium-hot tawa, dry, for about 1 minute, until it turns opaque and speckles lightly. flip and give the other side 1 minute. lift the half-cooked disc off, let it cool a minute, then roll it again to about 7mm thick. prick all over with a fork. return it to the tawa on low-medium heat, spoon a tablespoon of ghee around the edge and cook 3-4 minutes a side, pressing with a cloth, until deep gold with brown blisters. repeat with the remaining dough and serve hot with plain yogurt, mango pickle or sweet tea.

entries.title: Mitho Lolo
entries.snippet: sweet fennel-scented ghee flatbread, made for Cheti Chand and eaten with plain yogurt
entries.text: mitho lolo sindhi sweet fennel-scented ghee flatbread, made for cheti chand and eaten with plain yogurt vegetarian nut-free atta (wholewheat flour) jaggery ghee fennel seeds (saunf) green cardamom black pepper milk water salt rub 4 tbsp ghee into the atta with your fingertips for a couple of minutes, until the flour holds its shape when pressed in a fist. mix in the fennel, ground cardamom, cracked pepper and salt. pour in the strained jaggery water and the milk and bring it together into a stiff dough — softer than pastry, firmer than roti dough. add flour by the spoonful if it sticks. cover and rest 20 minutes. divide into 6 balls. roll each to about 8mm thick and 12cm across, dusting with flour — thicker than a paratha, and no need to be neat. cook on a medium-low tawa for about 2 minutes, until the surface dries and small blisters appear. flip. spoon a tablespoon of ghee around the edge and cook 2-3 minutes a side, pressing gently with a cloth, until both faces are freckled deep brown. stack the cooked lolos under a cloth so they steam and soften, and serve warm with plain yogurt or a glass of milk.

entries.title: Sai Bhaji
entries.snippet: spinach and chana dal cooked down with vegetables into a soft green mash, eaten with rice most weeknights
entries.text: sai bhaji sindhi spinach and chana dal cooked down with vegetables into a soft green mash, eaten with rice most weeknights vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier spinach dill (suva) chana dal potato eggplant / brinjal carrot tomato onion garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder cumin seeds neutral oil water salt heat the oil in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds, about 20 seconds. add the onion, garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 4 minutes, until the onion is translucent — you are not browning it. stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder and cook 3 minutes until the oil beads at the edges. add the drained chana dal, potato, eggplant and carrot and turn everything through the masala for a minute. pile in the spinach and dill with the water and salt. it will look impossibly full; press it down and it collapses within a minute. close the cooker and cook on high for 3 whistles, then lower the heat and give it 5 minutes more. let the pressure drop on its own. open up and mash everything against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle until it is coarse and green, not smooth. simmer uncovered 5-8 minutes, stirring, until it holds its shape on a spoon. check the salt. serve hot with steamed rice, a spoon of raw onion and a wedge of lemon.

entries.title: Sanna Pakora
entries.snippet: thin, shatteringly crisp gram flour fritters shot through with sliced onion
entries.text: sanna pakora sindhi thin, shatteringly crisp gram flour fritters shot through with sliced onion vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free besan (gram flour) onion potato green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) carom seeds (ajwain) anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) coriander powder red chilli powder turmeric powder baking soda neutral oil salt water toss the sliced onion with 1 tsp salt in a wide bowl and leave 10 minutes, then squeeze it lightly over the bowl and keep the liquid. add the potato, green chilli, coriander leaves, ajwain, crushed anardana, crushed coriander powder, chilli powder and turmeric to the onion and mix. sprinkle the besan and baking soda over the top and rub everything together with your fingers for 2 minutes without adding water. add water a tablespoon at a time until the mixture just clumps in your hand — thick and shaggy, nothing pourable. heat the frying oil in a kadhai to 170c. a pinch of batter should rise to the surface in about 4 seconds. stir 1 tbsp of the hot oil into the batter — it lightens the crumb. drop rough, loose spoonfuls into the oil, 6 or 7 at a time, and fry 4 minutes until pale gold. lift and drain on a rack. rest the first batch 5 minutes while you fry the rest. return all the pakoras to the oil, now raised to 185c, and fry 90 seconds more until deep gold and hard to the touch. drain and serve immediately with tamarind or tomato chutney.

entries.title: Seyal Bhaji
entries.snippet: potato and cauliflower smothered in a wet green coriander masala, quick and everyday
