entries.text: seyal bhaji sindhi potato and cauliflower smothered in a wet green coriander masala, quick and everyday vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier potato cauliflower peas coriander leaves (cilantro) onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder cumin seeds lemon / lime neutral oil water salt heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the onion and fry 6-7 minutes, until soft and just turning gold at the edges. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant. stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook 5 minutes until pulpy and oil-flecked. tip in the chopped coriander and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until it wilts right down and the masala turns dark green. add the potato, cauliflower and peas and turn them through until every piece is coated green. add the water, cover and cook on low 15 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the potato gives to a knife. uncover, raise the heat and cook 3 minutes more to dry off any loose liquid. squeeze over the lemon, check the salt and serve with phulka or plain rice.

entries.title: Seyal Gosht
entries.snippet: mutton braised down into a thick green coriander and mint masala
entries.text: seyal gosht sindhi mutton braised down into a thick green coriander and mint masala gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb coriander leaves (cilantro) mint green chilli garlic ginger onion tomato neutral oil turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala lemon / lime salt water blend the coriander, mint, green chilli, 8 garlic cloves and the ginger with 3 tbsp water to a coarse green paste. heat the oil in the pressure cooker and fry the 6 sliced garlic cloves for 40 seconds, until pale gold and fragrant. add the onion and cook 8 minutes over medium heat until soft and translucent. add the mutton, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. fry over high heat 10 minutes until the meat has released its juices and taken them back, and the pan looks dry. stir in the tomato and cook 6 minutes, until it collapses and oil beads at the edge of the mass. add the green paste and fry 5 minutes, stirring, until the colour shifts from bright grass green to deep olive. pour in the hot water, close the cooker and cook on high pressure 18 minutes, about 4 whistles. let the pressure fall on its own. open, and boil uncovered 6-8 minutes until the masala clings to the meat and there is no loose liquid in the pan. stir in the garam masala and lemon juice, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with phulka.

entries.title: Sindhi Besan Bhaji
entries.snippet: potatoes in a roasted gram flour gravy, tangy and thick enough to scoop
entries.text: sindhi besan bhaji sindhi potatoes in a roasted gram flour gravy, tangy and thick enough to scoop vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier besan (gram flour) potato onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder amchur (dry mango powder) coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water dry roast the besan in the kadhai over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and darkens by a shade. tip the roasted besan onto a plate and set it aside to cool. heat the oil in the same pan and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli, fry 45 seconds, then add the onion and cook 8 minutes until golden. add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder, and cook 6 minutes until the tomato breaks down completely. add the potato cubes and toss for 3 minutes so they take on the masala. sprinkle the roasted besan over the potatoes and stir for 1 minute to coat them evenly. pour in the hot water in a thin stream while stirring continuously, then add salt. cover and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the gravy has thickened enough to hold a spoon mark. stir in the amchur, cook 1 more minute, and finish with coriander leaves.

entries.title: Sindhi Biryani
entries.snippet: sharply sour, chilli-hot mutton biryani layered with potato, yogurt and dried fruit
entries.text: sindhi biryani sindhi sharply sour, chilli-hot mutton biryani layered with potato, yogurt and dried fruit gluten-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb basmati rice yogurt / dahi onion tomato potato ginger garlic green chilli mint coriander leaves (cilantro) dried apricots (khubani) red chilli powder turmeric powder coriander powder garam masala cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon cloves green cardamom black cardamom saffron kewra water ghee neutral oil water salt fry the sliced onion in the oil over medium heat, 15-18 minutes, stirring, until deep brown and shrunken. drain on paper and reserve. in the same oil, crackle the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and black cardamom for 30 seconds. add the marinated mutton and fry on high for 6-8 minutes, until the yogurt has dried onto the meat and the fat runs clear at the edges. stir in the tomato, coriander powder, half the green chilli, half the mint and coriander, and two-thirds of the birista. cook 5 minutes until the tomato collapses. add 1 cup water and salt, close the cooker and cook 4 whistles, then 12 minutes on low. release the pressure and boil off any thin liquid — the masala should be thick and clinging. fry the halved potatoes in a little oil until golden on the cut faces, then fold them into the meat with the dried apricot and cook 5 minutes. meanwhile bring 3 litres of well-salted water to a rolling boil, add the drained rice and cook 5-6 minutes only — a grain should snap in two when pressed, still white at the core. drain immediately. spread half the rice over the meat in a heavy pot, scatter the remaining birista, mint, coriander and green chilli, then the rest of the rice. drizzle over the saffron milk, kewra water and ghee. seal the pot with a tight lid, cook 2 minutes on high, then set it on the lowest possible heat (or a tawa under the pot) for 25 minutes. rest 10 minutes off the heat, then open and lift the rice from the sides with a flat spoon rather than stirring.

entries.title: Sindhi Chicken Curry
entries.snippet: chicken in a yogurt and onion gravy, sharp with green chilli and garam masala
entries.text: sindhi chicken curry sindhi chicken in a yogurt and onion gravy, sharp with green chilli and garam masala gluten-free nut-free healthier chicken yogurt / dahi onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli neutral oil turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder cumin powder (jeera) garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the onion 12 minutes over medium heat, until deep golden brown and shrunken to a third of its volume. add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and the green chilli, and fry 1 minute. add the tomato and cook 8 minutes, mashing with the back of the spoon, until it breaks down and oil pools at the edges. stir in the chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 30 seconds — no longer, or they scorch. turn the heat to low and add the marinated chicken with all its yogurt, stirring continuously for the first 2 minutes. raise the heat and fry the chicken 8 minutes until the pieces are opaque and the masala clings to them. add the water and salt, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 18 minutes until the chicken is tender at the bone. uncover and reduce 5 minutes to the gravy consistency you want. stir in the garam masala and lemon juice, rest 5 minutes covered, then finish with coriander leaves.

entries.title: Sindhi Dodo
entries.snippet: thick pearl millet flatbread studded with onion and green chilli, eaten with ghee
entries.text: sindhi dodo sindhi thick pearl millet flatbread studded with onion and green chilli, eaten with ghee vegetarian gluten-free nut-free bajra (pearl millet) flour onion green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) carom seeds (ajwain) ghee salt water mix the bajra flour, onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, ajwain and salt in a wide bowl. add the warm water a little at a time, working with your knuckles, until you have a firm dough that just holds together when squeezed. cover and rest the dough 10 minutes. divide into 6 balls. wet your palms and pat one ball out on a sheet of plastic or a damp cloth into a disc about 12cm across and 6mm thick. heat the tawa over medium heat until a drop of water skitters across it. lift the disc on your palm and lay it flat on the tawa. cook 2 minutes until the underside sets and dulls in colour. flip and cook 2 minutes more, then press the edges down with a folded cloth so the whole surface contacts the pan. flip once more and cook 1 minute until brown spots appear and the bread feels firm rather than doughy at the centre. smear generously with ghee and repeat with the remaining dough. serve hot with curd, garlic chutney or leftover sai bhaji.

entries.title: Sindhi Kadhi
entries.snippet: roasted gram flour and tamarind curry thick with drumstick and okra, the Sunday lunch of every Sindhi house
entries.text: sindhi kadhi sindhi roasted gram flour and tamarind curry thick with drumstick and okra, the sunday lunch of every sindhi house vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier besan (gram flour) neutral oil fenugreek seeds (methi) cumin seeds mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) tomato ginger green chilli turmeric powder red chilli powder drumstick (moringa pod) cluster beans (guar) potato carrot okra / bhindi tamarind coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai, crackle the fenugreek seeds and cumin, then the mustard seeds, curry leaves and hing. tip in the besan and roast on low heat, stirring constantly, 8-10 minutes until it is sandy-brown and smells like toasted biscuit. add the tomato, ginger and green chilli and cook 3 minutes until the tomato slumps. take the pan off the heat and pour in the hot water in a thin stream, whisking hard the whole time until smooth. return to the heat, add the turmeric, chilli powder and salt, and bring to a boil. simmer 10 minutes — it will thin out and then start to body up. add the drumstick and carrot and simmer 10 minutes. add the cluster beans and potato and simmer another 12-15 minutes, until a knife slides into the potato with no resistance. meanwhile fry the okra in the remaining 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 5-6 minutes, until the cut edges are dry and no longer ropy. stir in the tamarind pulp and the fried okra and simmer 5 minutes. taste: it should be assertively sour against the nutty besan. scatter the coriander over and let it stand 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice or bhuga chawal.

entries.title: Sindhi Seero
entries.snippet: coarse semolina halwa, heavy with ghee and cardamom, made for every good occasion
entries.text: sindhi seero sindhi coarse semolina halwa, heavy with ghee and cardamom, made for every good occasion vegetarian rava / sooji (semolina) ghee sugar water milk green cardamom almonds raisins (kishmish) salt bring the water, milk and sugar to a boil in a saucepan, stir until the sugar dissolves, and keep it on the lowest heat. melt the ghee in a heavy kadhai over low heat and fry the raisins for 30 seconds until they puff, then lift them out. fry the slivered almonds in the same ghee for 1 minute until pale gold, and lift them out too. add the rava to the ghee and roast over low-medium heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring constantly. add the pinch of salt and the crushed cardamom and stir for 30 seconds. take the kadhai off the heat and pour in the hot syrup in a steady stream, stirring hard with your other hand. return to low heat and cook 6-8 minutes, stirring, until the rava has drunk all the liquid and the mass pulls cleanly away from the sides of the pan. stir in most of the fried almonds and raisins, keeping some back. cover and rest off the heat for 5 minutes so the grains swell and soften fully. fluff with a fork, scatter the reserved nuts and raisins, and serve warm.

entries.title: Sindhi Teevan
entries.snippet: everyday mutton and potato curry with a thin, tomato-sharp gravy
entries.text: sindhi teevan sindhi everyday mutton and potato curry with a thin, tomato-sharp gravy gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier mutton / lamb potato onion tomato garlic ginger neutral oil cumin seeds bay leaf cinnamon black cardamom turmeric powder red chilli powder coriander powder garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) salt water heat the oil in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon and black cardamom for 30 seconds. add the onion and fry 10 minutes over medium heat until evenly golden brown. stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 90 seconds, until the raw smell lifts. add the mutton and brown over high heat 8 minutes, turning the pieces so every side catches colour. add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt, and stir for 1 minute to coat the meat. pour in the tomato puree and cook 10 minutes, until it darkens to brick red and oil separates at the sides. add the water, close the cooker and cook on high pressure 15 minutes, about 3 whistles. release the pressure naturally. open, add the potatoes, and simmer uncovered 15-18 minutes until a knife slides through them with no resistance. taste for salt, stir in the garam masala, and simmer 2 more minutes. scatter the coriander leaves and serve with plain rice or phulka.

entries.title: Sindhi Tomato Chutney
entries.snippet: slow-cooked sweet and sour tomato relish with garlic and a mustard tempering
entries.text: sindhi tomato chutney sindhi slow-cooked sweet and sour tomato relish with garlic and a mustard tempering vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tomato garlic ginger jaggery tamarind neutral oil mustard seeds cumin seeds nigella seeds (kalonji) fennel seeds (saunf) dried red chillies kashmiri chilli powder turmeric powder salt heat the oil in a heavy pan and crackle the mustard seeds until they pop, about 40 seconds. add the cumin, nigella, crushed fennel and broken red chillies, and fry 20 seconds. add the sliced garlic and ginger and fry 1 minute until the garlic is just golden at the edges. tip in the tomatoes with the turmeric, kashmiri chilli and salt, and stir well. cook uncovered over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the tomatoes have collapsed and lost their raw smell. stir in the jaggery and tamarind pulp and cook 12 minutes more, until the chutney darkens and thickens. taste and balance — more jaggery if it is too sharp, more tamarind if it is flat. take off the heat and cool completely in the pan before jarring.

entries.title: Tidali Dal
entries.snippet: three lentils cooked together into one soft, garlicky everyday dal
entries.text: tidali dal sindhi three lentils cooked together into one soft, garlicky everyday dal vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier chana dal moong dal urad dal (black gram) onion tomato garlic ginger green chilli neutral oil cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder red chilli powder garam masala coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt water drain the soaked chana dal and pressure cook all three dals with the water, turmeric and green chilli for 12 minutes, about 3 whistles. open the cooker and whisk the dal briefly — you want the moong broken down but the chana still holding as distinct grains. heat the oil in a small pan and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. add the asafoetida and the sliced garlic and fry 1 minute until the garlic is golden but not brown. add the onion and ginger and fry 6 minutes until the onion is soft and lightly browned. stir in the tomato and chilli powder and cook 6 minutes until the tomato collapses to a jammy mass. pour the tempering into the dal, add salt, and simmer 8 minutes so the flavours settle. stir in the garam masala and lemon juice off the heat. scatter the coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

entries.title: Adai
entries.snippet: a thick, coarse-ground four-lentil crepe, nuttier and heavier than dosa
entries.text: adai tamil nadu a thick, coarse-ground four-lentil crepe, nuttier and heavier than dosa vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) curry leaves ginger onion coconut (fresh or desiccated) coriander leaves (cilantro) sesame oil (gingelly / til) water salt drain the soaked rice, dals and chillies, keeping the soaking water aside. grind everything with the ginger, curry leaves, asafoetida and salt, adding water in small splashes, to a coarse batter with the texture of wet semolina. transfer to a bowl and stir in the chopped onion, coconut and coriander. the batter should be thick enough to mound on a spoon. rest the batter 20 minutes while the tawa heats over medium. pour a ladleful onto the hot tawa and spread outward with the back of the ladle to a 20cm round, about 5mm thick — thicker than a dosa. make a coin-sized hole in the centre and drizzle 1 tbsp sesame oil around the rim and into the hole. cook 3 to 4 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is a mottled deep brown. flip and cook 2 minutes more, pressing lightly with the spatula, then serve hot with avial or plain jaggery and butter.

entries.title: Akki Roti
entries.snippet: a rice flour flatbread patted straight onto the pan with onion, carrot and dill
entries.text: akki roti tamil nadu a rice flour flatbread patted straight onto the pan with onion, carrot and dill vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free rice flour onion carrot green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) dill (suva) curry leaves cumin seeds coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil water salt mix the rice flour, onion, carrot, green chilli, coriander, dill, curry leaves, cumin, coconut and salt in a wide bowl. add the hot water in stages, mixing with a spoon at first, then kneading with your hand once it is cool enough to touch. knead 3 minutes to a soft, smooth, slightly sticky dough that holds a shape when squeezed. divide into 6 balls. grease a square of banana leaf, parchment or the back of the cold tawa with coconut oil. place one ball on the greased surface and pat it outward with wet fingertips into a 18cm round about 3mm thick, dipping your fingers in water as you go. make three or four small holes in the roti with your finger. invert the roti onto a medium-hot tawa, or if patting directly on the tawa, set it on the flame now. drizzle oil into the holes and around the rim. cover and cook 3 minutes until the underside has brown spots and the top looks dry. flip and cook uncovered 2 minutes more, pressing the edges down. serve hot with coconut chutney, yogurt or a spoon of butter.

entries.title: Beans Poriyal
entries.snippet: finely chopped french beans steamed dry and finished with fresh coconut
entries.text: beans poriyal tamil nadu finely chopped french beans steamed dry and finished with fresh coconut vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier french beans coconut (fresh or desiccated) moong dal mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal green chilli dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coconut oil water salt heat the coconut oil and pop the mustard seeds. add the urad dal and chana dal and fry to a light gold, about 1 minute. add the red chilli, green chilli, curry leaves and hing and fry 15 seconds. tip in the chopped beans and drained moong dal with the turmeric and salt and toss to coat. add 4 tbsp water, cover, and cook on low heat for 8 minutes. uncover and check: the beans should be bright green and just tender, with no water left in the pan. if any liquid remains, raise the heat and toss for a minute until the pan is dry. turn off the heat, fold in the grated coconut, and serve with rice and rasam.

entries.title: Beetroot Poriyal
entries.snippet: sweet grated beetroot finished with coconut and a mustard tempering
entries.text: beetroot poriyal tamil nadu sweet grated beetroot finished with coconut and a mustard tempering vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier beetroot coconut (fresh or desiccated) mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal green chilli curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coconut oil water salt heat the coconut oil in a kadhai and crackle the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. add the urad dal and chana dal and fry until they turn a light straw gold. drop in the slit green chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida and let them splutter for 10 seconds. tip in the grated beetroot and salt and stir to coat in the oil. add the water, cover and cook over medium-low for 8 minutes until the beetroot is tender but still has a slight bite. uncover and cook off any liquid over higher heat for 2 minutes, stirring. turn off the heat, fold through the grated coconut and serve warm alongside rice and sambar.

entries.title: Bisi Bele Bath
entries.snippet: karnataka's one-pot rice and dal with vegetables, tamarind and hot ghee
entries.text: bisi bele bath tamil nadu karnataka's one-pot rice and dal with vegetables, tamarind and hot ghee vegetarian gluten-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) toor dal (pigeon pea) tamarind sambar powder cinnamon cloves dried coconut (copra) carrot french beans peas onion turmeric powder jaggery asafoetida (hing) curry leaves mustard seeds dried red chillies cashews ghee water salt pressure cook the toor dal with 2 cups water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, then mash it smooth. separately cook the rice with 2.5 cups water until softer than you would want for plain rice. boil the carrot, beans, peas and onion in 1 cup salted water for 8 minutes, until a knife goes in with slight resistance. add the tamarind extract, sambar powder, cinnamon, clove powder, roasted coconut and salt to the vegetables. simmer this uncovered 8 minutes, until the raw tamarind edge disappears and the mixture darkens. fold in the mashed dal and the jaggery and cook 5 minutes more. stir in the cooked rice with the remaining water, a little at a time, until it flows like thick porridge. heat 3 tbsp ghee, pop the mustard seeds, fry the cashews to pale gold, then add the chilli, curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering in, stir once, and serve very hot with the remaining ghee spooned over each plate.

entries.title: Bottle Gourd Kootu
entries.snippet: gentle dal and gourd stew thickened with ground coconut and cumin
entries.text: bottle gourd kootu tamil nadu gentle dal and gourd stew thickened with ground coconut and cumin vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier bottle gourd (lauki) moong dal coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli rice (short/medium grain) turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) coconut oil mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies curry leaves water salt pressure cook the moong dal with 1.5 cups water and the turmeric for 3 whistles, then mash it lightly. meanwhile simmer the cubed gourd in 1 cup water with a little salt for 8 minutes, covered. test it with a knife — it should give easily but still hold its cube shape. grind the coconut, 1 tsp cumin seeds, green chilli and raw rice with 1/2 cup water to a smooth paste. add the mashed dal to the gourd along with the salt and bring it to a simmer. stir in the ground coconut paste and the hing and cook 5 minutes on low heat. loosen with hot water until it is thicker than sambar but still spoonable. heat the coconut oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the urad dal, remaining cumin, red chilli and curry leaves. pour the tempering over the kootu and serve with rice and a poriyal.

entries.title: Cabbage Poriyal
entries.snippet: shredded cabbage cooked quick and sweet with coconut and split dals
entries.text: cabbage poriyal tamil nadu shredded cabbage cooked quick and sweet with coconut and split dals vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier cabbage onion coconut (fresh or desiccated) mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal green chilli dried red chillies curry leaves turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) coconut oil salt heat the coconut oil and pop the mustard seeds until they finish jumping. add the urad dal and drained chana dal and fry until golden, about 1 minute. add the red chilli, green chilli and curry leaves and let them crackle 15 seconds. add the onion and cook 3 minutes until soft and translucent. tip in the cabbage with the turmeric, hing and salt and toss hard to coat everything. cook uncovered on high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, tossing every minute. stop while it still has a slight crunch and smells sweet rather than sharp. take it off the heat, fold in the grated coconut and serve warm.

entries.title: Coconut Chutney
entries.snippet: fresh white chutney of coconut and roasted gram with a mustard tempering
entries.text: coconut chutney tamil nadu fresh white chutney of coconut and roasted gram with a mustard tempering vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier coconut (fresh or desiccated) chana dal green chilli ginger tamarind water coconut oil mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) salt put the coconut, roasted gram, green chilli, ginger, tamarind and salt in the blender jar. add 1/4 cup of the cold water and grind in short bursts, scraping down twice. add the rest of the water a spoon at a time until it grinds to a thick, just-pourable paste. grind 30 seconds more so it is smooth but still has a faint grain to it, then scrape into a bowl. heat the coconut oil in a small pan until it shimmers and pop the mustard seeds. add the urad dal and fry until it turns pale gold, about 40 seconds. add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing and let them crackle for 10 seconds. pour the tempering over the chutney and serve without stirring it in.

entries.title: Curd Rice
entries.snippet: cooling mashed rice set in yogurt with a mustard and chilli tempering
entries.text: curd rice tamil nadu cooling mashed rice set in yogurt with a mustard and chilli tempering vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) yogurt / dahi milk green chilli ginger curry leaves mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) pomegranate salt mash the warm cooked rice against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle until no whole grains remain. stir in the milk and salt and let it stand 5 minutes to cool further. fold in the whisked yogurt, the minced ginger and green chilli. check the consistency — it should be loose and pourable, since it thickens as it sits. heat the oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds. add the urad dal, fry to pale gold, then add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing off the heat. pour the tempering over the curd rice and fold it through once. top with pomegranate seeds and coriander and serve cool, not chilled.

entries.title: Idli
entries.snippet: Steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal, the lightest thing in Indian breakfast
entries.text: idli tamil nadu steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal, the lightest thing in indian breakfast vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) poha (flattened rice) salt soak the rice in one bowl and the urad dal with fenugreek in another, for 5 hours. soak the poha for 20 minutes before grinding. grind the urad dal first with cold water until white, fluffy and doubled in volume. test it: a spoon of batter should float in water. grind the rice to a slightly grainy paste, then fold the two together by hand with salt. cover loosely and ferment 8-12 hours until risen and bubbly. grease the idli plates, fill three-quarters full, and steam 10-12 minutes. a skewer should come out clean. rest 3 minutes before unmoulding, then serve with sambar and coconut chutney.

entries.title: Keerai Masiyal
entries.snippet: soft mashed greens with dal and a garlic tempering, the everyday rice-plate side
entries.text: keerai masiyal tamil nadu soft mashed greens with dal and a garlic tempering, the everyday rice-plate side vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier amaranth greens (chaulai) toor dal (pigeon pea) moong dal turmeric powder garlic dried red chillies cumin seeds mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) sesame oil (gingelly / til) water salt pressure cook the toor dal and moong dal with turmeric and 300ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own. meanwhile boil the greens in 100ml water with a pinch of salt, uncovered, for 5 minutes until they wilt to a quarter of their volume. mash the cooked dal with the back of a ladle until smooth. tip the greens and their liquid into the dal and mash together with a wooden masher for a minute. it should be thick and spoonable, not soupy. simmer 5 minutes over low heat, seasoning with salt. for the tempering, heat the sesame oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, red chillies and crushed garlic. fry until the garlic is golden at the edges, about 90 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida off the heat. pour the tempering over the masiyal, stir once and serve with hot rice and a spoon of sesame oil.

entries.title: Kesari Bath
entries.snippet: glossy saffron semolina pudding set soft with ghee, cashew and cardamom
entries.text: kesari bath tamil nadu glossy saffron semolina pudding set soft with ghee, cashew and cardamom vegetarian no-onion-garlic rava / sooji (semolina) sugar ghee milk water saffron green cardamom cashews raisins (kishmish) salt fry the cashews and raisins in 2 tbsp ghee until the nuts are golden and the raisins swell. lift them out and set aside. add 2 tbsp more ghee to the kadhai and roast the rava over low-medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes until it smells nutty and each grain is separate and pale gold. in another pan bring the water, milk and pinch of salt to a rolling boil. pour the boiling liquid into the roasted rava in a steady stream while stirring hard and continuously with the other hand. stir in the saffron milk, then cover and cook on low for 4 minutes until the rava has absorbed everything and looks fluffy. add the sugar all at once. the mixture will loosen and turn liquid again; do not panic. stir over low heat for 5 minutes until it thickens and starts leaving the sides of the pan. drizzle in the remaining ghee a tablespoon at a time, stirring, until the kesari is glossy and no longer sticks to the pan. fold in the crushed cardamom and the fried cashews and raisins, and take it off the heat. serve warm, either spooned into bowls or pressed into a greased tray and cut into squares once cool.

entries.title: Lemon Rice
entries.snippet: yellow rice cut with lemon, peanuts and split dals for crunch
entries.text: lemon rice tamil nadu yellow rice cut with lemon, peanuts and split dals for crunch vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) lemon / lime turmeric powder groundnut oil mustard seeds chana dal urad dal (black gram) peanuts dried red chillies green chilli curry leaves asafoetida (hing) ginger coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds. add the peanuts and fry 2 minutes until they darken a shade and smell roasted. add the chana dal and urad dal and fry until golden, about 1 minute. add the red chilli, green chilli, curry leaves and hing and let the leaves crackle for 15 seconds. stir in the turmeric and take the pan off the heat immediately. add the lemon juice and salt to the warm tempering and swirl to combine. tip in the cooled rice and fold gently with a flat spatula until every grain is yellow. rest 10 minutes off the heat for the flavour to soak in, then scatter the coriander and serve.

entries.title: Masala Dosa
entries.snippet: Fermented rice and lentil crepe with a spiced potato filling
entries.text: masala dosa tamil nadu fermented rice and lentil crepe with a spiced potato filling vegetarian vegan gluten-free nut-free dairy-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) potato onion green chilli ginger turmeric powder mustard seeds chana dal curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil salt soak the rice in one bowl, and the urad dal with the fenugreek in another, for 6 hours. grind the urad dal first with a little cold water until very light and fluffy, then the rice to a slightly grainy paste. combine, add salt and mix with your hand for a minute; the warmth helps it start. cover loosely and leave in a warm place 8-14 hours until doubled, bubbly and faintly sour. stir gently before use and thin with water to a pouring consistency. for the filling, heat oil, splutter the mustard seeds with the chana dal, curry leaves and asafoetida, add the onion, chilli and ginger and cook until soft. add turmeric, then the crumbled potato, salt and coriander. keep warm. heat a flat tawa until a drop of water skitters across it. rub with a halved onion dipped in oil, pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread outwards in a quick spiral. drizzle oil around the edge and cook until the underside is crisp and deep gold, 2-3 minutes. do not flip. place a scoop of potato in the centre, fold and serve straight away with coconut chutney and sambar.

entries.title: Medu Vada
entries.snippet: crisp-shelled urad dal doughnuts, cloud-soft inside, peppery with ginger
entries.text: medu vada tamil nadu crisp-shelled urad dal doughnuts, cloud-soft inside, peppery with ginger vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier urad dal (black gram) black pepper cumin seeds ginger green chilli curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) rice flour asafoetida (hing) neutral oil salt grind the drained dal with 2 to 3 tbsp of ice-cold water, in short bursts, to a thick fluffy paste. beat the batter with your hand for 3 minutes until it lightens in colour and feels aerated. test it by dropping a pinch into a bowl of water — it should float within seconds. fold in the pepper, cumin, ginger, chilli, curry leaves, coriander, hing and salt. heat the oil to 170c — a drop of batter should rise steadily, not shoot to the surface. wet your palm, take a lime-sized ball of batter, flatten it and make a hole through the centre with a wet thumb. slide the vada off your palm into the oil from close to the surface, and fry 4 or 5 at a time. fry 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until deep gold and the sizzle drops to a quiet crackle. drain on a rack rather than paper so the underside stays crisp, and serve immediately with coconut chutney.

entries.title: Milagu Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: a dark, peppery tamarind gravy roasted from whole spices, the household cure-all
entries.text: milagu kuzhambu tamil nadu a dark, peppery tamarind gravy roasted from whole spices, the household cure-all vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic healthier tamarind black pepper toor dal (pigeon pea) chana dal urad dal (black gram) dried red chillies coriander powder fenugreek seeds (methi) curry leaves mustard seeds asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder jaggery sesame oil (gingelly / til) salt dry roast the peppercorns, the three dals, the red chillies and fenugreek seeds in a kadhai over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the dals are reddish gold and the pepper smells sharp. turn off the heat, stir in the coriander powder and one sprig of curry leaves, and let the residual heat toast them for 30 seconds. cool completely, then grind to a fine powder in a dry blender. heat the sesame oil in the same kadhai and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the remaining curry leaves and the asafoetida. pour in the strained tamarind water with the turmeric and salt and bring to a rolling boil. boil hard, uncovered, for 8 minutes to cook out the raw edge of the tamarind. whisk the ground spice powder with 60ml water to a slurry and stir it in. simmer 10 to 12 minutes over low heat until the gravy thickens and the oil separates and floats in a dark ring on top. stir in the jaggery, cook 2 minutes more and take off the heat. serve a spoonful over hot rice with a poriyal and a papad.

entries.title: More Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: sour yogurt curry with ground coconut and cumin, never boiled
entries.text: more kuzhambu tamil nadu sour yogurt curry with ground coconut and cumin, never boiled vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi ash gourd (petha) coconut (fresh or desiccated) cumin seeds green chilli rice (short/medium grain) toor dal (pigeon pea) turmeric powder mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) coconut oil salt simmer the ash gourd in 1 cup water with the turmeric and salt for 8 minutes, until translucent at the edges. grind the coconut, cumin, green chilli, soaked rice and toor dal with 1/2 cup water to a very smooth paste. add the paste to the cooked gourd and simmer 6 minutes, until the raw rice smell disappears. take the pan off the heat and let it stop bubbling completely, about 2 minutes. pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring constantly as it goes. return to the lowest possible heat and warm it only until steam rises and it thickens slightly. check the salt and take it off the heat entirely. heat the coconut oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the fenugreek, red chilli, curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering over and serve with hot rice and a dry poriyal.

entries.title: Mysore Pak
entries.snippet: porous gram flour fudge that dissolves in ghee as you bite it
entries.text: mysore pak tamil nadu porous gram flour fudge that dissolves in ghee as you bite it vegetarian gluten-free nut-free besan (gram flour) ghee sugar water green cardamom dissolve the sugar in the water and boil until the syrup reaches one-string consistency, about 6 minutes. lower the heat and add the sifted besan in a thin stream, whisking hard so no lumps form. whisk until the mixture is smooth and glossy, about 1 minute. start adding the hot ghee one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting until each ladle is absorbed. keep going for 12 to 15 minutes as the mixture froths, bubbles and rises in the pan. watch for the moment it turns porous and foamy and the last ghee refuses to be absorbed and pools at the sides. pour it into the greased tray immediately without scraping the pan and level the top with the back of a ladle. wait 4 minutes, then score it into diamonds while still hot. cool completely for an hour before lifting the pieces out.

entries.title: Neer Dosa
entries.snippet: lacy, paper-thin rice crepes from the coast, soft and faintly sweet
entries.text: neer dosa tamil nadu lacy, paper-thin rice crepes from the coast, soft and faintly sweet vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) coconut oil water salt drain the soaked rice and grind it with the grated coconut and 250ml water to a completely smooth batter, 4 to 5 minutes in the blender. pour into a bowl, stir in the salt and thin with the remaining water until it is the consistency of thin milk. heat the tawa over medium-high until a drop of water skitters across it, then wipe it with a coconut-oil-dipped cloth. stir the batter well, then pour a ladleful from a height onto the hot tawa, moving in a spiral from the outside in. do not spread it with the ladle. cover and cook 60 to 90 seconds until the surface loses its wet sheen and the edges lift on their own. do not flip. fold the dosa in half and then in half again with a spatula and slide it onto a plate. wipe the tawa with the oiled cloth between each dosa and stir the batter every time, since the rice settles fast. serve warm with coconut chutney, a jaggery-coconut filling, or a coastal fish curry.

entries.title: Paruppu Payasam
entries.snippet: moong dal pudding sweetened with jaggery and finished in coconut milk
entries.text: paruppu payasam tamil nadu moong dal pudding sweetened with jaggery and finished in coconut milk vegetarian gluten-free moong dal jaggery coconut milk ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) coconut (fresh or desiccated) green cardamom dry ginger powder (saunth) water pressure cook the roasted dal with 2 cups water for 4 whistles until completely soft. mash the cooked dal lightly with a ladle, leaving some texture. melt the jaggery with 1/2 cup water on low heat, then strain out the sediment. add the strained jaggery syrup to the dal and simmer 8 minutes until it thickens and darkens. stir in the thin coconut milk and simmer 3 minutes more. take the pan off the heat and let it stop bubbling before adding the thick coconut milk. stir in the cardamom and dry ginger powder. heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the coconut slivers to gold, then the cashews, then the raisins until they puff. pour the ghee and fried garnish over the payasam and serve warm.

entries.title: Pesarattu
entries.snippet: a green whole-moong crepe topped with raw onion, ginger and chilli
entries.text: pesarattu tamil nadu a green whole-moong crepe topped with raw onion, ginger and chilli vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier whole moong (sabut moong) rice (short/medium grain) green chilli ginger cumin seeds onion coriander leaves (cilantro) neutral oil water salt drain the soaked moong and rice and grind with the whole green chillies, ginger, 1 tsp of the cumin and the salt to a smooth batter, adding water gradually. stir in the remaining cumin seeds whole, for texture. heat the tawa over medium-high, then rub it with half an onion dipped in oil. lower the heat slightly, pour a ladleful in the centre and spread outward in a slow spiral to a 22cm round. scatter a generous tablespoon of chopped onion, chilli and coriander over the wet surface and press it down with the ladle. drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge and cook 3 minutes until the base is crisp and speckled brown and the edges curl away. flip and cook 1 minute only, just to set the onion. fold in half and serve hot with allam pachadi or a plain coconut chutney.

entries.title: Puliyodarai
entries.snippet: dark tamarind rice heavy with sesame oil, peanuts and roasted spice
entries.text: puliyodarai tamil nadu dark tamarind rice heavy with sesame oil, peanuts and roasted spice vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) tamarind sesame oil (gingelly / til) mustard seeds chana dal urad dal (black gram) peanuts dried red chillies fenugreek seeds (methi) black pepper coriander powder sesame seeds turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) curry leaves jaggery salt heat 4 tbsp sesame oil in a heavy kadhai and pop the mustard seeds. add the peanuts, chana dal and urad dal and fry until all three are deep gold, about 3 minutes. add the red chillies, curry leaves and hing and fry 20 seconds until the chillies puff. pour in the tamarind extract with the turmeric, coriander powder, jaggery and salt — it will spit, so stand back. simmer on medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the paste thickens, darkens and the oil separates and pools at the edges. stir in the roasted fenugreek, pepper and sesame powder and cook 1 minute more, then take it off the heat. fold roughly half the paste into the cooled rice with the remaining 2 tbsp sesame oil. rest at least 30 minutes before serving so the rice takes on the colour evenly.

entries.title: Rasam
entries.snippet: thin peppery tamarind broth, sharp with tomato and crushed pepper
entries.text: rasam tamil nadu thin peppery tamarind broth, sharp with tomato and crushed pepper vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier tamarind tomato toor dal (pigeon pea) rasam powder black pepper cumin seeds garlic turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) curry leaves dried red chillies mustard seeds ghee coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt squash the tomatoes into the tamarind extract with your hand and add the turmeric, rasam powder and salt. simmer this uncovered on medium heat for 8 minutes, until the raw tamarind smell goes and the surface turns matte. stir in the crushed pepper and cumin and the garlic, and simmer 2 minutes more. pour in the mashed dal loosened with 2 cups of water and the dal cooking liquid. bring it to the point where a rim of froth rises at the edges, then take it straight off the heat. heat the ghee in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds, then add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering over the rasam and cover for 2 minutes to trap the aroma. stir through the coriander leaves and serve over hot rice, or in a tumbler alongside.

entries.title: Rava Dosa
entries.snippet: lacy, brittle semolina crepe you pour rather than spread
entries.text: rava dosa tamil nadu lacy, brittle semolina crepe you pour rather than spread vegetarian vegan dairy-free nut-free rava / sooji (semolina) rice flour plain flour (maida) cumin seeds black pepper green chilli ginger curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) onion water neutral oil salt whisk the rava, rice flour, maida and salt with 2 cups of water until completely lump-free. stir in the cumin, pepper, chilli, ginger, curry leaves, coriander and onion. add the remaining 2 cups of water and rest the batter 30 minutes. check the consistency — it should run off the ladle in a thin stream like full-cream milk. heat the tawa until quite hot, then lower the heat to medium — a drop of water should vanish instantly. pour the batter from a height in a ring around the outside, then fill the gaps with a few splashes. drizzle a teaspoon of oil around the edge and over the middle. cook undisturbed 2 to 3 minutes until the edges lift by themselves and the surface is dry and golden. flip and cook 45 seconds, or fold straight out of the pan if you like it very crisp. wipe the tawa with half an onion between dosas and stir the batter before each pour.

entries.title: Sakkarai Pongal
entries.snippet: rice and moong dal cooked soft in jaggery syrup with cardamom and fried cashew
entries.text: sakkarai pongal tamil nadu rice and moong dal cooked soft in jaggery syrup with cardamom and fried cashew vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) moong dal jaggery ghee cashews raisins (kishmish) green cardamom dry ginger powder (saunth) milk water coconut (fresh or desiccated) dry roast the moong dal in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until it smells nutty and turns a shade darker. wash the rice and roasted dal together, then pressure cook with the milk and 500ml water for 5 whistles. let the pressure fall naturally, open, and mash the rice and dal together with a ladle until creamy. meanwhile melt the jaggery with 150ml water in a separate pan over medium heat, stirring, then strain through a sieve to remove grit. boil the strained syrup 4 minutes until it thickens slightly and coats a spoon. pour the hot syrup into the mashed rice and stir over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan. fry the cashews, coconut slivers and raisins in 2 tbsp of the ghee until the nuts are golden and the raisins plump, then tip them in with their ghee. stir in the remaining ghee a spoonful at a time, along with the crushed cardamom and dry ginger powder. cook 2 minutes more until glossy, then serve warm.

entries.title: Sambar
entries.snippet: Toor dal and vegetables in a tamarind broth, built on freshly ground sambar powder
entries.text: sambar tamil nadu toor dal and vegetables in a tamarind broth, built on freshly ground sambar powder vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) tamarind drumstick (moringa pod) pumpkin okra / bhindi shallots (small red onions) tomato sambar powder turmeric powder asafoetida (hing) mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) dried red chillies curry leaves coriander leaves (cilantro) jaggery coconut oil salt pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric until completely soft, then whisk it smooth. simmer the tamarind extract with the shallots, tomato and harder vegetables, the sambar powder and salt for 12-15 minutes. add quicker vegetables like okra for the last 5 minutes. stir in the whisked dal and enough hot water to reach a pourable consistency. simmer 8 minutes; do not boil hard. temper mustard seeds, fenugreek, dried chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida in oil and pour it in. add jaggery if the tamarind is sharp, finish with coriander, and rest 10 minutes before serving.

entries.title: Thayir Vadai
entries.snippet: fried urad dal vadas soaked soft in seasoned yogurt, cold and gently spiced
entries.text: thayir vadai tamil nadu fried urad dal vadas soaked soft in seasoned yogurt, cold and gently spiced vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic urad dal (black gram) green chilli ginger black pepper curry leaves asafoetida (hing) yogurt / dahi milk mustard seeds dried red chillies coriander leaves (cilantro) red chilli powder neutral oil water salt drain the soaked dal thoroughly and grind to a thick, fluffy white batter, adding cold water a tablespoon at a time. a blob dropped in water should float. beat the batter by hand for 2 minutes to aerate it, then fold in the green chilli, ginger, crushed pepper, chopped curry leaves, asafoetida and salt. heat the oil to 170c. wet your palm, flatten a lime-sized ball of batter on it and make a hole through the centre with your thumb. slide the vadas into the oil, 4 at a time, and fry 4 to 5 minutes turning once, until pale gold — not dark. drain on paper, then drop the hot vadas straight into a bowl of warm salted water for 15 minutes. lift each vada out and press it gently between your palms to squeeze out the water. it should feel like a wrung sponge. arrange the vadas in a single layer in a shallow dish and pour the cold yogurt-milk mixture over them. refrigerate at least 2 hours so the vadas drink up the yogurt and swell. just before serving, heat 1 tbsp of the frying oil and crackle the mustard seeds, red chillies and remaining curry leaves, and pour it over. dust with chilli powder, scatter the coriander and serve cold.

entries.title: Thengai Sadam
entries.snippet: leftover rice tossed through toasted coconut, dals and curry leaves
entries.text: thengai sadam tamil nadu leftover rice tossed through toasted coconut, dals and curry leaves vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free no-onion-garlic healthier rice (short/medium grain) coconut (fresh or desiccated) mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal dried red chillies green chilli cashews curry leaves ginger asafoetida (hing) coconut oil salt spread the cooled rice on a wide plate, sprinkle with salt and 1 tbsp of the coconut oil, and separate the grains with your fingers. dry roast the grated coconut in a kadhai over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until it just turns pale gold and smells toasted. set aside. heat the remaining coconut oil in the same kadhai and crackle the mustard seeds. add the urad dal, chana dal and cashews and fry until all three are golden, about 2 minutes. add the red chillies, slit green chillies, ginger, curry leaves and asafoetida and fry 30 seconds until the leaves crisp. return the toasted coconut to the pan and stir for 1 minute so it takes up the tempering. turn off the heat, tip in the rice and fold everything together gently with a flat spatula. cover and let it sit 5 minutes so the flavours settle, then check the salt and serve.

entries.title: Tomato Chutney
entries.snippet: deep red cooked chutney, tangy and hot, for idli and dosa
entries.text: tomato chutney tamil nadu deep red cooked chutney, tangy and hot, for idli and dosa vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier tomato onion garlic dried red chillies urad dal (black gram) chana dal tamarind sesame oil (gingelly / til) mustard seeds curry leaves asafoetida (hing) salt heat 3 tbsp sesame oil and fry the urad dal and chana dal until golden, about 90 seconds. add the red chillies and fry 20 seconds until they darken and swell, then lift out the dals and chillies. in the same oil, cook the onion and garlic until the onion is soft and edged with brown, about 6 minutes. add the tomatoes, tamarind and salt and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes. keep going until the tomatoes lose all shape and the oil pools red at the sides of the pan. cool the mixture completely, then grind it with the reserved dals and chillies to a coarse paste, no water. heat the last 1 tbsp oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves and hing. pour the tempering over the chutney and stir it through.

entries.title: Tomato Pappu
entries.snippet: andhra everyday toor dal cooked soft with sour tomato and garlic
entries.text: tomato pappu tamil nadu andhra everyday toor dal cooked soft with sour tomato and garlic vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier toor dal (pigeon pea) tomato onion green chilli garlic turmeric powder tamarind red chilli powder mustard seeds cumin seeds dried red chillies curry leaves asafoetida (hing) neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt pressure cook the dal with the tomatoes, green chilli, turmeric and 2.5 cups water for 5 whistles. let the pressure drop naturally, open, and mash the dal against the side of the pot until smooth. add the salt, chilli powder and tamarind if using, with 1/2 cup water, and simmer 5 minutes. adjust with hot water until it pours thickly off the ladle. heat the oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin. add the crushed garlic and fry until the cloves turn golden at the edges, about 1 minute. add the onion and fry 3 minutes until soft and lightly browned. add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing and let them crackle for 15 seconds. pour the tempering into the dal, stir once, scatter the coriander and serve over hot rice.

entries.title: Upma
entries.snippet: soft savoury semolina with crackling dal, ginger and curry leaves
entries.text: upma tamil nadu soft savoury semolina with crackling dal, ginger and curry leaves vegetarian vegan dairy-free healthier rava / sooji (semolina) water onion green chilli ginger curry leaves mustard seeds urad dal (black gram) chana dal cashews neutral oil coriander leaves (cilantro) lemon / lime salt heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds until they jump and quieten. add the urad dal and chana dal and fry until both turn a light red-gold, about 90 seconds. add the cashews, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves and fry 30 seconds until the leaves crisp. add the onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 4 minutes — no browning. pour in the boiling water with the salt and let it come back to a rolling boil. lower the heat and add the roasted rava in a thin steady stream with one hand while stirring hard with the other. keep stirring for 2 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan. cover and steam on the lowest heat for 3 minutes, then turn off and rest 2 minutes. fluff with a fork, squeeze over the lemon and scatter the coriander.

entries.title: Uttapam
entries.snippet: thick fermented pancake with onion and tomato pressed into the top
entries.text: uttapam tamil nadu thick fermented pancake with onion and tomato pressed into the top vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) urad dal (black gram) fenugreek seeds (methi) onion tomato green chilli coriander leaves (cilantro) curry leaves sesame oil (gingelly / til) water salt grind the urad dal and fenugreek with about 3/4 cup cold water to a light, fluffy paste. grind the rice separately with 3/4 cup water to a batter with a fine sandy grain still in it. mix the two by hand with the salt, in wide circular strokes, for 2 minutes. cover and leave to ferment 8 to 12 hours until risen by half and smelling pleasantly sour. heat a tawa on medium until a flick of water dances and evaporates in about 2 seconds. pour a ladle of batter and spread it only slightly, to a thick round about 12cm across. scatter a handful of onion, tomato, chilli, coriander and curry leaves over the wet surface and press them in with the back of the ladle. drizzle a teaspoon of sesame oil around the edge and cook 3 minutes until the base is golden and the top has set matte. flip and cook 90 seconds on the topping side to caramelise the onion, then serve straight from the pan.

entries.title: Vatha Kuzhambu
entries.snippet: dark, oily tamarind gravy with shallots, spiked with fenugreek
entries.text: vatha kuzhambu tamil nadu dark, oily tamarind gravy with shallots, spiked with fenugreek vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free tamarind shallots (small red onions) sesame oil (gingelly / til) sambar powder dried red chillies garlic mustard seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) chana dal curry leaves asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder jaggery rice flour salt heat the sesame oil in a kadhai and pop the mustard seeds. add the fenugreek seeds and chana dal and fry 20 seconds until the fenugreek turns reddish. add the red chillies, curry leaves and hing and let them crackle. add the whole shallots and garlic and fry 5 minutes until the shallots are browned in patches and glossy. stir in the sambar powder and turmeric and fry 30 seconds in the oil. pour in the tamarind extract with the salt and jaggery and bring to a simmer. simmer uncovered on low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. it is done when the volume has dropped by a third and the sesame oil floats clear on top. if it is still thin after 25 minutes, stir in the slaked rice flour and cook 2 minutes more. rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with rice, a spoon of sesame oil and a poriyal.

entries.title: Ven Pongal
entries.snippet: soft rice and moong dal loaded with ghee, black pepper and cumin
entries.text: ven pongal tamil nadu soft rice and moong dal loaded with ghee, black pepper and cumin vegetarian gluten-free healthier rice (short/medium grain) moong dal ghee black pepper cumin seeds ginger curry leaves cashews asafoetida (hing) water salt pressure cook the rice and roasted dal with 5 cups water and the salt for 5 whistles. let the pressure fall on its own, then open and mash the mixture with a ladle until it is soft and shapeless. keep it on the lowest heat while you make the tempering, stirring so the base does not catch. heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cashews to pale gold, about 40 seconds. add the cumin seeds and crushed pepper and let them sizzle for 20 seconds. add the ginger, curry leaves and hing and fry until the leaves crisp. pour the whole tempering into the pongal and fold it through. check the consistency and loosen with hot water until it falls off the ladle in a thick sheet. serve immediately with the remaining ghee spooned over, alongside coconut chutney.

entries.title: Aloo ke Gutke
entries.snippet: boiled potatoes tossed in smoking mustard oil and chilli until the edges crisp
entries.text: aloo ke gutke himachali/pahari boiled potatoes tossed in smoking mustard oil and chilli until the edges crisp vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free no-onion-garlic potato mustard oil mustard seeds cumin seeds dried red chillies asafoetida (hing) turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder green chilli lemon / lime coriander leaves (cilantro) salt heat the mustard oil in a kadhai over high heat until it smokes and the sharp smell mellows, about 2 minutes. lower the heat to medium and crackle the mustard seeds until they pop, about 30 seconds, then add the cumin and broken red chillies. add the asafoetida and the slit green chillies and let them blister for 15 seconds. take the pan off the heat, stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, and count to five. return to medium heat, tip in the potato chunks and salt, and toss until every piece is coated yellow. spread the potatoes in a single layer and leave them undisturbed for 4 minutes so a crust forms underneath. turn them over in sections and fry another 5-6 minutes until the edges are brown and crisp in patches. squeeze over the lemon juice, scatter the coriander leaves and toss once. serve immediately, while the crust is still audible, with kumaoni raita or plain rice.

entries.title: Chainsoo
entries.snippet: dark roasted black gram dal from the kumaon hills, smoky and heavy
entries.text: chainsoo himachali/pahari dark roasted black gram dal from the kumaon hills, smoky and heavy vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier whole urad (sabut urad) mustard oil cumin seeds asafoetida (hing) garlic ginger green chilli dried red chillies turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder dry ginger powder (saunth) garam masala water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) dry-roast the whole urad in a heavy kadhai over medium heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring constantly, until the skins turn matte black-brown and the kitchen smells strongly nutty. cool the dal fully on a plate, 10 minutes, then grind to a coarse meal in a blender — the texture of semolina, not flour. grinding it warm turns it pasty. heat the mustard oil in the same kadhai until it just begins to smoke, then lower the heat and let it settle for 30 seconds. crackle the cumin seeds and broken red chillies for 20 seconds, then add the asafoetida. add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 2 minutes until the garlic is pale gold and no longer smells sharp. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, then immediately tip in the ground urad. fry on low heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring the whole time, until the meal darkens and loosens from the pan. pour in the hot water a ladleful at a time, whisking after each addition so no lumps form. add salt. simmer uncovered on low heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the dal is the colour of wet slate and thick enough to coat a spoon. stir in the dry ginger powder and garam masala, cook 2 minutes more, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes. scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot over plain rice with a spoon of mustard oil on top.

entries.title: Gahat ki Dal
entries.snippet: slow-cooked horse gram, nutty and mineral, the winter dal of every hill house
entries.text: gahat ki dal himachali/pahari slow-cooked horse gram, nutty and mineral, the winter dal of every hill house vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier horse gram (kulith) mustard oil cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) garlic ginger green chilli tomato turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder dry ginger powder (saunth) water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) drain the soaked horse gram and pressure-cook it with the litre of water and the turmeric for 6 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally, about 15 minutes. check a grain — it should crush easily between finger and thumb. if not, cook 3 more whistles. heat the mustard oil in a wide pan until it smokes lightly, then lower the heat. crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds for 20 seconds, then add the asafoetida. add the garlic and fry 2 minutes to pale gold, then the ginger and green chilli for 1 minute more. add the tomatoes with the coriander powder and chilli powder. cook 8 minutes on medium until the tomatoes collapse and oil beads at the edge of the masala. tip in the cooked horse gram with all its liquid and the salt. bring to a boil. simmer uncovered on low for 20-25 minutes, mashing a ladleful of grains against the side of the pan halfway through to thicken the broth. stir in the dry ginger powder and take off the heat. rest 5 minutes, scatter coriander leaves and serve with rice or mandua roti.

entries.title: Jhangora ki Kheer
entries.snippet: barnyard millet simmered slowly in milk with jaggery and cardamom, grainy and gentle
entries.text: jhangora ki kheer himachali/pahari barnyard millet simmered slowly in milk with jaggery and cardamom, grainy and gentle vegetarian gluten-free no-onion-garlic rice (short/medium grain) milk jaggery green cardamom ghee almonds raisins (kishmish) saffron toast the drained grain in the ghee over medium heat for 2 minutes until each grain is glossy and smells faintly nutty. pour in the milk, bring to a boil, then drop the heat to its lowest setting. simmer uncovered for 35-40 minutes, stirring every 4-5 minutes and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan with a flat spoon. keep going until the grains are soft and swollen and the milk has reduced by about a third, coating the spoon thickly. stir in the almonds and raisins and cook 3 minutes more, until the raisins plump. take the pan off the heat and let it stand for 8-10 minutes, until you can comfortably hold a hand against the side of the pan. stir in the grated jaggery until fully dissolved, then the crushed cardamom and the saffron milk. taste and add a little more jaggery if you want it sweeter, then rest 10 minutes for the flavours to settle. serve warm, or chill 2 hours and serve cold — it thickens considerably in the fridge.

entries.title: Kafuli
entries.snippet: garhwali spinach and fenugreek greens thickened to a silky, sour-edged green curry
entries.text: kafuli himachali/pahari garhwali spinach and fenugreek greens thickened to a silky, sour-edged green curry vegetarian gluten-free nut-free healthier spinach fenugreek leaves (methi) buttermilk (chaas) rice flour mustard oil cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder water salt ghee bring 200ml water to a boil, add the spinach and methi leaves, and blanch for 3 minutes until they wilt down and turn deep green. drain, keeping the green cooking water, and cool the greens under cold running water for 30 seconds. blend the greens with the green chillies, ginger and 4 tbsp of the reserved water to a coarse purée — leave a little texture rather than making it smooth. whisk the rice flour into the buttermilk until completely smooth and set aside. heat the mustard oil in a pan until it smokes lightly, then lower the heat and crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds for 20 seconds. add the asafoetida and garlic and fry 2 minutes until pale gold. stir in the turmeric and coriander powder, then add the green purée and the salt. cook 5 minutes on medium, stirring, until it darkens and tightens. turn the heat to its lowest setting and pour in the buttermilk mixture in a slow stream, stirring continuously in one direction. simmer very gently for 10-12 minutes, stirring often, until the curry thickens enough to hold a line drawn across the back of a spoon. taste for salt, rest 3 minutes off the heat, and serve in bowls with a teaspoon of ghee floated on top, alongside rice.

entries.title: Kumaoni Raita
entries.snippet: grated cucumber in yogurt sharpened with ground mustard until it stings the nose
entries.text: kumaoni raita himachali/pahari grated cucumber in yogurt sharpened with ground mustard until it stings the nose vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic yogurt / dahi cucumber mustard seeds turmeric powder green chilli red chilli powder black salt (kala namak) mustard oil dried red chillies coriander leaves (cilantro) water salt soak the mustard seeds in the 2 tbsp water for 10 minutes, then grind with the green chillies and turmeric to a smooth, bright yellow paste in a blender. squeeze the grated cucumber firmly in your fist over the sink and discard the liquid. whisk the yogurt in a bowl until completely smooth with no lumps, about 1 minute. fold in the mustard paste a teaspoon at a time, tasting as you go, until the raita is as pungent as you want it. stir in the squeezed cucumber, the salt and the black salt. heat the mustard oil in a small pan until it smokes, drop in the broken red chilli for 10 seconds, and pour the tempering over the raita. chill for at least 20 minutes so the mustard heat settles into the yogurt. dust with chilli powder, scatter the coriander leaves and serve cold with aloo ke gutke or rice.

entries.title: Mandua ki Roti
entries.snippet: dark finger millet flatbread, earthy and faintly sweet, soft only while hot
entries.text: mandua ki roti himachali/pahari dark finger millet flatbread, earthy and faintly sweet, soft only while hot vegetarian gluten-free nut-free no-onion-garlic ragi (finger millet) flour water salt ghee rice flour mix the ragi flour and salt in a heatproof bowl and make a well in the centre. pour in the boiling water all at once and stir hard with a wooden spoon for 30 seconds until it comes together as a shaggy, steaming mass. cover and leave 10 minutes, until cool enough to handle but still warm. knead in the bowl for 4-5 minutes with the heel of your hand until the dough is smooth, dark and slightly tacky — it should not crack when you press a ball flat. rest the dough covered with a damp cloth for 15 minutes. divide into 8 balls. dust a work surface with rice flour and pat each ball out with your palm into a 15cm round about 4mm thick, turning as you go. heat a tawa over medium-high until a drop of water skitters across it. lay a roti on the tawa and cook 60-70 seconds until the surface dulls and small pale spots appear. flip and cook the second side 60 seconds, pressing the edges gently with a folded cloth until it puffs in patches and dark freckles form. smear with ghee, stack in a cloth-lined box, and repeat with the rest. serve hot with gahat ki dal or chainsoo.

entries.title: Thechwani
entries.snippet: crushed radish and potato simmered with hill spices, coarse-textured and peppery
entries.text: thechwani himachali/pahari crushed radish and potato simmered with hill spices, coarse-textured and peppery vegetarian vegan gluten-free dairy-free nut-free healthier radish (mooli) potato mustard oil cumin seeds fenugreek seeds (methi) asafoetida (hing) garlic ginger green chilli turmeric powder coriander powder red chilli powder dry ginger powder (saunth) black pepper water salt coriander leaves (cilantro) crush the radish and potato in rough 3cm pieces — put them on a board and press down with the flat of a heavy knife, or pound with a pestle, so they split with ragged faces. heat the mustard oil in a pressure cooker until it smokes lightly, then lower the heat. crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds for 20 seconds, add the asafoetida, then the garlic, ginger and green chilli. fry 2-3 minutes until the garlic is gold and the raw smell is gone. stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder off the heat for 10 seconds, then return to the flame. add the crushed radish and potato with the salt and fry on medium-high for 8 minutes, stirring, until the radish loses its sharp smell and starts to catch on the base. pour in the water, close the cooker and cook for 3 whistles, then release the pressure naturally, about 10 minutes. open, mash a few pieces of potato against the side to thicken the gravy, and simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes until it clings rather than pools. stir in the dry ginger powder and crushed black pepper and cook 2 minutes more. rest 5 minutes, scatter coriander leaves and serve with rice or roti.
